The title of this chapter and section allude to Rosalind Krauss’s “Sculpture in the Expanded Field.” In this 1979 essay, she analyzes the historicism of postwar American art criticism, which assimilated modernist sculptural production into a universal formal category by constructing “a paternity” for it.[^en-intro-37] She argues that sculpture understood as a universal category alienates it from its historical boundedness and premodern logic of monumentality, as “it sits in a particular place and speaks in a symbolic tongue about the meaning or use of that place.”[^en-intro-38] Modernist sculpture and its criticism turned the monument into abstraction, “functionally placeless and largely self-referential.”[^en-intro-39] This autonomous mode of production would eventually collapse, as postmodern practice rejected modernism’s repressive paternity and insisted on putting art back into place. Sculpture, put into relational antinomy or proximity with landscape and architecture, became but one possible form in the expanded field. Krauss’s revisionist approach to the history of form suggests how a field like “Chinese contemporary art” needs expanding beyond historicist and hegemonic constructions: as either belated arrival on a global scene dominated by Western genealogies, or national patrimony of a China on the rise. The historical conditions through which Chinese contemporary art emerged necessitate an examination of aesthetics in relation to specific sites and histories, but without the presumption of national or cultural boundedness. This approach maps instead relational webs of meaning across space and time, deconstructing autonomous ideas of art as well as Eurocentric and masculinist discourses of belatedness.

本章及本节的标题都暗指罗莎琳德·克劳斯的《扩展场域中的雕塑》。在这篇1979年的文章中，她分析了战后美国艺术批评的历史主义——它通过为现代主义雕塑生产建构“一种父系”，将其吸收进一个普遍的形式范畴。[^zh-intro-37] 她论证，把雕塑理解为普遍范畴，会使它脱离自身的历史限定性和前现代的纪念碑性逻辑，因为“它坐落在一个特定位置，并以象征性的语言谈论该位置的意义或用途。”[^zh-intro-38] 现代主义雕塑及其批评把纪念碑变成抽象物，“在功能上无处所，且在很大程度上自我指涉。”[^zh-intro-39] 这种自主的生产模式最终会崩溃，因为后现代实践拒绝现代主义的压制性父系，坚持让艺术回到原位。雕塑在与景观和建筑的关系性对立或邻近中被放置，成为扩展场域中众多可能形式之一。克劳斯对形式历史的修正主义路径表明，像“中国当代艺术”这样的场域需要扩展，超越历史主义和霸权性建构：要么是迟到地抵达一个由西方谱系主导的全球场景，要么是崛起中国的民族遗产。中国当代艺术得以出现的历史条件，要求我们在具体场所和历史中考察美学，但不预设民族或文化的边界。这种方法转而绘制跨越空间与时间的关系性意义网络，解构自主的艺术观念，也解构欧洲中心主义和男性主义的迟到论话语。


〔原书 22〕

I label this field “Chinese contemporary art” rather than “contemporary Chinese art” because the works produced in the art worlds I describe most often get classified in China as *dangdai yishu*, literally meaning “contemporary art” but generally referring to works produced in particular media—oil painting, photography, video, installation, and performance art—seen as horizontally linked to contemporary art practice in the West.[^en-intro-40]

我把这个场域称为“Chinese contemporary art”（中国当代艺术），而不是“contemporary Chinese art”（当代中国的艺术），因为我所描述的艺术界中产生的作品，在中国最常被归类为“当代艺术”（dangdai yishu）——字面意思即“当代艺术”，但通常指以特定媒介创作的作品：油画、摄影、录像、装置和行为艺术，被视为与西方当代艺术实践横向相连。[^zh-intro-40]


〔原书 22, 23〕

When I began my fieldwork, many Chinese friends and acquaintances outside this domain reproached me for my interest in it, telling me that it didn’t really represent China. Art world participants I talked to were equally vexed, about the absence of a Chinese audience able to appreciate and understand their work. They earnestly debated and proposed ways to build a viewing public. By 2002, when I left Beijing after two years of fieldwork, the number of popular Chinese magazines devoted to dangdai yishu and of people beginning to frequent new contemporary art spaces gave an indication of their success.[^en-intro-41] This growing audience was part of China’s burgeoning urban middle class, for whom learning to appreciate dangdai yishu signified cosmopolitan distinction. This shifting ground of in/authenticity makes contemporary art a compelling way to examine Chinese cultural politics. Artists as arbiters of world culture became public tastemakers and therefore inadvertent state actors. Some made the most of the moment, but many remained cagey and critical. They struggled over what their representational labor amounted to, and to whom it should appeal. Using Anna Tsing’s metaphor of friction as the grip of encounter that drives global connections, close attention to the friction artists experienced and the images they produced in the process reveals how they also dig vertically into layers of history: of personal experience, of their training in institutions shaped by anticolonial nationalism and socialism, and of specific visual technologies and references.[^en-intro-42] These excavations are mixed and erratic, compiling an inventory of traces.[^en-intro-43] The more they “enter the world,” the more acute their efforts at inventory become. Yin Xiuzhen’s *Portable Beijing*, for example, conjures a life of transit and airport baggage carousels but also official visualizations of the capital city and gendered histories of needlework and factory labor.

我开始田野调查时，这一领域之外的许多中国朋友和熟人责备我对它感兴趣，告诉我它并不真正代表中国。与我交谈的艺术界参与者同样苦恼：中国缺乏能够欣赏和理解他们作品的观众。他们认真讨论并提出建立观看公众的方法。到2002年，当我结束两年田野调查离开北京时，专门报道当代艺术的通俗中文杂志数量，以及开始光顾新当代艺术空间的人数，显示出他们取得了一些成功。[^zh-intro-41] 这一不断增长的观众是中国蓬勃发展的城市中产阶级的一部分；对他们来说，学会欣赏当代艺术意味着世界主义的区隔。这种真/伪边界的变动，使当代艺术成为考察中国文化政治的引人入胜的方式。艺术家作为世界文化的仲裁者，成为公共趣味制造者，因而也成了无意的国家行动者。一些人大加利用这一时刻，但许多人仍保持谨慎和批判。他们为自己再现劳动的意义以及应当吸引谁而挣扎。借用罗安清（Anna Tsing）关于摩擦的隐喻——摩擦是推动全球连接的相遇之抓握——密切关注艺术家经历的摩擦及其在此过程中生产的图像，可以揭示他们如何也纵向挖掘历史的层层沉积：个人经验的层、在反殖民民族主义和社会主义塑造的机构中受训的层，以及特定视觉技术和参照的层。[^zh-intro-42] 这些挖掘混杂而游移，汇编成一份痕迹清单。[^zh-intro-43] 他们越是“进入世界”，清点工作的努力就越敏锐。例如，尹秀珍的《便携北京》召唤出一种中转与机场行李传送带的生活，同时召唤出官方的首都视觉呈现，以及针线活和工厂劳动的性别化历史。


〔原书 23〕

My analysis of this expanded field involves theoretical and methodological eclecticism at the intersection of anthropology, art history, and gender studies. In referring to the social realm of art production as an art world, I use a term coined by art critic Arthur Danto, who writes, “To see something as art requires something the eye cannot decry—an atmosphere of artistic theory, a knowledge of the history of art: an artworld.” [^en-intro-44] Sociologist Howard Becker elaborates on the term, to denote the collective activity that produces artworks and gives them aesthetic and sometimes other forms of value.[^en-intro-45] He demystifies the romantic cult of individual creation by demonstrating the diverse and coordinated activities of multiple participants necessary for art to be made and recognized as such. I refer to “art worlds” in the plural to indicate the multiple collectivities engaged in such activities; sometimes they overlap, other times they constitute themselves through antagonistic evaluations about what does or doesn’t count as art. Pierre Bourdieu’s theory of a “field of cultural production” argues that the artistic field cannot be reduced to a circumscribed group of people. Rather, it is one among other hierarchically organized, structurally homologous fields—the economic field, the educational field, the political field, among others—that coexist in relational play within the field of power.[^en-intro-46] Alfred Gell advocates an anthropology of art in which art objects serve not only as mediators between people but as social agents in and of themselves.

我对这一扩展场域的分析，涉及人类学、艺术史和性别研究交汇处的理论与方法折衷。在把艺术生产的社会领域称为艺术界（art world）时，我使用艺术批评家阿瑟·丹托创造的术语。他写道：“把某物看作艺术，需要某种眼睛无法辨识的东西——一种艺术理论的氛围，一种艺术史的知识：一个艺术界。”[^zh-intro-44]〔编者说明：本书所引英文作 decry（贬斥），与此处讨论视觉辨识的语境不合；译文按 descry（辨识）义处理，英文底本文字保留。〕 社会学家霍华德·贝克尔进一步阐发这一术语，用以指生产艺术品并赋予其审美价值、有时也赋予其他价值的集体活动。[^zh-intro-45] 他通过展示艺术被创作和承认所必需的多个参与者多样而协调的活动，祛除了个人创作的浪漫崇拜。我用复数“艺术界”（art worlds），以表明从事此类活动的多个集体；它们有时重叠，有时通过对什么算或不算艺术的对抗性评价而自我构成。皮埃尔·布迪厄的“文化生产场域”理论主张，艺术场域不能简化为一个划定的人群。相反，它是与其他等级化组织、结构同源的场域——经济场域、教育场域、政治场域等——共同在权力场域中关系性共存的场域之一。[^zh-intro-46] 阿尔弗雷德·盖尔倡导一种艺术人类学，其中艺术品不仅是人与人之间的中介，本身也是社会行动者。


〔原书 24〕

This focus on the personhood of art objects represents a turn away from isolated studies of “ethnic art” and sociological investigations of art institutions.[^en-intro-47] To the analysis of cultural production within a larger field of power, I add global and gendered dimensions. Chinese contemporary art is not a self-contained art world, a necessarily bourgeois pursuit, or a nationally circumscribed field of cultural production, but one structured by discrepant global connections and gender and class relations. While my analysis takes into account the role of institutions in amplifying or diminishing art’s agency, it also takes seriously the agency of art objects. Their expressive enchantments are precisely what send them circulating through the world, carving shifting channels of transmission and extending object and personhood across space and time.[^en-intro-48]

这种对艺术品人格性的关注，代表着背离对“族群艺术”的孤立研究和对艺术机构的社会学调查。[^zh-intro-47] 在更大权力场域内分析文化生产时，我加上了全球和性别维度。中国当代艺术不是一个自足的艺术界、一种必然的资产阶级追求，或一个民族限定的文化生产场域，而是一个由差异化的全球连接以及性别和阶级关系所结构的场域。我的分析虽然考虑机构在放大或削弱艺术能动性方面的作用，也认真对待艺术品的能动性。正是它们的表现性魅惑使它们在世界上流通，开辟不断变化的传播渠道，并把物与人格性延展于空间与时间之中。[^zh-intro-48]


〔原书 24〕

As an ethnographer, I understand my field to be more a habitus, “a cluster of embodied dispositions and practices,” than a geographically bound site.[^en-intro-49] In Beijing I traced a network of locations that included art classrooms, artist villages, foreign-run commercial galleries, Chinese-run art centers in new real estate ventures, and vacated factories and warehouses turned into guerrilla gathering spaces or renovated Soho-style exhibit halls. This field as network also extended to a rural corner of Yunnan Province, art spaces in Shanghai and Hong Kong, and symposiums on Chinese contemporary art in San Francisco, London, and New York. I brought to this field a feminist disposition influenced by art historians who analyze the critical field of gender within cultural production. As they have demonstrated, constructions of gender difference produce artistic hierarchies that relegate women to lesser categories, limit their participation in dominant practices, and when they work through these limitations to become influential innovators, marginalize their contributions.[^en-intro-50]

作为民族志学者，我理解自己的田野与其说是一个地理限定的地点，不如说是一种惯习（habitus）——“一组具身的性情与实践”。[^zh-intro-49] 在北京，我追踪一个地点网络，包括艺术教室、艺术家村、外国人经营的商业画廊、设在新房地产开发项目中的中国人经营的艺术中心，以及变成游击聚会空间或被改造成Soho式展厅的废弃工厂和仓库。作为网络的田野还延伸至云南省一个乡村角落、上海和香港的艺术空间，以及旧金山、伦敦和纽约关于中国当代艺术的研讨会。我把一种女性主义倾向带入这个田野，它受那些分析文化生产中性别批判场域的艺术史家影响。正如她们所证明的，性别差异的建构生产出艺术等级制，把女性归入较低范畴，限制她们参与主导实践；而当她们突破这些限制成为有影响力的创新者时，又将其贡献边缘化。[^zh-intro-50]


〔原书 24〕

Feminism in the Expanded Field

扩展场域中的女性主义


〔原书 24, 25〕

Feminist analysis of the field of cultural production—as a zone of encounter between different valuations of culture—involves more than just paying attention to women. I read contemporary art world activity through the historical Chinese feminist analytic of *nannü* (male/female), theorized by He-Yin Zhen in her 1907 essay “On the Question of Women’s Liberation.”[^en-intro-51] For He-Yin, nannü signifies not simply gender difference but the ongoing production of social abstractions and markings that create hierarchy, inequality, and injustice. The conceptual mechanism of *nannü youbie* (male/female differentiation) actively produces distinction as a form of power and domination, and therefore can also assume an adjectival form, as in He-Yin’s term *nannü jie* (nannü class).[^en-intro-52] Seen through this lens, the work of art becomes implicated in the production of such abstractions, whether of East and West, man and woman, or rural and urban. It reiterates symbolic orders, sometimes with a radical difference, always within a relationship of past to present. The iconic female revolutionary, red, bright, and shining in her militant rebellion and quest for modernity, haunts the redomesticated, depoliticized category of nüxing yishu; just as the iconic peasant hero, liberated by Mao’s call for the countryside to surround and capture the cities, haunts Beijing as cultural capital where rural migrants provide the rationalized, flexibilized labor to build its new monuments of global achievement. While Beijing is ostensibly the national center, I analyze it as an always-already uneven and gendered timespace that depends on the countryside, ideologically and economically. I trace how artists traverse this timespace of rural-urban relationality: through their references to the socialist tradition of “representing the people”; creation of artist villages at city’s edge; down-to-the-countryside pedagogical field trips; restaging of the Long March as art event; and employment and representation of rural migrants in experimental art practice.

对文化生产场域的女性主义分析——把它视为不同文化估值之间的相遇地带——不只是关注女性。我通过何殷震（He-Yin Zhen）在1907年《女子解放问题》一文中理论化的中国女性主义历史分析范畴“男女”（nannü）来阅读当代艺术界活动。[^zh-intro-51] 对何殷震而言，“男女”不仅意味着性别差异，还意味着不断生产社会抽象和标记，从而创造等级、不平等和不公。“男女有别”（nannü youbie）的概念机制主动生产差异，作为一种权力和支配形式，因此它也可以采用形容词形式，如何殷震的“男女阶级”（nannü jie）一词。[^zh-intro-52] 通过这一透镜，艺术作品便卷入了这类抽象的生产——无论是东方与西方、男人与女人，还是乡村与城市。它重申象征秩序，有时带着根本性差异，但始终处于过去与现在的关系之中。那个标志性的女性革命者——红色、明亮、闪耀，在战斗性的反叛与对现代性的追求中——萦绕在重新居家化、去政治化的“女性艺术”范畴之上；正如那位标志性的农民英雄——被毛泽东“农村包围城市并夺取城市”的号召所解放——萦绕在作为文化首都的北京之上：农村移民在那里提供理性化、灵活化的劳动，建造全球成就的新纪念碑。北京表面上是国家中心，我却把它分析为一个总是已经不均匀、被性别化的时空，它在意识形态上和经济上都依赖乡村。我追踪艺术家如何穿行于这种城乡关系性时空：通过援引“再现人民”的社会主义传统；在城市边缘创建艺术家村；下乡教学考察；把长征重演为艺术事件；以及在实验艺术实践中雇用和再现农村移民。


〔原书 25〕

Throughout *Experimental Beijing*, a feminist lens highlights the contradictions of an emerging art world, the dialectical tension between monumental and ephemeral visions of life during the heady new millennium conflation of Beijing, China, and the world. These contradictions include artists who desire and resist institutional recognition by both foreign art professionals and Chinese state entities; artists who utilize experimental art forms to document social upheaval and inequality while also being enlisted to repress reform-era injustices by creating art-enhanced spaces for pleasure and status; the simultaneous valorization of the artist as heroic, suffering cultural critic and as cosmopolitan entrepreneur; and the underrepresentation of women as artists in the face of female overrepresentation in Chinese modern and contemporary figurative expression. While the latter is most obviously related to gender, attention to how women have been symbolically positioned *and* professionally marginalized throws these contradictions into sharp relief. Dominant narratives have smoothed over these contradictions. A focus on gender thus produces a nonnormative history of Chinese contemporary art and cultivates a differential consciousness about the shifting role of art—as ideological, institutional, and imaginative—within various configurations of power.

在《实验北京》全书中，女性主义透镜突显一个新兴艺术界的矛盾，以及在新千年令人兴奋的北京、中国与世界融合中，纪念碑式与转瞬即逝的生活想象之间的辩证张力。这些矛盾包括：艺术家既渴望又抵抗外国艺术专业人士和中国国家实体的体制承认；艺术家利用实验艺术形式记录社会动荡与不平等，同时又被征召去通过创造艺术化的愉悦与地位空间来遮蔽改革时代的不公；艺术家同时被尊崇为英雄式、受难的文化批评家以及企业家式世界主义者；女性作为艺术家的代表性不足，却在中国现代和当代具象表现中女性形象过剩。虽然后者最明显地与性别相关，但关注女性在象征上如何被安置、在职业上如何被边缘化，会使这些矛盾更鲜明。主导叙事已抹平了这些矛盾。因此，聚焦性别可以生产一部非规范的中国当代艺术史，并培养一种关于艺术在不断变化的权力配置中（作为意识形态的、制度的和想象性的）角色的差异意识。


〔原书 26〕

As part of my habitus in the field, I conducted interviews with artists, art students and teachers, curators, and gallerists. I observed and drew and painted alongside students in art classrooms ranging from university-level academies to the state-run Children’s Center. I traveled from the massive new studios built by artists who had “made it” to the dusty, cramped apartments of those struggling to get by, from white-cube galleries in central Beijing or on the Bund in Shanghai to the urban enclaves of rural migrants working as artists’ assistants. As these interlocutors pulled me further into their worlds and visions of the world, I ended up interpreting for curators from the United States as they toured artists’ studios, translating and writing catalogue texts, and filming a video documentary of a feminist art happening. I returned during the summers of 2004 and 2006 as the curator of a feminist art exhibit that opened in Shanghai before traveling to Beijing and eventually Hong Kong; and again during the summer of 2007 for follow-up research.[^en-intro-53] These activities constituted my participation observation and served as collaborative interventions into art world status quos.

作为我在田野中的惯习的一部分，我访谈了艺术家、艺术学生和教师、策展人及画廊经营者。我在从大学层级的美术学院到国营儿童中心的艺术教室里，与学生一起观察、素描和绘画。我从“成功”艺术家建造的巨大新画室，走到艰难谋生者尘土飞扬的逼仄公寓；从北京市中心或上海外滩的白盒子画廊，走到农村移民作为艺术家助手工作的城市飞地。随着这些对话者把我进一步拉入他们的世界和世界观，我最终为来访的美国策展人担任翻译，陪他们参观艺术家画室，翻译并撰写图录文章，还拍摄了一部关于女性主义艺术事件的录像纪录片。2004年和2006年夏天，我又作为女性主义艺术展策展人回到中国，展览先在上海开幕，随后巡展至北京，最终到香港；2007年夏天，我再次回去做后续研究。[^zh-intro-53] 这些活动构成了我的参与观察，也成为对艺术界现状的协作干预。


〔原书 26〕

This ethnography gradually moves toward a story of feminist encounter between artist and ethnographer. The first two parts of the book provide context. Part I: Art Worldings presents millennial Beijing poised to “enter the world” as a site of culture industry formation, in which art overcomes and activates a historical material dialectic with past visions of the world. It follows how various social actors rework meanings of *xianfeng*/avant-garde in assertions of Beijing as China’s cultural capital, and how in the process they build new cultural institutions. Part II: Zones of Encounter presents two encounters between international curators and artists and Chinese counterparts: one in which the politics of cultural translation led to the exclusion of female artists from potential international circulation and another that became a protracted struggle over contending versions of feminism: international, national, and generational. This middle section of the book nests the story of feminist art encounters within the story of the global-local and East-West encounters that shape Chinese contemporary art. Parts I and II generate the analytic movement toward what I consider the book’s heart and soul. The three chapters of part III: Feminist Sight Lines each focus on an individual artist with whom I had an extended relationship.

这部民族志逐渐走向艺术家与民族志学者之间女性主义相遇的故事。前两部分提供语境。第一部分“艺术世界营造”呈现千禧年北京作为文化产业形成之地，准备“进入世界”，艺术在其中克服并激活与过去世界图景的历史唯物辩证法。它追踪各种社会行动者如何在把北京确立为中国文化首都的主张中重新加工先锋/前卫（xianfeng/avant-garde）的含义，以及他们在此过程中如何建立新的文化机构。第二部分“相遇地带”呈现国际策展人与艺术家和中国同行之间的两次相遇：一次是文化翻译政治导致女性艺术家被排除在潜在国际流通之外，另一次演变为围绕国际、国家和代际等相互竞争的女性主义版本的长期斗争。这一中间部分把女性主义艺术相遇的故事嵌套进塑造中国当代艺术的全球—地方、东西方相遇的故事之中。第一、二部分共同推动分析走向我眼中本书的心脏与灵魂。第三部分“女性主义视线”的三章分别聚焦一位与我有着长期交往的艺术家。


〔原书 26, 27〕

In the course of my fieldwork, I came to know female artists like Yin Xiuzhen who have achieved international recognition and circulation, but in Feminist Sight Lines I highlight the lives and works of three artists—Li Tianpian, He Chengyao, and Lei Yan—whose careers have followed less visible trajectories. I interpret their work as feminist because of a critical historiographical consciousness cultivated by being on the periphery. My encounters with these artists, their stories, and their artworks shifted my understanding of feminist art. They make visible transnational and trans-historical connections. These connections disrupt the frameworks that prevail in art criticism and museum curation: of Chinese contemporary art as brand new and nation-bound and of global feminist art as born in the West before spreading to the rest. They work to unhinge woman from the literal and figurative work she has performed for the nation in modern and contemporary art. Feminist art thus emerges as an epistemological field of practice rather than an object, event, or project, in which thinking relationally, in terms of social hierarchies, aesthetic form, and ideology, is foundational.[^en-intro-54] Feminist art, rather than originating in a particular time or place, has the potential to *world* in another way, to make visible other worlds-in-becoming. It creates new sight lines of knowledge, recognition, affiliation, and alliance in which art takes on an ethical dimension, of reordering the pain and pleasure of being in the world, of memorializing, of taking care.

在田野调查过程中，我认识了像尹秀珍这样获得国际认可与流通的女性艺术家，但在“女性主义视线”中，我着重书写三位职业生涯轨迹不那么显眼的艺术家——李天翩、何成瑶和雷燕。我把她们的作品解释为女性主义作品，是因为她们处于边缘所培养出的批判性历史编纂意识。与这些艺术家的相遇、她们的故事及作品，改变了我对女性主义艺术的理解。她们使跨国和跨历史的连接变得可见。这些连接扰乱了艺术批评和博物馆策展中盛行的框架：中国当代艺术是全新的且受民族束缚，全球女性主义艺术诞生于西方再传播到其他地区。她们努力把女性从她在现代和当代艺术中为国家所承担的实际的和象征性的工作中松脱出来。女性主义艺术由此浮现为一个认识论上的实践场域，而非一个对象、事件或项目；在其中，关系性思考——就社会等级、审美形式和意识形态而言——是基础性的。[^zh-intro-54] 女性主义艺术并非起源于某一特定时间或地点，而是具有以另一种方式营造世界的潜能，使其他正在生成的世界变得可见。它创造知识、承认、归属和联盟的新视线，艺术在其中承担伦理维度：重新安排在世间的痛苦与愉悦、纪念与照料。


〔原书 27〕

Using Chela Sandoval’s concept of differential oppositional consciousness, I argue that these artists’ peripheral positions shaped the development of a critical art practice. They not only deconstruct the ideological power of past forms of image making but also meta-ideologize, or create “new, ‘higher’ levels of signification built onto the older, dominant forms of ideology in a radical process.”[^en-intro-55] They take, for instance, Maoist representations of the woman soldier, so prevalent in literature, art, and film, and recast her in ways that question the instrumental use of her image by the state and redirect her critical potential toward different aims. Meta-ideologizing is an emancipatory technology of oppositional power that “moves in, through, and then outside of dominant ideology.”[^en-intro-56] As art practice, it reveals the long-durée global art world encounters that have shaped different worldings, or visions of the world, and the dependence of these worldings on particular understandings of gender.

借助切拉·桑多瓦尔“差异对立意识”的概念，我认为这些艺术家的边缘位置塑造了一种批判性艺术实践的发展。她们不仅解构过去图像制作形式的意识形态权力，还进行元意识形态化，即创造“新的、‘更高’的意指层次，以激进的过程加建于旧的、主导性的意识形态形式之上。”[^zh-intro-55] 例如，她们采用文学、艺术和电影中如此普遍的毛泽东主义女兵形象，并重新铸造她，以质疑国家对她形象的利用，并把她的批判潜能转向不同目标。元意识形态化是一种解放性的对立权力技术，它“进入、穿过，然后走出主导意识形态。”[^zh-intro-56] 作为艺术实践，它揭示塑造不同世界营造（或世界图景）的长期全球艺术界相遇，以及这些世界营造对特定性别理解的依赖。


〔原书 27, 28〕

Put another way, these women are “caught up” in a different way from male peers who moved from underground, “avant-garde” activity to positions of national and international influence. They are caught by a set of interlocking double binds, generated through cultural encounter over time, regarding female talent and representation. For example, traditional women of talent (*cainü*), cast as poetic and prone to flights of fancy, were seen as lacking the rationality to become disciplined national subjects, the “good wife and wise mother” or “mother of citizens” articulated by early twentieth-century reformers, whereas traditional virtuous women were seen as lacking the cultural literacy and education to likewise serve the new nation.[^en-intro-57] By the end of the twentieth century, the catch had become: women who “hold up half the sky” lack individual consciousness and innovation as artists, whereas women who identify with nüxing yishu, constrained by subjective interiority, lack public political consciousness. The double bind, conceived as a communication dilemma that results from two conflicting messages, sets a trap that ends in failure no matter what message one follows.[^en-intro-58] The resulting confusion sustained through habitual experience with this splintering form of negative injunction serves as a form of control without overt coercion.[^en-intro-59] Art can be a way of meditating on and moving beyond the dilemma, a method for confronting this form of control. The artists I focus on in part III create works that activate image worlds; their excavation and reworking of past images and ways of image making are multidirectional and meta-ideological. They cite across space and time, not as attribution or homage, but to shift our understanding of the world-making power of images past and future. The depth of their conceptual practice, while not usually recognized for this achievement, opens up interpretation of work by their male counterparts in terms other than those of a universalizing story of artistic expression.

换言之，这些女性被“困住”的方式，不同于那些从地下“前卫”活动走向国家和国际影响力位置的男性同行。她们被一组相互锁扣的双重束缚所困，这些束缚在长期文化相遇中围绕女性才能和再现而生成。例如，传统才女（cainü）被塑造成诗意、耽于幻想的形象，被视为缺乏成为有纪律的国家主体所需的理性——这些主体包括20世纪初改革者所阐述的“贤妻良母”或“国民之母”——而传统贤德女性则被视为缺乏文化素养和教育，无法同样服务于新国家。[^zh-intro-57] 到20世纪末，困境变成：“顶起半边天”的女性缺乏作为艺术家的个体意识和创新；而认同“女性艺术”的女性受限于主观内在性，缺乏公共政治意识。双重束缚被设想为由两条冲突信息造成的沟通困境，无论遵循哪条信息，最终都落入失败的陷阱。[^zh-intro-58] 由此产生的困惑通过这种分裂式负面禁令的习惯性经验得以维持，成为一种没有公开强制的控制形式。[^zh-intro-59] 艺术可以成为沉思并超越这一困境的方式，一种直面这种控制的方法。我在第三部分聚焦的艺术家创作激活图像世界的作品；她们对过去图像和图像制作方式的挖掘与再加工是多向的、元意识形态的。她们跨越空间和时间引用，不是为了标明来源或致敬，而是为了改变我们对过去和未来图像之世界营造力量的理解。她们概念实践的深度——尽管通常未因这一成就而被承认——打开了以不同于普遍化艺术表达叙事的方式来解释其男性同行作品的可能。


〔原书 28〕

Image Worlds and Worldings

图像世界与世界营造


〔原书 28, 29〕

The concept of the “image world,” central to my critical praxis, emerged from my encounters with these artists and their work. Image worlds highlight the relationships among images, in which the form and meaning of one is shaped by others, within a complex network invoked in the process of looking and making. Any single historicist line of influence and attribution thus ruptures into a web of meaning in which past works are not hermetically sealed but open to resignification from multiple directions. Image worlds also show how particular understandings of the world are made visible by the image and how images are works that draw on and remake a world of other images.[^en-intro-60] Image worlds take, in the words of Rasheed Araeen, “art as method.” It is art, as he writes, “by which modernity as an advancing force is defined by its exclusive European subjectivity; only art can confront neo-imperialism and offer a model of decolonialism.”[^en-intro-61] To think in terms of image worlds is to visualize the multidirectional tensions between colonial and decolonial forces (East-West and male-female) that shape the work of art enmeshed in a global network of power relations.

“图像世界”概念是我的批判实践的核心，它源于我与这些艺术家及其作品的相遇。图像世界突显图像之间的关系：在观看和创作过程中唤起的复杂网络里，一幅图像的形式与意义由其他图像塑造。因此，任何单一历史主义的影响与归属线索都会断裂成意义之网，过去作品在其中并非密闭，而是向着来自多个方向的再意义化敞开。图像世界也显示，对世界的特定理解如何通过图像变得可见，以及图像如何是汲取并重造其他图像世界的作品。[^zh-intro-60] 用拉希德·阿瑞恩的话说，图像世界“把艺术作为方法”。他写道，正是通过艺术，“现代性作为一种推进力量，由其排他性的欧洲主体性所定义；只有艺术能够直面新帝国主义，并提供去殖民化的范式。”[^zh-intro-61] 以图像世界来思考，就是把塑造艺术作品的殖民与去殖民力量（东西方、男性—女性）之间的多向张力可视化——这些艺术作品交织于全球权力关系网络之中。


〔原书 29〕

The work of art, in “setting up a world,” emerges in my fieldwork zone of encounter from tensions between different stagings of the world, or “worldings.”[^en-intro-62] Worldings have the aura of totality, yet the continual supplanting of one by another or the coexistence of radically different visions shatters any such sureness. A geneology of worlding as theoretical concept, followed by a tracing of several worldings that continually resurface in the palimpsest of Chinese contemporary art, sets the stage for my ethnographic argument that begins with part I: Art Worldings. These selected worldings gesture toward the expansive archive of images, and the webs of meaning in which they are implicated, that artists pull from as they develop their repertoire and potential to differentially remake the world.[^en-intro-63] The ways these worldings overlap with or haunt one another are foundational to the contradictions arising in the field of Chinese contemporary art.

艺术作品在“建立一个世界”时，在我的田野相遇地带中从世界不同上演方式或“世界营造”（worldings）之间的张力中浮现。[^zh-intro-62] 世界营造具有总体性的光环，然而一个不断取代另一个，或截然不同的世界图景共存，粉碎了任何这种确定性。追溯世界营造这一理论概念的家谱，随后追踪在中国当代艺术的重写本中不断重新浮现的几种世界营造，将为第一部分的民族志论证搭起舞台。这些精选的世界营造指向广阔的图像档案及其所牵连的意义之网，艺术家从中汲取素材，发展他们的作品储备与以差异方式重造世界的潜能。[^zh-intro-63] 这些世界营造彼此重叠或萦绕的方式，是中国当代艺术场域中矛盾的根基。


〔原书 29〕

Hong Hao’s *Selected Scriptures*, a series of silk-screen prints that resemble classical maps of exploration and discovery, presents interleaved, conflicting worldings. Each print’s map appears to be contained within a traditionally bound book, opened to a particular page. This fictitious atlas binds together, however, not the world’s nations, but differently imagined organizations of world space. Its maps scramble the world in any number of ways: by redrawing borders, shuffling place names, or altering the shape of geographic landmasses. In some, legends are labeled “Corrections.” Dotted-line routes of ancient seafaring vessels and modern fighter jets connote crisscrossing trade and military connections. For *New World Order I*, Hong identified nations with the names of large corporations. *New Topography* assigns vast tracts of land to First World countries and crowds the Third World within severely delimited boundaries. In *New Political World* (figure Intro.03), First and Third Worlds are reversed. The shape of the United States is shaded yellow and labeled the People’s Republic of China. A pink landmass sprouting the head, legs, and tail of a fox, labeled Mozambique, replaces Europe. The reiteration of “new” suggests a continual displacement of one world by another, although they all appear within the covers of a single book.

洪浩的《选集》系列丝网版画模仿古典探险与发现地图，呈现交错、冲突的世界营造。每幅版画中的地图似乎都被装在一本传统线装书里，翻到某一页。然而，这本虚构的地图集绑在一起的不是世界上各个国家，而是对世界空间的不同想象组织。它的地图以各种方式打乱世界：重画边界、打乱地名，或改变地理陆块的形状。有些地图的图例标着“更正”。古代航海帆船和现代战斗机的虚线航线，暗示着纵横交错的贸易与军事连接。在《新世界秩序I》中，洪浩用大公司的名字标识国家。《新地形学》把广阔土地分给第一世界国家，把第三世界挤进严格限定的边界。在《新政治世界》（导论图03）中，第一世界和第三世界颠倒过来。美国的形状被涂成黄色，标为中华人民共和国。一块粉色陆块长出狐狸的头、腿和尾巴，标为莫桑比克，取代了欧洲。“新”一词的反复出现暗示一个世界不断取代另一个世界，尽管它们都容纳在同一本书的封面与封底之间。


〔原书 30〕

![导论图03　洪浩，《选集——新政治世界》，1995年。纸上丝网版画，55厘米×76厘米。艺术家惠允。](web/assets/intro-b052.jpg)

INTRO.03 Hong Hao, *Selected Scriptures–New Political World*, 1995. Silkscreen on paper, 55 cm × 76 cm. Courtesy of the artist.

导论图03　洪浩，《选集——新政治世界》，1995年。纸上丝网版画，55厘米×76厘米。艺术家惠允。


〔原书 29, 30〕

Gayatri Spivak invokes the term *worlding* in her critique of imperialism and the role of literature as a crucial form of cultural representation in underwriting the imperialist project. She characterizes her notion of the “worlding of a world” as a vulgarization of Martin Heidegger’s philosophical idea of a world in relation to the earth, which shelters in its uninscribed spontaneity.[^en-intro-64] The world, as I understand Heidegger’s formulation, is the human abstraction of what happens on earth, an ideological construct that makes material social relations seem natural, of the earth. Through her postcolonial reading of Heidegger, Spivak describes a worlding as the implicit, naturalized script that suffuses the literature of European colonizing cultures in the creation of something that has come to be called “the Third World,” a narrative that organizes the world according to chronological, developmental stages. In this narrative, the colonized are robbed of the power to world, to represent their relationship to the earth. Spivak continues, “To consider the Third World as distant cultures, exploited but with rich intact literary heritages waiting to be recovered, interpreted, and curricularized in English translation fosters the emergence of ‘the Third World’ as a signifier that allows us to forget that ‘worlding,’ even as it expands the empire of the literary discipline.”[^en-intro-65] The colonized are hence consigned to the earth that shelters the colonizer worlding. The work of deconstruction becomes necessary to unforget or reveal this powerful process of concealment, in which the world of the historical people of the Third World, and especially the native woman, has been repressed.

佳亚特里·斯皮瓦克在批判帝国主义以及文学作为文化再现关键形式在支撑帝国主义工程中的作用时，援引了“世界营造”一词。她将自己“一个世界的世界营造”的观念，描述为对马丁·海德格尔关于世界与大地之关系的哲学观念的粗俗化——大地庇护于其未被书写的自发状态中。[^zh-intro-64] 据我对海德格尔表述的理解，世界是对大地上所发生之事的人类抽象，是一种意识形态建构，使物质社会关系显得自然，仿佛属于大地。通过她对海德格尔的后殖民阅读，斯皮瓦克把世界营造描述为一种隐含的、自然化的脚本，渗透在欧洲殖民文化文学之中，创造了后来被称为“第三世界”的东西——一种按年代和发展阶段组织世界的叙事。在这种叙事中，被殖民者被剥夺了营造世界的能力，即再现他们与大地关系的能力。斯皮瓦克继续说：“把第三世界视为遥远的文化，受剥削却拥有丰富完整的文学遗产，等待在英译中被恢复、解释和课程化，会促成‘第三世界’作为一个能指的出现，使我们忘记‘世界营造’，即使它扩展了文学学科的帝国。”[^zh-intro-65] 被殖民者因此被放逐到庇护殖民者世界营造的大地之上。解构工作因此成为必要，以“不忘却”或揭示这一强大的遮蔽过程——第三世界处于具体历史中的人民、尤其是本土女性的世界在其中被压抑。


〔原书 30, 31〕

This worlding persists in some of the ways Chinese art has been managed in Western art spaces, but is also disrupted by other worldings—those advanced by China’s successive modernity projects, each of which required a rupture from the immediate past. Rebecca Karl’s work, for example, on early Chinese nationalists demonstrates how they confronted Euro-American and Japanese imperialisms that had inscribed China as part of the Third World. They resisted through alternative ways of “staging the world”—tracing connections with political movements such as the Philippine revolution against the United States—in order to nurture an anticolonial consciousness.[^en-intro-66]

这种世界营造在西方艺术空间管理中国艺术的某些方式中延续，但也被其他世界营造所扰乱——那些由中国相继的现代性工程所推进的世界营造，每一个都要求与紧接其前的过去断裂。例如，丽贝卡·卡尔关于中国早期民族主义者的研究显示，他们如何面对把中国铭刻为第三世界一部分的欧美与日本帝国主义。他们通过另类的“上演世界”方式抵抗——追溯与菲律宾反美革命等政治运动的联系——以培育反殖民意识。[^zh-intro-66]


〔原书 31〕

Gendered Worldings

性别化的世界营造


〔原书 31〕

Extending the idea developed by these thinkers, I conclude this chapter with three worldings—semicolonial, anticolonial, and late socialist. Each is made visible through images and structured by gender. Taken together they provide a framework for placing Chinese contemporary art in the expanded field. The first of these, a semicolonial worlding, is characterized by a term used to signify that China was not colonized outright by a single power, but subject to multiple Euro-American and Japanese imperialisms.[^en-intro-67] Chinese contemporary artists’ uneasy relationship with the West emerges from a frequently invoked national memory of colonial humiliation.[^en-intro-68] As brass plaques at tourist sites in Beijing remind visitors, Western powers at the end of the nineteenth century and early twentieth century looted China’s imperial treasures.

延伸这些思想家的观念，我以三种世界营造结束本章——半殖民的、反殖民的和晚期社会主义的。每一种都通过图像变得可见，并由性别结构。合在一起，它们为把中国当代艺术置于扩展场域中提供了框架。第一种是半殖民地世界营造，其特征可用一个术语表示：中国并未被单一列强彻底殖民，而是受制于多个欧美及日本的帝国主义。[^zh-intro-67] 中国当代艺术家与西方的不安关系，源于常被援引的民族殖民屈辱记忆。[^zh-intro-68] 正如北京景点里的铜牌提醒游客，西方列强在19世纪末20世纪初掠夺了中国的皇家珍宝。


〔原书 31〕

In “Looting Beijing: 1860, 1900,” James Hevia argues that the 1860 moment of Opium War plunder created new markets and knowledge of Chinese objets d’art, firmly situating things Chinese “within a global discourse on the curiosities of non-European peoples, and as commodities, the common sense of capitalist market exchange.”[^en-intro-69] In the forty-year interim between 1860 and subsequent looting in 1900 when an eight-nation foreign alliance crushed the peasant uprising of the Boxer Rebellion, systematized practices of discernment grew in sophistication as auctioned objects passed into European and American markets.[^en-intro-70] Foreign art dealers opened shop in Beijing, and Western connoisseurs published tracts on Chinese art detailing classification schemes that guided the cataloging of items in institutions like London’s Victoria and Albert Museum and New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art.[^en-intro-71] These developments occurred simultaneously with the birth of modern exhibition spaces funded by the nation-state: the public museum and international exposition.

在《掠夺北京：1860，1900》一文中，何伟亚（James Hevia）认为，1860年鸦片战争掠夺时刻创造了新的中国艺术品市场和知识，把中国物品牢牢置于“关于非欧洲民族珍奇之物的全球话语中，并作为商品，置于资本主义市场交换的常识中。”[^zh-intro-69] 在1860年至1900年八国联军镇压义和团农民起义的后续掠夺之间的四十年里，随着拍卖物品进入欧美市场，系统化的鉴赏实践日益精致。[^zh-intro-70] 外国艺术商在北京开店，西方鉴赏家出版关于中国艺术的小册子，详述分类体系，指导伦敦维多利亚与艾尔伯特博物馆和纽约大都会艺术博物馆等机构的藏品编目。[^zh-intro-71] 这些发展同时发生于由民族国家资助的现代展览空间的诞生：公共博物馆和国际博览会。


〔原书 32〕

In an essay on British institutional framings of Chinese art, Craig Clunas admits to a moment of boyhood fetishism. His father took him, at the age of fourteen, to visit the Victoria and Albert Museum. Enthralled in the “Far Eastern Room” by a carved lacquer throne of the Chinese Emperor Qianlong (figure Intro.04), he waited for the guard to look away, then knelt before it. Decades later, after he has become curator of the same China collection, he unpacks the historical processes by which British public museums transferred Chinese objects from the domain of ethnography to that of “Chinese art,” in a containment of Chinese culture as something with “a glorious past, a decayed and exhausted present and no future,” a stage inviting theatricality.[^en-intro-72]

在一篇关于英国机构如何框定中国艺术的文章中，柯律格（Craig Clunas）承认自己少年时代有一段恋物癖时刻。他十四岁时，父亲带他参观维多利亚与艾尔伯特博物馆。他在“远东厅”被中国乾隆皇帝的雕漆宝座（导论图04）迷住，等警卫不注意时，在宝座前跪了下来。几十年后，他成为同一中国收藏的策展人，剖析英国公共博物馆把中国物品从民族志领域转移到“中国艺术”领域的历史过程：把中国文化收容为某种“有着辉煌过去、衰败枯竭的现在和没有未来”的东西，一个邀人上演戏剧性的舞台。[^zh-intro-72]


〔原书 32〕

Within this display of China as an exhausted “lost state,” the traditional Chinese woman came to stand as symbol of its decadent decay, and for Chinese reformers, of what they had to overcome to build a healthy, modern nation. As plundered Chinese objects entered Western collections, so did typifying postcards such as “Canton: Chinese Small Feet Beauty” (figure Intro.05) and “Chine: Chinoise à petit pied” (figure Intro.06).[^en-intro-73] These images were reprinted in a 2001 *Beijing Youth News* article. The first hand-colored studio photograph stages the woman with her silk-clad bound feet as one among several assembled Oriental objects. In the second photograph, captured in documentary black and white, the woman holds up her bare foot to the camera, exposing its bent shape to a voyeuristic, ethnographic gaze.[^en-intro-74] The newspaper article, “Deformity beneath a Glorious Costume,” introduces a book of postcards produced during the late Qing Dynasty, explaining that these foreign representations of China will give contemporary youth a sense of their civilization’s past “profound grief and bitterness.”[^en-intro-75] Vanquished China became equated with exotic images exposing how Chinese culture had deformed its women.

在这种把中国展示为一个枯竭的“失落国家”的陈列中，传统中国女性成为其腐朽衰败的象征；对中国改革者而言，也是他们为建立健康现代国家所必须克服之物的象征。随着被掠夺的中国物品进入西方收藏，典型化的明信片也进入其中，如《广州：中国小脚美人》（导论图05）和《中国：小脚中国女人》（导论图06）。[^zh-intro-73] 这些图像被重印在2001年《北京青年报》的一篇文章中。第一张手工上色的影楼照片把缠足裹着丝绸的女子摆置为一组东方物件中的一件。第二张照片以纪实黑白拍摄，女子向镜头抬起赤裸的脚，把弯曲的形状暴露给窥视性的民族志凝视。[^zh-intro-74] 报纸文章《华丽衣装下的畸形》介绍一本清末明信片集，解释说这些外国对中国的再现将让当代青年感受到其文明过去的“深切悲痛与苦涩”。[^zh-intro-75] 被征服的中国被等同于那些暴露中国文化如何戕害其女性的异域图像。


〔原书 32〕

In China’s treaty ports, where multiple foreign powers exerted economic and political control, reform-minded intellectuals sought to explain and change their world situation. As Tani Barlow details, they turned to internationally circulating evolutionary discourse informed by the male/female binary of Victorian anthropological sex theory.[^en-intro-76] They interpreted Chinese tradition as having unnaturally oppressed woman, thereby making China weak, and forged the idea of a new eroticized woman, *nüxing*, based on a theory that prioritized sexual difference and desire over Confucian protocols concerning the position of a kinswoman in the patriline. They believed that liberating women for sexual selection, to choose their own reproductive partners, would eugenically strengthen the Chinese people.

在通商口岸，多个外国列强施加经济和政治控制，改革派知识分子试图解释并改变自己的世界处境。正如白露（Tani Barlow）详细论述的，他们转向当时国际流通的进化论话语，这种话语受维多利亚人类学性别理论中男女二元论的影响。[^zh-intro-76] 他们解释中国传统的做法不自然地压迫了女性，从而使中国衰弱，并根据一种把性别差异与欲望置于儒家女性亲属父系位置礼法之上的理论，锻造了新的情欲化“女性”（nüxing）观念。他们相信，解放女性以进行性选择、选择自己的生育伴侣，将以优生方式增强中华民族。


〔原书 33〕

〔原书 33〕

〔原书 33〕

〔原书 34〕

Chinese progressive feminism and nüxing, a neologism made up of the ideographs for “female” and “sex,” emerged from the drive to form a modern nation that could stand up to colonialism. (A forward-looking term at the time of its coining, nüxing has since undergone a complex history of repeated disavowal and reclamation.) This Chinese conjunction of nation building and female liberation produced women as signifiers of modernity. This semicolonial worlding led Chinese nationalists at the turn of the century and later Marxist critics in the 1920s and 1930s to reimagine the globe through an anticolonial worlding. In contradistinction to the racialized hierarchy of more or less civilized or advanced cultures promoted by imperialist visions of the world, they drew a distinction between those who used cultural difference in order to legitimate violent colonial oppression and those who through historical consciousness struggled for revolutionary self-actualization. Chinese socialist art thus images an international axis in which the people of Asia, Africa, and Latin America stand in solidarity with Mao at the center. As Julia Andrews points out, the painting *Mao Zedong with the People of Asia, Africa, and Latin America* (figure Intro.07) by Jin Shangyi and Wu Biduan contains yet another historical layer of political realignment.[^en-intro-77] Both painters were influenced by Soviet socialist realism; Jin was a graduate of an important oil painting class taught in China by Soviet painter Konstantin Maksimov, and Wu had studied in Leningrad. They most likely drew on A. A. Myl’nikov’s *Awakening*, exhibited in China in 1957, which depicts the people of Africa, the Middle East, and the Americas marching together with raised fists. As the rift between China and the Soviet Union widened in the late 1950s, leading to an official split in 1960, Jin and Wu represented China at the global center of orthodox Communism.

中国进步女性主义与“女性”（nüxing）——一个由“女”与“性”两个汉字构成的新词——从建立一个能够抵抗殖民主义的现代民族国家的驱力中产生。（“女性”在创造之时是一个前瞻性的术语，此后经历了反复被否弃与收回的复杂历史。）这种国家建设与女性解放的中国式结合，把女性生产为现代性的能指。这种半殖民地世界营造，引导世纪之交的中国民族主义者和后来的20世纪20、30年代马克思主义批评家，通过一种反殖民世界营造重新想象全球。与帝国主义世界图景所推动的、按文明程度或先进程度划分的种族化等级不同，他们区分了两种人：一种利用文化差异为暴力殖民压迫辩护，另一种通过历史意识为革命的自我实现而斗争。中国社会主义艺术因此描绘了一条国际轴线：亚洲、非洲和拉丁美洲的人民与毛泽东团结在中心。正如安雅兰（Julia Andrews）指出，靳尚谊与吴必端合作的《毛泽东与亚非拉人民》（导论图07）还包含另一层历史性的政治重组。[^zh-intro-77] 两位画家都受苏联社会主义现实主义影响；靳尚谊毕业于苏联画家康斯坦丁·马克西莫夫在中国开办的重要油画班，吴必端则曾在列宁格勒学习。他们很可能借鉴了A. A. 米利尼科夫的《觉醒》——1957年曾在中国展出，描绘非洲、中东和美洲人民举拳同行。随着20世纪50年代末中苏裂痕扩大，并于1960年正式分裂，靳尚谊和吴必端把中国置于正统共产主义的全球中心。


〔原书 34, 35〕

This anticolonial worlding depended on a new conception of woman, as the nüxing of treaty-port reform discourse came to represent woman as bourgeois, desiring, and self-obsessed. Chinese Communist thinkers theorized a national revolutionary female subject; and *funü*—signifiying a massified subject to be mobilized for state political movements including class revolution—superseded the eroticized nüxing.[^en-intro-78] While class consciousness now eclipsed that of gender, the question of woman remained front and center in official ideology with the goal of proving a Marxist tenet fundamental to Maoist gender discourse, that “the degree of woman’s emancipation is the natural measure of the general emancipation.”[^en-intro-79] Socialist realism depicted women “holding up half the sky,” in paintings such as Pan Jiajun’s 1972 *I Am a “Seagull*”(figure Intro.08). Iron girls repaired high-voltage wires, welded girders, operated heavy machinery, shouldered guns, and harvested crops, dressed in the same clothes as men and performing the same tasks. They appeared again and again, “red, bright, and shining” (*hong guang liang*) with their gazes trained upward and outward, as official art pedagogy instructed. They became a fixture of visual culture, even as the number of prominent female artists during the height of socialism paled in comparison with their pictorial multiplicity and arguably even shrank from their ranks in early twentieth-century art circles when bourgeois women’s art education flourished in cities like Shanghai.[^en-intro-80]

这种反殖民世界营造依赖一种新的女性观念：随着通商口岸改革话语中的“女性”把女人再现为资产阶级的、充满欲望的、自我迷恋的，中国共产党思想家理论化了一个民族革命女性主体；“妇女”（funü）——意味着一个有待为包括阶级革命在内的国家政治运动而动员的集体化主体——取代了被情欲化的“女性”。[^zh-intro-78] 虽然阶级意识此时压倒了性别意识，女性问题仍在官方意识形态中居于中心和前沿，目标是证明一条对毛泽东主义性别话语至关重要的马克思主义原则：“妇女解放的程度是普遍解放的天然尺度。”[^zh-intro-79] 社会主义现实主义描绘“顶起半边天”的女性，如潘嘉俊1972年的《我是“海鸥”》（导论图08）。铁姑娘们维修高压电线，焊接钢梁，操作重型机械，扛枪，收割庄稼，与男人穿同样的衣服，做同样的工作。她们一次又一次出现，“红、光、亮”（hong guang liang），目光按官方艺术教育的要求向上向外注视。她们成为视觉文化的固定元素，尽管在社会主义鼎盛时期，知名女性艺术家的数量与她们在图像中的多重性相比相形见绌，甚至可以说少于20世纪初上海等城市资产阶级女性艺术教育繁荣时期艺术圈中的女性人数。[^zh-intro-80]


〔原书 35〕

〔原书 36〕

![导论图08　潘嘉俊，《我是“海鸥”》，1972年。油画。艺术家及广东美术馆惠允。](web/assets/intro-b067.jpg)

INTRO.08 Pan Jiajun, *I Am a “Seagull*,” 1972. Oil painting. Courtesy of the artist and the Guangdong Museum of Art.

导论图08　潘嘉俊，《我是“海鸥”》，1972年。油画。艺术家及广东美术馆惠允。


〔原书 35, 36, 37〕

Throughout the Cold War, Western museums limited their display of Chinese art to the antiquities of its lost empire, with the visual arts under Mao held at bay as political propaganda.[^en-intro-81] In the United States, abstract expressionism became the epitome of Western modern art’s will to freedom, its ideological promotion of abstraction, coded as more advanced in the language of formal innovation, over the political avant-garde.[^en-intro-82] While the artists I met during my fieldwork had trained in the visual styles and iconography of a revolutionary socialist worlding, their movement into a global art market forced them to confront late socialist “linked-up-with-the world” worldings. China’s integration with transnational capitalism reconfigured its global imaginary to one shaped not through alliance with Third World comrades but by connections with Asia and *Oumei* (Europe and America). This shift in visualizing the world comes into focus in a work like Wang Qingsong’s *Forum* (figure Intro.09). In this 2001 photograph, one in a series of staged, performative self-portraits, the artist appears as a modern-day Chinese bureaucrat sitting before a battery of microphones and photographers. The sign behind him announces, in Chinese and English, a fictitious “International Forum on Reestablishing Contemporary Civilization in China.” The logos on the sign for the event’s corporate sponsors range from Japan’s jvc to the yellow arches of McDonald’s; the microphones are marked with insignia for medial channels such as bbc, cnn, cctv, and Fox News, as well as national flags representing Canada, South Korea, and various European nations. The audience the artist addresses, with self-mocking seriousness, is clearly a capitalist West with links to the developmentalist economies of East Asia.

在整个冷战期间，西方博物馆对中国艺术的展示局限于其失落帝国的古物，毛泽东治下的视觉艺术被作为政治宣传拒之门外。[^zh-intro-81] 在美国，抽象表现主义成为西方现代艺术追求自由的意志的典范，其在意识形态上推崇抽象——在形式创新的语言中被编码为更先进——压过了政治前卫。[^zh-intro-82] 虽然我在田野调查中遇到的艺术家受训于革命社会主义世界营造的视觉风格和图像志，但他们进入全球艺术市场的过程迫使他们面对晚期社会主义“与世界接轨”的世界营造。中国与跨国资本主义的整合，把其全球想象重新配置为一种不再通过与第三世界同志结盟、而是通过同亚洲及欧美（Oumei）的连接来塑造的想象。这种世界观的变化在像王庆松的《论坛》（导论图09）这样的作品中显现。在这幅2001年的照片中——一组摆拍的表演性自画像之一——艺术家以现代中国官僚的形象出现，坐在一排麦克风和摄影师前。他身后的标牌用中英文宣布一个虚构的“重塑中国当代文明的国际论坛”。标牌上的企业赞助商标志从日本JVC到麦当劳的黄色拱门；麦克风上标有BBC、CNN、CCTV和福克斯新闻等媒体的标志，以及代表加拿大、韩国和多个欧洲国家的国旗。艺术家以自嘲的严肃态度所面对的听众，显然是与东亚发展主义经济体有联系的资本主义西方。


〔原书 37〕

Female contemporaries Cao Fei and Huang Yin examine the commercialized and gendered aspects of this new worlding by adorning the female body with the cosmopolitan fashions of Burberry’s trademark plaid and Louis Vuitton’s signature bag, markers of luxury precisely because their manufacturers claim the genuine articles are not made in China, although knock-off copies and many other Western name brands are produced by Chinese female factory labor. In Cao’s video *Rabid Dogs* (figure Intro.10), actors in Beijing opera-style makeup perform a parody of the city’s new class of office workers as groveling “rabid dogs.” Huang’s oil painting *Myth* (figure Intro.11) reproduces the sleek surfaces of commercial photography, only the model’s head turned coyly toward the viewer is that of a cartoonish smiling dog. They conflate the female body not only with the fashion markers of conspicuous consumption but with a commodity item signifying urbane wealth and leisure in China, the pet dog.

同代女性艺术家曹斐和黄引审视这一新世界营造的商业化和性别化方面：她们用博柏利（Burberry）标志性格纹和路易威登（Louis Vuitton）标志性手袋等世界主义时尚装饰女性身体——这些奢侈品标志之所以成立，恰恰因为制造商声称正品并非中国制造，尽管仿冒品和许多其他西方名牌实际上由中国女工生产。在曹斐的录像《疯狗》（导论图10）中，涂着京剧式妆容的演员戏仿这座城市的新白领阶层，把他们演成卑躬屈膝的“疯狗”。黄引的油画《神话》（导论图11）复制商业摄影的光滑表面，只是模特的头变成一只卡通式微笑的狗，腼腆地转向观众。她们把女性身体不仅与炫耀性消费的时尚标志混同，也与一种象征都市财富和闲暇的商品混同——宠物狗。


〔原书 37〕

In these images, which work through China’s bid to “link tracks with the world,” there lurks a suspicion of how Chinese accumulation of symbolic and cultural capital will translate into social capital in the eyes of the “world,” as well as of the repressions entailed in these dressed-up embodiments of “contemporary civilization.” The reverse anthropomorphism in *Rabid Dogs* and *Myth* resonates with the oft-repeated story of the colonial park in Shanghai with a sign forbidding the entrance of both Chinese and dogs. Cao’s artist statement for her video exudes resignation and indignation: “We are surely poor dogs, willing to act as animals and locked in the cage of modernization. When will we have the courage to bite our bosses ruthlessly, taking off our masks, peeling off our fur, and becoming a group of real rabid dogs?”[^en-intro-83]

在这些围绕中国“与世界接轨”的努力而运作的图像中，潜藏着一种疑虑：中国积累的象征资本和文化资本，在“世界”眼中将如何转化为社会资本；以及这些盛装打扮的“当代文明”化身所包含的压抑。《疯狗》和《神话》中的反向拟人，与一个反复讲述的故事相呼应：上海某座殖民公园的牌子禁止中国人和狗入内。曹斐关于录像的艺术家陈述流露出无奈与愤慨：“我们当然是可怜的狗，甘愿做动物，被锁在现代化的笼子里。什么时候我们才有勇气狠狠地咬老板，摘下面具，剥下皮毛，成为一群真正的疯狗？”[^zh-intro-83]


〔原书 37, 39, 40〕

The pieces by Cao and Huang also articulate with the resurgence of woman as nüxing in what Tani Barlow labels market feminism and traces through Chinese thinkers like Li Xiaojiang.[^en-intro-84] In the 1980s, Li led a critique of revolutionary modernity that sought to “recover” woman from the funü subject represented by state organizations. When Deng-era Marxist humanist philosophers critiqued the destruction of individual agency under Mao, Li identified the human subject they aimed to recuperate as male. In response, she theorized a female subject whose dehumanization had taken place most trenchantly at the level of the body and argued that Maoist culture had obliterated natural sex difference and denaturalized women’s bodies by requiring conformity to a male standard. Li posited instead an essential woman, whose creative powers lay in her physiological difference and could be realized through the pleasures of reproduction and domestic consumption.[^en-intro-85] Her position gained popular currency, especially among a growing sector of quasi-middle-class women and influenced the rise of cultural formations like nüxing yishu. This move to recuperate feminine subjectivity, however, also raised questions like those posed by the artistic representation of grinning, groveling canine women about commodification and containment.

曹斐和黄引的作品也与“女性”的复兴相呼应——白露称之为“市场女性主义”，并通过李小江等中国思想家加以追溯。[^zh-intro-84] 20世纪80年代，李小江领导了对革命现代性的批判，试图从国家组织所代表的“妇女”主体中“找回”女人。当邓时代的马克思主义人道主义哲学家批判毛泽东时代对个体能动性的摧毁时，李小江指出，他们试图恢复的人类主体是男性。作为回应，她理论化了一个女性主体，其去人性化最尖锐地发生在身体层面；她认为毛泽东主义文化消灭了自然的性别差异，通过要求女性身体服从男性标准而使其去自然化。李小江转而提出一种本质主义的女人，其创造力在于生理差异，并可通过生育和家庭消费的愉悦来实现。[^zh-intro-85] 她的立场获得了广泛欢迎，尤其是在日益壮大的准中产阶级女性中，并影响了“女性艺术”等文化形态的兴起。然而，这种恢复女性主体性的转向，也提出了像那些咧嘴、匍匐的犬女艺术形象所引发的关于商品化和收容的问题。


〔原书 38〕

〔原书 39〕

![导论图11　黄引，《仿路易威登广告系列——神话》，2004年。布面油画，192厘米×158厘米。艺术家惠允。](web/assets/intro-b074.jpg)

〔原书 40〕

In her essay “A Scene in the Fog,” feminist cultural critic Dai Jinhua describes 1990s Chinese culture as a “city of mirrors.” She writes, “Contemporary Chinese culture resembles a scene in the fog, transfixed between orientalism and occidentalism, interpellated by different, diametrically opposed power centers, existing in a proliferating, multiple, overlapping cultural space. The light optimistic boat is destined to be overloaded with the heritages of premodernity, modernity, Cold War-era and eighties culture.”[^en-intro-86] With this “light optimistic boat” metaphorically evoking a dream vision of China achieving global parity through the ferrying of its culture into the world, Dai reads from the surface the swelling currents that pull and batter the craft. *Experimental Beijing* follows the historical moment of Dai’s description, as the scene explodes with the millennial fervor of Olympic fireworks, which trail into dust and smoke in the aftermath. It examines the new cultural monuments to China’s global future that appeared on the horizon, even as other visions of being in the world glimmered at their powerful edges. It asks what can be gleaned from the ephemeral experiments that flash up from the shadows of history—those excavations of ruins always proximate to the construction site, those inventories of traces that deconstruct and remake from the rubble. As Beijing turned itself over to “enter the world,” the work of art collaborated with and subverted this new Chinese Dream. Wang Nengtao’s *Subversion–Earth* documents this worlding, as well as the uninscribed spontaneity of the earth, the possibility of subversion by those on the ground. Yin Xiuzhen’s *Portable Beijing* shuttles through the world while simultaneously giving shelter to an intimate, tactile history of other forms of social organization and connection. Chen Lingyang’s *25:00* glows with the magic hour fantasy of inhabiting the “real/male” world on one’s own terms. To place Chinese contemporary art in the expanded field, in “a proliferating, multiple, overlapping cultural space,” requires a double vision that holds monumental and ephemeral together.

在《雾中风景》一文中，女性主义文化批评家戴锦华把20世纪90年代中国文化描述为一座“镜城”。她写道：“当代中国文化像一处雾中风景，停驻在东方主义与西方主义之间，被不同的、截然相反的权力中心所质询，存在于一个不断增殖、多重、重叠的文化空间里。那只轻便乐观的小舟，注定要超载前现代、现代、冷战时代和八十年代文化的遗产。”[^zh-intro-86] 这只“轻快乐观的小舟”隐喻性地唤起一种梦想景象：中国通过把自身文化摆渡到世界而实现与世界平起平坐；戴锦华从表面读出牵拉、拍打这艘小舟的汹涌潮流。《实验北京》追随戴锦华所描述的历史时刻：场景随着奥运焰火的千禧年狂热而爆炸，焰火在余波中化为尘土与烟雾。它考察出现在地平线上的中国全球未来的新文化纪念碑，即使其他在世方式在这些强力的边缘闪烁微光。它追问能从历史阴影中闪现的短暂实验中拾取什么——那些总是临近工地的废墟挖掘，那些从瓦砾中解构并重造的痕迹清单。当北京转向“进入世界”时，艺术作品与这一新中国梦既合作又颠覆。王能涛的《颠覆——土地》记录了这种世界营造，也记录了大地上未被书写的自发状态，以及被地面上的人颠覆的可能性。尹秀珍的《便携北京》在世界中穿梭，同时庇护着其他社会组织与连接形式的亲密、可触历史。陈羚羊的《25:00》闪耀着魔幻时刻的幻想：按自己的方式栖居“真实/男性”世界。把中国当代艺术置于扩展场域中，置于“一个不断增殖、多重、重叠的文化空间中”，需要一种双重视线，同时把握纪念碑式与转瞬即逝之物。

[^en-intro-20]: The Chinese term *liumang* consists of two characters, *liu* meaning “to flow” and *mang* referring to “common people.” It connotes an “outsider” identity, someone who has fallen out of family, group, or state relations and therefore is potentially subversive. In the Chinese translation of the *Communist Manifesto*, the German term *lumpenproletariat* became *liumang wuchanzhe* (hooligan proletariat). The criminalization of hooliganism—activities such as gang fights, sexual assault on women, and disruption of public order—was codified under a provision of China’s 1979 Criminal Law and subsequently used to also police homosex between men. This historical anxiety about wide-ranging male activities outside of heteronormative kinship demonstrates the need for deconstruction of gendered masculine and feminine norms together. Dutton, *Streetlife China*, 62–74; Kang, “The Decriminalization and Depathologization of Homosexuality in China.”

[^zh-intro-20]: 中文词"流氓"由两个字组成："流"意为流动，"氓"指平民。它意味着一种"局外人"身份，即从家庭、群体或国家关系中脱落、因而具有潜在颠覆性的人。在《共产党宣言》的中译本里，德文词 *lumpenproletariat* 被译为"流氓无产者"。将流氓行为——如帮派斗殴、对妇女的性侵犯、扰乱公共秩序等活动——入罪，被写入1979年《中华人民共和国刑法》的一项条款，后来又用于管制男性之间的性行为。这种对异性恋规范亲属关系之外广泛男性活动的历史焦虑表明，有必要把性别化的男性与女性规范放在一起解构。Dutton, *Streetlife China*, 62–74；Kang, "The Decriminalization and Depathologization of Homosexuality in China"。

[^en-intro-40]: Chinese artists of the contemporary era employ a wider array of media than those represented by this interpretation of *dangdai yishu*. Calligraphers and ink painters continue to practice these “traditional” and, according to some, more Chinese art forms in the current moment and so can be considered contemporary artists. However, with a few notable crossover exceptions such as Xu Bing and Gu Wenda, they tend to be labeled under categories such as “new ink painting” (*xin shuimo hua*) or “national painting” (*guohua*), understood to be more firmly rooted in China and its diasporas. Concerted effort goes into differentiating “contemporary” and “traditional” forms, even though artists often work in both. The phrase “contemporary Chinese art” risks emphasizing the Chinese-ness of the art, a distinction I am more interested in analyzing than reifying.

[^zh-intro-40]: 当代中国的艺术家使用的媒介比"当代艺术"这一解释所代表的更为广泛。书法家和水墨画家在当下继续实践这些"传统"形式——一些人认为它们更具中国性——因此也可被视为当代艺术家。然而，除了徐冰、谷文达等少数引人注目的跨界例外，他们往往被归入"新水墨画"或"国画"等类别，被理解为更牢固地扎根于中国及其离散社群。人们付出大量努力区分"当代"与"传统"形式，尽管艺术家常常两者兼作。"contemporary Chinese art"（当代中国的艺术）这一说法有强调艺术之中国性的风险，而我更感兴趣的是分析这种区分，而非将其物化。

## 第一部分　艺术世界营造


〔原书 41〕

PART I: Art Worldings

第一部分　艺术世界营造


## 第一章　先锋北京


〔原书 43〕

One: Xianfeng Beijing

第一章　先锋北京


〔原书 43〕

The invitation for the now historic 1989 “no U-turn” exhibit in Beijing at the National Art Museum of China presents a translingual puzzle.[^en-ch01-1] The Chinese text at the top reads *Zhongguo xiandai yishu zhan* (Chinese modern art exhibit). The English text at the bottom, *China/Avant-Garde*, anticipates a foreign audience. It also introduces a discrepancy that reveals the problem of translation when understood as a process of producing linguistic equivalencies.[^en-ch01-2] What do we make of “modern” in Chinese versus “avant-garde” in English? Or of the French “avant-garde,” coined in the nineteenth century, in later Chinese and English contexts? Curator Gao Minglu explains that while *xiandai* (modern) in 1980s China signified newness, he and the editor of the exhibit catalogue agreed that “ ‘avant-garde’ made more sense than ‘modern’ as a translation of the original Chinese title.”[^en-ch01-3] Modern in English seemed outdated, suggesting even a period style. Avant-garde sounded cutting-edge. Gao notes that Chinese artists and critics first began using *qianwei* (literally, forward guard) and *xianfeng* (literally, advance front) toward the end of the 1980s. It was only after 1989 that they gradually replaced “modern” as descriptors for contemporary art practice.[^en-ch01-4]

1989年那场如今已载入史册的北京中国美术馆“禁止掉头”展览，其邀请函呈现出一个跨语言的谜题。[^zh-ch01-1] 上方的中文写着“中国现代艺术展”。下方的英文“China/Avant-Garde”则预示着一个外国观众群体。它还引入了一处差异，揭示出把翻译理解为生产语言对等物之过程时的问题。[^zh-ch01-2] 中文的“现代”与英文的“前卫”该如何理解？19世纪创造的法文“avant-garde”，在后来中文与英文语境中又意味着什么？策展人高名潞解释说，在20世纪80年代的中国，“现代”（xiandai）意味着新，但他和展览图录编辑一致认为，“用‘前卫’来翻译原中文标题比用‘现代’更说得通”。[^zh-ch01-3] 英文的“modern”显得过时，甚至暗示一种时期风格；前卫听起来则很前沿。高名潞指出，中国艺术家和批评家直到20世纪80年代末才开始使用“前卫”（qianwei，原文释为“前方卫队”）和“先锋”（xianfeng，原文释为“前进的锋线”）。也是在1989年之后，它们才逐渐取代“现代”，成为当代艺术实践的描述词。[^zh-ch01-4]


〔原书 43, 44〕

As Chinese art circulated under the label xianfeng/avant-garde in the 1990s, I found myself struck, at street level, by a Chinese context for the term that diverged from its cultural career in the West. I regularly slid money through a subway ticket window under a brass plaque engraved with the characters *gongren xianfeng hao* (vanguard worker designation), a distinction awarded to units demonstrating an exemplary socialist work ethic. I noticed the honorary title on red and gold placards displayed in the front windows of public buses. I recognized its cognate of *shaonian xianfeng dui* (young pioneers) on elementary school banners and in the nationalist children’s anthem whose lyrics impel young heirs of the Communist mantel to courageously advance toward victory. I noticed it in advertisements for electronics equipment, articles on home decorating, and public injunctions for Beijing to succeed in its bid for the Olympics, as well as on the cover of new art journals like *Jinri xianfeng* (Avant-garde today).[^en-ch01-5] It was a term still in flux, with a past that lived on in present juxtaposition with new meanings.

20世纪90年代，中国艺术以先锋/前卫（xianfeng/avant-garde）的标签流通时，我在街头层面被该词的中国语境所触动，它与这个词在西方经历的文化历程并不相同。我经常从地铁售票窗口递钱，窗口上方钉着一块铜牌，刻着“工人先锋号”（gongren xianfeng hao）——一种授予展现模范社会主义劳动伦理的单位的称号。我在公共汽车前窗的红金色标牌上注意到这一荣誉称号。我认出它的同源词“少年先锋队”（shaonian xianfeng dui）出现在小学横幅上，也出现在那首民族主义儿童歌曲里，歌词激励共产主义的年轻继承者勇敢向胜利前进。我在电子产品广告中注意到它，在关于家居装饰的文章中，在北京申奥成功的公共号召中，以及《今日先锋》这类新艺术杂志的封面上看到它。[^zh-ch01-5] 这是一个仍在变动的词，它的过去与新的含义并置，活在当下。


〔原书 44〕

![图1.01　高氏兄弟编，《中国前卫艺术状况》，南京：江苏人民出版社，2002年。书籍封面。封面作品：祁志龙，《中国姑娘》。](web/assets/ch01-b003.jpg)

FIG 1.01 Gao Brothers, eds., *Zhongguo qianwei yishu zhuangkuang* (The condition of Chinese avant-garde art), Nanjing: Jiangsu renmin chubanshe, 2002. Book cover. Cover art: Qi Zhilong, *China Girl*.

图1.01　高氏兄弟编，《中国前卫艺术状况》，南京：江苏人民出版社，2002年。书籍封面。封面作品：祁志龙，《中国姑娘》。


〔原书 44, 45〕

As a descriptor for the field I entered, xianfeng signifies the historical, political vanguard of Beijing as national capital *and* the forms of artistic activity it has fostered over time. It connotes revolutionary militarism and cultural cosmopolitanism. Only by assembling the translingual fragments of avant-garde/qianwei/xianfeng can we make sense of their cultural encounter in the context of Chinese contemporary art. Take for example the painting of a young woman in Red Guard uniform on the cover of a book titled *The Condition of Chinese Avant-Garde Art* (figure 1.01). Qi Zhilong’s *China Girl* references a Maoist history of vanguardism, yet is infused with the soft come-hither glow of contemporary commodity culture. It appeals to Western desires for a Chinese avant-garde as political fetish that ventriloquizes liberal freedom of expression. It represents a Chinese break from the collectivized past of Maoist modernity even while remaining influenced by its revolutionary aesthetics. It also represents the persistence of gender politics in the confluence of avant-garde ideologies.

作为对我所进入领域的描述，xianfeng 既意味着北京作为国家首都的历史性政治先锋，也意味着它长期培育的艺术活动形式。它包含着革命尚武精神与文化世界主义。只有把 avant-garde、qianwei、xianfeng 这些跨语言碎片组装起来，我们才能理解它们在中国当代艺术语境中的文化相遇。以一本题为《中国前卫艺术状况》的书封面为例（图1.01），画中是一位穿红卫兵制服的年轻女子。祁志龙的《中国姑娘》指涉毛泽东主义的先锋历史，却又注入当代商品文化那种柔软诱人的光晕。它迎合西方对中国前卫的欲望——把中国前卫当作一种政治恋物，替西方代言自由表达。它代表中国对毛泽东主义现代性集体化过去的断裂，同时又仍受其革命美学影响。它也代表着性别政治在前卫意识形态汇流中的持续存在。


〔原书 45〕

This chapter examines the remaking of Beijing first through an overview of cultural policy in relation to the capital city, and of avant-garde genealogies.[^en-ch01-6] It then portrays this remaking through a montage of ethnographic fragments organized around key art institutions—academy, palace, village, and museum—as they shift from sites of revolutionary nationalism to culture industry formation. Montage as method underlies the composition of this book, which assembles an account of cultural transition from closely observed ethnographic fragments and builds its argument across chapters. It is an assemblage whose theory of knowledge arises from dialectical contrasts between colliding myths of progress and modernity. Its compositional aesthetics reflect those of the artists I focus on, whose works often represent “dialectics at a standstill.”[^en-ch01-7] Bringing gender to the analysis heightens awareness of the relationship between avant-gardism and nationalism, and thus the need to deconstruct the avant-garde myth of originality as a repressive and colonizing technology whose professed faith in renewal and innovation masks its power plays.

本章首先概述与首都相关的文化政策及前卫谱系，以考察北京的再造。[^zh-ch01-6] 随后，本章通过围绕关键艺术机构——学院、宫、村和博物馆——组织的一组民族志碎片蒙太奇，描绘这种再造，观察它们如何从革命民族主义的场所转变为文化产业的形成之地。蒙太奇作为一种方法，是本书构成的底层逻辑：它从细致观察的民族志碎片中组装出一部文化转型叙述，并跨章节构建论证。这是一个拼装体，其知识理论产生于相互碰撞的进步神话与现代性神话之间的辩证对照。它的构成美学也映照我所聚焦的艺术家的美学，他们的作品常常表现“停顿中的辩证法”。[^zh-ch01-7] 把性别带入分析，会提高对前卫主义与民族主义之关系的自觉，也因此更需解构关于原创性的前卫神话——一种压制性的殖民化技术，它对革新与创新的公开信仰掩盖着权力游戏。


〔原书 45〕

Cultural Capital

文化资本


〔原书 45〕

The artists I interviewed lived in locations scattered throughout Beijing, a megacity at the turn of the millennium of more than 10 million people. The logistics of my research involved spending significant time on the subway, on buses, in cabs, or on carts attached to the back of three-wheeled motorcycles. In a Shijingshan District classroom, a college art teacher painted a wall-sized canvas crowded with popular figures ranging from politicians to movie stars, in a style influenced by propaganda posters and folk art. In the semirural Western Hills, a painter-turned-video artist from Anhui vented about local and global cultural hierarchies in a rudimentary brick dwelling rented from a farmer. In a Chongwen District high-rise, a painter-turned-performance artist living in a concrete-box apartment on the tenth floor took photos from her window of the construction site next door. In Songzhuang artist village, a cluster of studios built on farmland in Tongzhou District, the “political pop” painter whose massive compound I visited with a group of curators wasn’t home. Instead, a hired apprentice from the countryside worked away on one of his paintings that fetched record prices on the international market.

我访谈的艺术家住在北京各处。世纪之交的北京是一座拥有逾千万人口的特大城市。我的研究后勤意味着要在地铁、公共汽车、出租车或三轮摩托车后挂的板车上花费大量时间。在石景山区的一间教室里，一位大学美术教师画了一幅满墙大小的油画，画中挤满从政治家到电影明星的流行人物，风格受宣传画和民间艺术影响。在西山半乡村地区，一位来自安徽、从画家转行的录像艺术家在向农民租来的简陋砖房里，发泄对地方与全球文化等级的不满。在崇文区一栋高层建筑里，一位从画家转行的行为艺术家住在十楼的混凝土火柴盒公寓中，从窗口拍摄隔壁工地。在宋庄艺术家村——通州区农田上建起的一片画室群——我随一群策展人去了那位“政治波普”画家的巨大院落，但他不在家。一个从乡下雇来的学徒正替他画一幅在国际市场上创下纪录价格的画。


〔原书 46〕

![地图1.01　北京地图（西半部）。Tim Stallmann 绘制，使用作者笔记与 OpenStreetMap 数据。](web/assets/ch01-b008.png)

MAP 1.01 Map of Beijing (western half). Designed by Tim Stallmann using data from author’s notes and OpenStreetMap.

地图1.01　北京地图（西半部）。Tim Stallmann 绘制，使用作者笔记与 OpenStreetMap 数据。


〔原书 46, 47, 48〕

In spite of their differences, these artists routinely reiterated Beijing’s status as China’s “cultural center” (*wenhua zhongxin*), although their counterparts in the provinces often asserted the freedom of being “far from the emperor’s eye.” This belief in Beijing’s prominence persisted through the 1990s in spite of the fact that contemporary art exhibits in the capital were shut down with greater regularity than in other cities with burgeoning art scenes like Shanghai or Chengdu. The infamous reputation of the Beijing Ministry of Culture led to jokes about how censorship of an exhibit guaranteed foreign attention. When I asked artists, especially those without Beijing residence permits, work units, or familial connections, why they wanted to live there, some mentioned the large number of universities, including the Central Academy of Fine Arts, a historical sense of Beijing as imperial seat of culture, or even the creative tension of official opposition. Others responded along the lines of “because I can meet people like you,” meaning a foreigner. Beijing’s embassy districts and foreign-owned galleries catering to overseas buyers led to the development of a patronage system that attracted curators and art brokers from abroad. This magnetism eventually became a resource for the state’s remaking of Beijing.

尽管有种种差异，这些艺术家仍经常重申北京作为中国“文化中心”（wenhua zhongxin）的地位，尽管外省的同行常说“天高皇帝远”的自由。这种对北京重要性的信念在整个20世纪90年代持续存在，尽管首都的当代艺术展比上海或成都等艺术场景蓬勃发展的城市更频繁地被关闭。设在北京的文化部声名狼藉，以致人们开玩笑说，一个展览只要被查禁，就保证能引起外国关注。当我问艺术家——尤其是那些没有北京户口、单位或家庭关系的人——为什么想住在这里时，有人提到这里大学众多，包括中央美术学院；有人提到北京作为帝国文化中心的历史感；还有人提到官方反对所带来的创造性张力。其他人的回答则是“因为我能遇到像你这样的人”，意思是外国人。北京的使馆区和面向海外买家的外资画廊促成了一个赞助网络，吸引来自国外的策展人和艺术经纪人。这种吸引力最终成为国家再造北京的一项资源。


〔原书 47〕

![地图1.02　北京地图（东半部）。Tim Stallmann 绘制，使用作者笔记与 OpenStreetMap 数据。](web/assets/ch01-b010.png)

MAP 1.02 Map of Beijing (eastern half). Designed by Tim Stallmann using data from author’s notes and OpenStreetMap.

地图1.02　北京地图（东半部）。Tim Stallmann 绘制，使用作者笔记与 OpenStreetMap 数据。


〔原书 48〕

After the controversial closures of the *China/Avant-Garde* exhibit in 1989, followed by the events of June 4, the national Ministry of Culture initially turned its sights toward the south. The first China Art Exposition (*Zhongguo yishu bolanhui*), the nation’s largest showcase of contemporary art, was launched in 1993 in Guangzhou’s Chinese Import-Export Commodities Trade Center. This linkage between art and commerce occurred one year after Deng Xiaoping’s highly publicized tour of the south. During his visit to the special economic zones of Guangzhou and Shenzhen, he praised their commercial successes and advocated market reform as the way for China to overcome its recent domestic turmoil and open connections with the world through trade.

1989年中国现代艺术展引发争议地关闭，随后又发生6月4日事件，国家文化部最初把目光转向南方。1993年，全国最大的当代艺术展示会——第一届中国艺术博览会（Zhongguo yishu bolanhui）——在广州的中国进出口商品交易中心推出。艺术与商业的这种联结，发生在邓小平高调南巡一年之后。在访问广州和深圳经济特区期间，邓小平称赞其商业成就，主张把市场改革作为中国克服国内动荡、通过贸易与世界连接的道路。


〔原书 48〕

In 1995, organizers moved the China Art Expo to Beijing, claiming its location in Guangzhou had not garnered sufficient international attention. In the early 2000s, the weeklong art exposition continued to be held every summer in Beijing’s International Exhibition Center. Rows of numbered booths, rented by artists, galleries, art schools, publishing houses, antique dealers, and companies promoting art and culture, filled two cavernous halls. Many artists welcomed the Expo, in spite of its Ministry of Culture sponsorship, as an alternative to official exhibition spaces. After an initial period of enthusiasm, some dismissively likened the Expo to a hodgepodge marketplace, a maze of street stall *getihu* (independent entrepreneurs), with no distinction between good and bad. The most disparaging had begun showing their work in Beijing’s foreign-run galleries. Their desire for the distinction of market valuation ran counter to one of the original rationales for the Expo, a commercial twist on the socialist goal of “serving the people”: that offering art at affordable prices would combat elitism and make the nation’s art accessible to the general public.[^en-ch01-8]

1995年，组织者把中国艺术博览会移到北京，称其广州选址未能获得足够的国际关注。21世纪初，为期一周的艺术博览会仍每年夏天在北京国际展览中心举行。艺术家、画廊、美术学校、出版社、古董商以及推广艺术与文化的公司租下成排编号展位，填满两个巨大展厅。尽管博览会由文化部主办，许多艺术家仍把它当作官方展览空间之外的替代选择而欢迎它。最初的热情过后，一些人轻蔑地把博览会比作大杂烩市场，一个由街边摊位个体户（getihu）组成的迷宫，好坏不分。最不屑一顾的人已开始在北京外资画廊展出作品。他们对市场估值区隔的渴望，与博览会最初的理据之一相抵触——那是对社会主义“为人民服务”目标的商业式改写：以可负担的价格提供艺术，将对抗精英主义，使全国艺术为普通公众所接近。[^zh-ch01-8]


〔原书 48, 49〕

The move of the Expo also represented a symbolic struggle between north and south. After Guangzhou proved that promoting cultural festivals and programs was good for business, Beijing adopted the model. Jing Wang notes, “The recent hype about Beijing’s capital impact (*shoudu xiao-ying*) was the result of an intensifying image race orchestrated and monitored closely by the Department of the Strategies of Cultural Development in Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Beijing. As Shanghai and Guangzhou shifted their emphasis of urban planning from industrial to cultural economy, Beijing followed suit.”[^en-ch01-9] In 1996, Beijing’s Municipal Political Consultative Committee articulated a new development strategy, “founding the capital through culture” (*wenhua lidu*).[^en-ch01-10] They highlighted Beijing’s historical heritage as a reserve of cultural capital that financial or commercial cities like Shanghai and Guangzhou could never attain. The city government soon began investing in the large-scale construction of new cultural institutions, a trend that accelerated after Beijing won the bid in 2001 for the 2008 Olympics.[^en-ch01-11]

博览会的迁移也代表着南北之间的象征性斗争。在广州证明推广文化节庆和项目有利于商业之后，北京采用了这一模式。王瑾指出：“近来关于北京‘首都效应’（shoudu xiao-ying）的炒作，是上海、广州和北京的文化发展战略部门精心编排并密切监控的一场形象竞赛不断加剧的结果。当上海和广州把城市规划重点从工业经济转向文化经济时，北京也紧随其后。”[^zh-ch01-9] 1996年，北京市政协提出新的发展战略“文化立都”（wenhua lidu）。[^zh-ch01-10] 他们强调北京的历史遗产是文化资本的储备，上海和广州这类金融或商业城市永远无法获得。市政府很快开始投资大规模建设新文化机构，这一趋势在北京2001年赢得2008年奥运会主办权后加速。[^zh-ch01-11]


〔原书 49〕

This race between Beijing and other Chinese cities to develop the “tertiary sector” of culture as proof of their global arrival represented a major shift in national spatial ideology. Maoist rhetoric celebrated the revolutionary qualities of the rural peasantry as a vanguard force in the communist nation’s progress. A post-Mao focus on urbanization made cities the new national object of desire and resignified rural people as backward or stuck in the past. State-disseminated discourse on *suzhi* (quality) reinforced the idea that rural citizens, relative to their urban counterparts, most needed to raise their suzhi, even as official economic strategy led to widening material disparity between city and country.[^en-ch01-12] This state redirection and investment in cities corresponded with a transformation from coercive to regulatory forms of governance.[^en-ch01-13] For example, the Ministry of Culture, once viewed as a policing body, became the sponsor of the China Art Expo. In Jing Wang’s words, “The state’s rediscovery of culture as a site where new ruling technologies can be deployed and converted simultaneously into economic capital constitutes one of its most innovative strategies of statecraft since the founding of the People’s Republic.”[^en-ch01-14]

北京与其他中国城市之间这场发展文化“第三产业”、以证明其全球抵达的竞赛，代表着国家空间意识形态的重大转变。毛泽东主义修辞赞扬农村农民作为共产主义国家进步先锋力量的革命品质。后毛泽东时代对城市化的关注使城市成为新的国家欲望对象，并把农村人重新意指为落后或停滞在过去。国家传播的关于“素质”（suzhi）的话语强化了这一观念：与城市居民相比，农村公民最需要提高素质，即便官方经济战略导致城乡物质差距扩大。[^zh-ch01-12] 国家对城市的重新定向和投资，与治理从强制性形式向规制性形式的转变相对应。[^zh-ch01-13] 例如，文化部曾被视为管控机构，如今却成了中国艺术博览会的赞助者。用王瑾的话说：“国家重新发现文化，把它当作可以部署新的统治技术并同时转化为经济资本的场所，这是中华人民共和国成立以来最具创新的治国策略之一。”[^zh-ch01-14]


〔原书 49〕

Avant-Guard Genealogies

先锋谱系


〔原书 49, 50〕

Shi Xinning’s “*Duchamp Retrospective Exhibition” in China* (figure 1.02) juxtaposes iconic symbols of the avant-garde of Western art and Chinese socialism. In a fictional encounter of “impossible reality”—an altered reproduction of an image taken at an official visit to an industrial exhibition by one of Mao Zedong’s official photographers (figure 1.03)—Shi depicts the chairman intently inspecting Marcel Duchamp’s *Fountain*.[^en-ch01-15] On the one hand, it references the Great Leap Forward, Mao’s campaign beginning in 1958 to transform the country through rapid industrialization, when exhibits of modern amenities became a staple of Cold War politics. A year after Mao’s tour of the biogas exhibition, evidence of China’s progress toward surpassing capitalist development within fifteen years, Khrushchev and Nixon hotly debated their nations’ technological superiority in a model American kitchen on display in Moscow.[^en-ch01-16] Mao’s gaze turns a stove into a politic symbol of surpassing the enemy. On the other hand, Shi’s black-and-white painting references the avant-garde aesthetic of Marcel Duchamp, who promoted conceptual thought over visual pleasure. Duchamp’s idea of the readymade became the “antiart” move that secured his place of prominence in modern art history. Through a process of selection and alteration, he transformed ordinary manufactured objects into art. *Fountain*, the urinal he signed R. Mutt and first exhibited in 1917, has come to serve as a critique of the museum’s institutional power to convey artistic value. (Shi’s image collision draws the humorous connection between urinal and biogas stove: of excrement powering modernity.) Preparations for a Duchamp retrospective exhibition were in fact contemporaneous with the photo of Mao’s exhibition visit; it eventually opened in 1963 at the Pasadena Museum of Art. Shi makes these two avant-garde visions proximal. His documentary style of painting, based on his training in socialist realism at Shenyang’s Lu Xun Academy of Fine Arts, mimics the way artists under Mao reworked historical paintings in response to political winds.[^en-ch01-17] The resulting “impossible reality” imbricates the masculinist chess match of Cold War politics with that of Western modernist aesthetics. The readymade in Shi Xinning’s painting—the photograph he reproduces, the urinal he places in it—becomes a symbolic fetish animated by opposing versions of historicism and surpassing the other.

石心宁的《“杜尚回顾展”在中国》（图1.02）把西方艺术前卫与中国社会主义的标志性符号并置。在一次“不可能的现实”的虚构相遇中——毛泽东一位官方摄影师在参观工业展览时拍摄之图像的修改复制品（图1.03）——石心宁描绘主席专注地审视马塞尔·杜尚的《泉》。[^zh-ch01-15] 一方面，它指涉大跃进，即毛泽东从1958年开始通过快速工业化改造国家的运动，当时现代生活设施的展览成为冷战政治的常见项目。毛泽东参观沼气利用展览——被视为中国正朝着十五年内赶超资本主义发展的目标前进的证据——一年之后，赫鲁晓夫与尼克松在莫斯科展出的美国样板厨房里，就各自国家的技术优越性展开激烈辩论。[^zh-ch01-16] 毛泽东的凝视把一只炉子变成超越敌人的政治象征。另一方面，石心宁的黑白绘画指涉马塞尔·杜尚的前卫美学，他推崇概念思考高于视觉愉悦。杜尚的现成品观念成为“反艺术”举动，确立了他在现代艺术史上的显要地位。通过选择和改动，他把普通制成品变成艺术。他签署“R. Mutt”并于1917年首次展出的小便池《泉》，已成为对博物馆传达艺术价值之制度权力的批判。（石心宁的图像碰撞引出小便池与沼气炉之间的幽默联系：粪便驱动现代性。）杜尚回顾展的筹备，实际上与毛泽东参观展览的照片同时发生；展览最终于1963年在帕萨迪纳艺术博物馆开幕。石心宁使这两种前卫视野彼此邻近。他的纪实风格绘画基于在沈阳鲁迅美术学院接受的社会主义现实主义训练，模仿毛泽东时代艺术家根据政治风向修改历史画的方式。[^zh-ch01-17] 由此产生的“不可能的现实”，把冷战政治的男性主义棋局与西方现代主义美学的棋局嵌合在一起。石心宁画中的现成品——他复制的照片、他放入照片中的小便池——成为一个象征性恋物，由相互对立的历史主义版本和超越对方之欲所激活。


〔原书 50, 52〕

In my conversations with artists, they often reflected ambivalently on what it meant to be called avant-garde. One artist had created an altar to Mao Zedong in the corner of his studio, an installation piece as he called it. He provided a revisionist history as he looped avant-garde back to the role of culture in Maoist thought. At the center of the installation was an old dresser mirror purchased at a junk market. The slogan “to serve the people,” now chipped and faded, had been painted in red at the top of the mirror. Cultural Revolution images of Mao stuck in its wooden border framed the face of whoever looked into the mirror. Other propaganda images and a pair of red candles were laid as offerings in front of the mirror. His memory of the Cultural Revolution contained scars—police had investigated him as a teenager for allegedly writing an anti-Mao slogan on a village wall—but he remained in awe of the pervasiveness of its aesthetic, the everyday influence of decorated mirrors like the one he’d found discarded. He disparaged the materialistic ethos that permeated the current era and the professionalized circuits of its so-called avant-garde: “In my view, if we’re talking about people who make so-called avant-garde art, I think Mao Zedong was the greatest avant-garde artist. He really was unmatched. Under his orchestration, the clothes that people wore, the soldiers’ uniforms, were all blue, everything was that kind of thing, with everyone standing together. For avant-garde artists to do this today, that would really be an amazing piece. My worship for Mao is as an artist.... He was really an artist not a politician. He really couldn’t be a politician.”[^en-ch01-18]

在与艺术家的交谈中，他们常常矛盾地反思被称为前卫意味着什么。一位艺术家在画室一角做了一座毛泽东祭坛，他称之为装置作品。他把前卫绕回毛泽东主义思想中文化的作用，提供了一种修正主义历史。装置中央是一面从旧货市场买来的旧梳妆镜。镜子上方用红漆写着“为人民服务”，如今已斑驳褪色。嵌在木边框里的毛泽东文革时期图像，框住任何照镜者的脸。镜前摆放着其他宣传图像和一对红烛作为供品。他对文革的记忆带有创伤——十几岁时，警方曾调查他，指称他在村墙上写了反毛标语——但他对这种美学无孔不入的力量仍心存敬畏，比如他捡到的那面被丢弃的装饰镜，仍在日常生活中发挥影响。他贬斥弥漫在当下时代的物质主义风气，以及所谓前卫的专业化圈子：“在我看来，如果谈所谓前卫艺术的创作者，我认为毛泽东是最伟大的前卫艺术家。他真是无人能及。在他的编排下，人们穿的衣服、士兵的军装都是蓝色的，一切都是那一套，所有人站在一起。今天的前卫艺术家若能做到这一点，那才会是惊人的作品。我对毛的崇拜是作为艺术家……他真的是艺术家，不是政治家。他真的当不了政治家。”[^zh-ch01-18]


〔原书 51〕

![图1.02　石心宁，《“杜尚回顾展”在中国》，2001年。布面油画，100厘米×100厘米。](web/assets/ch01-b018.jpg)

FIG 1.02 Shi Xinning, “*Duchamp Retrospective Exhibition” in China*, 2001. Oil on canvas, 100 cm × 100 cm.

图1.02　石心宁，《“杜尚回顾展”在中国》，2001年。布面油画，100厘米×100厘米。


〔原书 51〕

![图1.03　徐肖冰，《毛泽东、王任重参观1958年沼气利用展览》，1958年。摄影。](web/assets/ch01-b019.jpg)

FIG 1.03 Xu Xiaobing, *Mao Zedong and Wang Renzhong Visit 1958 Exhibition of Biogas Uses*, 1958. Photograph.

图1.03　徐肖冰，《毛泽东、王任重参观1958年沼气利用展览》，1958年。摄影。


〔原书 52〕

At a dinner party of exactly the kind of artists he disparaged, contradictions still came to the fore. They gathered in a painter’s renovated apartment, which had just been featured in an interior design magazine. After discussion about home decorating principles, the pros and cons of ikea’s influence in Beijing, and the travails involved in securing visas for travel to overseas exhibits, the conversation turned toward the position of intellectuals in Chinese society. A debate broke out about Lu Xun, the highly regarded twentieth-century writer, social critic, and proponent of the leftist woodblock movement, canonized by the Chinese Communist Party after his death in 1936. One artist commented that for all their recent material accumulation and aspiration to cultural refinement, they couldn’t come close to Lu Xun’s lifestyle. He’d been reading Lu Xun’s diaries and was struck by the resources he had. Converting Lu Xun’s reported income into modern currency, he claimed it would be tens of thousands of yuan a month. In his assessment, Lu Xun spent most of his free time buying things—books, paintings, antiques, even old courtyard homes. Others joked that Lu Xun had become such an acerbic social critic because every morning he would bargain with art and antique dealers on Liulichang Street. Angry at being cheated out of a good price, he would return home and use his pen to curse people.
