〔原书 101, 102〕

Several pieces in Zhang’s *Run, Jump, Crawl, Walk* present explorations of a rapidly changing social environment amplified by the history of the exhibition site, its embodied labor, fantasies, and wounds. The digital photographs in Chen Lingyang’s *25:00* lightbox series illuminate an oversize female nude, the artist’s own body, in panoramic Beijing nightscapes (plate 2). She harbors an interior realm of possibility that looms within the “real” world, while also exposing human vulnerability on a monumental scale. In Zhuang Hui’s *June 25th, Cha Shan Town*, an arresting scene appears amid a dramatically lit, life-size diorama. Artificial grass and flowers sprout from the ground. Against a backdrop of white clouds and blue sky, a thick pink cotton cloud hovers. Framed by a grove of bamboo, a brightly dressed female mannequin stumbles forward with a hand to her face. Her eyes are closed and fake blood drips from them, down her fingers, and onto her orange top. Zhuang created this installation based on a story he read in a tabloid newspaper from southern China, where factories produce transnational consumer goods. Gang members had gouged out the eyes of a female rural migrant factory worker to sell on the black market for human body parts. The technicolor promise of the city produces surreal extremes of stratification and commodification.

张离《跑、跳、爬、走》中的几件作品探索了迅速变化的社会环境，这种探索被展览场所的历史、其具身劳动、幻想和创伤所放大。陈羚羊《25:00》灯箱系列中的数码照片，以全景式北京夜景照亮一个超大女性裸体——艺术家自己的身体（图版2）。她怀有一个内在的可能性领域，它隐现于“真实”世界之中，同时以纪念碑式的尺度暴露人的脆弱。在庄辉的《六月二十五日，茶山镇》中，一个引人注目的场景出现在戏剧性灯光下、真人大小的立体布景中。人造花草从地面生长出来。在白云和蓝天的背景前，悬着一团浓密的粉色棉云。在一丛竹子的框景中，一个穿着鲜艳的女性人体模型一只手掩面，踉跄向前。她双眼紧闭，假血从眼中滴下，顺着手指流到橙色上衣上。庄辉根据他在南方一份小报上读到的故事创作了这件装置：那里的工厂生产跨国消费品。帮派成员挖出一名农村女工的眼睛，在黑市上出售人体器官。城市色彩斑斓的承诺，制造出超现实的分层与商品化极端。


〔原书 102〕

All of these pieces contain holdover socialist sentiments, embedded in the artists’ archival materials, stylistic predispositions, and subject matter, yet were exhibited within the reform-era logic of display in a city where planners and developers strove to command world attention. In contrast with the marketing mission that justified cosred investment in the art center, these artists found in the unfinished, layered aspects of the site a space of imagination. It opened an optical unconscious, inspiring theatrical scenario. Their pieces work through the contradictions embodied in the site’s comingled collectivist and privatized ideologies. Cosmopolitan middle-class lifestyle was built on but also haunted by the displacement of a female urban proletariat and the exploitation of a floating population of rural migrants. This type of site-specific artistic rumination did not align with the vision of Ocean Paradise developers. Their decision to rent out the art center was an interim step toward their next more definitive move.

所有这些作品都含有残留的社会主义情感，嵌入艺术家的档案材料、风格倾向和题材之中，却是在改革时期的展示逻辑中展出——在一个规划者和开发商力求吸引世界目光的城市里。与为远洋地产投资艺术中心提供理由的营销使命相反，这些艺术家在场地的未完成、多层次特质中发现了一个想象空间。它打开了一种视觉无意识，激发出戏剧性场景。他们的作品处理场地混杂的集体主义与私有化意识形态所体现的矛盾。世界性中产阶级生活方式建立在对女性城市无产阶级的迁置和对农村流动人口剥削的基础上，同时又被它们萦绕。这种场域特定的艺术沉思与远洋天地开发商的愿景并不一致。他们决定把艺术中心出租，是迈向下一步更决定性行动的中途站。


〔原书 102, 103〕

Just over two years after the East Modern Art Center was inaugurated with a performance that involved brick throwing, a bulldozer tore into its glass-box renovation of the New Great Factory. Lumbering machines methodically reduced it to the same fate No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3 Cotton Mills had met, and then hauled away the rubble of bricks, concrete, and rebar. In its first phase, the Ocean International Center built on the site included four glassy high-rise towers, the tallest of which rose to thirty-three floors. The towers housed several major Chinese banks, a conference and business center, service apartments, and office space leased by companies such as GlaxoSmithKline, Hewlett-Packard, and Fujitsu. The second phase added two more office buildings connected by a retail mall.[^en-ch02-53] In my interviews with various participants in the East Modern Art Center experiment, I heard different stories. Some told me that if it reaped enough success, it would survive into the future. Others told me that it was always intended to be temporary. It eventually became a kind of installation or performance piece in and of itself.

远洋艺术中心以一场涉及扔砖的演出开幕两年多后，一台推土机冲进了它对新大厂房的玻璃盒式改造。笨重的机器有条不紊地将其化为国棉一厂、二厂、三厂曾遭遇的同样命运，然后运走砖块、混凝土和钢筋的瓦砾。在其第一阶段，建在原址上的海洋国际中心包括四座玻璃高层塔楼，最高者达三十三层。塔楼容纳数家中国大型银行、会议与商务中心、服务式公寓，以及葛兰素史克、惠普和富士通等公司租用的办公空间。第二阶段又增加两栋由零售商场连接的办公楼。[^zh-ch02-53] 在采访远洋艺术中心实验的各参与者时，我听到不同的说法。一些人告诉我，如果它取得足够成功，就会延续到未来。另一些人告诉我，它从一开始就打算是临时的。它最终本身成了一件装置或行为作品。


〔原书 103〕

The East Modern Art Center preceded new art districts like 798, a Bauhaus-style electronics complex originally built in the 1950s with East German assistance.[^en-ch02-54] When artists and gallerists began renting studio and exhibition space in factories there, it became Beijing’s next center of contemporary art activity, and just as soon was embroiled in debates about art’s commercial cooptation, as well as plans to demolish the factory buildings and develop a high-tech zone. After a protracted struggle between artists and leaders of the landholding company, the area received official designation as the Dashanzi Art District just before the 2008 Olympics.[^en-ch02-55]

远洋艺术中心先于798等新艺术区出现。798是一座包豪斯风格的电子工业建筑群，最初于1950年代在东德援助下建成。[^zh-ch02-54] 当艺术家和画廊经营者开始在那里租用工作室和展览空间时，它成为北京下一个当代艺术活动中心，并很快卷入关于艺术商业收编的争论，以及拆除厂房、发展高科技园区的计划。经过艺术家与土地持有公司领导层的长期斗争，该地区在2008年奥运会前不久被正式指定为大山子艺术区。[^zh-ch02-55]


〔原书 103〕

*Dancing with Mingong* likewise marked another trend in the Beijing contemporary art world: in 2001–2, a number of artists produced work focused on rural migrant workers.[^en-ch02-56] Several of these artists described an initial identification with mingong, as they also lived in relatively poor and disenfranchised conditions on the margins of showcase Beijing.[^en-ch02-57] Then as new exhibition and market opportunities arose, they gained new cultural capital and sometimes financial security. Their artistic representation of mingong as emblematic of new forms of social inequality often led to conflicts over ethics or fair compensation. A 2003 group show titled *Together with Migrants*, curated by Yang Xinyi and featuring the work of fifteen artists, epitomized this phenomenon. Organized in conjunction with a unesco project for rural poverty reduction, the exhibit ran for one week in the newly opened Today Art Museum. The disjuncture between social justice work and contemporary art exhibited in a space like the Today Art Museum emerged in a comment by Huang Ping, a sociologist affiliated with the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and a collaborating member of the unesco project. He bluntly stated, “We are not that happy with the exhibit. We want to show what the migrants contribute to society, but the artists have only depicted their poverty and desperation.”[^en-ch02-58]

《与民工共舞》同样标志着北京当代艺术界的另一趋势：2001至2002年，多位艺术家创作了聚焦农村外来民工的作品。[^zh-ch02-56] 其中几位艺术家描述了他们最初对民工的认同，因为他们也生活在展示北京边缘相对贫穷、权利被剥夺的条件下。[^zh-ch02-57] 随着新的展览和市场机会出现，他们获得了新的文化资本，有时也获得经济保障。他们对民工作为社会不平等新形式象征的艺术再现，常常引发关于伦理或公平报酬的冲突。2003年由 Yang Xinyi 策展、十五位艺术家参展的群展《与移民同在》集中体现了这一现象。该展览与联合国教科文组织的一个农村减贫项目合作举办，在新开馆的今日美术馆展出一周。社会正义工作与在今日美术馆这类空间展出的当代艺术之间的脱节，体现在中国社会科学院社会学家、教科文组织项目合作成员黄平的评论中。他直言：“我们对展览不太满意。我们想展示移民对社会的贡献，但艺术家只描绘了他们的贫穷和绝望。”[^zh-ch02-58]


〔原书 103〕

Art as Investment or Public Aesthetics

作为投资的艺术，还是公共美学


〔原书 103, 104〕

The Today Art Museum, conceived as part of the Pingod real estate development on the southern side of the cbd, appeared not long after the East Modern Art Center met its end.[^en-ch02-59] The developers hired the same architect, Yung Ho Chang, to convert a heating plant on the site into a mixed-use sales center and art museum. His studio’s approach to the renovation took into account the structure’s planned obsolesce: “The mix of commercial and cultural activities is strategic although not entirely unique in Beijing. The facility’s temporality means a very quick and low budget job.”[^en-ch02-60] Yet, over a decade later, the museum still stood, and was flourishing.

今日美术馆是作为中央商务区南侧苹果社区房地产项目的一部分而构思的，在远洋艺术中心终结后不久出现。[^zh-ch02-59] 开发商聘请同一位建筑师张永和，将场地上的一座供热厂改造成混合用途的售楼处和美术馆。他的工作室对改造的处理考虑了这座建筑按计划将被淘汰的临时性质：“商业与文化活动的混合具有战略性，尽管在北京并非完全独特。设施的临时性意味着工程必须非常快速且预算很低。”[^zh-ch02-60] 然而十多年后，美术馆依然矗立，并且蓬勃发展。


〔原书 104〕

If the East Modern Art Center left itself open to site-specific experimentation or resonance, the Today Art Museum founders cultivated a progrowth culture industry scheme, in which the creation of commodity value for real estate and for contemporary art works were closely intertwined. The design of the museum’s galleries followed the international white cube standard. The museum had a gift center, bookstore, and café, as well as membership and educational outreach programs. It offered storage space to contemporary art collectors. In 2009, it counted Mercedes-Benz, Montblanc, and Shanghai Tang among its many corporate sponsors. In 2010, Credit Suisse underwrote a Today Art Award. Several art magazines were published under the Today imprint, including *Dajia* (Master) and *Caijing* (Finance). The former identified and featured the work of “master” artists, often those included in the museum’s collection. The latter provided market analysis, including recent auction statistics for different categories ranging from porcelain to classical ink painting to contemporary art.

如果说远洋艺术中心为场域特定实验或共鸣敞开大门，今日美术馆的创办者则培育了一种亲增长的文化产业方案，为房地产和当代艺术创造商品价值在其中紧密交织。美术馆展厅的设计遵循国际白色立方标准。馆内设有礼品中心、书店和咖啡馆，还有会员及教育推广项目。它为当代艺术收藏家提供存储空间。2009年，其众多企业赞助商包括梅赛德斯-奔驰、万宝龙和上海滩。2010年，瑞信赞助了“今日艺术奖”。今日品牌旗下出版了几本艺术杂志，包括《大家》和《财经》。前者识别并推介“大师级”艺术家的作品，往往是美术馆收藏中的艺术家。后者提供市场分析，包括从瓷器、古典水墨到当代艺术等不同类别的近期拍卖统计。


〔原书 104〕

It might be argued that the success of the Today Art Museum represents the maturing of contemporary art institutions in China. It certainly demonstrates Chinese adoption of the globalizing model of corporate art intervention analyzed in Britain and the United States by Chin-tao Wu.[^en-ch02-61] Under Thatcher and Reagan in the 1980s, public arts funding was increasingly transferred to the corporate sector, which in return was able to raise its public image by trading in cultural respectability. Pingod leaders sent several of the Today Art Museum staff on a research tour of Western museums to study exactly this management model.[^en-ch02-62] The museum they created succeeded in laying claim to a smooth story of bourgeois arrival that contained unruly histories. It did not threaten or invite critique of Beijing as a growth machine in the making.

或许可以辩称，今日美术馆的成功代表中国当代艺术机构的成熟。它无疑证明中国采纳了吴金桃在英美分析过的企业介入艺术的全球化模式。[^zh-ch02-61] 在1980年代撒切尔和里根治下，公共艺术资助越来越多地转移到企业部门，企业则借助文化带来的声望来提升自身公众形象。苹果社区的领导者派今日美术馆的几位员工赴西方博物馆考察，专门研究这种管理模式。[^zh-ch02-62] 他们创建的美术馆成功地把自己包装成一部资产阶级登场的平滑叙事，掩饰了其中桀骜不驯的历史。它既未威胁北京作为一部正在形成的增长机器的运作，也未引发对这一进程的批判。


〔原书 104, 105〕

The East Modern Art Center circa 2001 represented a moment in a landscape of museum transformation. It provides a window onto the messy, nascent relationship of state-led urban renewal, privatized real estate, and art. Its embodiment of other ways of being in the city and in the world eventually became part of the wreckage left in the Ocean Paradise wake. Draw into this nexus, artists grappled with how to respond, aesthetically and practically, to the social changes reflected in the art world politics of their everyday lives. They adapted to the new ideological context of cultural industry development in Beijing but not without a struggle over the politics of form. Aesthetics have material consequences because they have the power to promote or puncture particular visions, and artists work at precisely this juncture. The frequency with which Chinese contemporary artists inserted themselves into their own work seems in part a meditation on the question of how their labor and skills fit into this changing landscape.

2001年前后的远洋艺术中心代表了博物馆转型景观中的一个时刻。它提供了一个窗口，让人看到国家主导的城市更新、私有化房地产与艺术之间混乱而初生的关系。它所体现的在城市与世界中生活的其他方式，最终成为远洋天地身后废墟的一部分。艺术家被卷入这一交织网络，努力思考如何在美学上和实践中回应艺术界日常政治所反映的社会变化。他们适应了北京文化产业发展的新意识形态语境，但并非没有形式的政治斗争。美学具有物质后果，因为它们有能力推动或刺破特定愿景，而艺术家正是工作在这个接合点上。中国当代艺术家频繁把自己插入作品，似乎部分是对其劳动和技能如何融入这一变化景观的沉思。


〔原书 105〕

At the Today Art Museum, art was recognized as worth collecting as a financial investment. It contributed to creating a distinct middle-class cultural sensibility for the Pingod real estate development. A 2007 billboard outside of the construction site announced: “cbd • Art Gallery Street • Hotel Lifestyle • Home. Today Art Museum, Asia’s largest Chinese contemporary art gallery, is uniquely linked with the world.” When artists whose engagement with site-specific art once led them out of the studio and into public spaces began to create installations and performances specifically for privatized museum sites like this one, they moved away from a public counteraesthetics.

在今日美术馆，艺术被认为值得作为金融投资来收藏。它为苹果社区房地产项目塑造独特的中产阶级文化感性作出了贡献。2007年建筑工地外的一块广告牌宣称：“CBD·艺术街区·酒店式生活·家。今日美术馆，亚洲最大的中国当代艺术馆，与世界的独特链接。”当曾因参与场域特定艺术而走出画室、进入公共空间的艺术家，开始专门为这种私有化美术馆场所创作装置和表演时，他们便远离了公共的反美学。


〔原书 105〕

In 2007, in the shadow of the partially constructed Koolhaas-designed cctv Headquarters, preparations were underway to demolish the only socialist-era apartment building still standing on the site. Most of the residents had already moved out, but several families refused to leave. With property-based activism on the rise, protest strategies aimed to delay demolition and gain better relocation compensation.[^en-ch02-63] Holdouts became known as “nail households” because they stood out in their resistance to being hammered down into submission. Those in the cctv case had painted graffiti on an exterior wall facing the traffic-congested Third Ring Road. Their slogans, whose aesthetics draw on Chinese traditions of big character posters and socialist murals, included:

2007年，在部分建成的库哈斯设计央视总部大楼的阴影下，拆除工地上唯一仍存的社会主义时期公寓楼的准备工作正在进行。大多数居民已经搬走，但有几户拒绝离开。随着以财产为基础的行动主义兴起，抗议策略旨在拖延拆迁、争取更好的安置补偿。[^zh-ch02-63] 拒不搬迁者被称为“钉子户”，因为他们在抵抗被锤打屈服方面格外突出。央视案例中的居民在面向交通拥堵的三环路的院墙上涂写涂鸦。他们的标语在美学上借鉴中国大字报和社会主义壁画传统，包括：


〔原书 105〕

The party and its people have suffered disaster.

Is it legal for CCTV officials to steal the people’s property?

Demolition and relocation results from the coalition of government and business.

The Olympics are here, I have no home.

党和人民遭了灾。

央视领导盗窃人民财产合法吗？

拆迁是官商勾结的结果。

奥运来了，我无家可归。


〔原书 105〕

The layers of paint under the large white characters indicated the ongoing battle to speak and to silence. The next day, August 13, 2007, all of the slogans had been painted over in black, including the one declaring: “The darkness of cctv.”[^en-ch02-64]

白色大字下层层叠叠的油漆，表明持续进行的言说与噤声之战。第二天，2007年8月13日，所有标语都被黑色油漆覆盖，包括那条写着“央视的黑暗”的标语。[^zh-ch02-64]


〔原书 106〕

![图2.07　涂写在“拆”字标记上的“保护”（baohu），央视工地外，2007年。James Tweedie 摄。](web/assets/ch02-b067.jpg)

FIG 2.07 *Baohu* (protect) graffitied over *chai* (demolish) designation, outside the cctv site, 2007. Photograph by James Tweedie.

图2.07　涂写在“拆”字标记上的“保护”（baohu），央视工地外，2007年。James Tweedie 摄。


〔原书 106〕

Adam Chau has analyzed the painting of the big character *chai* (demolish) on the walls of buildings slated for demolition as a text act, a visual form of expression shot through with power.[^en-ch02-65] The formal characteristics of the sign do not just communicate; they act on their audience. This is visual symbolism of a most site-specific nature, as are protests that use the same socialist form of big-character painting against the authoritarian power of urban renewal. On a wall outside the cctv site, blue graffiti painted over a white chai sign spilled outside the circle surrounding the character and declared, “protect!” (figure 2.07). While observers of these emerging forms of activism, which also include protests by laid-off workers seeking more just compensation, see them as a hopeful trend in making growth machine social costs more visible, they also acknowledge that communities often have few resources to rely on in the face of deve-lopment backed by the government.[^en-ch02-66]

Adam Chau 将待拆建筑墙上“拆”字的书写分析为一种文本行为、一种渗透着权力的视觉表达形式。[^zh-ch02-65] 这一标志的形式特征不仅传达信息，还作用于观众。这是最具场域特定性的视觉象征，使用同一社会主义大字报形式的抗议针对城市更新的威权权力，也是如此。在央视工地外的一面墙上，覆盖白色“拆”字的蓝色涂鸦溢出字符周围的圆圈，宣告“保护！”（图2.07）。这些新兴行动主义形式也包括下岗工人争取更公正补偿的抗议。观察者将它们视为让增长机器的社会成本更可见的充满希望的潮流，但他们也承认，面对政府支持的发展，社区往往几乎没有资源可依靠。[^zh-ch02-66]


〔原书 106, 107〕

When artists explored new opportunities for display created by real estate developers, they ran up against limitations to represent in any politically effective way the inherent inequality of showcase Beijing. As Song Dong reflected, “We’re no saviors.” When city residents attempted to resist the imprint of urban development plans on their homes and communities, their protests had little efficacy due to the relative weakness of community power. In terms of China’s booming museum system, this situation translated into few display opportunities independent from progrowth coalition development. Chinese urban planners concerned with the way these coalitions victimize the very people they claim to represent resist the channeling of their labor according to growth machine logic. Their call for planners to recognize the political nature of their work and to “link aesthetic imagination with the public interest” is one that like-minded artists might also heed.[^en-ch02-67]

当艺术家探索房地产开发商所创造的新展示机会时，他们遭遇了限制：无法以任何政治有效的方式再现展示北京内在的不平等。正如宋东所反思的，“我们不是救世主。”当城市居民试图抵抗城市开发计划对其家园和社区的印记时，由于社区权力相对薄弱，他们的抗议收效甚微。就中国蓬勃发展的博物馆体系而言，这种情况意味着独立于亲增长联盟开发项目的展示机会寥寥无几。关心这些联盟如何伤害其声称代表的人们的中国城市规划者，抵制按照增长机器逻辑来引导他们的劳动。他们呼吁规划者认识自身工作的政治性质，“将审美想象与公共利益联系起来”——志同道合的艺术家或许也会听从这一呼吁。[^zh-ch02-67]


〔原书 107〕

How might artists attuned to site-specificity develop a paradigm of community collaboration, on a deeper level than hiring mingong, as part of their practice? Remembering the “failure” of the East Modern Art Center enables historical consciousness about the changing role of museums in China’s capital and how they implicate artists, influence their practice, and frame their artwork. Its history smashed and buried on many levels, what remains is a museum that is neither snow globe nor bell jar, but an archive of alternative possibilities. Scale models of Beijing seductively promise a dreamworld of leisure, culture, and cosmopolitan distinction. They train sight lines in powerful ways, organizing migrant and aesthetic labor alike in their realization. How they meet the ground, however, can also set into motion other arcs of the imagination. The afterimage of a brick hurtling through space shatters their smooth surface into pieces.

艺术家若要敏锐地对待场域特定性，如何在比雇用民工更深的层面上发展一种社区合作范式，作为其实践的一部分？记住远洋艺术中心的“失败”，可以形成关于博物馆在中国首都角色变化的历史意识，以及它们如何牵连艺术家、影响其实践并框定其作品。它的历史在许多层面上被砸碎、掩埋，所留下的是这样一座博物馆：既不是雪花玻璃球，也不是玻璃钟罩，而是一座另类可能性的档案。北京的比例模型诱惑地许诺一个由休闲、文化和世界性区隔构成的梦想世界。它们以强有力方式训练视线，在实现过程中同样组织着移民劳动与审美劳动。然而，它们如何落地，也可以启动想象力的其他弧线。一块砖头在空中飞驰的残影，将它们的平滑表面击碎成片。

## 第二部分　相遇地带


〔原书 109〕

PART II: Zones of Encounter

第二部分　相遇地带


## 第三章　围城


〔原书 111〕

Three: The Besieged City

第三章　围城


〔原书 111〕

From late 2000 to 2002, I lived in a socialist-era, five-story brick building in Xicheng District. I rented my one-bedroom apartment from a woman named Art Soldier, who worked in the state film bureau. She and her husband had moved into a new commodity apartment in a nearby high-rise development. Meanwhile many of her former neighbors, who remained in the older work-unit housing, launched a variety of *zhuangxiu* projects. Zhuangxiu means to fix up or redecorate and became a craze that besieged the city. The sounds of the neighborhood permeated my reprieve from Beijing’s streets: vendors’ calls from the vegetable market outside the enclosed balcony where I hung laundry to dry; wind banging screens and hissing its way around window frames; the grunts of sex on the other side of my bedroom wall; the lonely tune of someone whistling in the dim, concrete stairwell. But more than any other sound, I awoke to that of drilling, hammering, and sawing. Entrepreneurs on the nearby thoroughfare renovated their shops and restaurants. Some boasted bright lights, shiny glass and metal, and synthetic color schemes. Others cultivated a more pastoral aesthetic, such as the restaurants whose managers hired folk artists to paint landscape murals on their exteriors. The character *chai* (demolish) showed up in broad swaths, its white paint dripping down walls, like a command for the city to translate its old appearance into something new.

从2000年底到2002年，我住在西城区一栋社会主义时期的五层砖楼里。我从一个名叫文艺兵的女人那里租下一套一居室公寓，她在国家电影局工作。她和丈夫已经搬进附近一栋高层楼盘的新商品房。与此同时，她的许多仍住在老旧单位宿舍的前邻居纷纷启动各种装修工程。装修的意思是修理或重新装饰，它成为一种围困城市的狂热。社区的声音渗入我从北京街头回到的喘息空间：封闭阳台外菜市场的叫卖声——我在那里晾衣服；风拍打纱窗、绕着窗框呼啸的声音；卧室墙另一侧的性爱呻吟；昏暗混凝土楼梯间里某人孤独的口哨曲调。但最常把我唤醒的，是钻孔、锤击和锯木的声响。附近大道上的店主翻新店铺和餐馆。有些以明亮的灯光、闪亮的玻璃和金属以及合成色彩为傲。另一些则培养更田园的审美，例如有些餐馆经理雇民间艺人在外墙绘制山水壁画。“拆”（chai）字大片出现，白漆顺着墙壁滴下，仿佛是命令这座城市把旧貌改写成新颜。


〔原书 111, 112〕

Aspirational dramas unfolded on the television screen in my darkened apartment, where I retreated after long days of commuting around the city for classes, interviews, and meetings. Amid Hong Kong soap operas of the rich and famous, South Korean family sagas, and Mainland dynastic costume dramas, I caught episodes of *Wei Cheng* when the ten-part series reran on China Central tv. Based on a 1947 novel by Qian Zhongshu, the adaptation first aired in 1991, gaining wide viewership and popularity. The title of the novel, translated as *The Besieged City* or *Fortress Besieged*, entered 1990s Chinese lexicon along with words like “stock market,” “privacy,” and “mba.” It became a popular metaphor referring to marriage, feeling stuck, striving under false pretenses, and human dissatisfaction.[^en-ch03-1] Qian’s satirical novel, whose depiction of bourgeois life fell out of print under Mao, tells the story of urban middle-class Fang Hongjian. After frittering years away in Europe under the pretext of advanced study, he runs out of money, buys a fake doctoral diploma from the United States (the name of the granting institution transliterated into Chinese is Charlatan University), and returns to Shanghai in 1937 on the eve of World War II. Fang enters into one after another of failed relationships with women, who range from a fiancée in an arranged marriage to a female classmate who earned a Ph.D. in Europe before getting caught as a plagiarist. His continual longing for what he does not currently possess turns into an everyday tragicomedy of human isolation likened to the Chinese condition of Shanghai in the late 1930s, an extraterritorial city of surreptitious freedoms but one governed by foreign concessions and beset by the Japanese.

在我昏暗的公寓里，电视屏幕上上演着充满向往与追求的电视剧——那是我为上课、采访和会议在城市里奔波一整天后退守的地方。在香港富豪名流肥皂剧、韩国家庭史诗剧和内地古装剧之间，我赶上《围城》十集电视剧在中央电视台重播。该剧改编自钱锺书1947年的小说，1991年首播，获得广泛收视和欢迎。小说标题被译作 The Besieged City 或 Fortress Besieged，与“股市”“隐私”以及“MBA”等词一起进入1990年代的中国词汇。它成为一个流行隐喻，指涉婚姻、受困感、在虚假前提下奋斗以及人的不满足。[^zh-ch03-1] 钱锺书的讽刺小说在毛泽东时代因描写资产阶级生活而绝版，讲述城市中产阶级方鸿渐的故事。他以进修访学为名在欧洲虚度数年，花光钱后从美国买了一张假博士文凭（授予学位的机构中文译名为“克莱登大学”），于第二次世界大战前夕的1937年回到上海。方鸿渐接连卷入与女性的失败关系，从包办婚姻的未婚妻，到在欧洲获得博士学位、后来被抓出抄袭的女同学。他对当下所无之物的持续渴望，变成一部关于人际孤立的日常悲喜剧，被比作1930年代末上海的“中国处境”——一座享有隐秘自由的治外法权城市，却由外国租界统治，并受日本侵扰。


〔原书 112〕

The opening sequence of each television episode shows the original edition of Qian’s book, followed by translations published in the United States, Soviet Union, France, Germany, Japan, and Taiwan. A voiceover intones, “People surrounded inside the city want to flee out, people outside of the city want to rush in; in the face of marriage or occupation, such is human desire.” This series tagline alludes to the French proverb Qian used as epigraph to his novel: “Marriage is like a fortress besieged: those who are outside want to get in, and those who are inside want to get out.”[^en-ch03-2] Lost in this itinerary of translation is the uncanny way that Qian’s title in Chinese provides a metaphor that resonates into both past and future. A literal translation of *wei cheng* is “surrounded cities,” evoking images of the old walled imperial capital, the colonial city besieged by Western powers during the Opium Wars, the wartime city under Japanese control, the revolutionary city surrounded as in Mao’s injunction by the purifying countryside, and the new millennial city rife with construction attempting to overcome this siege of history by “linking tracks with the world.”[^en-ch03-3]

每一集电视剧的片头都展示钱锺书小说的原版，以及在美国、苏联、法国、德国、日本和台湾出版的译本。旁白吟诵：“城里的人想逃出去，城外的人想冲进来；面对婚姻或职业，人的欲望便是如此。”这句系列宣传语暗指钱锺书用作小说题记的法语谚语：“婚姻像一座被围困的城堡：城外的人想冲进去，城里的人想逃出来。”[^zh-ch03-2] 在这一翻译旅程中失落的，是钱锺书的中文标题所提供的那种诡异隐喻力量——它同时回响于过去与未来。“围城”的字面翻译是“被包围的城市”，令人想起旧日有城墙的帝国首都、鸦片战争中被西方列强围困的殖民城市、战时受日本控制的城市、被毛泽东所谓具有净化作用的乡村所包围的革命城市，以及新千年里到处是建设、试图通过“与世界接轨”来克服这一历史围困的城市。[^zh-ch03-3]


〔原书 112〕

Marriage enters the metaphorical conceit in relation to questions of fidelity and modernity. What should one believe in and remain loyal to: tradition, family, romance, revolution, socialism, capitalism, nation, or world? In the words of the docent in my neighborhood museum whose logic jumped from censorship to divorce to discrimination to immigration: you’d be a fool to believe someone would love you for your whole life. *Wei cheng* captures a sense of caution about the promise of any ideological arrangement.

婚姻进入这一隐喻构思，与忠诚和现代性的问题相关。人应当相信并忠于什么：传统、家庭、爱情、革命、社会主义、资本主义、民族，还是世界？用我家附近博物馆那位讲解员的话说——他的逻辑从审查跳到离婚，再到歧视，再到移民：你要是相信有人会爱你一辈子，那就是傻瓜。《围城》捕捉到对所有意识形态安排之承诺的警觉。


〔原书 113〕

As I was pulled into serving as a Chinese-English interpreter in several transnational encounters between Chinese artists and curators from abroad, the phrase *wei cheng* wound its way into our discussions. Artists invoked it to describe their relationship with the international art market. Precariously balanced against their desire to “get out” was that of returning and gaining respect at home. As translators of Chinese and Western aesthetics, they might serve as exemplars of cosmopolitanism or become susceptible to accusations of excessive fidelity to one or another artistic tradition.

当我在中国艺术家与海外策展人的若干跨国相遇中被拉去担任中英口译时，“围城”一词蜿蜒进入我们的讨论。艺术家用它描述自己与国际艺术市场的关系。与“走出去”的渴望如履薄冰地相平衡的，是回来并在国内获得尊重的渴望。作为中国与西方美学的翻译者，他们可能成为世界主义的典范，也可能轻易被指责对某一艺术传统过度忠诚。


〔原书 113〕

Serving as an interpreter put a new spin on the perennial if falsely dichotomous insider-outsider dilemma of ethnographers.[^en-ch03-4] Did I share greater insider status with curators from the United States or with Chinese artists I’d spent nominally more time with? What were the ethics of translation that became part of curatorial selection?[^en-ch03-5] Who might I betray in the exchange, given the disciplinary tension between art and anthropology, in which an anthropologist might be called on to interpret linguistic and cultural nuance but not artistic value? The more I became involved in these zones of cultural encounter, the more aware I grew of the transnational, *nannü* rules of the game and resulting exclusion of particular kinds of artists.[^en-ch03-6]

担任口译员，为民族志学者由来已久却虚假二分的内外困境增添了新的转折。[^zh-ch03-4] 我与美国策展人，还是与名义上相处更久的中国艺术家，共享更多“内部人”身份？构成策展选择的翻译伦理是什么？[^zh-ch03-5] 鉴于艺术与人类学之间的学科张力——人类学家可能被要求解释语言和文化细微之处，却不被要求判断艺术价值——我可能在交换中背叛谁？我越深入这些文化相遇地带，就越意识到跨国性的男女游戏规则，以及由此对特定类型艺术家的排斥。[^zh-ch03-6]


〔原书 113, 114〕

Participants in these encounters struggled with the constraints of a world organized according to a nation-state system. This framework structured the institutions they represented, as well as the ones they aspired to be accepted by, or the ones they had trained in. These institutions included museums, cultural organizations, international exhibitions, and art academies, as well as embassies that supported cultural exchange projects and issued or denied visas for artists to travel. The curators and artists I interpreted for readily apprehended and passionately debated the legacy of colonialism and racism within these institutions. They articulated visions of minority cosmopolitanism, even as they silently reiterated other powerful social distinctions in making art worthy of the world stage. Taking on the task of the translator presented a unique opportunity for ethnographic participant-observation but also implicated me in the behind-the-scenes of cultural production. Within the circles of male artists who dominated the Chinese contemporary art scene, I learned about the girlfriends, Chinese and foreign, who had served as translators and cultural brokers. One artist had gone through so many that others jokingly referred to him as Lianhe Guo, or United Nations. At one point, in my weariness with the sexual innuendo that was part of the scene, I fantasized about creating a performance piece in a photography studio where I would invite male artists to take wedding photographs with me. These mental theatrics provided an outlet for my own aggravation but more importantly revealed multidirectional anxieties produced by striving to be of the world: a wariness of being used, of being someone’s ticket in or out, of being judged inauthentic.

这些相遇的参与者挣扎于一个按民族国家体系组织的世界所施加的限制。这一框架结构了他们所代表的机构，也结构了他们渴望被其接纳的机构，或他们接受训练的机构。这些机构包括博物馆、文化组织、国际展览和艺术学院，也包括支持文化交流项目、为艺术家签发或拒发旅行签证的大使馆。我为其口译的策展人和艺术家轻易理解并激烈辩论这些机构内部的殖民主义与种族主义遗产。他们阐述少数者世界主义的愿景，却在让艺术配得上世界舞台的过程中，默默重申其他强大的社会区分。承担译者的任务，为民族志参与观察提供了独特机会，但也把我卷入文化生产的幕后。在主导中国当代艺术界的男性艺术家圈子里，我了解到那些充当翻译和文化中介的中外女友。一位艺术家的女友换得太频繁，其他人开玩笑称他为“联合国”。有时，我对场景中性暗示的厌倦达到顶点，便幻想创作一件行为作品：在一间摄影棚里，我会邀请男性艺术家与我拍摄婚纱照。这些脑内戏剧是我气愤情绪的出口，但更重要的是，它们揭示了努力“属于世界”所产生的多向焦虑：害怕被利用，害怕成为某人进入或离开的入场券，害怕被判断为不真实。


〔原书 114〕

Authorship and Originality

作者身份与原创性


〔原书 114〕

In the besieged city of zhuangxiu, efforts to make Beijing global and of foreign curators to find Chinese artists who would globalize their institutions, the artwork of Wang Yin highlights tensions in the debate about what counts as art. It translated styles like the folk murals outside restaurants near my apartment into global contemporary art. His experiments with authorship and originality also reflected post-Mao rearrangements of social relations and subjectivities around notions of labor, property, and community. In 2000, Wang Yin began working with a village artist from Henan Province. He hired the painter, who specialized in colorful motifs common in rural decorative murals, to work in his Tongzhou studio. The painter executed scenes from his craftsman’s repertoire on stretched canvas or black flannel. In *2000, No*. 7, his landscape combines mist-shrouded mountains, green valleys, lotus flowers, and modern high-rise buildings in the verdant distance. On top of this landscape, Wang Yin painted in broad, expressionist brushstrokes a large, grey-toned figure. His muscular mass reclines barefoot against the pine tree in the foreground, head jutting forward at an awkward angle. His body remains incompletely realized, with parts of the background, a spot of red and blotch of green, showing through a forearm and thigh. The painting presents an encounter of idioms from differently organized art worlds—decorative mural and modernist oil painting—each of which take away part of the other, in a pastiche recognized by the contemporary art market as the conceptual work of Wang Yin, not the anonymous painter who “prepared” his canvases.[^en-ch03-7]

在装修围城、北京走向全球的努力，以及外国策展人寻找能使其机构全球化的中国艺术家之际，王音的作品凸显了关于什么才算艺术的辩论中的紧张。他的作品把我公寓附近餐馆外墙的民间壁画之类风格转译成全球当代艺术。他对作者身份与原创性的实验，也反映了毛泽东之后围绕劳动、财产和社区观念对社会关系与主体性的重新安排。2000年，王音开始与一位来自河南的乡村画师合作。他雇这位擅长乡村装饰壁画中常见彩色图案的画师，在他的通州工作室工作。画师在绷好的画布或黑色法兰绒上绘制其工匠技艺中熟悉的场景。《2000年，第7号》中的山水融合了云雾缭绕的群山、翠绿山谷、荷花和远处苍翠中的现代高楼。在这幅山水之上，王音以宽大、表现主义的笔触画了一个巨大的灰色调人物。他肌肉发达的身躯赤脚斜倚在前景的松树上，头以别扭的角度向前探出。他的身体仍未完全成形，背景的一部分——一块红色和一块绿色——从一条前臂和大腿处透出。这幅画呈现了来自不同组织方式的艺术世界的语汇相遇——装饰壁画与现代主义油画——彼此都消减了对方的一部分，形成一种被当代艺术市场认定为王音观念作品的拼贴，而非那位为其“准备”画布的匿名画师的拼贴。[^zh-ch03-7]


〔原书 114, 115〕

The base layer of *Sandstorm* (plate 8) presents a brightly pigmented tableau of traditional Chinese imagery: rushing waterfalls, a junk sailing down a river, a pagoda in the distance, soaring cranes symbolizing longevity. Wang has then obliterated the scene with blunt, thickly applied repetitive strokes in muted shades of brown that cover the entire canvas. The painting’s title alludes to the massive sandstorm that enveloped Beijing in March 2002, the result of increasing desertification in China’s northwest, obliquely referencing fraught relations between city and country and the politics of reduced visibility. A reverse layering seems to occur in *Flower* (figure 3.01), as peonies blossom over an abstract color field, although small details of drips and washes over the flowers suggest multiple, successive overpaintings. For this piece, Wang asked his village counterpart to execute a design of flowers receding to the horizon, creating a sense of deep perspectival space. The peony flickers between folk symbol of wealth and minimalist motif in dialogue with modernist ideas of abstraction, replication, and alienation. The hierarchical separation of manual and mental, rural and urban labor becomes manifest in a painting largely in the hand of one painter but under the direction and bearing the name of another.

《沙尘暴》（图版8）的底层是一幅色彩明亮的中国传统意象图景：奔腾的瀑布、顺流而下的帆船、远处的宝塔、象征长寿的飞鹤。王音随后用钝拙、厚涂、重复的笔触，以柔和的棕色覆盖整幅画布，抹去这一场景。画名暗指2002年3月笼罩北京的大规模沙尘暴——中国西北日益严重的沙漠化的结果，迂回地指涉城乡之间紧张的关系和能见度降低的政治。《花》（图3.01）中似乎发生了反向分层：牡丹在抽象色域上绽放，尽管花朵上的滴痕和晕染等小细节暗示多次连续的覆盖绘制。为这件作品，王音请他的乡村合作者绘制一幅向地平线退去的花卉图案，营造出纵深透视空间感。牡丹在民间财富象征与极简主义母题之间闪烁，与现代主义的抽象、复制和异化观念对话。脑力劳动与体力劳动、城市劳动与乡村劳动的等级分离，在一幅主要由一位画师动手、却由另一位指导并署名的画作中显露出来。


〔原书 115〕

![图3.01　王音，《花》，2001年。布面油画，200厘米×300厘米。艺术家惠允。](web/assets/ch03-b011.jpg)

FIG 3.01 Wang Yin, *Flower*, 2001. Oil on canvas, 200 cm × 300 cm. Courtesy of the artist.

图3.01　王音，《花》，2001年。布面油画，200厘米×300厘米。艺术家惠允。


〔原书 115, 116〕

I first met Wang Yin while interpreting for a group of curators from the United States as they toured Beijing artists’ studios. As Wang discussed his work, he spoke consciously about disrupting the myth of the autonomous artist, undermining notions of originality, and even making obvious the social economy of art by hiring a painter to work for him. The reassertion of the autonomous artist over the anonymous folk painter in *his* meeting with the curators remained a silent subtext. Wang’s hand or conceptual input altered the paintings in a way that transformed them into globally recognized art, while the portability of works on canvas rather than walls enabled them to enter this system of exchange. In his 1942 “Talks at the Yan’an Conference on Literature and Art,” Mao Zedong exhorted the nation’s “cultural army” to stand with the people, to get to know them in order to represent China in its revolutionary struggle: “We must use what belongs to workers, peasants, and soldiers themselves, and therefore, the task of learning from workers, peasants, and soldiers comes before the task of educating them.”[^en-ch03-8] Wang reversed Mao’s call that artists go to the countryside to learn from the people, hiring the people instead to come to his studio. This mode of cultural production drew on and painted over a socialist understanding of art as communal effort.

我第一次遇见王音，是在为一群美国策展人参观北京艺术家工作室时担任口译。王音谈论自己的作品时，有意识地讲到打破自主艺术家的神话、削弱原创性观念，甚至通过雇用一个画师为其工作，让艺术的社会经济机制变得显而易见。然而在与策展人会面时，自主艺术家相对于匿名民间画师的优越地位被再次确立，仍是无声的潜台词。王音的手或观念投入改变了画作，使其转化为全球认可的艺术；而画布作品相对于墙面作品的可携带性，使它们得以进入这一交换体系。1942年，毛泽东在《在延安文艺座谈会上的讲话》中号召全国的“文化军队”与人民站在一起，了解人民，以便在革命斗争中表现中国：“我们必须用属于工人、农民和士兵自己的东西，因此，向工人、农民、士兵学习的任务先于教育他们的任务。”[^zh-ch03-8] 王音颠倒了毛泽东要艺术家下乡向人民学习的号召，改而雇用人民来到他的工作室。这种文化生产方式挪用并覆盖了把艺术理解为集体努力的社会主义观念。


〔原书 116〕

In her study of the translated modernity of early twentieth-century Chinese literature, Lydia Liu writes, “Strictly speaking, comparative scholarship that aims to cross cultures can do nothing but translate.... But leaving aside the marital trope of fidelity and the logocentric notion of truth—concepts that readily lend themselves to deconstructionist criticism—what else do we know or can we say about translation and its implications for cross-cultural understanding?”[^en-ch03-9] This chapter considers her question in relation to Chinese contemporary art as a dialogic construction. The work of Wang Yin and the hired folk painter provides a visual metaphor for the formal, linguistic, and cultural mediations that occur in artistic production and valuation. It demonstrates the making of art as a process that involves multiple social actors but also the superimpositions, alterations, and erasures that result from their exchange.

刘禾在关于二十世纪初中国文学翻译现代性的研究中写道：“严格说来，旨在跨越文化的比较研究除了翻译之外别无他法……但是，暂且抛开忠实的婚姻隐喻和逻各斯中心的真理观念——这些概念很容易成为解构主义批评的对象——关于翻译及其对跨文化理解的含义，我们还能知道什么、还能说什么呢？”[^zh-ch03-9] 本章把她的问题放在中国当代艺术作为一种对话性建构的语境中考察。王音与受雇民间画师的作品，为艺术生产和评价中发生的形式、语言与文化中介提供了一个视觉隐喻。它表明艺术制作是一个涉及多重社会行动者的过程，也涉及他们在交换中造成的叠印、修改和擦除。


〔原书 116, 117〕

In the encounters I interpreted for, the curators looked at the work shown to them and dialogically, through statement and question, tried to frame the images in terms of their developing exhibit ideas. The artists, in turn, provided personal, historical, and cultural context for their work. In this interplay of linguistic and pictorial, a precursor to the relationship of art and wall text in a museum exhibit, the curators and artists looked and talked and mutually interpreted the art at hand. They also depended on my Chinese-English interpretation, and my subjectivity entered the discussion, innocuously in moments of “good” translation and disruptively in moments of “bad” translation. In the most egregious case of the latter, I expressed (in English only) frustration with an artist’s use of sexualized female figures. My fatigue with the abundance of this type of imagery, exacerbated by recognition of very few female artists, wore through. The curators responded to my remark by pushing the artist to explain his use of this imagery. He gave short, elusive replies about sexual repression under Communism and desire unleashed in its aftermath. Later, one of the curators chastised me, saying that my tone of voice had caused the artist to shut down. When I later ran into the artist at exhibit openings, his antagonist stance made it clear that he too blamed me for interfering.

在我担任口译的相遇中，策展人观看展示给他们的作品，并通过陈述和提问进行对话，试图根据自己正在形成的展览思路框定图像。艺术家则反过来提供作品的个人、历史和文化背景。在这种语言与图像的相互作用中——它是博物馆展览中艺术与墙面文字关系的前身——策展人和艺术家观看、交谈，并相互阐释眼前的艺术。他们还依赖我的中英口译，而我的主体性进入了讨论：在“好”翻译的时刻无害，在“坏”翻译的时刻具有破坏性。后者的一个最恶劣案例，是我（只用英语）表达了对一位艺术家使用性化女性形象的不满。我对这类图像泛滥的厌倦，加之意识到得到认可的女性艺术家寥寥无几，终于按捺不住。策展人回应我的评论，逼艺术家解释他对这类图像的使用。他给出简短而含糊的回答，说这是共产主义下的性压抑及其后释放的欲望。后来，一位策展人斥责我，说我的语气让艺术家闭了嘴。后来我在展览开幕式上遇到这位艺术家时，他敌对的态度清楚表明，他也怪罪我干涉。


〔原书 117〕

Art in a Global Age

全球时代的艺术


〔原书 117〕

I was first drawn into the role of interpreter in April 2001, after asking an independent Chinese curator if I could follow along on the studio tours he often arranged for curators visiting from abroad. Frequently called on as a consultant on Chinese avant-garde art, Huang Du had recently served on advisory committees for biennials in the United States, Cuba, Argentina, and Italy.[^en-ch03-10] For him, this work represented an important sideline to his decade-long employment as an editor at *Meishu* (Fine arts), the official journal of the Chinese Association of Artists. In a juggling act of professional identities, Huang promoted to his international colleagues the kind of art that *Meishu* had denounced in a series of articles that year criticizing nudity in performance art and other “immoral” forms of art. He enthusiastically spoke the language of European cultural theory, often dropping words in English like *postmodern, simulacra, implosion*, and *intersubjectivity* into conversations in Chinese. Huang Du invited me to join him and Philippe Vergne, curator of visual arts for the Walker Art Center in Minneapolis, through long days of Beijing studio visits. Vergne, originally from France, was on his first visit to China. He had four days to do initial research for a 2003 exhibit to feature artwork from Brazil, China, India, Japan, South Africa, and Turkey, part of a global initiative launched by the Walker in 1998. Huang managed conversation in English quite well, but as the first day progressed, he encouraged me to take on the task of interpreting between Vergne and the artists. Huang continued to weigh in on both sides, in English and Chinese.

我第一次被拉入口译角色是在2001年4月，当时我请求一位中国独立策展人，让我跟随他经常为海外来访策展人安排的工作室参观。黄笃经常被聘为中国先锋艺术顾问，最近刚担任美国、古巴、阿根廷和意大利双年展的顾问委员会成员。[^zh-ch03-10] 对他而言，这份工作是他在《美术》——中国美术家协会官方刊物——任职编辑十年间的一项重要副业。黄笃在职业身份之间耍杂技，向国际同行推介的正是《美术》那年在一系列文章中谴责的艺术：那些文章批评行为艺术中的裸体和其他“不道德”艺术形式。他热情地说着欧洲文化理论的语言，常在中文交谈中夹带 postmodern、simulacra、implosion、intersubjectivity 等英文词。黄笃邀请我和明尼阿波利斯沃克艺术中心视觉艺术策展人菲利普·韦尔涅一起，度过漫长数日的北京工作室参观。韦尔涅原籍法国，首次访问中国。他有四天时间为2003年一个将展出巴西、中国、印度、日本、南非和土耳其艺术的展览做初步研究——这是沃克中心1998年发起的全球计划的一部分。黄笃的英语交流能力相当不错，但第一天进行下去，他鼓励我承担韦尔涅与艺术家之间的口译工作。黄笃继续用中英文在两边发表意见。


〔原书 117〕

Philippe Vergne introduced the future Walker show to the artists he met as one that would feature “non-Western” artists. In later catalogue texts, he and contributing colleagues refer to their organizing principle in terms of globality or globalization, citing theoretical influences ranging from Arjun Appadarai to Saskia Sassen, Homi Bhabha to Stuart Hall. Vergne balanced ideas developed by these scholars of modernity, urbanism, postcolonialism, and cultural studies with the concerns of the institution he represented in China and elsewhere in his research travels. The Walker Art Center, one of many foreign art institutions to send curators to China to learn more about its contemporary art scene, had a particular rationale for the exhibit that became *How Latitudes Become Forms: Art in a Global Age* (February–May 2003).

菲利普·韦尔涅向他遇到的艺术家介绍未来的沃克展览时，说它将展出“非西方”艺术家。在后来的图录文章中，他和参与撰稿的同事以全球性或全球化表述其组织原则，引用从阿尔君·阿帕杜莱、萨斯基娅·萨森到霍米·巴巴、斯图亚特·霍尔的理论影响。韦尔涅把这些现代性、城市主义、后殖民主义和文化研究学者的观念，与他所代表机构的关切相平衡——在中国以及其他研究旅行地也是如此。沃克艺术中心是众多派策展人来中国了解当代艺术现场的外国艺术机构之一，它对最终成为《纬度如何成为形式：全球时代的艺术》（2003年2月—5月）的展览有一套特定理由。


〔原书 118〕

Museum staff and consultants, involved in their own discussion of what it meant to be a global city, wanted to better represent the diversity of Minneapolis. Kathy Halbreich, director of the Walker Art Center, writes: “Minneapolis is one of the nation’s most rapidly changing cities and is now more culturally, ethnically, and economically diverse than ever before.... To be a more locally engaged institution, we need to become more sensitive to the increasingly inter-connected world reflected in the demographics of our own community.”[^en-ch03-11]

博物馆员工与顾问们参与各自关于何为全球城市的讨论，希望更好地呈现明尼阿波利斯的多样性。沃克艺术中心馆长凯西·哈尔布雷希写道：“明尼阿波利斯是全国变化最快的城市之一，如今在文化、族裔和经济上比以往任何时候都更加多元……要成为一个更深入本地参与的机构，我们需要对自身社区人口结构所反映的日益互联的世界更加敏感。”[^zh-ch03-11]


〔原书 118〕

Huang Du and the artists with whom we met could converse fluently about international contemporary art trends. Philippe Vergne spoke easily about their work in relation to particular schools, movements, and forms, but he also strove to understand historical, cultural details less familiar to him but relevant to the artwork he encountered. Early in his visit, he asked an artist about his use of the color red by noting possible associations of it with objects like Mao’s Little Red Book. The artist purposefully ignored the political implications of the question by giving a strictly formal answer. I also found myself rephrasing in English expressions of frustration by artists like Zhu Jia, who remained suspicious of being chosen for international exhibitions simply for their nationality. I tried to provide context, ranging from decades-old debates about urban planning in Beijing to the political history of cabbage distribution, in relation to the works of art we viewed. Over dinner one evening, I translated the shared desire of Huang and Vergne for global art as a stage for artistic exchange where it was no longer necessary to flag artists by their national identities.

黄笃和我们见到的艺术家都能流畅谈论国际当代艺术趋势。菲利普·韦尔涅也能轻松地把他们的作品与特定流派、运动和形式联系起来，但他同时努力理解那些他不太熟悉、却与所遇作品相关的历史与文化细节。访问之初，他问一位艺术家为什么使用红色，提到红色可能与毛泽东的《红宝书》等物有关。那位艺术家有意无视问题的政治含义，给出纯形式的回答。我也发现自己要用英语重述朱加等艺术家的不满——他们始终怀疑自己入选国际展览仅仅因为国籍。我试图提供背景，从数十年前关于北京城市规划的辩论，到白菜分配的政治史，与我们所看的作品联系起来。某天晚餐时，我翻译了黄笃和韦尔涅的共同愿望：让全球艺术成为艺术交流的舞台，在那里不再有必要以国族身份标示艺术家。


〔原书 118, 119〕

At this point, I broke into the conversation to argue for the importance of cultural specificity in the midst of this hopeful vision. I reminded them of the years of training in Chinese language, history, and culture that had come into play as I interpreted the ground that helped them place various artworks into curatorial discourses of globalization, appropriation, or modernity, to draw attention to the complex processes underlying this translation effort of fitting “original” intentions together with their complements. In the equation of Chinese X = English Y, the trick of the equal sign (the more forgettable, the job better done) makes the passage to formal synonymy seem smooth and transparent when it also contains histories of inequality. What, for example, the director of the Walker Art Center and the director of the World Art Museum at Beijing’s Millennium Monument might mean by reference to “global art/*shijie yishu*” emerges from specific, nonequivalent understandings about the role of art in the global system and its modern nation-state components. While there may be an “international language of art” that crosses national borders, those who speak it do so from different subject positions and fields of reference, some of which have more canonical power in the world than others.[^en-ch03-12]

此时，我插话为文化特殊性在这幅充满希望的愿景中的重要性辩护。我提醒他们，正是凭借多年在汉语、中国历史与文化方面的训练，我才能阐释相关背景，帮助他们把各种作品置入全球化、挪用或现代性的策展话语；我想让他们注意，这一把“原初”意图与其对应物拼合起来的翻译努力，底层过程何其复杂。在汉语 X = 英语 Y 的等式中，等号的把戏（越不引人注意，工作做得越好）使通向形式同义的道路显得平滑透明，而它同时包含不平等的诸历史。例如，沃克艺术中心馆长与北京中华世纪坛世界艺术馆馆长各自提到“全球艺术／世界艺术”（shijie yishu）时，其含义源自对艺术在全球体系及现代民族国家组成部分中之角色的特定而不对等的理解。尽管可能存在一种跨越国界的“国际艺术语言”，那些言说它的人却从不同的主体位置和参照场域出发，其中一些在世界上的权威性高于另一些。[^zh-ch03-12]


〔原书 119〕

The Language of Art/Yishu

“art／艺术”的语言


〔原书 119〕

In her analysis of literature, national culture, and translated modernity in semicolonial China, Lydia Liu challenges conventional understandings of translation with her concept of translingual practice. This practice, which she traces through neologisms introduced into Chinese from Japanese and European languages, accounts for the meaningful alterations that occur when words travel through time and cultural-linguistic space. As Liu explains, she “examines the process by which new words, new meanings, discourses, and modes of representation arise, circulate, and acquire legitimacy within the host language due to, or in spite of, the latter’s contact/collision with the guest language.”[^en-ch03-13] For example, the contemporary Chinese term for “art” ( *yishu*) is as a return graphic loan. The two pictographs for *yi* and *shu* once formed a classical Chinese-character compound that signified the broad range of skills—in social rites, music, archery, chariotry, literature, and mathematics—Confucian scholars were expected to master. The character compound was then borrowed by the Japanese to translate the modern European meaning of “art” and then reintroduced through Japan into modern Chinese.[^en-ch03-14] I translated “art” as yishu as if they were interchangeable, yet a long history of travel, profound anxiety about the future of Asia in the world, and Western and Japanese colonial incursions preceded my ability to do so. Related twentieth-century ideological building blocks include *wenhua*/culture (return graphic loan), *xiandai*/modern (Sino-Japanese-European loanword), and *bowuguan*/museum (neologism derived from missionary-Chinese texts).

刘禾在分析半殖民地中国的文学、民族文化与翻译现代性时，以“跨语际实践”概念挑战对翻译的常规理解。这一实践——她通过从日语和欧洲语言引入汉语的新词加以追踪——解释了词语穿越时间和文化语言空间时发生的有意义变化。如刘禾所解释，她“考察新词、新意义、话语和再现方式如何由于宿主语言与宾客语言的接触／碰撞，或尽管存在这种接触／碰撞，仍在宿主语言中产生、流通并获得合法性”。[^zh-ch03-13] 例如，当代汉语中的“艺术”一词是一个回流的书写借词。“艺”和“术”两个字曾构成一个古汉语复合词，指儒家学者应掌握的广泛技能——礼、乐、射、御、书、数。该复合词随后被日语借用，用以翻译欧洲现代意义上的“art”，再经由日本重新引入现代汉语。[^zh-ch03-14] 我把“art”译为“艺术”，仿佛二者可以互换，然而在这一能力形成之前，已经存在漫长的旅行史、对亚洲在世界中未来的深切焦虑，以及西方和日本的殖民入侵。相关的二十世纪意识形态基石还包括文化／culture（回流的书写借词）、现代／modern（汉日欧借词）和博物馆／museum（源自传教士中文文本的新造词）。


〔原书 119, 120〕

In the period of Liu’s analysis of Chinese literature, 1900–37, Chinese writers participated in a multitude of translingual practices because of the conditions of imperialism. In order to resist, they turned to words and ideas borrowed from the West, often via Japan as the major interpreter of Western modernity for China. They relentlessly translated European texts into Chinese, carving a largely one-way channel. Liu asks of this passionate, sometimes desperate engagement, “Is there a difference between colonization and self-colonization? If so, what does the difference tell us about the meaning of agency?”[^en-ch03-15] She also argues that while Chinese more often serves as host language to a Western guest (curators in the case at hand) than the other way around, it is nonetheless a host that does not simply receive, but changes the guest language through approximate translation and insertion into Chinese texts and contexts. A long history of cultural encounter has shaped this biculturality, linguistic copresence of East and West, or coauthorship performed through everyday language use.

在刘禾所分析的中国文学时期，即1900至1937年，中国作家因帝国主义处境而参与了大量跨语际实践。为了抵抗，他们转向从西方借来的词语和观念，且往往经由作为西方现代性主要阐释者的日本。他们不懈地把欧洲文本译成中文，开辟出一条基本单向的渠道。刘禾对这一热切、有时绝望的投入问道：“殖民与自我殖民之间是否存在差异？如果存在，这一差异告诉我们能动性的意义是什么？”[^zh-ch03-15] 她还论证，虽然中文更经常充当西方宾客的宿主语言（就本案例而言，宾客是策展人），而不是相反，但这个宿主并不只是接收，而是通过近似翻译和嵌入中文文本与语境来改变宾客语言。漫长的文化相遇史塑造了这种双文化性、东西方的语言共存，或通过日常语言使用完成的共同书写。


〔原书 120〕

Liu’s analysis of Goethe’s term *Weltliteratur* (world literature), coined in 1827 and taken up by early twentieth-century writers in China, presents the Chinese problematic in a way that remains insightful for discussions of “global art.” She cites a passage from Goethe in which the term first appears: “He who understands and studies the German language finds himself on the *market* where all nations offer their *merchandise*, he plays the interpreter in proportion as he *enriches* himself. And thus every translator should be considered a mediator striving to promote this universal spiritual *exchange* and taking it upon himself to make this generalized *trade* go forward. For whatever may be said of the inadequacy of translation, it remains one of the most essential and most worthy activities in the general traffic of the world (italics added by Liu).”[^en-ch03-16] In her discussion of the Chinese translation, *shijie wenxue* (world literature), Liu describes its burden of justifying China’s seat at the table of a modern international community: “As it happens, Chinese writers do not share the optimistic outlook that characterizes Goethe’s confidence about the German language and literature. Unlike the latter, who saw himself presiding over a *world market* wherein all nations offer their *merchandise* to him while he plays the translator magnanimously as he *enriches* himself, May Fourth writers turn to European literature largely with the intention of learning how to produce a national canon worthy of being accepted by world literature and being valued by the West.”[^en-ch03-17] As ethnographer-interpreter, I examine the complex intentionalities embodied in the objects that pass through art institutions and the translingual practices that frame them. To speak of *dangdai yishu*/contemporary art under the weight of proving China’s current place in the world is also to insist on cultural specificity alongside appeals for artistic universality.

刘禾对歌德1827年创造、后被二十世纪初中国作家采用的“Weltliteratur”（世界文学）一词的分析，以至今仍具洞察力的方式呈现了中国问题。她引用歌德首次使用该词的段落：“懂得并研究德语的人，身处所有民族陈列其商品的市场；他越使自己富有，就越扮演翻译者的角色。因此，每一位译者都应被视为一位中介者，努力促进这种普遍的精神交流，并承担推动这场普遍贸易前行的责任。因为无论人们如何谈论翻译的不足，它仍然是世界普遍交往中最根本、最值得从事的活动之一（斜体为刘禾所加）。”[^zh-ch03-16] 在讨论中文译词“世界文学”时，刘禾描述了它证明中国在现代国际社会席位的负担：“恰巧，中国作家并不共享歌德对德国语言和文学的乐观信心。歌德看到自己主持一个世界市场，所有民族向他陈列商品，而他慷慨地扮演译者、充实自身；与此不同，五四作家转向欧洲文学，很大程度上是想学习如何生产一种配得上被世界文学接受、被西方珍视的民族经典。”[^zh-ch03-17] 作为民族志学者兼口译员，我考察穿过艺术机构的物品所承载的复杂意图性，以及框定它们的跨语际实践。在证明中国当前世界地位的重负下谈论“当代艺术”，也意味着在呼吁艺术普遍性的同时坚持文化特殊性。


〔原书 120〕

Asia and Our Moment

亚洲与我们此刻


〔原书 120, 121〕

My second stint as interpreter occurred seven months later, when three curators from the Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (ybca) in San Francisco arrived in Beijing. They had shared notes and ideas with Philippe Vergne as part of their preparation and contacted Huang Du, who again served as a local guide. This time I actively prearranged my role in their visit, with everyone’s understanding that it would be part of my fieldwork. When the visiting curators asked me beforehand for input on artists who fell outside the usual circuit, I mentioned the privileging of a largely male avant-garde. At their request, I made arrangements for them to meet with several female artists. In Beijing, René de Guzman, Doryun Chong, and Eungie Joo began a multicity tour of the region that also included Chengdu, Tokyo, Osaka, and Taipei. This trip constituted first-stage research for an exhibition to feature emerging or mid-career Asian artists in China, Japan, Korea, and Taiwan. They later decided to include artists from Thailand as the exhibit took shape under the title *Time After Time: Asia and Our Moment* (2003). They conceptualized it as an Asian cities show connecting Asia to the location of the museum they represented, the Pacific Rim city of San Francisco with its history of Asian immigration.

我第二次担任口译是在七个月后，旧金山耶尔巴布埃纳艺术中心（YBCA）的三位策展人来到北京。他们与菲利普·韦尔涅交换了笔记和想法，作为准备工作的一部分，并联系了再次担任当地向导的黄笃。这一次，我主动预先安排了自己在访问中的角色，所有人都理解这将成为我田野工作的一部分。当来访策展人事先问我哪些艺术家处在通常圈子之外时，我提到先锋艺术在很大程度上偏重男性。应他们要求，我安排他们会见几位女性艺术家。在北京，勒内·德古兹曼、Doryun Chong 和 Eungie Joo 开始了一次多城市区域之行，还包括成都、东京、大阪和台北。此行是为一个展出中国、日本、韩国和台湾新兴或中生代亚洲艺术家作品的展览做第一阶段研究。随着展览以《一次又一次：亚洲与我们此刻》（2003）为题成形，他们后来决定加入泰国艺术家。他们把它构想为一个亚洲城市展，将亚洲与他们所代表博物馆所在地——太平洋沿岸的旧金山及其亚洲移民史——联系起来。


〔原书 121〕

As Visual Arts Curator of the ybca, René de Guzman had hired Doryun Chong and Eungie Joo as collaborating consultants on the project. He later mentioned that differentiating between their individual interests as curators would “add to the poignancy of what is invariably lost in translation,” noting that his curatorial concerns were largely defined by the goals of the ybca as an institution: “The project for me signifies an attempt at defining an international program that grows out of geo-centric motives.”[^en-ch03-18] With a doctoral degree in Ethnic Studies, Eungie Joo brought to the conversation a commitment to increasing the visibility of U.S. artists of color and challenging institutional rubrics that limit understanding of their work. Doryun Chong’s involvement in the exhibit planning emerged from his training as an art historian of contemporary art in East Asia.

作为YBCA视觉艺术策展人，勒内·德古兹曼聘请 Doryun Chong 和 Eungie Joo 担任项目合作顾问。他后来说，区分他们各自作为策展人的兴趣，会“加剧翻译中必然失落之物的辛酸”，并指出他的策展关切主要由YBCA作为机构的目标界定：“这个项目对我而言，象征着一次尝试：定义一个从地缘中心动机生长出来的国际项目。”[^zh-ch03-18] 拥有族裔研究博士学位的 Eungie Joo 为对话带来一种承诺：提高美国有色人种艺术家的可见度，并挑战限制人们理解其作品的机构准则。Doryun Chong 参与展览策划，源自他作为东亚当代艺术史学者的训练。


〔原书 121, 122〕

On their first night in Beijing, we met in their hotel bar, where de Guzman gave Huang Du and me some background to the ybca and its goals of serving a city that “has been the primary gateway for infusing Asian peoples into the fabric of America and this region.”[^en-ch03-19] As part of this introduction he mentioned that the San Francisco “South of Market” urban renewal project, where the larger Yerba Buena Center is located, had previously displaced several minority and immigrant communities. I later gained a fuller picture of this project, originally envisioned after World War II as a large-scale commercial convention-sports-office complex that would secure San Francisco’s international importance. Over the years, city business leaders, corporate councils, and elected officials pushed to have the “South of Market” area declared blighted, appropriated from its current residents, and bulldozed to make way for their redevelopment scheme. Decades of neighborhood and union protest, legal wrangling, and political conflict stalled this land-grab until the late 1970s when construction began.[^en-ch03-20] The displaced population included migratory workingmen, dockworkers, warehouse and factory workers, and immigrants—African Americans from the South, Germans, Irish, Greeks, Japanese, and Filipinos.[^en-ch03-21] At the beginning of the twenty-first century, the ybca as a public museum in the center of the redeveloped area was charged with a new mandate to culturally connect the city back to these previously displaced communities.

他们抵达北京的第一晚，我们在酒店酒吧见面，德古兹曼向黄笃和我介绍YBCA的背景及其目标——服务一座“一直是把亚洲各民族注入美国及本地区肌理的主要门户”的城市。[^zh-ch03-19] 作为介绍的一部分，他提到旧金山“市场街南”（South of Market）城市更新项目曾迁置若干少数族裔和移民社区，而更大的耶尔巴布埃纳中心就坐落于此。我后来更全面地了解该项目：它最初在二战后被构想为一个大型商业会议—体育—办公综合体，以确保旧金山的国际重要性。多年来，城市商界领袖、企业委员会和民选官员推动把“市场街南”地区宣布为破败区，从其现有居民手中征用，并用推土机夷平，为他们的再开发计划让路。数十年的社区与工会抗议、法律纠纷和政治冲突拖延了这场土地掠夺，直到1970年代末建设才开始。[^zh-ch03-20] 被迁置人口包括流动工人、码头工人、仓库和工厂工人，以及移民——来自南方的非裔美国人、德国人、爱尔兰人、希腊人、日本人和菲律宾人。[^zh-ch03-21] 二十一世纪初，作为再开发区域中心公共博物馆的YBCA，负有一项新使命：在文化上重新建立这座城市与这些先前被迁置社区的联系。


〔原书 122〕

The ybca curators, like Philippe Vergne, came to China informed by particular institutional motivations that arose, in their case, from San Francisco’s history of striving to become a global city. Its story of dispossession and then attempt at redress presents a picture of complicity between culture and commerce similar to that of “New Beijing.” The curators also informally discussed their personal links to Asia as an additional rationale for their involvement in the exhibition project. René de Guzman and Eungie Joo are second-generation Filipino and Korean Americans, respectively; and Doryun Chong left South Korea in his late teens to pursue higher education in the United States. They narrated abbreviated life histories of immigration and experience as ethnic Americans, as did I, emphasizing a difference in their art world position as Asian American interlocutors.

像菲利普·韦尔涅一样，YBCA策展人来到中国时，带着特定的机构动机——就他们而言，这些动机源自旧金山努力成为全球城市的历史。它剥夺然后试图补偿的故事，呈现出文化与商业共谋的图景，与“新北京”相似。策展人们还非正式地谈到自己与亚洲的个人联系，作为参与展览项目的额外理由。勒内·德古兹曼和 Eungie Joo 分别是第二代菲律宾裔和韩裔美国人；Doryun Chong 在青少年晚期离开韩国，赴美接受高等教育。他们讲述简略的移民和族裔美国人生活史，我也一样，强调他们作为亚裔美国对话者在艺术界位置上的差异。


〔原书 122〕

Are You Among Those Invited?

你在受邀者之列吗？


〔原书 122〕

This intersection of institutional and personal stakes informed the conversations that unfolded during the ybca curators’ visit to Beijing. Persistent themes in these conversations included the struggle for artistic recognition and representation, the role of the nation-state in these struggles, and ambivalence on the part of artists and curators about national identifications. On the one hand, artists may not see themselves and their work as aligned with national ideology. On the other hand, the notions of artist as soldier and artist as dissident are both structured by a modern system of nation-state governance, as are the art institutions that produce artists, curators, and exhibitions.

机构利益与个人利害的交汇，影响了YBCA策展人访问北京期间的对话。这些对话中反复出现的主题包括争取艺术承认与再现的斗争、民族国家在这些斗争中的角色，以及艺术家和策展人对国族认同的矛盾心理。一方面，艺术家可能不认为自己及作品与民族意识形态一致。另一方面，“艺术家作为战士”和“艺术家作为异见者”的观念，都由现代民族国家治理体系所结构，生产艺术家、策展人和展览的艺术机构也是如此。


〔原书 122, 123〕

On their first day of studio tours, Huang Du accommodated multiple demands on his schedule by bringing along another visiting curator. Ute Meta Bauer, a professor at the Institute for Contemporary Art at the Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Vienna, was in town through programming arrangements made by the Beijing branch of the German Goethe Institut. On the previous evening, many Chinese artists I knew had attended the lecture she gave at the institute about her role as cocurator in *Documenta 11*. The Documenta exhibitions, presented once every five years in Kassel, Germany, since 1955, serve as surveys of international contemporary art, each distinguished by the programmatic vision of the curator selected to direct the show. Okwui Enwezor, Nigerian by birth, headed *Documenta 11* as the first non-Western curator to hold the directorship, and in an unprecedented move, he selected six cocurators to help orchestrate an expanded exhibition concept, consisting of five platforms to take place between March 2001 and September 2002 in locations including Vienna, Berlin, New Delhi, St. Lucia, Lagos, and Kassel.[^en-ch03-22] From what I later heard about Bauer’s talk, many in the audience had pressed her for information about what the curatorial team sought in submissions and whether Chinese work would be represented. The Goethe Institut, whose mission is to promote German language and culture overseas, as the venue for this conversation provides a reminder of the ongoing history of culture and power.

在他们参观工作室的第一天，黄笃为了兼顾日程上的多项要求，还带上了另一位来访策展人。乌特·梅塔·鲍尔是维也纳美术学院当代艺术研究所教授，因德国歌德学院北京分院安排的项目而来到北京。前一天晚上，我认识的许多中国艺术家参加了她在学院所作的讲座，谈她作为第十一届卡塞尔文献展联合策展人的角色。文献展自1955年以来每五年在德国卡塞尔举办一次，是对国际当代艺术的概览，每届都因被选为总监的策展人的纲领性愿景而独具特色。出生于尼日利亚的奥奎·恩维佐担任第十一届文献展总监，是首位担任该职的非西方策展人；他以前所未有的举动选出六位联合策展人，协助编排一个扩展的展览概念，由五个平台组成，于2001年3月至2002年9月间在维也纳、柏林、新德里、圣卢西亚、拉各斯和卡塞尔等地举行。[^zh-ch03-22] 从后来听到的关于鲍尔讲座的情况看，许多听众追问策展团队在投稿中寻找什么，以及中国作品是否会被代表。歌德学院的使命是在海外推广德国语言和文化，而它作为这场对话的场所，提醒人们文化与权力的历史仍在继续。


〔原书 123, 124〕

Huang Du took us that morning to the apartment studio of Hong Hao, who four and half years earlier had perpetrated an elaborate art hoax as a challenge to the Euro-American centrism of international art and Chinese desire to be recognized by it. In May 1997, he and fellow artist Yan Lei sent out fake *Documenta 10* letters, typed in German on letterhead they had meticulously reproduced by silk-screen print, inviting artists across China to participate in a special show called *From the Other World—Chinese Avant-garde* (Aus der anderen Welt—chinesische Avantgarde). The letter, which was signed Ielnay Oahgnoh (the two artists’ names in pinyin spelled backwards), gave a local contact number to call for more information. When artists rushed to call it, they discovered it connected them to a public telephone booth. The anger of those fooled by the invitations reached such a level that Hong and Yan issued an apology letter in the *Jiangsu Pictorial* art journal. Their prank letter made obvious the host-guest power dynamics at work in the translation of Chinese contemporary art into the “world market” of art. The title of their fake exhibit plays on a Western framing of China as part of a distant, foreign world, not yet coeval with the one into which they send their art. The letter’s signature, a neologistic pun contrived of names spelled backwards, imitates the authorial aura of the foreign word, even if incomprehensible, within a Chinese context. In Hong Hao’s cramped apartment, Bauer handed him a business card. (Huang had briefed her before the meeting about Hong’s history as fake Documenta representative.) Grasping her card in both hands as a gesture of respect, Hong impishly stated that it would now be easier for him to duplicate the logo and start issuing his own Documenta business cards.

那天上午，黄笃带我们去了洪浩的公寓工作室。四年半前，洪浩策划了一场精心设计的艺术骗局，挑战国际艺术的欧美中心主义，以及中国渴望被其承认的心态。1997年5月，他和艺术家颜磊寄出伪造的第十届文献展邀请函，用他们精心丝网印刷复制的信笺纸以德文打字，邀请全中国艺术家参加一个名为《来自另一个世界——中国先锋艺术》（Aus der anderen Welt—chinesische Avantgarde）的特别展览。信末署名 Ielnay Oahgnoh（两位艺术家名字的拼音倒序拼写），并留下一个本地联系电话供咨询。艺术家们急忙打过去，发现那连接到一个公用电话亭。受骗者的愤怒达到如此程度，以致洪浩和颜磊在《江苏画刊》上发表道歉信。他们的恶作剧信件揭示了把中国当代艺术翻译进艺术“世界市场”时的主客权力动态。假展览的标题戏耍了西方把中国框定为遥远、陌生世界的一部分——尚未与他们送艺术进入的世界同时代。信件署名是以姓名倒拼构成的新造双关，模仿外文词在中国语境中的作者光晕，即便它不可理解。在洪浩局促的公寓里，鲍尔递给他一张名片。（黄笃此前已向鲍尔简要介绍过洪浩假冒文献展代表的经历。）洪浩双手接过名片以示尊重，却顽皮地说，现在他复制标志、开始印发自己的文献展名片会更容易。


〔原书 124〕

In the afternoon, the curators headed for the second-floor cafe of Beijing’s Sanlian Bookstore, where the editors of *Du shu* (Reading), a well-known journal of culture and politics, had organized a roundtable discussion with Ute Meta Bauer and local artists and art scholars.[^en-ch03-23] Daisy Yiyou Wang, a Chinese-born art historian who at the time was pursuing a PhD at Ohio University, served as the Chinese-English interpreter. Bauer began by giving a brief history of Documenta. After World War II, at a time when many German artists had emigrated or been killed, Arnold Bode, a painter and professor from Kassel, hoped to reestablish Germany’s place as a participant in world cultural discourse and international art developments. In 1955, he organized a retrospective of twentieth-century art and presented work that the Nazis had declared degenerate, including artists such as Picasso, Ernst, Arp, Matisse, Kandinsky, and Moore. This vision of cultural exchange on the global level focused, in the first ten exhibits, mainly on Europe and North America. The selection of Enwezor to direct the eleventh exhibition in 2001–2 placed high expectations on his ability to globalize the event.

下午，策展人们前往北京三联书店二层的咖啡馆，著名文化与政治杂志《读书》的编辑在那里组织了一场与乌特·梅塔·鲍尔及本地艺术家、艺术学者的圆桌讨论。[^zh-ch03-23] 出生于中国的艺术史学者王伊悠（Daisy Yiyou Wang）当时正在俄亥俄大学攻读博士，担任中英口译。鲍尔首先简要介绍文献展历史。二战后，许多德国艺术家或流亡或遇害，来自卡塞尔的画家、教授阿诺德·博德希望重新确立德国作为世界文化话语和国际艺术发展参与者的地位。1955年，他组织了一场二十世纪艺术回顾展，展出被纳粹宣布为“堕落”的作品，包括毕加索、恩斯特、阿尔普、马蒂斯、康定斯基和摩尔等艺术家。这种全球层面文化交流的愿景，在前十届展览中主要聚焦欧洲和北美。选择恩维佐执导2001至2002年的第十一届展览，使人们高度期待他能让这一活动全球化。


〔原书 124〕

The *Du shu* roundtable conversation gradually turned to the difficulty of organizing shows that claim to be global in reach, since an immediate impulse usually arises to demonstrate adequate representation from all “significant” geographic regions; and artists then begin to suspect curators of basing their selections more on where artists live than on their work. Bauer explained that she had frequently run into this dilemma, for example, at her talk the night before, when she fielded questions about whether or not *Documenta 11* would include Latin American or Asian artists. She responded that this identification by geographic lumping doesn’t seem important to most artists, who don’t want to act as national representatives. Philippe Vergne would express a similar sentiment several months later, in March 2002, during a roundtable organized for the opening of the Walker’s *How Latitudes Become Forms* exhibit:

《读书》圆桌讨论逐渐转向组织号称具有全球覆盖面的展览之困难，因为人们通常立刻想展示所有“重要”地理区域都有充分代表；艺术家随后便开始怀疑策展人的选择更多基于艺术家居住地，而非作品。鲍尔解释说，她经常遇到这一困境，例如前一天晚上的讲座中，有人问她第十一届文献展是否会包括拉丁美洲或亚洲艺术家。她回答说，这种按地理归类的身份认定对大多数艺术家似乎并不重要，他们不想充当国家代表。几个月后，2002年3月，菲利普·韦尔涅在为沃克中心《纬度如何成为形式》展览开幕组织的圆桌讨论中表达了类似感受：


〔原书 124, 125〕

What does it mean when you enter a studio in Johannesburg or in São Paulo or in Beijing and say, “I’m here because I’m doing a global show and you’re a global artist”?... Should we conceive of the show as a global show, or should we find a theme around globalization, or should we talk about something else? Is the show about art and practices? I also have the feeling when entering the studios that artists really want to be included in exhibitions about something else. They don’t want to be in a global show.[^en-ch03-24]

当你走进约翰内斯堡、圣保罗或北京的一间工作室，说：“我来这里是因为我在做一个全球展，而你是一位全球艺术家”，这意味着什么？……我们应该把展览设想为一个全球展，还是围绕全球化寻找一个主题，还是谈论点别的？展览是关于艺术与实践的吗？我走进工作室时也有这种感觉：艺术家真正想被纳入的是关于别的东西的展览。他们不想参加一个全球展。[^zh-ch03-24]


〔原书 125〕

Bauer continued by saying she sometimes wished, as a curator, that artists would say no more often if they felt a national or any other ideological framework being imposed on them.

鲍尔接着说，作为策展人，她有时希望，如果艺术家感到民族或其他意识形态框架被强加于己，他们能更经常地说“不”。


〔原书 125〕

Eungie Joo then broke into the discussion to say that for artists marginalized by art world politics, where the odds are already stacked against them, it’s hard to say no. They don’t know when they might get another chance and feel compelled to take whatever they get, even if it’s not ideal.[^en-ch03-25] She also brought up another potential danger for the global ambitions of the Enwezor-directed *Documenta 11* by comparing its possible long-term impact to the backlash that occurred after the 1993 Whitney Biennial in New York, labeled by critics as the “politically correct” biennial. Curator Elisabeth Sussman selected artwork that she felt would reach groups not usually drawn to the museum and that reflected debates about multiculturalism, particularly its critiques of mainstream representation and institutional framing. An unprecedented number of artists of color as well as female and gay and lesbian artists exhibited work. Pieces included in the show took on political issues, ranging from the aids crisis to police violence against Rodney King. Attacks against the show, calling it didactic moralizing, lacking in aesthetic and formal value, and even “worthless junk,” came from within and without the art establishment, including a broadside by *60 Minutes*.[^en-ch03-26] Joo characterized this biennial as an antidote used to counteract previous institutional denial on the part of the Whitney, but in a tokenistic way that enabled critics to characterize “minority art” as “bad art.” Once it was all said and done, guilt had been expunged; a commitment to racial or gender justice could be checked off and forgotten; and artists marginalized by the U.S. art mainstream stood in no better position than before. Bauer replied that opportunities to get a foot in the door and gain symbolic capital must be embraced as one way of trying to wedge to door open wider.

Eungie Joo 随后插话：对于被艺术界政治边缘化的艺术家而言，胜算本就对他们不利，说“不”很难。他们不知道下一次机会何时到来，感到只能接受所能得到的一切，即便并不理想。[^zh-ch03-25] 她还提出恩维佐执导的第十一届文献展全球抱负面临的另一个潜在危险：她将其可能的长期影响，与1993年纽约惠特尼双年展后发生的反弹相比较——批评者当时把该展称为“政治上正确”的双年展。策展人伊丽莎白·萨斯曼选出的作品，是她认为能触及通常不被吸引到博物馆的群体、并反映多元文化主义辩论——尤其是对主流再现和机构框定的批评——的作品。参展的有色人种艺术家以及女性、男同性恋和女同性恋艺术家人数前所未有。展品处理从艾滋病危机到警察对罗德尼·金的暴力等政治议题。对展览的攻击——称其说教、缺乏审美和形式价值，甚至“毫无价值的垃圾”——来自艺术界内外，包括《60分钟》的猛烈抨击。[^zh-ch03-26] Joo 把这场双年展描述为一剂解药，用来抵消惠特尼此前的机构性否认，却以一种象征性点缀的方式，使批评者得以把“少数族裔艺术”定性为“坏艺术”。一切尘埃落定后，负罪感被消除；对种族或性别正义的承诺可以打勾然后遗忘；被美国艺术主流边缘化的艺术家处境并不比从前更好。鲍尔回答说，必须抓住踏进门、获得象征资本的机会，作为把门撬得更宽的一种方式。


〔原书 125, 126〕

I drew in my notes a schematic of the three discourses that came into conflict in the conversation that afternoon (figure 3.02). While interrelated, these discourses also bear the traces of their historical formation, and tensions remain among them. The Documenta position arises from a German historical moment of skepticism with regard to national politics but a simultaneous desire for Germany to regain a position of world prominence by serving as a Weltliteraturlike platform for cross-cultural exchange between nations. The position articulated by Joo through her example of the 1993 Whitney Biennial presents a kind of diversity nationalism, in which marginalized artists in the United States seek to expand the definition of American cultural citizenship, and thereby make visible the imperialist links between the United States and other parts of the world. The significance of China’s positioning below Europe and the United States hinges on Chinese artists’ ready acknowledgement that no exhibits in China garnered the international attention that Documenta and the Whitney Biennial did. Their desire to emerge on the global stage as a culture capable of commanding the world’s attention represented a conflicted nationalism, of which they were sometimes deeply critical, but that was sustained nonetheless by an art system structured by national institutions.

我在笔记上画了那天下午对话中相互冲突的三种话语的示意图（图3.02）。这三种话语虽然相互关联，却也带有各自历史形成的痕迹，彼此之间的紧张持续存在。文献展立场源于德国的一个历史时刻：对国家政治持怀疑态度，同时渴望德国通过充当类似世界文学的国与国跨文化交流平台，重新获得世界显要地位。Joo 通过1993年惠特尼双年展所表述的立场，呈现一种多元性民族主义：美国被边缘化的艺术家寻求扩展美国文化公民身份的定义，从而使美国与世界其他地区之间的帝国主义联系变得可见。在图中把中国置于欧洲和美国下方的意义，取决于中国艺术家乐于承认：中国没有哪个展览能获得文献展和惠特尼双年展那样的国际关注。他们渴望作为能够赢得世界注意的文化出现在全球舞台，这代表一种矛盾的民族主义——他们有时深刻批判它，但这种民族主义仍由一个以国家机构为结构的艺术体系所维系。


〔原书 126〕

![图3.02　相互冲突的国际/国内文化话语。](web/assets/ch03-b040.png)

FIG 3.02 *Conflicting inter/national discourses of culture*.

图3.02　相互冲突的国际/国内文化话语。


〔原书 126〕

Germany United States Global Cultural Exchange Diversity Politics China Bid for World Recognition

图内文字：德国；美国；全球文化交流；多元性政治；中国；争取世界承认。


〔原书 126, 127〕

Yan Lei, Hong Hao’s collaborator in the *Documenta 10* letter hoax, created that same year a piece titled *Are You Among Those Invited to the German Exhibition*? (plate 9). This painting features a Chinese fencer ready to begin a match: one hand poised to pull down a face mask, the other brandishing a sword. An arc of red flags cuts a dramatic diagonal against the blue sky behind her. The symbol repeated on the flag, a lower case “d” with an “x” superimposed over it, is the logo for *Documenta 10*. At the top, Yan painted the title question in Chinese characters and pinyin, in a style reminiscent of socialist propaganda posters. He conflates the competition of Chinese artists for invitations to international art exhibits with the desire to compete for one’s country in the Olympic Games. His choice of a female fencer to represent the nation also references the “iron girl” attitude of socialist gender formations, a striking contrast with the overwhelmingly male representation in Chinese contemporary art worlds and a reminder of the gender politics also at play in determining who is among those invited.[^en-ch03-27] Although the ybca curators had requested that I make arrangements for them to meet with several female artists in Beijing, Huang Du disagreed with my recommendations and convinced them not to waste their time on these meetings. After the first one, the ybca curators collectively agreed and asked me to cancel the rest. In his research on professionalization of the arts in post-Mao China, Richard Kraus observes that this process did not as a matter of course lead to liberalization or greater equality. Rather the building of shared structures created exclusionary practices. He cites as example the statistics for Writers Association membership, which show a sharp decline between 1981 and 1988 in the number of women and ethnic minority members, with the male-to-female ratio increasing by a factor of almost seven.[^en-ch03-28]

颜磊——洪浩在文献展邀请函骗局中的合作者——同年创作了《你在被邀请参加德国展览的人当中吗？》（图版9）。这幅画描绘一名准备开始比赛的中国击剑手：一只手准备拉下面罩，另一只手挥舞长剑。一道红旗弧线在蔚蓝天空背景下划出戏剧性对角线。旗帜上重复的符号——一个上面叠加“x”的小写“d”——是第十届文献展的标志。颜磊在画面上方用汉字和拼音写出标题中的问题，风格令人想起社会主义宣传画。他把中国艺术家争取国际艺术展邀请的竞争，与代表国家参加奥运会的渴望混为一谈。他选择女击剑手代表国家，也指涉社会主义性别塑造中的“铁姑娘”姿态，这与中国当代艺术界压倒性的男性代表形成鲜明对比，也提醒人们注意决定谁在受邀者之列的性别政治。[^zh-ch03-27] 尽管YBCA策展人曾要求我安排他们见几位北京的女性艺术家，黄笃却不赞同我的推荐，并说服他们不要把时间浪费在这些会面上。第一次会面之后，YBCA策展人一致同意，让我取消其余安排。理查德·克劳斯在研究毛泽东之后中国的艺术专业化时观察到，这一过程并未自然带来自由化或更大平等。相反，共同结构的建设制造了排他性实践。他举作家协会会员统计为例：1981至1988年间，女性和少数民族会员人数急剧下降，男女比例几乎增至原来的七倍。[^zh-ch03-28]


〔原书 127〕

Saying No

说不


〔原书 127〕

On November 30, 2001, the ybca curators’ second full day of meeting artists, we drove east of the city center toward the mixed rural-urban Tongzhou District. After three studio visits in the morning, we stopped for lunch at a new two-story restaurant on the side of a dusty road. Around our table sat the three ybca curators, Huang Du, Wang Yin, two other artists from the morning’s agenda, the driver of our car, and myself. I sat stuffing steamed dumplings into my mouth, enjoying a reprieve from my role as interpreter. The beginnings of a lively debate about exactly what I momentarily hoped to escape grumbled in our smoke-filled banquet room. In discussing the unequal parameters of the international art world, in which Chinese artists gained success by inclusion in exhibits in the West but not the other way around, the Chinese artists launched into a complaint about the dominance of English. They described how they often feel misinterpreted or misunderstood when participating in international exhibits but cannot express themselves well enough in English to enter into meaningful conversation.

2001年11月30日，YBCA策展人用一整天会见艺术家的第二天，我们驱车前往市中心以东城乡交错的通州区。上午走访三个工作室后，我们在一条尘土飞扬的路边一座新开的两层餐馆停下吃午饭。桌边坐着三位YBCA策展人、黄笃、王音、上午日程中的另外两位艺术家、我们的司机和我。我坐着把蒸饺塞进嘴里，享受摆脱口译角色的一刻。一场关于我此刻希望逃离之事的激烈辩论的苗头，在烟雾缭绕的包间里低声酝酿。中国艺术家在讨论国际艺术界不平等的参数——中国艺术家靠参加西方展览取得成功，反过来却不行——时，开始抱怨英语的支配地位。他们描述自己参加国际展览时常常感到被误读或误解，却无法用英语充分表达，以进行有意义的对话。


〔原书 127, 128〕

Eungie Joo agreed that a formidable communication gap presents itself at such events and that they as artists have to make certain demands. Drawing on the conversation with Ute Meta Bauer the day before, she said she understood not having the luxury to “say no,” even if the opportunity taken under these conditions might entail inevitable miscommunication, but that they should demand professional interpreters as part of a contractual agreement to participate. She emphasized that contemporary art requires more explanation and contextualization than other forms of art, making adequate translation more imperative than ever. Her foregrounding of a demand to be recognized—to have a voice—is rooted in the U.S. diversity politics strategy of claiming collective injustice in order to lobby for equal representation in the nation and its institutions. But the Chinese artists at the table wanted not just to be included more equally in a U.S. museum but to have the power to produce and interpret contemporary art on their own home ground. For them, more translation does not necessarily change the rules of the game, if the “general traffic of the world” is still directed toward the West.

Eungie Joo 同意这种场合存在巨大的沟通鸿沟，艺术家必须提出某些要求。她借用前一天与乌特·梅塔·鲍尔的对话说，她理解没有“说不”的奢侈，即便在这种情况下抓住的机会可能带来不可避免的误传，但他们应当要求在参展合同中配备专业口译员。她强调，当代艺术需要比其它艺术形式更多的解释和语境化，因此充分的翻译比以往更加迫切。她突出“被承认”的要求——拥有声音——根源在于美国多元性政治的策略：申明群体遭受的不公，以争取在国家及其机构中获得平等代表。但桌边的中国艺术家不仅想更平等地被纳入一家美国博物馆，还想在自己的土地上拥有生产和阐释当代艺术的权力。对他们而言，如果“世界普遍交往”仍以西方为方向，更多翻译未必改变游戏规则。


〔原书 128〕

Joo’s use of the phrase “say no” signified having the power to refuse others’ framings, an idea that arose repeatedly in the ybca curators’ conversations. At our lunch table, I translated “say no” in the most literal word-to-word fashion of *shuo bu* rather than the more “native” term *jujue*, meaning “to refuse.” Through this choice, I made tongue-in-cheek reference to an anti-U.S. bestseller called *China Can Say No*.[^en-ch03-29] While I did not have time to explain the linguistic genealogy of these two syllables to the curators, the artists at the table recognized it with a knowing laugh. Many Chinese intellectuals critiqued this book as inflammatory nationalist rhetoric, but its mid-1990s popularity represented ambivalence about increased economic and cultural ties between China and the West. The book’s cover depicts the Great Wall guarded by a composite figure with the head of the Statue of Liberty affixed to the body of a military police officer. At the top, the copy reads, “China says no, not to seek confrontation, but for a more equal dialogue.” This book introduced the translated phrase *shuo bu* into everyday Chinese lexicon.

Joo 使用“说不”一语，意味着拥有拒绝他人框定的权力，这一观念在YBCA策展人的交谈中反复出现。在我们的午餐桌上，我用最字面的逐词方式把“say no”译成“说不”，而不是更“地道”的“拒绝”。通过这一选择，我半开玩笑地指涉一本反美畅销书《中国可以说不》。[^zh-ch03-29] 我虽没有时间向策展人解释这两个音节的语言谱系，桌边的艺术家却会心一笑，认出了它。许多中国知识分子批评这本书是煽动性的民族主义修辞，但它在1990年代中期的流行，代表了对中国与西方经济文化联系日益紧密的矛盾心理。书的封面描绘长城，守卫它的是一个合成形象：自由女神像的头颅接在军警的身体上。上方文案写道：“中国说不，不是为了寻求对抗，而是为了更平等的对话。”这本书把译词“说不”引入日常汉语词汇。


〔原书 128, 129〕

It followed a trend of books in Asia about “saying no,” beginning with *The Japan That Can Say No* in 1989. The high sales of this book in Japan received so much attention in the U.S. Congress, where some used it as justification for trade sanctions against Japan, that it was translated into English.[^en-ch03-30] The phrase “say no” in Japanese is adopted from English, with the “no” untranslated.
