1 Chinese women artists wish to replace the concept of “Womanhouse” with the title “Dialogue with Lugu Lake” or “Dialogue with Judy Chicago at Lugu Lake.”

2 All participants in the entire Lugu Lake art activity assert the moral and legal rights to works in their own names.

3 Each artist/participant will maintain the copyright to her own work.

4 The artists wish to have a clearly defined written agreement. The contents of the agreement will be agreed on by both sides, with signatures constituting a binding contract.

1　中国女性艺术家希望以“与泸沽湖对话”或“在泸沽湖与朱迪·芝加哥对话”的标题，取代“女人屋”概念。

2　整个泸沽湖艺术活动的所有参与者主张以其本人名义享有作品的道德与法律权利。

3　每位艺术家／参与者保留自己作品的著作权。

4　艺术家希望有一份明确界定的书面协议。协议内容由双方商定，签字构成有约束力的合同。


〔原书 153〕

Although some of the artists chose to abstain, a majority signed this terse and circumspect document, couched in the language of international copyright law and individual possession. This instance of “saying no” took place less than one year after China’s official entry to the wto, at a time when Western critics bashed China as a pirate nation whose acts of copying marked them as culturally inferior.

虽然一些艺术家选择弃权，多数人签署了这份简短而谨慎的文件；它用国际著作权法与个人占有的语言写成。这一“说不”事件发生在中国正式加入世贸组织不到一年后——当时西方批评者抨击中国是盗版国家，其仿制行为表明文化低劣。


〔原书 153〕

When the artists arrived that rainy morning at Chicago’s guesthouse, Lu Jie announced that she lay sick in bed on the second floor and would not be able to meet with them, so they presented their signed list of demands to Lu Jie. Several artists added to the critique what they saw as the hierarchical presentation of the “proposals exhibit,” hung earlier that morning under the direction of Lu and Qiu. Chicago’s *What If Women Ruled the World* prayer flags flew from the guesthouse entranceway, whereas the Chinese artists’ proposals were displayed on the walls of the courtyard inside. Lu took their manifesto and comments upstairs to Chicago’s room. As they waited, Lei Yan mused, “Even though we are in the Lugu Lake area, we have no discursive power.” Sun Guojuan responded, “Right, we were inserted into someone else’s work. Moreover, before that, we didn’t even discuss this, I mean, nobody told us there would be a Womanhouse, we didn’t know until yesterday. That’s to say, when we enter into Womanhouse, it’s someone else’s, we become someone else’s work.”

当艺术家们在那个雨晨抵达芝加哥的客栈时，卢杰宣布她病倒在二楼床上，无法会见他们，于是他们向卢杰呈交签名的要求清单。几位艺术家还在批评中补充了她们眼中“方案展”的等级化展示——当天早晨早些时候在卢杰和邱志杰指导下挂起。芝加哥的《如果女人统治世界》经幡从客栈入口飘扬，而中国艺术家的方案则展示在院内院墙上。卢杰把他们的宣言和意见带上楼，走进芝加哥的房间。等待时，雷燕沉思道：“即使我们身在泸沽湖地区，我们也没有话语权。”孙国娟回应：“对，我们被插入别人的作品。而且在此之前，我们甚至没有讨论过这件事，我是说，没人告诉我们会有个‘女人屋’，我们直到昨天才知道。也就是说，当我们进入‘女人屋’时，它已经是别人的了，我们成了别人的作品。”


〔原书 153, 154〕

Lu Jie returned to report that although upset, Chicago had agreed to all four of their points. Rather than taking her concession as a victory, they continued to debate the differences that had brought them to a head. Anger mixed with remorse, exhaustion, and cigarette smoke. Lu lectured the artists about his responsibilities as a curator to their foreign guest and thanked them in a strained tone for their efforts. A primary complaint to emerge from the artists’ side was that they hadn’t had enough time with Chicago to communicate their ideas, let alone come to a consensus about an overall plan. Lu again went upstairs to update Chicago, and this time she emerged and was helped downstairs, to uncertain applause from her audience. She sat with the artists and through Horikawa tearfully described how hurt she felt by their criticism: “I wanted to try to offer my strength to serve their art. And it hurts me that they seem to have taken that in the wrong spirit.... I came here to make art. I don’t want to talk forever. We don’t have that much time. I came to make art.”[^en-ch04-36] While she interpreted their manifesto as hurtful criticism impeding their ability to make art, the manifesto itself could also be understood as a work of situational art, already months in the conceptualization, the final form of which emerged from hours of intense discussion at Lugu Lake.

卢杰回来报告说，芝加哥虽感不快，但同意了他们的全部四点要求。然而，他们没有把她的让步当作胜利，而是继续辩论那些导致双方冲突激化的分歧。愤怒混合着悔意、疲惫和香烟烟雾。卢杰向艺术家们讲述自己作为策展人对远方客人的责任，并用勉强的语气感谢他们的努力。艺术家一方提出的主要抱怨是，他们没有足够时间与芝加哥交流想法，更不用说就总体方案达成共识。卢杰再次上楼向芝加哥更新情况；这一次，她出来了，被人扶下楼，迎来听众不确定的掌声。她与艺术家们坐在一起，通过 Horikawa 含泪描述他们的批评让她多么受伤：“我想试着贡献自己的力量来服务她们的艺术。而她们似乎误解了我的这番心意，这让我很伤心……我来这里是为了创作艺术。我不想永远谈下去。我们没有那么多时间。我是来创作艺术的。”[^zh-ch04-36] 她把他们的宣言理解为伤人的批评，认为这妨碍了大家进行艺术创作；而宣言本身也可以被理解为一件情境艺术作品——它已经构思数月，最终形式则从泸沽湖数小时激烈讨论中产生。


〔原书 154〕

Over the next two days, several artists displayed photographs, paintings, and installations at Chicago’s inn. Due to its remove from nearby village and tourist activity, the audience for these pieces consisted of artists, camera crews, and guesthouse employees. Other artists who required local participation or different environmental settings staged their pieces in the village or on its southern lakeshore. They attracted slightly more varied audiences. Judy Chicago continued, as planned, to do a critique of each Chinese artist’s work. These conversations, although asymmetrical in their presumption of a student-teacher relationship, involved at least a focused, two-way discussion of individual pieces.

接下来两天，几位艺术家在芝加哥的客栈展示照片、绘画和装置。由于客栈远离村庄和旅游活动，这些作品的观众由艺术家、摄制组和客栈员工组成。其他需要本地参与或不同环境背景的艺术家，在村里或南岸湖畔展演作品，吸引了略微多样的观众。朱迪·芝加哥按计划继续逐一点评每位中国艺术家的作品。这些对话虽然预设师生关系而不对称，至少涉及对单件作品专注的双向讨论。


〔原书 154〕

The Politics of Site Specificity

场域特定性的政治


〔原书 154, 155〕

The artworks exhibited as a result of these collective activities explored the limits of site-specific art practice, while fissures between what the site meant to various participants challenged monolithic understandings of what is feminist or what is Chinese. For Judy Chicago, Lugu Lake represented, in part, the internationalization of *Womanhouse*, a feminist instance of site-specific art fundamental to her own history as an artist. The dilapidated mansion that she, Miriam Shapiro, and their Feminist Art Program students chose for *Womanhouse* provided a physical space for exploring gendered norms in terms of domesticity. The difference between a bourgeois urban home and a rural guesthouse built as tourist lodging seemed lost in translation. For the Chinese artists who refused to “be inserted into someone else’s work,” the site specificity of this 1970s U.S. feminist project, and its white, middle-class preoccupations did not translate to Lugu Lake or their own experiences in a socialist society that since the 1950s had actively mobilized women as part of the public labor force. The extent of this gap became apparent in the multiplicity of their responses to the siting of *The Long March* at Lugu Lake.

这些集体活动展出的作品探索了场域特定艺术实践的限度，而地点对不同参与者的意义之间的裂隙，也挑战了对何谓女性主义、何谓中国的单一理解。对朱迪·芝加哥而言，泸沽湖部分意味着《女人屋》的国际化——一个场域特定艺术的女性主义实例，对她自己的艺术家历史至关重要。她、米里亚姆·夏皮罗和女性主义艺术项目的学生为《女人屋》选择的破败豪宅，提供了一个物理空间，用以探索家庭性方面的性别规范。资产阶级城市住宅与作为旅游住宿建造的乡村客栈之间的差异，似乎在翻译中丢失了。对于那些拒绝“被插入别人的作品”的中国艺术家而言，这一1970年代美国女性主义项目的场域特定性及其白人、中产阶级关切，无法翻译到泸沽湖，也无法翻译到她们自己在1950年代以来积极动员女性参与公共劳动力的社会主义社会中的经验。这一鸿沟的程度，在她们对《长征》落户泸沽湖的多样回应中变得明显。


〔原书 155〕

Site specificity as a form of anti-institutional art praxis located outside of the museum/gallery system has developed since the late 1960s in different directions. Key paradigms have explored a site’s physical, materialist characteristics; the ideological network of social spaces and economies that structure it; and the public concerns, such as community identity and politics, that extend it beyond an art context.[^en-ch04-37] These experiments broke down borders governing artistic production and reception, even as museums and galleries simultaneously attempted to embrace site-specific art. Lu Jie’s *The Long March* is positioned precisely at the crux of this conundrum. His orchestration of artistic explorations of various sites along the historical Long March route moved art out of metropolitan museum and gallery spaces, but was also meant to attract international institutional attention, which it did. Documentary photographs and video, exhibited alongside Lu’s curatorial précis, were included in *Art and China’s Revolution* (2008–9) at the Asia Society in New York. While the *The Long March* in New York presents an opportunity for resiting Chinese revolutionary art and politics as important world historical events, it also smooths over the complexity of how artists engaged the original site of creation. Their pieces respond to the physical terrain of Lugu Lake, imaginaries of alternative Mosuo sociality, the growing influence of tourism on ethnic minority groups, Chinese socialist image making practices, and even the institutional power of Judy Chicago.

场域特定性作为一种位于博物馆／画廊系统之外的反机构艺术实践，自1960年代末以来沿不同方向发展。关键范式探索地点的物理、物质特征；结构它的社会空间与经济体的意识形态网络；以及把场域延伸到艺术语境之外的公共关切，如社区认同和政治。[^zh-ch04-37] 这些实验打破了支配艺术生产与接受的边界，即便博物馆和画廊同时试图拥抱场域特定艺术。卢杰的《长征》正处在这一难题的症结上。他对沿历史长征路线各地点艺术探索的组织，把艺术移出大都市博物馆和画廊空间，但也意在吸引国际机构关注——它确实做到了。纪实照片和录像与卢杰的策展说明一起，被纳入纽约亚洲协会的《艺术与中国革命》（2008—9）。虽然纽约的《长征》为把中国革命艺术与政治重新定位为重要的世界历史事件提供了机会，它也抹平了艺术家如何介入原始创作地点的复杂性。他们的作品回应泸沽湖的物理地形、对另类摩梭社会性的想象、旅游业对少数民族群体日益增长的影响、中国社会主义图像制作实践，甚至朱迪·芝加哥的机构权力。


〔原书 155, 156〕

Li Shurui, a student in 2002 in the painting department at the Sichuan Academy of Fine Art, described her decision to join *The Long March* as accidental and her contribution to the exhibit as outside the theme proposed by Judy Chicago. She and two classmates, among the youngest participants in the project, maintained the most distance from the tensions brewing between artists, Lu, and Chicago. Li’s installation, *Seeing Mountains, Seeing Water*, consisted of twenty box-shaped tents fashioned out of mosquito netting and bamboo poles. She staked them in the lake in an arc echoing the shoreline (plate 10). This minimalist tracing of Lugu Lake’s geographic contour places the white cube of gallery display within the landscape, a mark of artistic intervention on the environment. The juxtaposition of the tents with the mountainous backdrop also references the Chinese literati tradition of painting, in which an amateur artist wandered through a landscape, committing the journey to memory, before returning to a small studio or pavilion to paint it. Li spoke of the interior space demarcated by each tent and her feeling that the walls, while porous, framed the water in a way that differentiated inside from outside. As water lapped through the airy spaces, she also noted that they create a sense of voyeurism, of being compelled to peer inside, just as tourists to Lugu Lake desire an inner glance at the Mosuo system of sexual relations.

李姝睿是2002年四川美术学院绘画系的学生，她把加入《长征》的决定描述为偶然，把自己的参展贡献描述为偏离芝加哥提议的主题。她和两位同学属于项目中最年轻的一批参与者，与艺术家、卢杰和芝加哥之间酝酿的紧张保持最大距离。李姝睿的装置《看山看水》由二十顶用蚊帐布和竹竿制成的箱形帐篷组成。她把它们插在湖中，排成与岸线呼应的弧线（图版10）。这种对泸沽湖地理轮廓的极简描摹，把画廊展示的白色立方体置于风景之中，成为艺术介入环境的一个标记。帐篷与群山背景的并置也指涉中国文人绘画传统：业余艺术家漫游山水，把旅程铭记于心，然后回到小画室或亭中作画。李姝睿谈到每顶帐篷划出的内部空间，以及她觉得四壁虽通透，却把水面框定，区分内外。当水波拍过通风的空间时，她指出，它们还制造出一种窥视感，一种被迫向里张望的感觉，正如来泸沽湖的游客渴望窥见摩梭性关系制度的内里。


〔原书 156, 157〕

The site-specific investigations of Lei Yan focused on the gendered history of the Long March. As with the “seeding machine” symbolism she and Sun Guojuan explored as preparation for their participation, Lei drew on her experience in the military, a socialist institution that championed female soldiers’ mobilization even while continuing to treat them as different from and less than male counterparts. Her deployment of historical photographs of male and female Long March comrades probes the internal power dynamics of the original historical event, as well as the art experiment under the same name to follow sixty years later. She responded to Chicago’s “what if” fantasy with a pair of digitally altered black-and-white photographs asking linked, retrospective questions: *What If the Long March Had Been a Women’s Rights Movement*? (figure 4.04) and *What If They Had Been Women*? (figure 4.05). She shifts the subjunctive mood of Chicago’s verbal construction to the past unreal conditional, which roots dreams for future justice in historically, culturally specific conditions. The first photograph features prominent female activists, including Cai Chang, Deng Yingchao, and Kang Keqing, who joined the Red Army on its 1934 trek. The second photograph features male party leaders, Mao at the center, standing on the same patch of ground, adorned with 1930s female hairstyles. In each photo a regiment of female soldiers marches in the background, but in opposite directions, as if toward the future, as if toward the past. Lei intended for the photographs to be hung side by side, stereoscopic images that don’t quite match up. The same miniature, camouflage-dressed figure of the artist herself, peering through binoculars at her historical predecessors, appears in the bottom right corner of each. Lei Yan proposed hanging her photographs on two large windows facing the courtyard of the guesthouse where Chicago was staying. Lu Jie worried her Mao Zedong in drag might attract official criticism of the overall exhibit, so the images were hung back-to-back, with the one of male leaders facing inward. This decision, which Lu himself reflected on as a form of self-censorship, provided one response to Lei’s questions: while it is a fait accompli for socialism to garb women in the image of men as part of its politics of liberatory revolution, the reverse remains dangerous and hidden.

雷燕的场域特定考察聚焦长征的性别化历史。正如她和孙国娟为参与而准备的“播种机”象征，雷燕动用了自己在军队的经历——一个倡导动员女兵、却仍把她们视为不同于并低于男性同行的社会主义机构。她使用男女长征同志的历史照片，探查原始历史事件内部的权力动态，以及六十年后同名艺术实验中的权力动态。她用一对数字修改的黑白照片回应芝加哥的“如果”幻想，提出相互关联的回顾性问题：《如果长征是一场女权运动？》（图4.04）和《如果他们是女人？》（图4.05）。她把芝加哥口头构念中的虚拟语气转为过去非真实条件句，把对未来正义的梦想扎根于历史、文化特定的条件。第一张照片中有蔡畅、邓颖超、康克清等著名女性行动者，她们随红军参加了1934年开始的长征。第二张照片中是男性党的领导人们，毛泽东居于中央，站在同一片土地上，却被配上1930年代女性发型。每张照片背景中都有一队女兵行军，但方向相反，仿佛走向未来，仿佛走向过去。雷燕原计划把两张照片并排悬挂，成为不太对得上的立体图像。右下角都有同一个身着迷彩的艺术家本人微小人像，正用双筒望远镜审视她的历史前辈。雷燕提议把照片挂在两扇朝向芝加哥所住客栈院子的大窗上。卢杰担心她那张男扮女装的毛泽东可能招致官方对整个展览的批评，于是照片被背对背悬挂，男性领导人那张朝内。卢杰自己反思这一决定是一种自我审查，它回应了雷燕的问题：社会主义作为解放革命政治的一部分，让女性穿上男性形象的外衣，这已是既成事实；而反向操作仍然危险且被隐藏。


〔原书 157〕

Sun Guojuan’s installation piece, also displayed at Chicago’s guesthouse, explored the dynamics of tourism in Luoshui. In *Stuck to You*, Sun continued her use of sugar, a material integral to her photographic series *Sweetness Forever*, which paired nude images of the artist’s body covered in sugar with still-life arrangements of similarly coated beauty products. Sun extended her depiction of the saccharine surface of market reform from the realm of femininity to touristic consumption of ethnic difference. She staged her installation in a room with a traditional Mosuo hearth, with stools for female family members on the right and male family members on the left. On the walls she hung photographs and explanatory passages about Mosuo culture collected from tourist publications. On the floor, she scattered chunks of sticky candy and strips of paper printed with Mosuo lineage names. As people walked through the room, candy and paper stuck to the bottom of their shoes, and they had to scrap off the sticky mess upon exiting. *Stuck to You* implicated tourists seeking escape and titillation in the process of social disruption they leave behind.

孙国娟的装置作品也在芝加哥客栈展出，探索落水村旅游业的动态。在《粘住你》中，孙国娟延续对糖的使用——这一材料对她摄影系列《永远甜蜜》至关重要；该系列把艺术家身体覆满糖的裸体图像，与同样裹糖的美容产品静物摆置并置。孙国娟把对市场改革甜腻表面的描绘，从女性气质领域延伸到对民族差异的旅游消费。她把装置布置在一个有传统摩梭火塘的房间，右侧是女性家庭成员坐凳，左侧是男性家庭成员坐凳。墙上挂着她从旅游出版物收集的摩梭文化照片和说明段落。地上散落粘性糖果块，以及印有摩梭世系名的纸条。人们走过房间时，糖果和纸粘在鞋底，出去时必须刮掉粘腻的杂物。《粘住你》把寻求逃避和刺激的游客，卷入他们留下的社会混乱过程。


〔原书 157, 159〕

Huang Ru, Li Shurui’s classmate at the Sichuan Academy of Fine Art, focused like Lei Yan on gender in socialist visual culture, through an exploration of the ccp tradition of open-air cinema (*lutian dianying*). The party employed cinema as a form of political consciousness-raising, through development of state-directed production studios and circulation of films to rural populations. Mobile open-air cinemas, with a screen and projector temporarily set up in villages, projected images of the new nation throughout the countryside. For *Open-Air Cinema*, Huang Ru arranged for old thirty-five-millimeter prints of classic Chinese movies, all featuring women in lead roles, to be projected in the courtyard of a Luoshui guesthouse. She explained that as a member of the generation born toward the end of high socialism, the piece involved learning how to navigate the official institutional channels necessary to rent the projector, screen, speakers, and film prints. Of all the pieces created at Lugu Lake, Huang’s drew the largest audience in spite of rainy weather. Local villagers, including those in costume who had wandered over from their evening performance at the Mosuo Cultural Museum, mingled together with Chinese and foreign tourists under umbrellas and roof eaves as they watched films such as *Sister Jiang*. This 1978 film adaptation of an opera popularized in the 1960s tells the story of an underground Communist who in 1948 struggles valiantly against the Guomindang.[^en-ch04-38] On the way to deliver an important directive to troops in northern Sichuan, Sister Jiang learns her husband has been killed and joins the peasant commander Double-Gun Grandma as leader of the guerrilla forces. When a traitor betrays her, Guomindang officers imprison Sister Jiang on the site of the former Sino-American Cooperative Association (saco). Before her execution on the eve of Chongqing’s liberation, she sings a climatic number “I Sacrifice My Youth for Communism” amid chains and torture instruments.[^en-ch04-39] Huang’s *Open-Air Cinema* not only presents a popular 1970s female image radically different from that assumed by the original *Womanhouse* artists, but also raises questions about the rural-urban traffic of images in China especially relevant in Lugu Lake, a community repeatedly imaged by outsiders in various myth-making projects.

黄茹是李姝睿在四川美术学院的同班同学，她像雷燕一样聚焦社会主义视觉文化中的性别，探讨中共的露天电影传统。党把电影用作政治觉悟提升的形式，发展国家指导的制片厂，并把影片发行到农村人口中。流动露天电影院在村庄临时架起幕布和放映机，把新国家的形象投射到乡间各地。为创作《露天电影》，黄茹安排在落水村一家客栈的院子里放映中国经典影片的旧35毫米拷贝，这些影片都以女性为主角。她解释说，作为出生于高度社会主义末期的一代，这件作品涉及学习如何打通租用放映机、幕布、扬声器和胶片拷贝所需的官方机构渠道。在泸沽湖创作的所有作品中，黄茹的作品尽管遇雨，仍吸引了最多观众。当地村民，包括身着演出服、从摩梭文化博物馆晚间演出走过来的人，与中外游客一起打着伞、站在屋檐下，观看《江姐》等影片。这部1978年根据1960年代流行歌剧改编的电影，讲述一名地下党员1948年英勇对抗国民党的故事。[^zh-ch04-38] 在前往川北向部队传达重要指示途中，江姐得知丈夫遇害，加入农民司令双枪老太婆，成为游击队领导人。叛徒出卖她后，国民党军官把她关押在旧中美合作所（SACO）所在地。在重庆解放前夕被处决前，她在镣铐和刑具中唱出高潮唱段《我为共产主义把青春贡献》。[^zh-ch04-39] 黄茹的《露天电影》不仅呈现了与原始《女人屋》艺术家所设想截然不同的1970年代流行女性形象，也提出关于中国城乡图像流通的问题；这在泸沽湖尤为重要——这是一个不断被外来者以各种神话制造项目拍摄的社区。


〔原书 158〕

![*图4.04　雷燕，《如果长征是一场女权运动？》，2002年。数码照片。艺术家惠允。*](web/assets/ch04-b049.jpg)

FIG 4.04 Lei Yan, *What If the Long March Had Been a Women’s Rights Movement*? 2002. Digital photograph. Courtesy of the artist.

*图4.04　雷燕，《如果长征是一场女权运动？》，2002年。数码照片。艺术家惠允。*


〔原书 158〕

![*图4.05　雷燕，《如果他们是女人？》，2002年。数码照片。艺术家惠允。*](web/assets/ch04-b050.jpg)

FIG 4.05 Lei Yan, *What If They Had Been Women*? 2002. Digital photograph. Courtesy of the artist.

*图4.05　雷燕，《如果他们是女人？》，2002年。数码照片。艺术家惠允。*


〔原书 159, 160〕

In their interpretation of the Lugu Lake site, Su Ruya and Song Yanping embraced the romanticized portrait of Mosuo sexual emancipation highlighted in representations by outsiders. Both staged critical reflections on the Han nation-state, and its disciplining of citizens’ sexual relations through marriage and reproduction, on the ground of an imagined Mosuo cultural landscape of free love. For *Goddess Mountain—Eternal Woman* (plate 11), Su Ruya stood at the edge of the lake in a wind-billowed, flowered nightgown and flung roses—the imported, cosmopolitan symbol of romantic love—into the water: an offering to Gamu Mountain, central in local iconography as protective site for the Mosuo mother goddess. Su described herself as an eternal bride devoted to the dream of unfettered passion, the open boat in which a lover could ply his charms but never possess her. In contrast with this romantic oblation, Song Yanping’s nearby installation *Fire Extinguisher* (figure 4.06) presented a stark triangular arrangement of tripods made of tree branches stuck into the gravely beach. They resembled rudimentary domestic structures. From the center of each tripod hung a frilly white cloth bag, symbolizing the promise of marital happiness, filled with either rice or sand. She lit a fire beneath each, but the wind and lack of sufficient kindling kept the flames from reaching the bottom of each bag, as Song had intended. Instead, she poked a hole in the cloth, so that the contents of the womb-shaped bags steadily poured out and extinguished the flames beneath: a process of depletion dramatically staged against the alternative “nature” of Lugu Lake. The empty bags swung limply in the wind. In these artworks, Chinese women used a cosmopolitan art activity to revision the Chinese nation-state, but in the process Mosuo women became the silenced ground for their reconfiguration of gendered subject-object relations.[^en-ch04-40]

在诠释泸沽湖地点时，苏茹娅和宋雁萍拥抱了外来者再现中突出强调的摩梭性解放浪漫形象。两人都以想象的摩梭自由恋爱文化景观为场地，对汉族国家及其通过婚姻与生育规训公民性关系展开批判性反思。为《女神山——永恒的女人》（图版11），苏茹娅站在湖边，身穿被风吹起的碎花睡裙，把玫瑰——进口的、世界性的浪漫爱情象征——抛入水中：献给格姆女神山，它在地方图像学中是摩梭母神保护圣地的核心。苏茹娅把自己描述为永恒的新娘，献身于无拘激情的梦想；那是敞开的船，爱人可以施展魅力，却永远无法占有她。与这种浪漫奉献相对，宋雁萍附近的装置《灭火器》（图4.06）呈现树杈三脚架插在砾石滩上的鲜明三角排列。它们像简陋的家庭结构。每个三脚架中央挂着一只镶褶边的白布袋，象征婚姻幸福的承诺，里面装满米或沙。她在每个袋子下点火，但风大、引火物不足，火焰未能像她预期的那样烧到袋底。于是她在布上戳洞，让子宫形状袋中的东西不断漏出，浇灭下方火焰：一个消耗过程，在泸沽湖另类“自然”的背景下戏剧性上演。空袋在风中无力摇摆。在这些作品中，中国女性用世界主义的艺术活动重新想象中国民族国家，但在这一过程中，摩梭女性成为她们重构性别主客体关系的沉默基底。[^zh-ch04-40]


〔原书 160〕

![*图4.06　宋雁萍，《灭火器》，2002年。装置。作者摄。*](web/assets/ch04-b052.jpg)

FIG 4.06 Song Yanping, *Fire Extinguisher*, 2002. Installation. Photograph by author.

*图4.06　宋雁萍，《灭火器》，2002年。装置。作者摄。*


〔原书 160, 161〕

Zhang Lun’s *Lugu Lake—Happy Existence* (plates 12 and 13) represents a multilayered approach to its site, which takes on the institutions of tourism, sociological research, ethnic classification, and Judy Chicago herself. It is part of a larger imagined series documenting the impact of China’s economic reforms on personal circumstances and desires. In locations around the country, including shopping malls and automobile showrooms, Zhang would ask individuals to fill out short surveys with information such as age, gender, hero, and personal aspirations, to accompany photographs taken on-site.[^en-ch04-41] In Luoshui, Zhang staged her piece at the Mosuo Cultural Museum. In order to raise revenue to build and maintain museum exhibits, its founders encouraged commercial activity, and each evening a ticketed performance took place in its central courtyard, with tourists joining a song-and-dance circle led by Luoshui residents dressed in Mosuo costume. Zhang transformed the display of a Mosuo family hearth into a photography studio. She covered the walls with a pink-toned print of one of her oil-painted flower photographs and affixed a Lugu Lake tourist map to the center of the back wall. This backdrop accentuated the artificial representation of Mosuo life consumed by tourists. With the aid of the village chief, Zhang arranged for fifty villagers to take turns being photographed with Judy Chicago, turning the tables by making her into the tourist attraction. One by one, they stepped out of the performance in the courtyard to fill out a survey and be photographed with the visiting feminist dignitary. The survey adapted for Lugu Lake asked if participants had heard of the “feminist master Judy Chicago” and if they thought the Mosuo should be recognized as an independent ethnic nationality; most answered “no” to the first and “yes” to the second. Zhang requested that Chicago, who had hesitantly agreed to participate, sit in the place reserved for female elders and pour tea for each Mosuo person as they entered and sat down. The first person to pose with Chicago was the Luoshui village chief. After the twelfth cup of tea, Chicago appeared fed up with her role in the piece. She exclaimed, “No one in America would believe I’d poured tea for anyone!” and left the scene. In an angry outburst of her own, Zhang Lun raged over the music from the courtyard about Chicago’s intransigence, which had disrupted her plans. Suddenly her face lit up, and she declared, “The Mosuo will pour tea for the Mosuo!” She continued taking photos as each following Mosuo person poured a cup of tea for him or herself.

张伦的《泸沽湖——快乐的存在》（图版12、13）代表一种多层次的地点处理方法，向旅游、社会学研究、民族分类等制度以及朱迪·芝加哥本人发起挑战。它属于一个更大的想象系列，记录中国经济改革对个人处境与欲望的影响。在全国各地，包括购物中心和汽车展厅，张伦请个人填写简短问卷，内容如年龄、性别、英雄、个人愿望，与现场拍摄的照片相配。[^zh-ch04-41] 在落水村，张伦把作品设在摩梭文化博物馆。为筹集建造和维护展览的收入，创办者鼓励商业活动，每晚在中央庭院举行售票演出，游客加入由身着摩梭服装的落水村民带领的歌舞圈。张伦把摩梭家庭火塘的展示转变成摄影棚。墙上覆着一张粉色调的油画花卉照片印刷品，后墙中央贴着泸沽湖旅游地图。这一背景强化了游客所消费的摩梭生活的虚假再现。在村长帮助下，张伦安排五十位村民轮流与朱迪·芝加哥合影，反客为主，使她成为旅游景点。他们一个接一个从庭院演出中走出来，填写问卷，与来访的女性主义贵宾合影。为泸沽湖改编的问卷询问参与者是否听说过“女性主义大师朱迪·芝加哥”，以及是否认为摩梭应被承认为独立民族；多数人对第一个问题答“不”，对第二个答“是”。芝加哥此前已犹豫地同意参与。张伦请她坐在为女性长者保留的位置上，为每位走进来坐下的摩梭人倒茶。第一个与芝加哥合影的是落水村村长。倒到第十二杯茶时，芝加哥似乎厌倦了自己在这件作品中的角色。她喊道：“美国没人会相信我给任何人倒过茶！”然后离开了场景。张伦也愤怒爆发，在庭院音乐声中怒斥芝加哥的不妥协打乱了她的计划。突然，她脸上一亮，宣布：“摩梭人给摩梭人倒茶！”她继续拍照，随后每位摩梭人给自己倒了一杯茶。


〔原书 161〕

This moment of breakdown, marked by the disappearance of Chicago in Zhang’s images, is indicative of the “dialogue” that occurred at Lugu Lake. Just as some of the artists, including Chicago, used imaginaries of the Mosuo as the basis for their participation in art world, feminist, and nation-state debates, Zhang used Judy Chicago. She flattened Chicago as an individual artist with a complex subjectivity into an institution to be challenged, thus calling attention to Chicago’s own flattening (or Lu Jie’s positioning of her in this role) of her Chinese peers. Turned into the cardboard-cutout doyenne of a Western-centered narrative of feminist art, Chicago responded by boycotting, which in her words is “the absolute opposite of what should have happened.”

这一崩溃时刻——以芝加哥在张伦照片中的消失为标志——指示了泸沽湖发生的“对话”。正如包括芝加哥在内的一些艺术家把摩梭想象作为参与艺术界、女性主义和国家辩论的基础，张伦利用了朱迪·芝加哥。她把拥有复杂主体性的个体艺术家芝加哥压平成一个供人挑战的机构，从而引起人们注意芝加哥本人（或卢杰对她的定位）对中国同行的压平。芝加哥被变成以西方为中心的女性主义艺术叙事中纸板剪影般的女性元老，她的回应是抵制；用她的话说，这是“应该发生的事情的绝对反面”。


〔原书 161, 162〕

The divergent responses of these artists to the fantastical siting of the Long March at Lugu Lake demonstrate the instability of the sign “woman.” The resources they drew on to be recognized as authors of their own sign—to undo the homogenization and colonization of complex female subjectivities—came from historically and culturally specific archives of theorizing about women and social justice. Their undoing of “womanhouse” demonstrates vigorous and ongoing inquiry into how to dismantle symbolic systems that catch women in double binds. In their site-specific attempts at collaboration with a local community, they also demonstrated the risk of what Hal Foster calls “the artist as ethnographer,” in which “the quasi-anthropological role set up for the artist can promote a presuming as much as a questioning of ethnographic authority.” [^en-ch04-42] The art sited at Lugu Lake opened debates about the assumption of female artists as a “community” but held little meaning for local residents. A Mosuo teenage boy observing one of the lakeside performance pieces commented, “It’s no different from all the films and television dramas filmed here. They come, we don’t really know what they’re doing, and then they leave and we never see them again.”

这些艺术家对长征落户泸沽湖这一幻想地点的不同回应，展示了“女人”符号的不稳定性。她们为被承认为自身符号作者——为消解复杂女性主体性的同质化与殖民化——所动用的资源，来自历史和文化特定的女性与社会正义理论档案。她们对“女人屋”的拆解，展示了对如何拆除使女性落入双重束缚的象征系统的持续而有力的探询。在与当地社区场域特定的合作尝试中，她们也展示了哈尔·福斯特（Hal Foster）所谓“艺术家作为民族志学者”的风险：“为艺术家设立的准人类学角色，既可能促进对民族志权威的质疑，也可能促进对它的推定。”[^zh-ch04-42] 在泸沽湖就地创作的艺术开启了关于把女性艺术家预设为“共同体”的辩论，却对当地居民意义甚微。一个摩梭少年观看一件湖畔行为作品时评论道：“这跟在这里拍的所有电影电视剧没什么不同。他们来了，我们其实不知道他们在做什么，然后他们走了，我们再也见不到他们。”


〔原书 162〕

The Question of Feminism in Chinese Contemporary Art

中国当代艺术中的女性主义问题


〔原书 162〕

What was being worked out at Lugu Lake had little to do with, in Mao’s terms, “learning from the people.” It had much more to do with a question of feminism in Chinese contemporary art. In transnational encounters, artists, curators, and critics repeatedly asked whether “feminist art” existed in China. Variations included “does China have any great women artists?” or “why have there been no great Chinese feminist artists?” The latter arose in consideration of whether there was anything feminist about the work assembled under the label *nüxing yishu* (women’s art), such as site six of *The Long March* at Lugu Lake. Descriptions of exhibits organized around the topic defined the work as either feminist or feminine or both, blurring the terms in the categorical creation of nüxing yishu, which sometimes refers to art by women and sometimes serves as shorthand for *nüxingzhuyi yishu*, or feminist art. An overview of responses to this line of questioning demonstrates the contradictions involved in discussions of feminism and Chinese contemporary art, highlighting the contradictions that fissure this art world in general.

泸沽湖所推敲的东西，与毛泽东所说的“向人民学习”几乎无关，而更多关乎中国当代艺术中的女性主义问题。在跨国相遇中，艺术家、策展人和批评家反复询问中国是否存在“女性主义艺术”。变体包括“中国有任何伟大的女性艺术家吗？”或“为什么中国没有伟大的女性主义艺术家？”后者是在思考以“女性艺术”（nüxing yishu）标签集合的作品——如泸沽湖《长征》第六站——是否有任何女性主义成分时提出的。围绕该主题组织的展览说明，把作品界定为女性主义的、具有女性气质的，或两者兼有，在“女性艺术”这一类别创造中模糊了术语，它有时指女性创作的艺术，有时作为“女性主义艺术”（nüxingzhuyi yishu）的简称。对这类质疑回应的概览，展示了关于女性主义与中国当代艺术的讨论中涉及的矛盾，凸显了使这个艺术界整体产生裂隙的矛盾。


〔原书 162〕

Beijing-based curator and critic Liao Wen recalls the first time she heard the question, her immediate ironic response, and how the encounter led her to curate one of the first exhibits to grapple with the issue:

北京策展人、批评家廖雯回忆第一次听到这个问题、她当即的讽刺回答，以及这次相遇如何促使她策划最早直面该问题的展览之一：


〔原书 162〕

In 1992, a curator from a British national museum traveled to China to investigate the new art being produced. Perhaps because she discovered that most artists were men she was particularly excited to meet me, a female colleague. She asked me if feminist art existed in China. I responded that since China had not resolved its human rights issues, it was hardly possible to talk about women’s rights, not to mention feminist art. We both dismissed the topic with a laugh. I did not realize at the time that this acted as a catalyst for some profound thinking.[^en-ch04-43]

1992年，一位来自英国国家级博物馆的策展人来中国考察正在产生的新艺术。也许因为她发现大多数艺术家都是男性，她见到我——一位女性同行——时特别兴奋。她问我中国是否存在女性主义艺术。我回答说，中国连人权问题都尚未解决，遑论女性权利，更不用说女性主义艺术了。我们俩都一笑置之。我当时并未意识到，这竟成为一些深刻思考的催化剂。[^zh-ch04-43]


〔原书 163〕

In 1995, Liao curated an exhibit titled *Women’s Approach to Chinese Contemporary Art*, which featured twelve female artists whose work demonstrated for her the “embryonic” state of a Chinese women’s art on the verge of developing a distinct formal language.[^en-ch04-44] She then published an art historical survey titled *Feminism as Method: Women’s Art*, which surveys both the representation and role of women in premodern, Maoist, and reform-era Chinese art.[^en-ch04-45] In it, she inserts a section on Western female artists, ranging from Berth Morisot to Cindy Sherman, right before her discussion of 1990s art in China. This sequencing sets up a century of Western art history as the road out (*chulu*) of the past for contemporary Chinese women. Liao thus became an important translator of Western feminist art history into China, and in 1999–2000, she deepened this research through six months of fieldwork in the United States. Her interviews with influential artists of the 1970s feminist movement such as Judy Chicago, Miriam Shapiro, and Carolee Schneemann ran as a regular feature of the new art magazine *Next Wave* (Xin chao) in 2001.

1995年，廖雯策划了题为《中国当代艺术中的女性方式》的展览，展出十二位女性艺术家，她们的作品向她展示了中国女性艺术处于“萌芽”状态，即将发展出独特的形式语言。[^zh-ch04-44] 她随后出版了艺术史综述《女性主义作为方式：女性艺术》，考察女性在前现代、毛泽东时代和改革时期中国艺术中的再现与角色。[^zh-ch04-45] 书中，她在讨论1990年代中国艺术之前插入一节西方女性艺术家，从贝尔特·莫里索到辛迪·舍曼。这一排序把百年西方艺术史设为当代中国女性走出过去的“出路”（chulu）。廖雯由此成为把西方女性主义艺术史译介到中国的重要人物；1999至2000年，她通过在美国六个月田野调查深化了这一研究。她对1970年代女性主义运动重要艺术家朱迪·芝加哥、米里亚姆·夏皮罗和卡罗琳·施尼曼的访谈，于2001年作为新艺术杂志《新潮》的固定栏目发表。


〔原书 163〕

Beijing-based artist Feng Jiali’s response to the question in 2000, as posed by U.S.-based curator Britta Erickson and published in *Art AsiaPacific*, laments the lack of feminist theoretical reflection in the sudden burst of exhibits featuring art by Chinese women: “In the 1990s and 2000 there have been more exhibitions of women’s art than at any other time in China’s history.... This marks a significant change, a change that does not necessarily represent a progression or liberation of the creative powers of women in China. For the most part, so-called ‘women’s art’ in China is based purely on the sex of the artist, and not necessarily on recognition of the life-experience differences created by gender.” [^en-ch04-46] In her accompanying article, Erickson notes the “rise of a feminist spirit in contemporary Chinese art” driven by “an increasing awareness of the extent to which women have been marginalized by the art system.” [^en-ch04-47]

北京艺术家 Feng Jiali 对2000年由常驻美国的策展人林似竹（Britta Erickson）提出并发表于《艺术亚太》的同一问题作出回应，哀叹在中国女性艺术展览突然爆发之际缺乏女性主义理论反思：“1990年代和2000年，中国女性艺术展览比历史上任何时期都多……这标志着一个重大变化，但这种变化未必代表中国女性创造力的进步或解放。中国的所谓‘女性艺术’大多纯粹基于艺术家的生理性别，而未必基于对社会性别所造成的生活经验差异的认识。”[^zh-ch04-46] 林似竹在配文中指出，“中国当代艺术中女性主义精神的兴起”由“对女性被艺术系统边缘化程度日益增长的认识”所驱动。[^zh-ch04-47]


〔原书 163, 164〕

In 2008, *New York Times* art critic Holland Cotter interviewed another Beijing-based artist, Lin Tianmiao. Of their conversation, he writes, “Yet she is cautious about applying the term feminist to herself or her work. Why? The concept is too Western. It is too vague. China is not ready for feminism. China has its own brand of feminism.” [^en-ch04-48] This ambiguous characterization fails to account for Lin’s own nüxing yishu history in the preceding decade. Lin’s work was included in many of the early exhibits of work by female artists, such as Liao Wen’s *Women’s Approach to Chinese Contemporary Art*. Initially these efforts challenged institutional marginalization and brought recognition to artists like Lin Tianmiao. However, as the category congealed and underwent institutionalization, nüxing yishu became another form of containment, in for example the patronizing list of “essential characteristics of women’s art” (including childlike fantasy; apathy toward politics, history, and philosophy; and general disinterest in the male world) produced by Jia Fangzhou, curator of the 1998 survey exhibit *Century Woman*.[^en-ch04-49] For Lin Tianmiao, experimentation with the opportunities afforded by nüxing yishu as a way of theorizing the relationship between art politics and practice quickly led to disappointment and disavowal of the term.

2008年，《纽约时报》艺术评论家霍兰·科特采访了另一位北京艺术家林天苗。他这样写道：“但她对用“女性主义”一词描述自己或自己的作品持谨慎态度。为什么？这个概念太西方了。太含糊。中国还没有准备好接受女性主义。中国有自己品牌的女性主义。”[^zh-ch04-48] 这一含糊的定性未能考虑林天苗此前十年的“女性艺术”历史。她的作品被纳入许多早期女性艺术家展览，如廖雯的《中国当代艺术中的女性方式》。最初这些努力挑战机构边缘化，为林天苗等艺术家带来承认。然而，随着类别凝固并经历制度化，“女性艺术”变成另一种限制形式。例如，1998年综述展《世纪·女性》策展人贾方舟列出的恩赐式“女性艺术本质特征”（包括稚气的幻想；对政治、历史和哲学的淡漠；以及对男性世界普遍不感兴趣）。[^zh-ch04-49] 对林天苗而言，利用“女性艺术”所提供的机会来理论化艺术政治与实践关系的实验，很快导致失望和对该词的否认。


〔原书 164〕

These responses to the question of feminism in Chinese contemporary art reveal two tendencies. First, the term *feminist* is invoked without specifying what it references: an intentional mode of artistic expression, a methodology for interpreting visual forms of representation, or an analytic for examining the politics and social relations of art worlds. Second, the transnationalism permeating the field of Chinese contemporary art provides the context for the questioning. If Chinese contemporary art is a zone of cultural encounter, the same might be said of feminism, as a field of thought, practice, and social mobilization. Even claims of difference, as for example that between Chinese and Western feminism, do not precede but are made and consolidated through the process of encounter.

这些对中国当代艺术女性主义问题的回应揭示两种倾向。第一，“女性主义”一词被援引，却没有说明它指什么：一种有意的艺术表达模式，一种阐释视觉再现形式的方法，或一种考察艺术界政治与社会关系的分析工具。第二，渗透中国当代艺术领域的跨国主义为质疑提供了语境。如果中国当代艺术是一个文化相遇地带，女性主义作为一个思想、实践和社会动员领域亦然。甚至差异的主张——例如中国与西方女性主义之间的差异——也不是先于相遇而存在，而是通过相遇过程被制造和巩固。


〔原书 164, 165〕

As Chinese contemporary art emerged on the international stage during the 1990s and early 2000s, a minor strain of criticism persistently noted the relative invisibility of female artists. Holland Cotter’s article “China’s Female Artists Quietly Emerge” provides a footnote to the art market phenomenon of Chinese artists suddenly selling work for record prices at Sotheby’s and elsewhere. Briefly surveying artwork by Chinese women, Cotter calls it some of the most innovative around, even though it doesn’t garner the same attention as that of their male peers. He concludes, “Contemporary art in China is a man’s world. While the art market, all but nonexistent in 1989, has become a powerhouse industry and produced a pantheon of multimillionaire artist-celebrities, there are no women in that pantheon.”[^en-ch04-50] He was not the first to notice. Ever since the first major exhibits of Chinese avant-garde art appeared, largely in Western art spaces, critics attentive to gender engaged in a counting game that asked where the women were. Britta Erickson gives the following count for early overseas shows: of the sixteen artists in *China Avant-Garde* in Berlin in 1993 only one was female; *China’s New Art, Post-1989* in Hong Kong also in 1993 included fifty-two men and two women; and *China*! in Bonn in 1996 exhibited the work of thirty-one artists, none of whom were female.[^en-ch04-51] The outrage of German women over this exclusion motivated the curation of *Half of the Sky: Contemporary Chinese Women Artists* at Bonn’s Frauenmuseum in 1998. Melissa Chiu provides a similar count for international exhibitions of Chinese contemporary art in 1997: “Women accounted for only three of the eighteen artists in *Another Long March* in Japan, one of seven artists in *Immutability and Fashion* in Holland, and none of the ten artists in *In Between Limits* in Korea.”[^en-ch04-52] She notes the same trend in major exhibitions within China: only two out of thirty-nine artists in the *First Academic Exhibition of Chinese Contemporary Art* (1996–97) were female, and four of twenty-nine in the 1996 Shanghai Biennale.

1990年代和2000年代初，中国当代艺术在国际舞台出现时，一小股批评声音持续指出女性艺术家的相对不可见。霍兰·科特的文章《中国女性艺术家悄然浮现》为中国艺术家突然在苏富比等地以创纪录价格售出作品的艺术市场现象添加了一个脚注。科特简要回顾中国女性作品，称其为周围最具创新性的艺术之一，尽管不如男性同行的作品那样受关注。他总结道：“中国当代艺术是一个男人的世界。艺术市场在1989年几乎不存在，如今已成为强大的产业，并造就了一批拥有数百万财富的艺术家名人，但万神殿中没有女性。”[^zh-ch04-50] 他不是第一个注意到这一点的人。自中国先锋艺术首批重要展览主要出现在西方艺术空间以来，关注性别的批评家就玩起数数游戏，追问女性在哪里。林似竹给出早期海外展览的统计：1993年柏林《中国先锋》十六位艺术家中只有一位女性；同样在1993年香港的《后八九中国新艺术》包括五十二位男性和两位女性；1996年波恩《中国！》展出三十一位艺术家的作品，其中没有女性。[^zh-ch04-51] 德国女性对这种排斥的愤怒，促成了1998年波恩女性博物馆《半边天：中国当代女性艺术家》的策划。梅利莎·邱（Melissa Chiu）为1997年中国当代艺术国际展览提供了类似统计：“在日本《另一个长征》的十八位艺术家中，女性仅占三位；在荷兰《不变与时尚》的七位艺术家中占一位；在韩国《界限之间》的十位艺术家中一位也没有。”[^zh-ch04-52] 她指出中国国内大型展览也有同样趋势：第一届中国当代艺术学术展（1996—97）三十九位艺术家中只有两位女性，1996年上海双年展二十九位中有四位。


〔原书 165〕

This numbers game arose from a palpable lack of gender parity, yet the “counting who counts” mode of protest rarely goes further to theorize about why this situation persists. The response instead has largely been the organization of exhibits, such as *Half of the Sky*, inside and outside of China, devoted to the equalizing task of representing Chinese women artists, sometimes as a national subcategory of Asian women artists. Their organizers do not invoke specific feminist theories or platforms. They do, however, contribute to conflicting theorizations of “woman.” To speak of “woman” is always a theoretical proposition, because to do so conceives of a group of individuals as bound by some commonality, and such conceptions are never politically innocent. The critical and curatorial projects that consolidated nüxing yishu often relied on an archive of Western feminist art praxis as a frame of reference, such that inviting Judy Chicago to Lugu Lake seemed an imperative for recognition. The marginalization of women is not solely the result of Chinese “traditional culture,” although some make this reductionist claim, but at least in part the way in which Chinese contemporary art has gone global. Its troubled relationship with feminism lies in the assumption of a universal understanding of what the term means, when in fact it harbors multiple histories of thought, action, critique, and resistance. At odds with one another, these histories create an interlocking set of double binds, generated through cultural encounter over time, regarding female talent and representation.

这种数字游戏源于明显的性别失衡，但“数谁算数”的抗议模式很少进一步理论化为何这种状况持续。回应反而主要是在国内外组织《半边天》之类展览，致力于再现中国女性艺术家的平等化任务，有时把她们作为亚洲女性艺术家的国族子类别。组织者没有援引具体女性主义理论或纲领。然而，他们确实参与了关于“女人”的相互冲突的理论化。谈论“女人”总是一种理论命题，因为这样做把一群个体设想为被某种共同性绑定，而这种设想绝非政治上无辜。巩固“女性艺术”的批评与策展项目，往往依赖西方女性主义艺术实践档案作为参照框架，以致邀请朱迪·芝加哥到泸沽湖似乎成了一种获得承认的必要。女性的边缘化不只是中国“传统文化”的结果——尽管有人作这种还原论断言——至少部分是中国当代艺术全球化方式的结果。它与女性主义的紧张关系，在于假定该词含义有普遍理解，而实际上它容纳了多种思想、行动、批评与抵抗的历史。这些历史彼此相悖，围绕女性才能与再现，通过长期文化相遇，产生一组相互交织的双重束缚。


〔原书 166〕

Interlocking Double Binds

相互交织的双重束缚


〔原书 166〕

Two questions gave rise to my use of the double bind as an interpretive move. First, why has the increasingly rich and sophisticated scholarship (Chinese and Western) on gender, women’s movements, and feminism in China proven to be a blind spot for art curators and critics? They reference other bodies of theory as a form of cosmopolitan art world participation but rarely turn to feminist scholars of China. Even when turning to feminist theory, Lu Jie proposed that *Long March* participants at Lugu Lake read Julia Kristeva rather than prominent Chinese feminist theorists, such as Marxist humanist Li Xiaojiang or literary critics Dai Jinhua and Meng Yue, who adapted Kristeva to develop their theory of Chinese *écriture féminine*. The second question concerns Chinese art critics and curators who resist Western frames that interpret Chinese contemporary art as derivative or belated. Given that stance, why do they then accept and even promote the idea that nüxing yishu is in a protodevelopmental stage compared to Western feminist art, seemingly displacing a fear of China’s backwardness on the global stage onto its women?

两个问题促使我把双重束缚用作阐释策略。第一，为什么日益丰富精深的关于中国性别、妇女运动与女性主义的研究（中国与西方的研究），对艺术策展人和批评家而言竟是盲点？他们援引其他理论体系作为世界性艺术界参与的形式，却很少转向研究中国的女性主义学者。即便转向女性主义理论，卢杰也提议泸沽湖的长征参与者阅读朱莉娅·克里斯蒂娃，而不是马克思主义人道主义者李小江，或文学批评家戴锦华、孟悦等著名中国女性主义理论家——后者借鉴并改造克里斯蒂娃的理论，发展出中国式女性书写理论。第二个问题涉及那些抵制把中国当代艺术解释为派生或落后的西方框架的中国艺术批评家和策展人。既持这种立场，他们为何又接受甚至推广这样一种观念：与西方女性主义艺术相比，“女性艺术”处于原初发展阶段？这似乎把对中国在全球舞台落后的恐惧，转移到中国女性身上。


〔原书 166〕

The double bind describes a communication dilemma resulting from two conflicting messages, which trap their recipient in “unresolvable sequences of experiences,” a no-win situation of inevitable failure.[^en-ch04-53] It also provides a feminist analytic that seeks a way out, in which the double bind can be viewed as zen koan. Only by deconstructing the double bind as an insidious form of control does release from it become possible. The production and interpretation of art in a meta-ideological mode present powerful means of doing so. Interlocking double binds arising from the art world encounter of Chinese and Western feminisms structured the schizophrenia of mutual recognition and rejection experienced by Judy Chicago and her Chinese “collaborators.” The artists at Lugu Lake actively struggled through one or several of these double binds. Laying them out is the first step in moving beyond the trap they set.

双重束缚描述由两个冲突信息造成的沟通困境，它们把接收者困在“无法解决的经验序列”中，一种必然失败的无解局面。[^zh-ch04-53] 它也提供一种寻求出路的女性主义分析，其中双重束缚可被视为禅宗公案。只有把双重束缚解构为一种阴险的控制形式，才可能从中解脱。以元意识形态模式生产和阐释艺术，提供了做到这一点的有力手段。中国与西方女性主义在艺术界相遇所产生的相互交织的双重束缚，结构了朱迪·芝加哥及其中国“合作者”所体验的相互承认与拒绝的精神分裂。泸沽湖的艺术家积极挣扎于其中一种或数种双重束缚。把它们摆出来，是走出其陷阱的第一步。


〔原书 166, 167〕

1) The first double bind provides a historical basis for contemporary troubles. It returns to the efforts of early twentieth-century reformers to create a modern Chinese nation capable of standing up to colonialism.[^en-ch04-54] One foundational influence was Victorian sex theory, which they adopted to displace Confucian kinship protocols with the neologism of nüxing (literally, female sex). Nüxing recast woman as a sexed, biological entity requiring liberation from arranged marriages for sexual selection, which would lead to the eugenic strengthening of the Chinese people. Communist thinkers later jettisoned nüxing as the bourgeois and individualist woman, replacing her with their theorization of funü (women as a collectivity), a massified revolutionary subject to mobilization for state political movements. The Chinese archive of visual art that corresponds with these changing conceptualizations of woman reflects the radical difference between representations of nüxing and funü. Paintings such as Nude in Front of Window (figure 4.07) by Pan Yuliang, who left Shanghai in 1937 to spend the rest of her life in Paris, demonstrate a nüxing sensibility. Her departure from China corresponded with the rise of funü as the Chinese Marxist category of political praxis that replaced nüxing in images like Shan Lianxiao’s 1971 propaganda poster To Be an Upright Person, Be This Kind of Person (figure 4.08). Shan, a painter employed by the Dalian Electronic Ceramics Factory, pairs the heroine from The Red Lantern revolutionary opera with a female Red Guard, exhorting viewers to identify with collective funü subjecthood, to “be this kind of person.”

1）第一种双重束缚为当代麻烦提供历史基础。它回溯二十世纪初改革者创建能够抵抗殖民主义的现代中国国家的努力。[^zh-ch04-54] 一个基础性影响是维多利亚时代的性理论，他们采用它，以“女性”（nüxing，字面意为女性性别）这一新词取代儒家亲属礼制。“女性”把女人重铸为性的、生物性的实体，需要从包办婚姻中解放出来，以进行性选择，进而导致中国人的优生强化。共产党思想家后来抛弃“女性”这个资产阶级、个人主义女人，代之以他们对“妇女”（funü，作为集体）的理论化——一个被大众化、为国家的政治运动而动员的革命主体。与这些变化中的女人概念相应的中国视觉艺术档案，反映了“女性”与“妇女”再现之间的根本差异。潘玉良1937年离开上海、余生留在巴黎，她的《窗前裸女》（图4.07）等画作展示了一种“女性”感性。她离开中国，恰逢“妇女”作为中国马克思主义政治实践范畴兴起并取代“女性”——例如Shan Lianxiao1971年的宣传画《做人要做这样的人》（图4.08）。在大连电子陶瓷厂工作的画家Shan Lianxiao，把革命歌剧《红灯记》中的女英雄与一位女红卫兵并置，劝告观者认同集体的“妇女”主体性，“做这样的人”。


〔原书 167〕

![*图4.07　潘玉良，《窗前裸女》，1940年。布面油画，24厘米×44厘米。*](web/assets/ch04-b070.jpg)

FIG 4.07 Pan Yuliang, *Nude in Front of Window*, 1940. Oil on canvas, 24 cm × 44 cm.

*图4.07　潘玉良，《窗前裸女》，1940年。布面油画，24厘米×44厘米。*


〔原书 167, 168〕

Herein lies the bind: Embracing these new theorizations of woman as nüxing or funü enabled women to actively participate in the public realm of cultural production. But embracing the subject positions of erotic or massified woman also cast them as lesser human beings, as needing liberation, such that to be active in cultural production was seen as exceptional rather than normative for women.

束缚就在于此：拥抱这些关于女人的新理论——作为“女性”或“妇女”——使女性得以积极参与文化生产的公共领域。但拥抱情欲化或大众化女人的主体位置，也把她们塑造为次等的人，需要解放，以致在文化生产中活跃被视为女性的例外而非常态。


〔原书 168〕

![*图4.08　Shan Lianxiao，《做人要做这样的人》，1971年。宣传画。*](web/assets/ch04-b072.jpg)

FIG 4.08 Shan Lianxiao, *To Be an Upright Person, Be This Kind of Person*, 1971. Propaganda poster.

*图4.08　Shan Lianxiao，《做人要做这样的人》，1971年。宣传画。*


〔原书 168〕

These successive articulations of theoretical woman—the active and layered history of thinking about gender and women’s liberation in China—also led to the difficulty of translating the term feminist. Within China gender studies, it is commonplace to comment on the many coinages in Chinese over the twentieth century to refer to the singular term feminism in English: nüquan zhuyi, nüxing zhuyi, nannü pingdeng zhuyi, nüquang yundong, funü yundong.[^en-ch04-55] Of this linguistic disquiet, Barlow notes, “It is significant that the historical flexibility of colloquial Chinese has allowed for so many ways to phrase the word feminism or the movement to center female subjects.”[^en-ch04-56] She emphasizes that this ongoing linguistic reworking is a constitutive part of feminist practice in Sinophone criticism.

这些关于理论女人的相继表述——中国关于性别和妇女解放思想的活跃而多层次历史——也导致“女性主义”一词的翻译困难。在中国性别研究中，人们常谈及二十世纪汉语为英语单一术语 feminism 创造的多种说法：女权主义、女性主义、男女平等主义、女权运动、妇女运动。[^zh-ch04-55] 关于这种语言不安，白露指出：“值得注意的是，汉语口语的历史灵活性允许如此多方式来表述女性主义一词，或使女性主体中心化的运动。”[^zh-ch04-56] 她强调，这种持续的语言重铸是华语圈批评中女性主义实践的构成部分。


〔原书 168, 169〕

Indeed, the phrasing of women’s or feminist art as nüxing yishu signals another reworked understanding of “woman.” It represents reform-era rejection of the Maoist, statist formulation of funü through the humanistic argument that it suppressed female subjectivity in the attempt to remake women in the image of men. A new nüxing, bearing residues of it conceptual predecessor, appeared in accounts such as the following by art critic Xu Hong: “After 1989 individual experimentation began to emerge in Chinese art, bringing to an end the relentless collectivist symbolism of previous years. Women’s consciousness began to emerge and women began to explore their own experience and find an appropriate form of expression. Most female artists sought to define the nature of women’s consciousness or affirm women’s consciousness itself.”[^en-ch04-57] Yang Li, curator of The Metamorphosing Female (Zhuanbian zhong de nüxing), a 2008 exhibit in Shanghai, writes in a similar vein: “Compared with their predecessors, the female artists of the new generation are more independent and more aware of their female consciousness. Based on their instincts and rich emotions, they create artworks from their unique female perspectives, depicting their real experiences, and forming in this process their highly individualized artistic languages.”[^en-ch04-58] This emphasis on the artistic development of women’s consciousness based on embodied female experience pervades work such as Liu Hong’s paintings from the 1990s. The isolated figures in her Soliloquy series (figure 4.09) are hybrids that combine the nüxing nude and the collective red funü visage/blindfold and engage in an introspective discourse, as if on the verge of emerging from past constraints. Liu, a member of the painting faculty at the Sichuan Academy of Fine Art who became emblematic of nüxing yishu in accounts such as Liao Wen’s Feminism as Method: Women’s Art, traveled together with students and friends to Lugu Lake as an observer. The trap of female exceptionality persists in the nominal rejection of feminism by Chinese artists whose work, nonetheless, reflects complex forms of gender consciousness. The recuperation of women marginalized by the international art market system through the currency of nüxing yishu reveals a freighted relationship with the history of feminist praxis in China. Nüxing yishu often ended up feeling like a restrictive category, as in site six at Lugu Lake or art history chapters that partition women to the side.

的确，把女性或女性主义艺术表述为“女性艺术”，标志着对“女人”的另一种重铸理解。它代表改革时期对毛泽东时代国家主义“妇女”表述的人道主义拒绝，理由是这种表述在试图按男性形象重塑女性时压制了女性主体性。一种新的“女性”带着其概念前身的残余，出现在如下艺术批评家徐虹的叙述中：“1989年之后，个人实验开始在中国艺术中出现，终结了此前数年持续不休的集体主义象征表达。女性意识开始浮现，女性开始探索自身经验并寻找适当表达形式。大多数女性艺术家试图界定女性意识的本质，或肯定女性意识本身。”[^zh-ch04-57] 2008年上海展览《转变中的女性》策展人 Yang Li 也写下类似的话：“与前代相比，新一代女性艺术家更独立，也更自觉地意识到自己的女性意识。基于本能和丰富情感，她们从独特的女性视角创作，描绘真实经验，并在这一过程中形成高度个人化的艺术语言。”[^zh-ch04-58] 这种基于具身女性经验对女性意识艺术发展的强调，遍及刘虹1990年代的绘画等作品。她《独白》系列（图4.09）中的孤立人物是混合体：结合了“女性”裸体与集体红色“妇女”的面容／眼罩，进行内省式言说，仿佛即将从过去的约束中浮现。刘虹是四川美术学院绘画系教师，在廖雯《女性主义作为方式：女性艺术》等叙述中成为“女性艺术”的象征；她与学生和朋友一起前往泸沽湖作为观察者。女性例外性的陷阱，在中国艺术家对女性主义名义上的拒绝中持续存在，尽管她们的作品反映了复杂的性别意识形式。通过“女性艺术”的通货，被国际艺术市场体系边缘化的女性得以恢复，这揭示了与中国女性主义实践史沉重的关系。“女性艺术”常常最终成为一个限制性类别，正如在泸沽湖第六站，或把女性分到旁侧的艺术史章节中。


〔原书 169, 170〕

2) If Chinese women struggle to be added to the canon of Chinese contemporary art, and through engagement with it, to change the possible options of what this art can be, then they hazard being seen as outside or derivative of the male-dominated avant-garde that has defined it so far. If Chinese women struggle to be added to the canon of feminist art, and through engagement with it, to change the possible options of what this art can be, then they hazard being seen as derivative of or just a local branch of international (Western) feminist art.

2）如果中国女性努力被加入中国当代艺术经典，并通过参与改变这种艺术可能是什么，那么她们就有被视为局外人或迄今定义该领域的男性主导先锋之派生者的风险。如果中国女性努力被加入女性主义艺术经典，并通过参与改变这种艺术可能是什么，那么她们就有被视为国际（西方）女性主义艺术的派生者、或仅仅是其地方分支的风险。


〔原书 170〕

![*图4.09　刘虹，《独白》第10号，1997年。布面油画，150厘米×150厘米。艺术家惠允。*](web/assets/ch04-b076.jpg)

FIG 4.09 Liu Hong, *Soliloquy, No. 10*, 1997. Oil on canvas, 150 cm × 150 cm. Courtesy of the artist.

*图4.09　刘虹，《独白》第10号，1997年。布面油画，150厘米×150厘米。艺术家惠允。*


〔原书 170, 171〕

This double bind reveals a parallel between how the international market conferred value on a male avant-garde in China after 1989 and the emergence of nüxing yishu around 1995, the year Beijing hosted the UN Fourth World Conference on Women. In the Western critique surrounding the conference of the Chinese state’s hostility to human and therefore women’s rights, the art corollary was to ask why China doesn’t have the kind of feminist art that the West does. Artists like Lin Tianmiao, whose work appeared in several of these 1990s shows, concludes however, “In the end, all the exhibitions seemed to achieve was to simply demonstrate that Chinese women could produce art.”[^en-ch04-59] In her 2008 interview with Holland Cotter, she disavows any feminist identification. She was also one of the only female artists to participate in the Long March outside of the Lugu Lake “women’s section.”

这一双重束缚揭示了国际艺术市场在1989年后赋予中国男性先锋价值，与1995年前后“女性艺术”兴起之间的平行关系——那一年北京主办联合国第四次世界妇女大会。在围绕该会议的西方批评中，中国国家对人权、从而是对女性权利的敌视，艺术上的对应物就是追问为什么中国没有西方那种女性主义艺术。林天苗等艺术家的作品出现在若干这类1990年代展览中，她却总结说：“最终，所有展览似乎只达到了一个效果：证明中国女性能够创作艺术。”[^zh-ch04-59] 在2008年接受霍兰·科特采访时，她否认任何女性主义认同。她也是除泸沽湖“女性部分”之外，少数参与长征的女性艺术家之一。


〔原书 171〕

3) If contemporary artists in China attempt to redefine their feminism by critiquing or distancing themselves from the Maoist approach to women’s liberation, then they cut themselves off from the historical resources of China’s long twentieth-century of feminist activism. If contemporary artists in China attempt to redefine their feminism by drawing on China’s historical resources, then international feminists view them as too statist or too socialist.

3）如果中国当代艺术家试图通过批评毛主义妇女解放路径或与之保持距离来重新定义其女性主义，那么她们便切断了自己与中国漫长二十世纪女性主义行动主义历史资源的联系。如果中国当代艺术家试图利用中国历史资源重新定义女性主义，那么国际女性主义者就会认为她们太国家主义或太社会主义。


〔原书 171〕

This double bind reveals the poverty of an international feminist rhetoric that erases the influence of Chinese Marxist feminism on the thinking of Western feminist theories of the 1960s and 1970s. Take, for example, Julia Kristeva’s About Chinese Women and the zest with which she describes her feminist interlocutors: “These girls who brandish pistols and paintbrushes, who liberate themselves from their husbands and fathers under the portrait of Mao, and leave their children, their calligraphy, their exploits in the field of production, science, or the current ideological campaign, as the sole evidence of their jouissance.”[^en-ch04-60] Visual art in the mode of “these girls who brandish pistols and paintbrushes” is now so abject, propaganda not art or recuperable only through parody, in its international art market status that it must be eradicated as precursor to contemporary feminist art practices.

这一双重束缚揭示了国际女性主义修辞的贫乏，它抹除了中国马克思主义女性主义对1960和1970年代西方女性主义理论的影响。例如朱莉娅·克里斯蒂娃的《中国妇女》，以及她描述其女性主义对话者时的热情：“这些手持手枪和画笔的姑娘，在毛泽东画像下从丈夫和父亲那里解放出来，把自己的孩子、书法，以及在生产、科学或当前意识形态运动领域的功绩，留作她们享乐的唯一证据。”[^zh-ch04-60] “这些手持手枪和画笔的姑娘”式的视觉艺术，如今在国际艺术市场地位中如此低贱——是宣传而非艺术，或只有通过戏仿才可挽救——以致它作为当代女性主义艺术实践前身的地位也必须被抹去。


〔原书 171〕

At Lugu Lake, Lei Yan and Huang Ru drew on precisely these historical resources, in comic, sincere, and critical ways, yet work such as theirs rarely circulates outside of China.

在泸沽湖，雷燕和黄茹恰恰动用了这些历史资源，以喜剧性、真诚而批判的方式；然而她们这样的作品很少在中国以外流通。


〔原书 171〕

4) If Chinese female artists continue to work in socialist genres, such as socialist realist painting, then they identify with the patriarchal order of the state, which liberated them in name but not in action. If Chinese female artists attempt to redefine their art practice through dialogue with the Western archive of feminist art from the 1960s and 1970s, then they are seen as latecomers, less advanced, in need of feminist tutelage or rescue by the West.

4）如果中国女性艺术家继续使用社会主义类型，如社会主义现实主义绘画，那么她们便认同了国家的父权秩序——这个秩序在名义上而非实际上解放了她们。如果中国女性艺术家试图通过与1960和1970年代西方女性主义艺术档案对话来重新定义艺术实践，那么她们就会被视为后来者、不那么先进，需要西方的女性主义教导或拯救。


〔原书 171, 172〕

Unlike the reworking of socialist image making practices by Lei and Huang, the site-specific installation and performance pieces at Lugu Lake by Li Shurui, Su Ruya, and Song Yangping draw on transnationally circulating, postmodern modes of art making. This generic engagement with the cosmopolitan sphere of art, even though grounded in resolutely local concerns and aesthetics, opens them up to being labeled as belated, of modeling themselves after the site-specificity of Chicago’s Womanhouse thirty years later.

与雷燕、黄茹对社会主义图像制作实践的改造不同，李姝睿、苏茹娅和宋雁萍在泸沽湖的场域特定装置与行为作品，动用了跨国流通的后现代艺术制作模式。这种通过艺术类型参与世界主义艺术领域的方式，尽管扎根于坚定的地方关切与美学，却使她们被贴上迟来者的标签，被视为三十年后模仿芝加哥《女人屋》场域特定性的效仿者。


〔原书 172〕

This double bind opens the door to instances in which Western curators have organized exhibits of Chinese “women’s art” that locates the empowerment of Chinese women in gallery and publication spaces outside of China, often under statements such as “there has been no feminist movement in China comparable to that in the West.”[^en-ch04-61] An example of the extreme end of this phenomenon is the following gloss from the 2002 exhibit Femininity in Contemporary Asian Art, curated by Patricia Karetzky for galleries at City College of New York and Bard College: “In communication as well, women in Asia are set apart from those in Western society in their general reticence to interact in mixed company.... Their conversation is measured, their voices childlike in pitch and simple in verbal expression. These cultural restraints on female social behavior are the result of traditional Asian values. The women in this exhibition have experienced Western style freedom of expression and as a result are aware of the varied cultural paradigms of feminine behavior and ideas of femininity.”[^en-ch04-62]

这一双重束缚为以下情况打开大门：西方策展人组织中国“女性艺术”展览，把中国女性的赋权定位于中国境外的画廊和出版物空间，往往以“中国没有可与西方相比的女性主义运动”之类声明为前提。[^zh-ch04-61] 该现象极端一端的例子，是帕特里夏·卡雷茨基（Patricia Karetzky）为纽约城市学院和巴德学院画廊策划的2002年展览《当代亚洲艺术中的女性气质》中的如下说明：“在交流方面也是如此，亚洲女性与西方社会女性不同，她们普遍不愿在男女混合的场合交往……她们的谈吐有分寸，声调像孩童般尖细，言语表达简单。这些对女性社会行为的文化约束，是亚洲传统价值观的结果。本次展览中的女性体验过西方式的表达自由，因此意识到女性行为与女性气质观念的不同文化范式。”[^zh-ch04-62]


〔原书 172〕

5) If Chinese feminist art is posited as something with local roots and concerns and resistant to Western interpretation, then it does not circulate overseas and accrue the value conferred by international recognition, such as exhibition in “world-class” Western museums or auction at Sotheby’s. If Chinese feminist art is posited as an outgrowth of cross-border artistic and intellectual exchange, then it tends to be seen as simply a local, particular instantiation of the “universal” Western model.

5）如果中国女性主义艺术被设定为有地方根源和关切、抵制西方阐释，那么它就不会在海外流通，也无法获得国际承认所赋予的价值，例如在“世界级”西方博物馆展出或在苏富比拍卖。如果中国女性主义艺术被设定为跨境艺术与思想交流的产物，那么它往往只被视为“普遍”西方模式的地方、特殊实例。


〔原书 172〕

The depth of local knowledge—regarding ethnic classification in China, the development of tourist economies as part of post-Mao market reform, and Han imaginaries of the nation’s ethnic nationalities—fundamental to a nuanced understanding of pieces such as Sun Guojuan’s Stuck to You or Zhang Lun’s Lugu Lake–Happy Existence may present a challenge for international audiences. But these cosmopolitan art experiments, which started, after all, from their own nuanced understanding of local knowledge such as “who is Judy Chicago” and “what is Womanhouse,” also challenge a Western-centered version of cosmopolitanism. Being seen as simply a local, particular instantiation of the “universal” Western model is exactly what the Chinese artists at Lugu Lake resisted in their use of copyright as a situational art piece. Their manifesto responded to and attempted to undo this last double bind.

关于中国民族分类、后毛泽东市场改革中旅游经济的发展，以及汉族对国家少数民族想象的深层地方知识，对于细致理解孙国娟《粘住你》或张伦《泸沽湖——快乐的存在》等作品至关重要，却可能对国际观众构成挑战。但这些世界主义艺术实验毕竟始于她们对“谁是朱迪·芝加哥”“什么是《女人屋》”等地方知识的细致理解，也挑战了以西方为中心的世界主义版本。被视为“普遍”西方模式的地方、特殊实例，正是泸沽湖中国艺术家通过把著作权用作情境艺术作品所抵制的。她们的宣言回应并试图拆解这最后一种双重束缚。


〔原书 173〕

Copyright as Situational Art, as Feminist Intervention

作为情境艺术的著作权，作为女性主义介入


〔原书 173〕

The manifesto presented via Lu Jie to Judy Chicago on the artists’ second day in Lugu Lake represents debates that had been brewing long before Chicago arrived in China. The document’s final form, distilled in hours of contentious, late-night discussion, likewise represents a momentary crystallization of the artists’ ongoing thought processes and experiments with materials at hand, in this case, the language of copyright, authorship, and intellectual property circulating widely in China at the time. The manifesto as contract, requiring that all parties become signatories, served as a means of channeling grievances against the interlocking double binds that positioned Chinese women artists at the margins of Chinese contemporary art and global feminist art. Through their presentation of it to Lu and Chicago, they subverted the smooth unfolding of the curatorial plan envisioned by either figure. Although Lu Jie returned to the historical event of the Long March to assert the originality of Chinese cultural production and its cosmopolitan influence, he did so through the assumption of a leadership position that rankled those whom he rallied to the cause. In his negotiation with the artists about the issues they raised, he ended up lecturing them about his responsibilities as a curator. His ironic adoption of Communist political language slid into the register of hardened official rhetoric. Judy Chicago performed her assigned role of pedagogical feminist authority, which aligned with the teaching style she developed in the early 1970s as an instructor in the Feminist Art Programs at Fresno State College and California Institute of the Arts.[^en-ch04-63] Her encounter with Chinese artists at Lugu Lake, however, was not one with students, but women who saw themselves as peers with different yet valuable knowledge. They, in turn, enacted an oppositional politics, a radical questioning of authority that drew on Maoist revolutionary tradition. Yet, in the moment of China’s linkage with transnational capitalism, their challenge to authority came in a claim to authorship rights.

在艺术家们抵达泸沽湖的第二天，通过卢杰呈交给朱迪·芝加哥的宣言，代表了在芝加哥来华之前早已酝酿的辩论。文件最终形式在数小时充满争议的深夜讨论中凝练而成，同样代表艺术家持续思考过程与手头材料实验的短暂结晶——在此，材料就是当时在中国广泛流通的著作权、作者身份和知识产权语言。宣言作为合同，要求各方签署，成为宣泄不满的渠道，针对的是把中国女性艺术家置于中国当代艺术和全球女性主义艺术边缘的相互交织的双重束缚。通过向卢杰和芝加哥呈交宣言，她们颠覆了两人各自设想的策展计划的平滑展开。尽管卢杰回到长征历史事件，以主张中国文化生产的原创性及其世界主义影响，但他这样做时所采取的领袖位置，却令被号召者恼怒。在与艺术家协商她们提出的问题时，他最终向她们讲授自己作为策展人的责任。他讽刺性地挪用共产党政治语言，滑入僵硬的官方修辞语调。朱迪·芝加哥扮演了分配给她的女性主义教育权威角色，这符合她1970年代初在弗雷斯诺州立学院和加州艺术学院女性主义艺术项目任教师时形成的教学风格。[^zh-ch04-63] 然而，她在泸沽湖与中国艺术家的相遇不是与学生，而是与那些视自己为同行、拥有不同而有价值知识的女性。她们反过来实施一种对抗政治，一种借用毛主义革命传统对权威的激进质疑。然而，在中国与跨国资本主义接轨的时刻，她们对权威的挑战以著作权主张的形式出现。


〔原书 173, 174〕

They issued their manifesto approximately one decade after Deng Xiaoping’s “tour of the south” in January 1992, an official turn toward accelerated marketization and privatization. Shortly after, China became a signatory to the Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works. As Ariana Hernández-Reguant describes in her work on the late socialist art industry in Cuba, European powers established this convention in 1886 during an initial stage of decolonization, especially of the Spanish empire, to protect ownership of scientific and artistic works developed in a colonial context.[^en-ch04-64] Indigenous knowledge had contributed significantly to “Western” products ranging from pharmaceuticals to painting styles, yet the modernist regime of intellectual property erased these non-Western linkages and the role of copying in innovation and creativity. Cultural borders were inscribed under the philosophical banners of civilization and possessive individualism, with citizens invested with rights and duties under the nation-state. Modern, Western jurisprudence also uniquely privileged intellectual labor over manual labor by granting creative workers property rights over their ideas, a practice antithetical to socialism’s commitment to collectivism and rejected by countries like the People’s Republic of China until post-1992 market integration. At the end of the millennium, as China prepared to enter the World Trade Organization, officials revised national laws, including those concerning copyright enforcement, to conform to WTO regulations. The encounter between Judy Chicago and Chinese artists took place less than one year after China’s official entry to the WTO. Of the persistent criticism of China as pirate nation, Laikwan Pang observes that the international property rights regime fosters culturalist myths of original and counterfeit: “The legitimate commodity has an author, while the pirated product does not. If China is seen as world pirate, the country then lacks an author/subject position in the international community proper.”[^en-ch04-65] The prominence of copyright discourse in public debate about China’s global status seeped into the Lugu Lake manifesto assertion of a Chinese author/subject position in relation to Judy Chicago as stand-in for global feminist art.

她们发表宣言大约在邓小平1992年1月“南方之行”十年后——那是官方转向加速市场化与私有化的时刻。此后不久，中国成为《保护文学和艺术作品伯尔尼公约》签署国。正如阿里亚娜·埃尔南德斯-雷关特（Ariana Hernández-Reguant）在其关于古巴晚期社会主义艺术产业的研究中所描述，欧洲列强于1886年在去殖民化初期——尤其是西班牙帝国去殖民化——制定该公约，以保护在殖民语境中发展的科学与艺术作品的所有权。[^zh-ch04-64] 从药品到绘画风格，原住民知识对“西方”产品有重大贡献，但现代主义知识产权制度抹除了这些非西方联系，以及复制在创新和创造中的作用。文化边界在文明和占有式个人主义的哲学旗帜下被铭刻，公民在民族国家下被赋予权利与义务。现代西方法理学还赋予智力劳动高于体力劳动的独特特权，赋予创意工作者对其观念的财产权；这种做法与社会主义对集体主义的承诺相悖，也被中华人民共和国等国拒绝，直到1992年后市场一体化。千禧年之交，中国准备加入世界贸易组织时，官员修订国家法律，包括著作权执法相关法律，以符合WTO规定。朱迪·芝加哥与中国艺术家的相遇发生在中国正式入世不到一年后。针对中国作为盗版国家的持续批评，彭丽君（Laikwan Pang）观察到，国际知识产权制度助长关于原创与伪造的文化主义神话：“合法商品有作者，盗版产品则没有。如果中国被视为世界盗版者，那么这个国家在国际共同体中便缺乏作者／主体位置。”[^zh-ch04-65] 著作权话语在中国全球地位公共辩论中的突出地位，渗入泸沽湖宣言，主张中国作者／主体相对于作为全球女性主义艺术替身的朱迪·芝加哥的位置。


〔原书 174, 175〕

Lisa Rofel has argued that the quest of the Chinese state to “fold economic reform into neoliberal institutions such as the WTO” creates an environment in which individuals learn to desire the possession of one’s self and the intellectual labor associated with that self, thus leading to self-regulation of the subject.[^en-ch04-66] While the Chinese artists at Lugu Lake were invested in the neoliberal idea of laying claim to the product of their own knowledge and labor, they also worked from a Long March–inspired tradition of revolutionary, oppositional politics to defend a collective desire for recognition as artists who are not exploited as symbolic resources but who themselves act as authors of symbols. They do not take up copyright itself as something to defend or attack; rather, it becomes a rich semiotic form that helps them address the problem of the interlocking double binds that constrain them. It is as a collective, in a collaboratively produced document, that they assert possession of an individual self. They do so to resist being subsumed under someone else’s authority, one they believe does not have their collective interest at heart. Their adoption of the global language of copyright serves as a critical response to versions of feminism imposed on them by others—by Judy Chicago, Lu Jie, or the Chinese state. Their efforts against being authoritatively framed by someone else included persuading me to document their activities in a way they believed would be more on their terms than what Lu Jie and his team recorded. In the same guerrilla fashion, they also documented and presented their interpretation of the encounter that had taken place in Luoshui. Upon returning from Lugu Lake, Kunming-based artists Fu Liya and Sun Guojuan organized an exhibition at the Yunnan Art Academy, where they displayed written and photographic records of the journey to Lugu Lake, the events that transpired, and artworks completed on site. The exhibit ran from August 4–8, 2002, and an estimated four hundred people came to view it.

罗丽莎论证，中国国家“把经济改革纳入WTO等新自由主义制度”的追求，创造了一种环境，个人在其中学会渴望拥有自我及与自我相关的智力劳动，从而导致主体的自我规训。[^zh-ch04-66] 泸沽湖的中国艺术家虽然投入于主张自身知识与劳动产品的新自由主义观念，却也借助受长征启发的革命性对抗政治传统，以捍卫一种集体欲望：被承认为艺术家，不被当作象征资源剥削，而是自己作为符号的作者。她们并不把著作权本身当作要捍卫或攻击的对象；相反，它成为一种丰富的符号形式，帮助她们处理约束自己的相互交织的双重束缚。她们是在一份合作生产的文件中，作为一个集体，主张对个体自我的占有。她们这样做，是为了抵制被纳入他人的权威——她们相信那并不把她们的集体利益放在心上。她们采用全球通行的著作权语言，批判性地回应朱迪·芝加哥、卢杰或中国国家等他人强加给她们的女性主义版本。她们反对被别人权威地框定，努力还包括说服我以她们认为更符合自身意愿的方式记录活动，而不是卢杰团队所记录的那样。她们以同样的游击方式，记录并呈现自己对落水村相遇的诠释。从泸沽湖回来后，昆明艺术家付丽雅和孙国娟在云南艺术学院组织了一场展览，展出前往泸沽湖的书面与摄影记录、发生的事件，以及现场完成的作品。展览于2002年8月4日至8日举行，估计有四百人前来观看。


〔原书 175, 176〕

Judy Chicago at Lugu Lake was not a unique phenomenon. As she asserted there, “Other women have done Womanhouses all over the world.” She has served as an inspiration to female artists around the world, yet the way she is brought into “other” locations often positions her as central to a canon of feminist art that starts with the West and then attempts to fold non-Western artists into its narrative. Artists involved in these projects have similarly resisted this after-the-fact, enfolding move, in ways that draw on culturally specific histories of art, gender, and feminism. For example, Judy Chicago joined Taiwanese, Korean, and Japanese women artists in the 1997–1998 *Lord of the Rim: In Herself/For Herself* exhibit, held in the small northern Taiwanese city of Hsin Chuang. In a more polite politics of acknowledgement and detachment, the participating Asian artists carried out their own site-specific work focusing on local women laborers in this industrial textile city, exploring gender, class, and ethnicity in the context of Pacific Rim industrialization, militarism/imperialism, and transnational trade. In Ying-Ying Chien’s analysis of the exhibit, the “minor” transnational networks explored by the artists involved did not need to be mediated by or disseminated through the metropolitan West. Their work instead made Chicago’s inclusion in the exhibit peripheral: “In one corner of the *Lord of the Rim* exhibit space there runs continuously a video about Judy Chicago called ‘Women’s House,’ which takes its inspiration from concepts and imagery of a woman’s art that Chicago developed in the 1970s; this quiet full flowering in 1990s Taiwan-Hsin Chuang may well have exceeded what Chicago expected to find here.”[^en-ch04-67] The artists who participated in site six of *The Long March* similarly attest to the need for radical reformation of what constitutes the “global” feminist art canon, so that it allows for the multiple historical contingencies through which feminist artists and artwork come into being.[^en-ch04-68] Disavowing a unifying project of feminism is not a sign of failure but of the ongoing debate and critical reflection at the heart of feminist thought and intervention.

朱迪·芝加哥在泸沽湖并非独特现象。正如她在那里所宣称的，“世界各地的其他女性也做过《女人屋》。”她一直是世界各地女性艺术家的灵感来源，但她被带入“其他”地点的方式，往往把她置于从西方开始的女性主义艺术经典中心，然后试图把非西方艺术家纳入其叙事。参与这些项目的艺术家同样抵制这种事后纳入，方式动用了文化特定的艺术、性别和女性主义历史。例如，朱迪·芝加哥参加了1997至1998年在台湾北部小城新庄举办的《边缘之主：在她自身／为她自身》展览，与台湾、韩国和日本女性艺术家一起。亚洲参展艺术家以一种更礼貌的承认与疏离政治，开展自己的场域特定作品，聚焦这座纺织工业城市的本地女工，在环太平洋工业化、军国主义／帝国主义与跨国贸易语境中探讨性别、阶级和族裔。在简瑛瑛（Ying-Ying Chien）对展览的分析中，艺术家所探索的“次要”跨国网络无需通过西方大都市来中介或传播。她们的作品反而使芝加哥在展览中的存在变得边缘：“在《边缘之主》展览空间的一个角落，持续放映着一部关于朱迪·芝加哥的录像，名为《女人屋》，其灵感来自芝加哥1970年代发展的女性艺术观念与意象；这场1990年代台湾新庄的安静盛放，很可能超出了芝加哥在此地所期待见到的。”[^zh-ch04-67] 参与《长征》第六站的艺术家同样证明，需要彻底改革“全球”女性主义艺术经典的构成，使其容纳女性主义艺术家和作品得以生成的多种历史偶然。[^zh-ch04-68] 否弃一个统一的女性主义计划，不是失败的标志，而是处于女性主义思想与介入核心的持续辩论与批判反思的标志。


〔原书 176〕

The artists in the Feminist Sight Lines chapters to follow exhibit exactly this kind of ongoing reflection. They excavate, in their work and life histories, the institutions and sociohistorical processes that made them as artists and women. Their critical historiographical consciousness, cultivated by being on art world peripheries, unhinges woman from the literal and figurative work she has performed for the nation in modern and contemporary art. Their attempts to move in, through, and outside of dominant ideologies about women respond to the control exerted by interlocking double binds. My encounters with them likewise shifted my understanding of feminist art, from a label for a particular object, event, or project to an epistemological field of practice. Their aesthetics respond to the state socialist legacy of monumentality in Chinese contemporary art through an emphasis on ephemerality: of life, of art, of archival fact. They address the problematic of art as monument, through explorations of a genre like large-scale history painting, of a cultural symbol like the Great Wall, or of an event like the Long March. They remember loss and erasure and call into question an impulse to monumentality, on the scale of the nation, premised on disappearance.

随后“女性主义视线”各章中的艺术家，恰恰展现了这种持续反思。她们在作品与生活史中发掘造就她们作为艺术家和女性的机构与社会历史过程。她们在艺术界边缘培养的批判性历史编纂意识，把女人从她在现代与当代艺术中为国家承担的实际与象征性劳动中松脱。她们试图进入、穿越并走出关于女性的主导意识形态，回应相互交织的双重束缚所施加的控制。我与她们的相遇同样改变了我对女性主义艺术的理解：它不再是一个特定物品、事件或项目的标签，而是一个认识论实践领域。她们的美学通过强调短暂性——生命、艺术、档案事实的短暂性——回应中国当代艺术中的国家社会主义纪念碑性遗产。她们通过探索大型历史画之类类型、长城之类文化象征，或长征之类事件，处理艺术作为纪念碑的问题。她们记住失落与抹除，并质疑一种以消失为前提、以国家为尺度的纪念碑性冲动。

When radical women divorced their husbands, they could lose leadership positions. For example, as detailed in Gilmartin, when Xiang Jingyu left Cai Hesen, older brother of Cai Chang, she was removed from her directorship of the Women’s Bureau and sent to Moscow for further “study” in 1925. [^en-ch04-68]: In 2010, the Tate Modern in London, one of the most influential art museums in the world, displayed a timeline of major artistic movements and figures from the twentieth and twentieth-first centuries. All of the artists listed under its plotting of “Feminism,” a movement assigned to the 1960s, hailed from dominant Euro-American centers. The absence of contemporaries from other locations reflects a set of historiographical and political problems around the institutionalization of feminist art in the West. This occlusion of feminist art and artists from non-Western contexts was also in evidence at the 2009 exhibition *Elles* at the Centre Pompidou in Paris, whose curators proposed a revision of the category of contemporary art by representing it exclusively through works by women artists in the museum’s permanent collection. Contemporaneous attempts to survey feminist art practice on a more global scale partially challenged the Tate and Pompidou narratives. *Global Feminisms* (2007, Brooklyn Museum of Art) and *Wack! Art and the Feminist Revolution* (2007, MoCA, Los Angeles and PS1, New York City) invoked the figure of the postcolonial or non-Western woman artist, even as their curators subsumed multiple histories of feminism within a single overarching narrative centered in the West.
