When a right-wing student punched him in the face, Beuys responded by letting blood drip from his nose, displaying his wound as he saluted the crowd with a crucifix held up in his other hand. Photographed again in her apartment for this experiment in connecting her personal life to art via the historical avant-garde, He Chengyao performs Beuys’s spontaneous ritualistic action, although she stands nude and confronts an invisible audience. In *A Salute to Mama (With Respect to Joseph Beuys*) (figure 6.09), her raised arm suggests less the ironic fascist gesture of Beuys’s salute and more of a grasping after the unseen, the ephemeral, spirits that haunt. She holds in her other hand not a crucifix but a framed photograph of her mother, who as a reproduction becomes a sacrificial talisman that she also physically reembodies by stripping bare. He Chengyao’s copies are mimetic in that they obsessively and bodily reproduce mass spectacularity, family history, and the historical avant-garde, in order to put the self in differential tension with a complex overlay of Others. She performs a kind of “ethnographic surrealism,” in James Clifford’s terms, that reverses the historical direction of French Dada-ists rummaging around for collage materials at the Musée de l’Homme.[^en-ch06-35]

何成瑶随后转向约瑟夫·博伊斯，宣称信奉他“艺术疗愈伤口”的信念，并对他的一个自发“行动”进行个人重演。1964年在德国亚琛技术学院举行的激浪派艺术家节上，博伊斯表演了一件作品，激怒了几名观众，他们冲上舞台。一名右翼学生朝他脸上打了一拳，博伊斯让鼻血滴下，展示伤口，同时用另一只手举起十字架向人群致意。何成瑶再次在自己的公寓中接受拍摄，进行这一通过历史先锋派把个人生活与艺术联系起来的实验；她表演博伊斯的自发仪式行为，但赤身裸体，面对不可见的观众。在《向妈妈致敬（致约瑟夫·博伊斯）》（图6.09）中，她举起的手臂与其说暗示博伊斯致意中讽刺性的法西斯手势，不如说是在抓取不可见的、短暂的、萦绕的魂灵。她另一只手拿的不是十字架，而是母亲的一张装框照片；照片作为复制品成为牺牲护身符，她又通过脱光衣服在身体上重新赋形。何成瑶的复制是一种模仿：执念般、身体性地复制大众奇观、家庭历史和历史先锋派，以使自我与层层叠叠的复杂他者保持差异张力。她实施的是詹姆斯·克利福德（James Clifford）所谓一种“民族志超现实主义”，颠倒了法国达达主义者在人类博物馆翻找拼贴材料的历史方向。[^zh-ch06-35]


〔原书 232〕

![*图6.09　何成瑶，《向妈妈致敬（致约瑟夫·博伊斯）》，2001年。行为。摄影：Han Lei。艺术家惠允。*](web/assets/ch06-b100.jpg)

FIG 6.09 He Chengyao, *A Salute to Mama (With Respect to Joseph Beuys*), 2001. Performance. Photography credit: Han Lei. Courtesy of the artist.

*图6.09　何成瑶，《向妈妈致敬（致约瑟夫·博伊斯）》，2001年。行为。摄影：Han Lei。艺术家惠允。*


〔原书 233〕

Performance/Image/Sign

行为／图像／符号


〔原书 233〕

He Chengyao’s early photographed performances led her in 2002—approximately one year after *Opening the Great Wall*—to stage a performance that fully embodied, rather than just testified to, the experience of her mother at the hands of the Lei Feng uncles who tried to cure her with acupuncture. For *99 Needles* (plate 16), He Chengyao asked a friend trained in Chinese medicine to prepare her body for a set of performance images. She wanted her entire body pierced with ninety-nine acupuncture needles. She arrived at the clinic where her friend worked during the lunch hour so that they could complete the work without interference from doctors or patients who might question the appropriateness of this “treatment.” The night before her period had begun, and her friend warned her of the contraindication against acupuncture during menstruation. He Chengyao insisted on going through with the plan. In fact, this violation seemed in keeping with the piece. Several other friends were on the scene to record the process through video and photography. After all of the needles had been inserted, somewhat hastily because of the excessive number requested and the restriction of time, He Chengyao walked outside and stood against a gray brick wall for a series of photographs. One needle had been imprecisely inserted, and she began to bleed from a spot above her right wrist. She became increasingly light-headed and finally fainted, crumpling to the ground, before the doctor rushed over to begin removing the needles.

何成瑶早期摄影行为引导她在2002年——大约《开放长城》一年后——实施一场完全具身化、而非仅仅见证母亲在雷锋叔叔们手中被针灸治疗的经历的行为。为《九十九根针》（图版16），何成瑶请一位受过中医训练的朋友为她的身体作准备，以拍摄一组行为图像。她想让全身扎上九十九根针灸针。她在午休时间来到朋友工作的诊所，以便不受医生或病人干扰地完成，因为他们可能质疑这种“治疗”是否恰当。前一天晚上她月经来了，朋友警告经期针灸的禁忌。何成瑶坚持按计划进行。事实上，这种违禁似乎与作品一致。另外几位朋友在场，用录像和摄影记录过程。所有针都插入后——由于要求的数量过多、时间有限，动作有些仓促——何成瑶走到外面，背靠灰砖墙站立，拍了一系列照片。一根针插入不精确，她右腕上方开始流血。她越来越头晕，最终昏倒，瘫倒在地，医生冲过来开始拔针。


〔原书 233〕

One criticism of performance art in the Mainland has focused on the narrowness of its immediate audience, usually made up of a few art circle insiders. The “performance” circulates mostly as photographic reproduction, entering domestic and international image economies in this mediated form. He Chengyao’s photographs embrace this problem as at the heart of any attempt to express the expressionless, becoming sign *at the same time* the sign is deployed to probe the trauma of thus being robbed of expression.

对大陆行为艺术的一种批评聚焦于其直接观众狭窄，通常只有几个艺术圈内部人。“行为”主要以照片复制形式流通，以这种中介形式进入国内和国际图像经济。何成瑶的照片把这一问题当作任何试图表达失去表达能力之物的尝试的核心：成为符号的同时，符号也被用来探查由此被剥夺表达的创伤。


〔原书 233, 234〕

Her performance photographs might be read as “typical” representations of the oppression, with particularly gendered dimensions, suffered under modern political movements in China. However, her resolutely transnational dialogue with masculinist avant-garde forms injects her art practice with an awareness of how women’s bodies (and lives) get caught within and between socialist and capitalist systems of sign making, reproduction, and circulation. Her images extend the critique that Lingzhen Wang has made about the limitations of the “exposure literature,” “literature of the wounded,” or “literature of reflection” that emerged after Mao’s death, creating a public space for reflection on the excesses of past political movements, especially the Cultural Revolution.[^en-ch06-36] Wang argues that these works isolated the impact of politics on individual lives as the only realm of personal experience legitimate for public airing. Gendered forms of private oppression—stories about unhappy marriages, domestic abuse, or expressions of female sexual desire deemed inappropriate—did not fulfill the requirements for politically significant content. He Chengyao’s work registers such trauma, at the level of the body, caused by attempts to separate the impossibly intertwined personal experiences of the public and political, particularly when image economies of different eras interacted under the cultural conditions of late socialism–late liberalism that characterized new millennial China. Her performance photographs reveal how gender underpins nationalism and globalization, but also the contradictions that arise in the zone of encounter of Chinese contemporary art.

她的行为照片可以被解读为人们在中国现代政治运动中所遭受压迫的“典型”再现，其中带有特别的性别维度。然而，她与男性主义先锋形式坚决的跨国对话，为她的艺术实践注入一种意识：女性的身体（和生命）如何陷入社会主义与资本主义符号制造、复制和流通体系之内及之间。她的图像延伸了王玲珍对“暴露文学”“伤痕文学”或“反思文学”局限性的批评——这些文学在毛泽东去世后出现，创造了一个反思过去政治运动——尤其是文化大革命——中种种过激行为的公共空间。[^zh-ch06-36] 王玲珍论证，这些作品把政治对个人生活的影响孤立为唯一可合法公开的个人经验领域。性别化的私人压迫——不幸福婚姻、家庭暴力或被视为不恰当的女性性欲表达——不符合具有政治意义内容的要求。何成瑶的作品在身体层面记录了这种创伤，其成因是将公共与政治的不可分交织的个人经验强行分离，尤其当不同时代的图像经济在晚期社会主义—晚期自由主义文化条件下——这是千禧年中国新时期的特征——相互作用时。她的行为照片揭示性别如何支撑民族主义和全球化，也揭示中国当代艺术相遇地带中产生的矛盾。


〔原书 234〕

![*图6.10　何成瑶，《幻象》，2002年。行为。摄影：刘辉。艺术家惠允。*](web/assets/ch06-b105.jpg)

FIG 6.10 He Chengyao, *Illusion*, 2002. Performance. Photography credit: Liu Hui. Courtesy of the artist.

*图6.10　何成瑶，《幻象》，2002年。行为。摄影：刘辉。艺术家惠允。*


〔原书 234, 235〕

For He Chengyao, however, performance as a cathartic form of release and healing remained vital. In February 2002, several months before *99 Needles*, she staged another piece at the China Art Archives and Warehouse, where the previous year she had stripped off her top and descended a staircase for *With Respect to Duchamp. Illusion* (figure 6.10) took place outside, in an open courtyard. For the performance, she wore a billowing hand-sewn white robe that hung to her ankles. She walked barefoot across pale winter grass toward a long grey brick wall. Across from the wall stood a male friend. He held close to his chest a heart-shaped dressing-table mirror, with an iris and a flying bird etched on its surface. The mirror reflected sunlight onto the wall. The slightest manipulation of the mirror in his hands sent the spot of light skittering over the bricks. It landed first on He Chengyao’s face, causing her to squint. It then moved across her body. She grabbed and patted her chest as she tried to catch it, and then caressed her side as it slid down her leg to the ground. The small sunlike spot moved erratically across the wall, and she chased after it, jumping up, crouching down, frantically slapping the bricks, speeding up and slowing down according to its movements. The white robe flew, ghostlike, behind her. Sometimes instead of pursuing the light, she tried to evade it, dodging away from or cowering beneath its capricious, perpetual motion. The recording of a Buddhist meditation chant, accompanied by drums, bells, and zither, played in the background, mixing with birdsong, clicking camera shutters, and the rumble of construction trucks and workers’ shouts on the other side of the wall. He Chengyao began to audibly pant from her exertions. Almost ten minutes into the game, the light returned to its starting point, illuminating her face. She came to a standstill and bowed her head. In documentary photographs of the performance, her figure registers only as a white blur of motion in front of the towering grey wall, an ephemeral presence on the verge of disappearing, or an active force in reordering the pain and pleasure of being in the world.

然而，对何成瑶而言，行为作为宣泄性的释放和疗愈形式仍然至关重要。2002年2月，即《九十九根针》几个月前，她在北京中国艺术文件仓库实施另一件作品；前一年她曾在那里脱掉上衣、走下楼梯，完成《向杜尚致敬》。《幻象》（图6.10）在户外露天庭院进行。她穿着一件飘动的、手工缝制的白色长袍，长及脚踝。她赤脚走过苍白的冬草，走向一堵长长的灰砖墙。墙对面站着一位男性朋友。他把一面心形梳妆镜紧贴胸前，镜面刻着一朵鸢尾花和一只飞鸟。镜子把阳光反射到墙上。他手中镜子稍有移动，光斑就在砖上滑动。它先落在何成瑶脸上，使她眯起眼睛，然后移过她的身体。她抓握、拍打自己的胸口，试图捉住光，随后当光斑滑下她的腿落到地面时，她抚摸身体侧面。小小的太阳般光斑在墙上不规则移动，她追逐它，跳起、蹲下、疯狂拍打砖墙，随它的运动加速、减速。白袍像幽灵般在她身后飞扬。有时她不去追光，而是试图躲开它，闪避或蜷伏在其反复无常、永不停歇的运动下方。背景播放着伴随鼓、钟和古筝的佛教诵经录音，与鸟鸣、相机快门声，以及墙另一边建筑卡车轰鸣和工人喊声混在一起。何成瑶开始明显喘息。游戏进行近十分钟时，光回到起点，照亮她的脸。她停下来，低下头。在行为的纪实照片中，她的身影只是高耸灰墙前一道因运动而模糊的白色身影，一个濒临消失的短暂存在，或一股重新安排身处世界的痛苦与快乐的活动力量。

This radical shift in attitude toward notions of privacy and shame became central to her developing art practice and body politics of exposure.

[^zh-ch06-15]: 何成瑶是她的真名。我之所以在本章使用真名，只是因为在几个月后她撤回了匿名的请求，并催促我公开她的名字。这种对隐私与羞耻观念的彻底转变，成为她发展中的艺术实践与曝光身体政治的核心。

[^en-ch06-16]: A popular postsocialist discourse on sex characterizes “natural” contemporary sexual expression as liberation from the “unnatural” socialist silencing of sexual desire as bourgeois and therefore politically immoral. The story of He Chengyao’s birth out of wedlock reveals instead a continuity across eras of sexual desire, even outside of established norms, and cautions that the question should not be whether there was more or less sex in different periods but how the specific forms, regulations, and social interpretations of it differ across eras.

[^zh-ch06-16]: 一种流行的后社会主义性话语，把"自然的"当代性表达描述为对社会主义"不自然的"性欲压抑的解放——后者曾把性欲视为资产阶级的、因而在政治上不道德的。何成瑶非婚出生的故事，反而揭示了性欲跨越不同时代的连续性，即使身处既定规范之外；它也提醒我们，问题不应是不同时期的性更多还是更少，而是性的具体形式、规制与社会解释如何在各时代有所不同。

[^en-ch06-17]: The Great Leap Forward, a campaign led by Mao from 1958 to 1961 to rapidly industrialize the country, resulted in widespread famine during the period.

[^zh-ch06-17]: 大跃进是毛泽东自1958年至1961年领导的一场使国家迅速工业化的运动，在期间导致了普遍饥荒。

[^en-ch06-18]: Although He Chengyao refers several times to her family as traditional, their household does not follow conventional descriptions of traditional Chinese kinship organization, in which a model type of patrilineality, patrilocality, and patriarchy privileges the importance of male lineage and emphasizes agnatic relations, those between male kin, above others. For more on gender and kinship, see Croll, *Feminism and Socialism in China*; Johnson, *Women, the Family, and Peasant Revolution in China*; Ono, *Chinese Women in a Century of Revolution*; and Stacey, *Patriarchy and Socialist Revolution in China*. The family in He Chengyao’s account fits more closely an alternative kinship form known as uxorilocal marriage, characterized by a man who marries into a family lineage with no male descendents and takes the surname of his wife. He Chengyao’s father’s residence with his wife and mother-in-law seems, however, based primarily on his wife’s mental illness.

[^zh-ch06-18]: 尽管何成瑶多次称她的家庭是传统的，她的家庭住户结构并不符合对中国传统亲属组织的常规描述。在这种组织的一种典型模式中，父系继嗣、父居制与父权制赋予男性世系首要地位，并强调男性亲属之间的宗族关系高于其他关系。关于性别与亲属关系的更多讨论，见 Croll, *Feminism and Socialism in China*；Johnson, *Women, the Family, and Peasant Revolution in China*；Ono, *Chinese Women in a Century of Revolution*；以及 Stacey, *Patriarchy and Socialist Revolution in China*。何成瑶叙述中的家庭，更接近一种称为入赘婚的替代性亲属形式：男子嫁入没有男性后代的家族世系，并随妻姓。不过，何成瑶的父亲与妻子和岳母同住，似乎主要是出于妻子患有精神疾病。

[^en-ch06-19]: *Tales of Liaozhai* was written by Pu Songling (1640–1715) shortly after the fall of the Ming dynasty and founding of the Qing. The stories are filled with fox-fairies, ghosts, and other spirits who deliver rewards and punishments to good or bad mortals. Pu Songling based his tales on popular legends and folklore and wrote during an era of strict censorship. His retellings of supernatural stories, which he collected or friends sent him, indirectly criticized the rule of the new Manchu rulers.

[^zh-ch06-19]: 《聊斋志异》为蒲松龄（1640—1715）在明朝灭亡、清朝建立后不久所作。这些故事充满狐仙、鬼魂和其他精灵，它们对善恶凡人或赏或罚。蒲松龄以民间传说和民俗为素材，写作于一个审查严苛的时代。他重述自己搜集或友人寄来的神怪故事，间接地批判了新满族统治者的统治。

[^en-ch06-20]: In February 1964 the ccp launched a mass campaign for citizens to “learn from the pla” as exemplars of ideological correctness and technical proficiency, or in sloganistic parlance as “both red and expert.” This political movement emerged from a conflict over the future direction of party-army relations. By the late 1950s increased stratification and professionalism within the army—a move away from the Maoist model of egalitarianism—had led to strained relations between the military and civilians, as well as between commanders and political commissars. After the failed Great Leap Forward, Mao sought to reconsolidate his control over “reactionary” moderates within the party and turned to the pla as a power base outside of the party to support his position. Under Lin Biao’s leadership, the army trend toward professionalism was curtailed through a reassertion of revolutionary values and politics among the troops. For example, in 1963 Lin Biao arranged for publication of *Quotations from Chairman Mao* (the “little red book”) and distributed it widely throughout the military. During the ensuing years of the Cultural Revolution, the pla took on a wider range of administrative and civil functions than ever before, particularly at the local level. Demobilization of troops into the pla’s Production and Construction Corps to work on civilian projects reached a peak in the late 1960s and early 1970s. During this period, ccp leadership called on the pla in contradictory ways, to maintain order *and* to encourage revolutionary activity, so that the military served as an equilibrium force during a period of extreme politics. At times they expected the pla to give training and guidance to Red Guards, and at other times used the pla to control Red Guard radicalism when factional fighting threatened to completely disrupt social order. In 1968 the central government ordered Red Guards to surrender their weapons to the pla, and subsequently used the pla to run classes on university campuses and in industrial enterprises to “reeducate” Red Guards. See Dreyer, *China’s Political System*; Joffe, “The Chinese Army in the Cultural Revolution”; Ruwitch, *Lei Feng and the “Learn from Lei Feng” Campaign of 1963*; and Shichor, “Demobilization.”

[^zh-ch06-20]: 1964年2月，中共发起了一场群众运动，号召公民"学习解放军"，以他们为思想正确、技术过硬的典范，或用口号化的话说，是"又红又专"。这场政治运动源于围绕党军关系未来方向的一场冲突。到1950年代末，军队内部日益加剧的等级化与专业化——偏离毛泽东式的平等主义模式——已使军民关系以及指挥员与政治委员之间的关系趋于紧张。大跃进失败后，毛泽东力图重新巩固对党内"反动"温和派的控制，于是把解放军当作党外的权力基础来支持自己的立场。在林彪领导下，军队的专业化倾向因革命价值与政治在部队中的重申而受到遏制。例如，1963年林彪安排出版《毛主席语录》（"红宝书"），并在军队中广泛分发。在此后的文化大革命岁月里，解放军承担了比以往更广泛的行政与民事职能，尤其是在地方层面。部队复员进入解放军生产建设兵团、从事民用工程，在1960年代末和1970年代初达到高峰。在此期间，中共领导层以相互矛盾的方式调用解放军：既维持秩序，又鼓励革命活动，使军队在一个极端政治的时期充当平衡力量。有时他们期望解放军对红卫兵进行训练和指导，有时又用解放军控制红卫兵的激进主义，因为派系武斗有可能彻底破坏社会秩序。1968年，中央政府命令红卫兵向解放军交出武器，随后又用解放军在大学校园和工业企业开办学习班，"再教育"红卫兵。见 Dreyer, *China's Political System*；Joffe, "The Chinese Army in the Cultural Revolution"；Ruwitch, *Lei Feng and the "Learn from Lei Feng" Campaign of 1963*；以及 Shichor, "Demobilization."

[^en-ch06-21]: “Learn from Lei Feng” became the most famous and long-lived propaganda piece to come out of the general “learn from the pla” campaign, in which individual soldiers and entire pla units were promoted as ideological symbols for national emulation. Lei Feng was a common solider, a son of poor peasants from Hunan, whose posthumously published diary espoused self-sacrificing service to the revolution, country, comrades, and above all Mao Zedong. The Japanese had killed his father, and his mother’s suicide after a rape by her landlord-employer’s son left Lei Feng an orphan, placed in the care of his aunt and uncle. One year after his mother’s suicide, in August 1949, the People’s Liberation Army freed their village, and Lei Feng entered school. He eventually joined the pla and became a squad leader and member of the party, a common soldier who made up for his small size by sheer determination and devotion to the cause. As a servant to the people he declared, “I will be a screw that never rusts and will glitter anywhere I am placed.” In 1962, he died at the age of twenty-two in a truck accident. Immediately after his death, military leaders within the Shenyang army base promoted his story, exhorting soldiers to “study Lei Feng, aspire to Lei Feng, surpass Lei Feng.” By 1963, party leaders published Lei Feng’s diary as a more widespread propaganda tool. The good deeds he recorded in the diary included sending his meager savings to a fellow soldiers’ parents who were devastated by a flood, serving tea and food to officers and recruits, and washing his comrades’ feet and darning their socks after a long march. Many suspect that it was not necessarily the soldier Lei Feng but propaganda writers who penned the famous and possibly fictitious, or at least enhanced, diary that later served to popularize his story of model behavior. See Dreyer, *China’s Political System*, 248; Landsberger, “Lei Feng”; Ruwitch, *Lei Feng and the “Learn from Lei Feng” Campaign of 1963*; Spence, *The Search for Modern China*, 597–99; 727.

[^zh-ch06-21]: "学雷锋"成为这场普遍的"学习解放军"运动中最著名、最长寿的宣传作品；在这场运动中，单个士兵和整个解放军单位被推举为供全国效仿的思想符号。雷锋是一名普通士兵，湖南贫农的儿子。他身后出版的日记宣扬为革命、国家、同志，尤其是为毛泽东自我牺牲的服务。日本人杀害了他的父亲；母亲在被地主雇主的儿子强奸后自杀，使雷锋成为孤儿，由亲属抚养（原文为 aunt and uncle）。母亲自杀一年后，1949年8月，人民解放军解放了他们的村庄，雷锋进入学校。他最终参加解放军，成为班长和党员；这个普通士兵以纯粹的决心和对事业的忠诚弥补了自己身材的矮小。作为人民的勤务员，他宣称："我要做一颗永不生锈的螺丝钉，放到哪里就在哪里闪光。"1962年，他二十二岁时死于一场卡车事故。他死后不久，沈阳军区内部的军队领导人便宣传他的故事，勉励士兵"学雷锋、赶雷锋、超雷锋"。到1963年，党领导人出版了雷锋日记，作为更广泛传播的宣传工具。他在日记中记录的好事包括：把微薄的积蓄寄给一位同志在水灾中遭受重创的父母；为军官和新兵端茶送饭；在长途行军后为战友洗脚、补袜子。许多人怀疑，写下那本著名、可能虚构或至少经过加工的日记的未必是士兵雷锋，而是宣传工作者；这本日记后来使他的模范行为故事广为人知。见 Dreyer, *China's Political System*, 248；Landsberger, "Lei Feng"；Ruwitch, *Lei Feng and the "Learn from Lei Feng" Campaign of 1963*；Spence, *The Search for Modern China*, 597–99; 727。

[^en-ch06-22]: This form of petty entrepreneurship, or *getihu* business, has typically been associated with market reform beginning in the 1980s as distinguished from the centralized command economy under Mao. The seemingly anomalous business run in the 1970s by He Chengyao’s father raises questions about the continuity of local market practices throughout the socialist era, during which getihu were never entirely abolished.

[^zh-ch06-22]: 这种小本经营，或称个体户生意，通常与1980年代开始的市场改革相联系，以区别于毛泽东时代的中央指令经济。何成瑶的父亲在1970年代经营的这门看似反常的生意，提出了关于整个社会主义时期地方市场实践之连续性的问题——在那一时期，个体户从未被完全废除。

[^en-ch06-23]: He Chengyao, e-mail communication.

[^zh-ch06-23]: 何成瑶，电子邮件交流。

[^en-ch06-24]: Stories of women driven mad by traumatic circumstances haunted the traditional Chinese storytelling repertoire. *White-haired Girl*, a folk opera about a victim of landlord oppression who flees to the hills, became one of the Communist eight model plays performed in opera, ballet, and film. Witke, *Comrade Chiang Ch’ing*, 430–32. He Chengyao’s mother, by contrast, experienced her first episode of mental illness after condemnation by her Communist work unit.

[^zh-ch06-24]: 因创伤境遇而发疯的女人的故事，萦绕在中国传统说书曲目中。《白毛女》是一部关于地主压迫的受害者逃入山中的民间歌剧，后来成为共产党八部样板戏之一，以歌剧、芭蕾和电影的形式演出。Witke, *Comrade Chiang Ch'ing*, 430–32。相较之下，何成瑶的母亲是在受到其共产党工作单位的谴责后首次发作精神疾病的。

[^en-ch06-25]: He Chengyao, “In the Mirror.”

[^zh-ch06-25]: He Chengyao, "In the Mirror."

[^en-ch06-26]: In performance works such as Yoko Ono’s *Cut Piece* (1964) and Marina Abramović’s *Rhythm 0* (1974), the artists presented their passive bodies to an audience that responded with increasing aggression. Audience members completely cut away Ono’s clothes with a pair of scissors. Abramović offered a table with seventy-two objects that audience members were allowed to use in any way they chose. The atmosphere of the encounter grew violent over the six hours of the performance.

[^zh-ch06-26]: 在小野洋子的《Cut Piece》（1964）和玛丽娜·阿布拉莫维奇（Marina Abramović）的《节奏0》（1974）等行为作品中，艺术家把自己被动的身体交给观众，而观众的反应越来越具有侵略性。观众用一把剪刀把小野的衣服完全剪掉。阿布拉莫维奇提供了一张桌子，上面摆着七十二件物品，观众可以任意使用。在这场行为持续六小时的过程中，相遇的气氛变得暴力。

[^en-ch06-27]: Caplin, *Andy Warhol: Made in China*.

[^zh-ch06-27]: Caplin, *Andy Warhol: Made in China*。

[^en-ch06-28]: See Wu, *Transience*, 30–35. Mao Zedong is famously said to have declared, “You’re not a real man until you’ve climbed the Great Wall.”

[^zh-ch06-28]: 见 Wu, *Transience*, 30–35。毛泽东有句名言："不到长城非好汉。"

[^en-ch06-29]: In 1988, Marina Abramović, New York-based Yugoslavian self-described “grandmother of performance art,” and her long-time partner Ulay also staged their final piece together on the Great Wall. In *The Great Wall Walk*, they started at opposite ends of the wall and each walked 2,500 kilometers toward each other; they met in the middle and said good-bye.

[^zh-ch06-29]: 1988年，自称"行为艺术祖母"的常驻纽约的南斯拉夫艺术家玛丽娜·阿布拉莫维奇与她长期伴侣乌雷（Ulay），也在长城上实施了他们最后一件共同作品。在《长城行走》中，他们从长城两端出发，各自步行两千五百公里向对方走去；他们在中点相遇，然后道别。

[^en-ch06-31]: Merewether, “The Spectre of Being Human.”

[^zh-ch06-31]: Merewether, "The Spectre of Being Human."

[^zh-ch06-32]: 《下楼梯的裸体，第2号》以 E. 马雷（E. Marey）等人的定格摄影为基础。

[^en-ch06-33]: Tomkins, *Duchamp: A Biography*.

[^en-ch06-35]: Clifford, *The Predicament of Culture*.

## 第七章　被伪装的历史


〔原书 236〕

Seven: Camouflaged Histories

第七章　被伪装的历史


〔原书 236〕

A woman in a camouflage tank top and pants stands on swampy ground with binoculars held to her eyes. The artist Lei Yan appears in this guise in the pair of photographs *What If the Long March Had Been a Women’s Rights Movement*? (figure 4.04) and *What If They Had Been Women*? (figure 4.05) that she created for *The Long March* encounter with Judy Chicago at Lugu Lake. As a former career soldier in the People’s Liberation Army (pla), she does not naively revisit the imagery of the woman soldier so central to Communist revolutionary cultural production. She reinhabits a subjectivity that shaped her life and art in order to review it from the focus afforded by the optical device—the binoculars or camera—she raises to her eyes. With this pair of photographs and the continuation of her *What If* series that followed, Lei Yan activates an image world of women viewing the world anew through binoculars, a complex network of images invoked in the process of looking and making.

一个身穿迷彩背心和迷彩裤的女人站在沼泽地上，双手举着望远镜贴在眼前。艺术家雷燕以这副模样出现在两幅一组的照片《如果长征是一场女权运动？》（图4.04）和《如果他们是女人？》（图4.05）中。这两幅照片是她为"长征"项目在泸沽湖与朱迪·芝加哥相遇而创作的。作为中国人民解放军（PLA）的一名退役职业军人，她并非天真地重访共产主义革命文化生产中如此核心的女兵形象。她重新栖居于一种塑造了她人生与艺术的主体性，以便从她举到眼前的视觉器具——望远镜或相机——所提供的焦点去审视它。通过这两幅照片以及随后延续的《如果》系列，雷燕激活了一个由举着望远镜重新观看世界的女性构成的图像世界，一个在观看与创作过程中被唤起的复杂图像网络。


〔原书 236, 237〕

A woman in a long black skirt and high-collared jacket stands at water’s edge. Strokes of green ink sprout around the hem of her skirt and weave through the pattern on her jacket. The blue of the bow in her hair echoes the gradations of wash tinting water, sky, and distant mountains. Three small sailboats cleave to and accentuate the horizon line. With her back to the viewer, the woman gazes through binoculars, not at the water, boats, or mountains, but upward toward a flying machine in the top right corner. The black-and-white form suggests an airplane, but closer inspection reveals a fantastical abstraction, an assemblage of crosshatched shapes. The wings are not flush with one another. A basket or a net hangs from the undercarriage, with a sandbaglike form dangling down. This illustration (figure 7.01) appeared on the October 1916 cover of *The Women’s Eastern Times* (Funü shibao), a journal published in Shanghai during the first six years of Republican-era China (1911–49). Its new woman on the verge of flight from earth into the heavens stands as one instance in a genealogy of women with binoculars to their eyes.[^en-ch07-1] Twenty some years earlier, Wu Youru, a popular illustrator of urban vignettes for the pictorial supplement to Shanghai’s *Shenbao* newspaper, had depicted three courtesans on an upper balcony “sightseeing” with a pair of binoculars.[^en-ch07-2] Framed by the balcony balustrade, they gaze out from an interior space, over the rooftops of neighboring buildings, toward something beyond the image’s edge. The woman holding the binoculars leans over, tilting her line of sight slightly downward. These elegantly attired “blossoms” of the pleasure quarter display not only their conspicuous consumption of modern technology, but also their visual mastery. They are caught, as they are looked at, in the act of looking. The world-making power of vision, outward and upward, symbolizes women’s move out of the “inner quarters” of traditional Chinese society.

一个身穿黑色长裙、高领上衣的女人站在水边。绿色墨迹从裙摆周围生出，穿行于她上衣的图案之间。她发间蝴蝶结的蓝色，与晕染水面、天空和远山的深浅墨色相互呼应。三只小帆船紧贴并凸显出地平线。女人背对观者，举着望远镜，看的不是水面、船只或群山，而是右上方一架飞行器。那黑白形体像是飞机，细看却是奇异的抽象构成，由一组交叉排线的形状拼合而成。两翼并不齐平，起落架下挂着一只篮子或一张网，还有一个沙袋状的东西垂下来。这幅插图（图7.01）刊于1916年10月《妇女时报》封面。该刊于民国（1911—1949）最初六年间在上海出版。那位即将从大地飞向天空的新女性，构成了"举着望远镜的女人"谱系中的一个实例。[^zh-ch07-1]二十多年前，为上海《申报》图画副刊绘制市井小品的著名画家吴友如，曾描绘过三名妓女站在楼上阳台上，举着一副望远镜"看风景"。[^zh-ch07-2] 她们被阳台栏杆框住，从室内空间向外望去，越过邻近建筑的屋顶，看向图像边缘之外的某物。举望远镜的女子俯身向前，视线微微下倾。这些衣饰优雅的风月场的"花朵"，不仅展示着对现代技术的炫耀性消费，也展示着视觉上的掌控力。她们在被观看的同时，也被捕捉于观看的动作之中。向外、向上的视觉所具有的世界营造之力，象征着女性走出传统中国社会的"内闱"。


〔原书 237〕

![*图7.01　《妇女时报》第20期封面插图，1916年10月。*](web/assets/ch07-b003.jpg)

FIG 7.01 Cover illustration, *Funü shibao* (The women’s eastern times) no. 20, October 1916.

*图7.01　《妇女时报》第20期封面插图，1916年10月。*


〔原书 237, 238〕

During the New Culture movement of the early Republican period, the “woman question” preoccupied reformers in their quest to overturn China’s feudal and colonial history. They saw women as central to the project of modernity, even as they debated how to liberate women and what their role in the new nation would be. Reform efforts simultaneously gave rise to a literary revolution, as authors began to use *baihua*, or vernacular, instead of classical Chinese, which for centuries had preserved literacy as an elite domain. Popular newspapers and magazines flooded the urban market, creating a new reading public. Women became a target audience, and while nationalists discussed the “woman question” often through their desire as humiliated male colonial subjects to emerge on the world stage, female readers and writers articulated their thoughts and stories in these new publications.[^en-ch07-3] The illustration on the October 1916 cover of *The Women’s Eastern Times* presents this aspiring female subject with her power of vision and dreams of flight. Two articles within narrate the heroism of Zhang Xiahun, a young woman who, on attending a Shanghai air show, insisted on flying. She ignored the head of the aviation school, who tried to dissuade her, and proclaimed her flight would “open a new era of Chinese women pilots, forge a new dawn in the history of female bravery, and merit several lines in China’s aviation history.” [^en-ch07-4] When a strong wind arose and caused the plane to crash, she walked away injured but triumphant. This new woman, binoculars aimed toward the horizon, haunts the pair of photographs Lei Yan created almost a century later for *The Long March*. Garbed now in camouflage and black military boots, she stands her ground not on a balcony or at water’s edge but on the battlefield of history.

在民国初年的新文化运动中，"妇女问题"成为改革者力图推翻中国封建与殖民历史的核心关切。他们将女性视为现代性工程的核心，同时也在争论如何解放妇女、妇女在新国家中应扮演何种角色。改革同时催生了一场文学革命：作者们开始使用白话而非文言，而文言几个世纪以来一直使识字成为精英的专属领域。通俗报刊与杂志大量涌入城市市场，造就了新的阅读公众。女性成为目标读者；民族主义者讨论"妇女问题"，往往出于身为受辱的男性殖民臣民、渴望登上世界舞台的欲望，而女性读者与作者则在这些新出版物中表述自己的思想与故事。[^zh-ch07-3] 《妇女时报》1916年10月号的封面插图，呈现的正是这样一位怀抱视觉之力与飞行之梦、心向高处的女性主体。同期两篇文章讲述了年轻女子 Zhang Xiahun 的英勇事迹：她参观上海一场飞行表演时，坚持要乘坐飞机。她不顾航空学校校长的劝阻，宣称自己的飞行将"开辟中国女飞行员的新纪元，为女性勇敢史缔造新的黎明，并在中国航空史上赢得数行记载"。[^zh-ch07-4] 一阵强风刮来，飞机坠毁；她受伤脱身，却带着胜利者的姿态。这位把望远镜对准地平线的新女性，幽灵般萦绕着雷燕近一个世纪后为"长征"创作的那两幅照片。如今她一身迷彩、脚蹬黑色军靴，不再站在阳台或水边，而是坚守在历史的战场上。


〔原书 238, 239〕

Lei Yan’s *What If* series inspired the conception of feminist sight lines that frames this final section of the book. I interpret her work as feminist because of its critical historiographical consciousness cultivated by being on the periphery. I met Lei Yan, as described in chapter 4, not in Beijing but in rural Yunnan, albeit through an art exhibit organized in and emanating from the “cultural capital” of Beijing. She works primarily in Kunming but trained in the pla Arts Academy in Beijing and continues to exhibit her work there. Her center-off-center position, as well as the conjunction of the turning point of her career after retirement from the military with that of Chinese contemporary art production, informs the transhistorical and transnational connections her artwork makes visible. The feminist sight lines opened by her evolving body of work provide a critical vantage on the work of art in the era of late socialism-late liberalism, as these two social projects and their management of difference and inequality intertwine. When she and Ai Weiwei both responded through their art to state image control of the 2008 Wenquan earthquake, she entered into relational monumental/ephemeral proximity with China’s most globally recognized art world figure. Viewed together, the questions Lei’s work raises about conventional narratives of Chinese contemporary art emerge in particular relief.

雷燕的《如果》系列启发了本书最后一部分用以统摄全局的"女性主义视线"概念。我之所以将她的作品解读为女性主义的，是因为它带有一种由边缘位置培养出来的批判性史学意识。如第四章所述，我与雷燕相遇不在北京，而是在云南乡间，尽管那是通过一场在北京"文化首都"中组织并向外辐射的艺术展览。她主要在昆明工作，却曾在北京的解放军艺术学院受训，并继续在那里展出作品。她偏离中心的中心位置，以及她退役后艺术生涯的转折点与中国当代艺术生产的转折点相合，都塑造了她的作品所揭示的跨历史、跨国联系。她不断演化的作品所开启的女性主义视线，为审视晚期社会主义—晚期自由主义时代的艺术提供了一个批判性视点，因为这两种社会工程及其对差异与不平等的管理正相互交织。当她与艾未未都以艺术回应国家对2008年汶川地震图像的控制时，她与中国最受全球瞩目的艺术界人物进入了纪念碑式／短暂性的关系性邻近之中。将两人的作品并置来看，雷燕作品对当代中国艺术常规叙事提出的问题便格外清晰地显现出来。


〔原书 239〕

Feminist Sight Lines

女性主义视线


〔原书 239〕

Binoculars bring something distant into closer view. Side-mounted mirror-symmetrical telescopes, designed to be hand held, produce an impression of depth that makes the scene viewed three-dimensional. When Lei Yan shows up in her stereoscopelike images *What If the Long March Had Been a Women’s Rights Movement*? and *What If They Had Been Women*?, she reverses the sight line of her historical counterparts from the previous turn of the century. The courtesan as public figure of urbanity and the learned new woman of the Republic gaze toward an imagined future, what once seemed impossibly distant suddenly brought near. In 2002, Lei trains her binoculars back on a Communist past meant to seem distant in reform-era discourse about linking tracks with the capitalist world. Instead, she brings it near, as historical figures from 1934 loom large on the horizon.

望远镜能把远处之物拉近。两侧镜像对称、可手持的望远镜产生景深，使所观景物显得立体。当雷燕以她那两幅立体镜式的照片《如果长征是一场女权运动？》和《如果他们是女人？》现身时，她颠倒了上一个世纪之交与她遥相呼应的那些女性的视线。作为城市性公共形象的妓女，与民国博学的新女性，都凝望着一个想象出来的未来——那曾显得遥不可及的一切，忽然被拉到了近前。2002年，雷燕把望远镜调转，回望一段在改革时代关于与世界资本主义接轨的话语中被刻意显得遥远的共产主义过去。她反而把它拉近，让1934年的历史人物赫然矗立在地平线上。


〔原书 239, 240〕

The feminist grammar of her “what if” titles is akin to that of the future anterior employed by Tani Barlow in her reading of Ding Ling’s Maoist literary corpus. Barlow argues that the revolutionary injunction for cultural workers like Ding to “enter life” (*shenru shenghuo*) meant more than living with and representing the common people. It expressed a Maoist cultural idiolect that invented language for mass consciousness and action on the historical horizon, a dialectical process of “anticipate, initiate, reflect, criticize, regroup, and reanticipate.”[^en-ch07-5] As Ding entered life in this sense, her stories and novels not only reflected this process, they became part of the process, even while holding on to the speculative question about what “women” would become through their enunciation as such. The future anterior guides the historian to focus on theoretical claims from the past about the potential women were imagined to embody. Barlow uses this grammatical construction as a methodology for reassessing not only the legacy of Chinese feminism but of feminism as an international mode of thought linked to colonialism and globalization, as much a measure of one’s place in the world order as a demand for liberation. The future anterior makes possible a speculative question: What will women have been? It does not presume to know what the “woman” predicated by feminism existentially is or was but endeavors to understand how the category of woman has been mobilized toward future change of an untenable status quo.[^en-ch07-6] The artworks produced by Lei Yan through her participation in *The Long March* raise related questions about what women might have become if they had not been caught by the double binds of Chinese Communist history. She roams back and forth over this and more recent historical terrain, performing an auto-ethnographic excavation of the institutions and socio-historical processes that made her as both artist and woman.

她那些"如果"标题的女性主义语法，近似于白露（Tani Barlow）在解读丁玲毛泽东时代文学文本时所用的"将来完成时"。白露认为，对丁玲这样的文化工作者发出的"深入生活"的革命号召，并不只是与群众共同生活并表现他们。它表达的是一种毛泽东时代的文化独特语汇，为历史地平线上的群众意识与行动发明语言，是一个"预判、倡导、反映、批评、重组、再预判"的辩证过程。[^zh-ch07-5] 当丁玲以这种方式进入生活时，她的小说和故事不仅反映了这一过程，也成为过程的一部分，同时还保留着一个思辨性问题："妇女"通过被如此言说将会变成什么。将来完成时引导历史学者关注过去的理论主张——关于女性被想象可以承载的潜能。白露用这一语法结构作为一种方法，不仅重新评估中国女性主义的遗产，也重新评估女性主义作为一种与殖民主义和全球化相连的国际思想方式；它既是衡量一个人在世界秩序中所处位置的尺度，也是对解放的要求。将来完成时使一个思辨性问题成为可能：女性将会曾经成为什么？它并不自以为知道女性主义所断定的"女人"在存在论上是什么或曾是什么，而是努力理解"女人"这一范畴如何被动员起来，以推动对一个难以维持的现状的未来改变。[^zh-ch07-6]雷燕通过参与"长征"创作的作品，提出了相关问题：如果女性没有被中国共产党历史的双重束缚所捕获，她们可能会成为什么？她在这片历史地形与更晚近的历史地形之间来回漫游，对自己既成为艺术家又成为女人所凭借的建制与社会历史过程，进行了一场自我民族志式的挖掘。


〔原书 240〕

Lei Yan’s trajectory as an artist began with a career in the Chinese military that spanned three decades. Born into a Kunming military family in 1957, she joined the army at age fourteen and served over the years as a soldier, nurse, and officer. As part of her early duties, she gained sketching skills and responsibility for drawing her unit’s blackboard announcements. In 1976, she began studying printmaking. She also transferred to the Kunming Military District Creative Works Team and had her work shown in China’s National Military Art Exhibition. With her next assignment to a local military hospital, she became an official painter tasked with illustrating teaching materials for the military medical school. After “reform and opening,” the school opened a multimedia lab, where she studied color photography. She also served, as a nurse, during the prolonged border conflicts of the Sino-Vietnamese War. In 1989, she tested into the first printmaking course offered by the People’s Liberation Army Arts Academy in Beijing and arrived in the capital shortly after the *China/Avant-Garde* exhibit at the National Art Museum of China brought new attention and notoriety to contemporary practices such as installation and performance art. After graduating in 1991, she returned to Kunming and experimented, outside her official capacity, with new styles and subject matter. She joined a group of artists working in Kunming’s Chuang Ku, or Loft community, established in a former factory, where she set up a studio after her retirement from the military in 2001.[^en-ch07-7] After she and fellow Kunming-based artist Sun Guojuan joined Judy Chicago at site six of *The Long March*, they participated in cross-cultural art exchanges to Sweden facilitated by TGC Nordica, a Chinese-Swedish organization that opened a gallery space in the Kunming Loft complex in 2000. Through this gallery, Lei and Sun curated a series of exhibitions featuring the work of female artists from Yunnan.[^en-ch07-8]

雷燕的艺术生涯始于在中国军队中度过的三十年。她1957年出生于昆明的一个军人家庭，十四岁入伍，此后多年先后当过士兵、护士和军官。早年职责之一，是学习素描，并负责绘制部队的黑板报。1976年，她开始学习版画。她后来调入昆明军区创作组，作品入选全军美术作品展。下一次被分配到当地一所军医院后，她成为专职画家，负责为军医学校的教学材料绘制插图。改革开放后，学校开设多媒体实验室，她在那里学习彩色摄影。在中越战争漫长的边境冲突中，她还担任过护士。1989年，她考取解放军艺术学院在北京开设的第一届版画课程，并在"中国现代艺术展"于中国美术馆举办、使装置和行为艺术等当代实践引起新的关注与争议后不久抵达首都。1991年毕业后，她回到昆明，在官方职责之外尝试新的风格与题材。她加入了在昆明"创库"（由一家旧工厂改建的艺术家社区）工作的艺术家群体，并于2001年退役后在那里设立工作室。[^zh-ch07-7] 她与同在昆明的艺术家孙国娟一起在"长征"第六站与朱迪·芝加哥会合后，又参加了由 TGC Nordica 促成的赴瑞典跨文化艺术交流。这家中国—瑞典机构于2000年在昆明创库开设画廊。通过这家画廊，雷燕与孙国娟策划了一系列展览，呈现云南女性艺术家的作品。[^zh-ch07-8]


〔原书 240, 241〕

Lei Yan is not particularly well known outside of minor transnational networks linking, for example, Yunnan with Scandinavia. Nor is her path to becoming an artist via the military one typically associated with contemporary art practice, especially that in an avant-garde, anti-institutional mode, although it does bring back into the picture the longer translingual history of avant-garde/*xianfeng* in China. It is precisely this center-off-center position that informs her work. The pieces she began creating after her retirement exemplify a critical historiographical consciousness, a feminist reflection on past avant-gardes that temporally confounds the straight logic of innovation, progress, and coming before. She works from within a national representational corpus, subjecting it to various experiments informed by transnational art movements, to reveal the fields of violence—literal and figural—it has enacted. She is a propagandist turned deconstructionist, with a vision in which the *nannü* relations between man and woman inform other socially reproduced abstractions—past and present, rural and urban, China and the world—that create injustice.

雷燕在连接云南与斯堪的纳维亚等地的小型跨国网络之外并不特别知名。她经由军队成为艺术家的道路，通常也不被与当代艺术实践联系在一起——尤其是那种先锋、反建制的实践——尽管它确实把中国"先锋"（xianfeng）更长时段的跨语言历史重新带回了画面。正是这种偏离中心的中心位置，塑造了她的作品。退役后开始创作的作品体现出批判性的史学意识，一种对过往先锋派的女性主义反思，在时间上扰乱了创新、进步、先行的直线逻辑。她从一套国家表征语汇内部工作，让它经受各种受跨国艺术运动启发的实验，从而揭示它曾施行的暴力场域——字面的与比喻的。她是从宣传家转变为解构者的人，在她的视野中，男女（nannü）关系塑造着其他由社会再生产出来的抽象对立——过去与现在、乡村与城市、中国与世界——并制造不公。


〔原书 241〕

Three sociohistorical categories—the woman soldier, the military artist, and the woman artist—have shaped Lei Yan’s life and art. The ways they intersect throw into question conventional narratives of feminist art in global and national contexts. Her career does not, for example, fit easily into the story of feminist art emerging from 1960s Euro-American Second Wave feminist critiques of the art world and its social and formalistic hierarchies. It similarly resists Chinese articulations of *nüxing yishu* as a post-socialist recuperation of female subjectivity that domesticates and depoliticizes work by women and thereby cuts it off from interpretation within larger contexts of the nation and beyond. Lei Yan’s artistic practice, its subject matter and formal aesthetics, requires consideration beyond the borders of the nation because of its critique of loss and sacrifice in the name of the nation. She arguably becomes a feminist artist in spite of or because of her original training as an artist in what is arguably the sine qua non of the modern Chinese nation-state, the People’s Liberation Army of the Chinese Communist Party.

女兵、军旅艺术家和女性艺术家这三个社会历史范畴，塑造了雷燕的人生与艺术。它们相互交汇的方式，使全球与民族语境中女性主义艺术的常规叙事受到质疑。例如，她的职业生涯不易被纳入这样一个故事：女性主义艺术诞生于1960年代欧美第二波女性主义对艺术界及其社会与形式等级所进行的批判。她的职业生涯同样难以纳入中国对"女性艺术"（nüxing yishu）的表述——那种把女性艺术当作后社会主义对女性主体性的收复，驯化并去政治化女性创作，从而使女性作品无法在民族国家内部及更大语境中被解读。雷燕的艺术实践、题材与形式美学，要求超越民族国家边界来考察，因为它批判以民族之名造成的丧失与牺牲。可以说，她成为女性主义艺术家，或是突破了最初的艺术训练所设下的限制，或恰恰得益于这种训练；训练她的机构是中国共产党领导的中国人民解放军，而这一机构可谓现代中国民族国家不可或缺的条件。


〔原书 241〕

The categories of woman soldier (*nübing*), military artist ( *junyi*), and woman artist (*nüxing yishujia*) are historical catachreses, master words whose appearance in speech mark a departure from traditional usage (i.e., woman, soldier, artist) and serve to consolidate new social formations. In *The Question of Women in Chinese Feminism*, Tani Barlow argues that “woman” as expressed in the Chinese neologisms of *nüxing* and *funü* emerged as a theoretical category, rather than a universal given, out of the Chinese drive to form a modern nation. These historical catachreses and their analogues of nübing, junyi, and nüxing yishujia are ideological entities with explanatory power that over time served to organize everyday thinking.

女兵（nübing）、军旅艺术家（junyi）和女性艺术家（nüxing yishujia）这些范畴是历史性的词语误用，是主导词；它们在言语中的出现标志着对传统用法（即女人、士兵、艺术家）的偏离，并有助于巩固新的社会构形。在《中国女性主义中的女性问题》中，白露认为，"女性"与"妇女"这些中文新词所表达的"女人"，是在中国建设现代民族国家的驱动下作为理论范畴而非普遍给定物出现的。这些历史性的词语误用，以及女兵、军艺、女性艺术家等对应词，都是具有解释力的意识形态实体，在历史中逐渐组织起日常思维。


〔原书 241, 242〕

Beginning in the 1920s, the woman soldier in China signified a new subject, a woman liberated from traditional kinship protocols and empowered to fight for the idea of a new nation, free from feudal rule and its patriarchal oppressions, as well as colonial incursion and orientalist depictions of Asian women oppressed by their “culture” as justification for invasion. Xie Bingying served as one early model of this emerging subject. Born in 1906, she struggled to get an education, escaped from an arranged marriage, moved in and had a child with her lover, and served in the National Revolutionary Army in the fight against local warlords in the 1920s and the Japanese in the 1930s. The publication of her war diaries, first in 1928, followed by updated versions, made her story available for wide public consumption.[^en-ch07-9] In breathless prose, she wrote, for example, of her first night after joining the female company of Wuhan’s Central Military and Political School: “I thought how in only a few hours we would be carrying guns and sticks, marching to the cry of ‘one-two-three-four.’ *Solider*. What a powerful word! I would not have believed that we Chinese women, repressed by ancient custom for thousands of years, would see the day when we would become soldiers. Now we must work hard to carry out our responsibility, to change society, to destroy the powers of feudalism.”[^en-ch07-10] The woman soldier, glorified in films such as *Daughters of China* (1949), *The Red Detachment of Women* (1961), and *The Red Lantern* (1970), became a key figure in the Chinese Communist Party’s pantheon of heroic representation. The woman soldier and her visibility in film, propaganda posters, and painting supported party rhetoric about female emancipation and gender equality. She also provided women with a new subject position, a potentiality some embraced, even as they continued to encounter gender hierarchy and sexual violence in the military and elsewhere.[^en-ch07-11]

从1920年代开始，中国的女兵意味着一种新的主体，一个从传统亲属礼法中解放出来、被赋权为建立一个新国家的理念而战的女人，她既摆脱封建统治及其父权压迫，也对抗殖民入侵以及东方主义将亚洲女性描绘为受其"文化"压迫、从而为侵略辩护的做法。谢冰莹是这一新兴主体的早期典范之一。她1906年出生，为受教育而挣扎，逃离包办婚姻，与恋人同居并育有一个孩子，1920年代在国民革命军中参加讨伐地方军阀的战斗，1930年代又投身抗日。她的战地日记于1928年首次出版，此后又出过增订版，使她的故事得以广泛流传。[^zh-ch07-9] 她用令人屏息的文字写道，例如，加入武汉中央军事政治学校女生队后的第一夜："我想着，再过几个小时，我们就要扛起枪和棍棒，随着'一二三四'的口令行进。士兵。多么有力的词！我简直无法相信，我们中国女性被古老礼俗压抑了数千年，竟能活着看到成为士兵的一天。现在我们一定要努力履行自己的责任，改变社会，摧毁封建势力。"[^zh-ch07-10] 女兵在《中华女儿》（1949）、《红色娘子军》（1961）和《红灯记》（1970）等影片中被颂扬，成为中国共产党英雄表征殿堂中的关键形象。女兵及其在电影、宣传画和绘画中的可见性，支撑着党关于妇女解放与性别平等的修辞。她也为女性提供了一个新的主体位置，一种有些人欣然拥抱的可能性，尽管她们在军队内外仍不断遭遇性别等级与性暴力。[^zh-ch07-11]


〔原书 242, 243〕

The modern conception of the military artist or art soldier dates to the Red Army’s establishment of its guerrilla base in Yan’an, where Mao Zedong compelled culture workers to become willing oxen, heads bowed to serve the people. His selective quotation from Lu Xun’s poem “Self Mockery” as final salvo in his talks on literature and art draws power from Lu’s conviction that only culture could save China from the habits of thought and behavior that had made it weak. Mao’s didactic interpretation of the quoted couplet, however, disregards ironic contrasts in the full poem, whose narrator reflects on the defiant gestures of his past and ends with a desire to retreat from the outside world to “a small house hidden away.”[^en-ch07-12] Mao emphasized cultural defiance, reformulation, and revolutionary anticipation over contemplative ambivalence, clearing the ground for ccp institutionalization of culture workers and performance troops. The Yan’an Lu Xun Arts Academy was established in 1938, two years after the death of its namesake.[^en-ch07-13] As part of this institutional legacy, the People’s Liberation Army Arts Academy, established in Beijing in 1960, began offering advanced training for members of military cultural troops in art, dance, drama, literature, and music. Culture as the front line continued during the Cultural Revolution in Red Guard art activities such as the 1967 *Long Live the Victory of Chairman Mao’s Revolutionary Line* exhibit at the National Art Museum of China.[^en-ch07-14] Ballet, film, and opera productions like *The Red Detachment of Women* effectively fused together the figures of woman soldier and military artist.

军旅艺术家或艺术战士的现代观念，可追溯到红军在延安建立游击根据地时期。毛泽东迫使文化工作者做甘愿俯首为人民服务的牛。他在文艺讲话结尾选择性引用鲁迅《自嘲》中的诗句，其力量来自鲁迅的信念：只有文化才能把中国从使其积弱的思维与行为习惯中拯救出来。然而，毛泽东对所引诗句的说教式解释，无视整首诗中的反讽对照；诗中的叙述者回望自己昔日的桀骜姿态，最后却渴望从外部世界退隐到"躲进小楼"。 [^zh-ch07-12] 毛泽东强调文化上的反抗、重新表述与革命预判，而非沉思性的矛盾心理，从而为中国共产党将文化工作者和演出队伍建制化扫清道路。延安鲁迅艺术学院成立于1938年，即其命名对象去世两年之后。[^zh-ch07-13]作为这一制度遗产的一部分，1960年在北京成立的解放军艺术学院开始为军队文艺团体的成员提供美术、舞蹈、戏剧、文学和音乐方面的高级培训。文化作为前线，在文化大革命期间的红卫兵美术活动中延续，例如1967年在中国美术馆举办的"毛主席革命路线胜利万岁"展览。[^zh-ch07-14] 芭蕾、电影和歌剧作品如《红色娘子军》，有效地把女兵与军旅艺术家的形象熔合在一起。


〔原书 243〕

The idea of the woman artist arose in a post-Mao context, as the Chinese art historical category of nüxing yishu gained currency in the 1990s, casting a retrospective net that pulled modernist figures into its project. It emerged in exhibit catalogues and art criticism in 1995, the year Beijing hosted the United Nations Fourth World Conference on Women, and then served as the organizing rubric for the *Century Woman* exhibit at the National Art Museum of China in 1998. Following the centennial frame of the exhibit’s title, catalogue essays on early twentieth-century painters such as Pan Yuliang and Qiu Ti discussed them as predecessors of a “women’s art” shaped by women’s unique psychobiological predispositions. This discursive formation, as part of post-Mao feminist humanist thought that sought to recuperate a female subjectivity from the state mobilization of women, identifies a subject different from that signified by female artist (*nü yishujia*), or artist who happens to be a woman. The curator of *Century Woman*, Jia Fangzhou, defined in his catalogue introduction the main characteristics of this art: it draws inspiration from personal reflection and experience, demonstrates “artistic intuition,” breaks from rational thought, focuses on the minutiae of daily life rather than politics, and develops both material and method from “handicrafts” associated with women.[^en-ch07-15] Two years later, in *A History of Chinese Contemporary Art, 1990–1999*, one of the first comprehensive surveys of this period, Chinese art historian Lü Peng relegated almost all female artists to a chapter titled “Women’s Art,” rather than as contributors to movements discussed in other chapters, such as political pop, cynical realism, or conceptual art.[^en-ch07-16]

女性艺术家的观念兴起于后毛泽东时代。中文艺术史范畴"女性艺术"在1990年代流行开来，回溯性地张开一张网，把现代主义人物也拉进其计划。它于1995年出现在展览图录和艺术批评中——那一年北京主办了联合国第四次世界妇女大会——随后成为1998年中国美术馆"世纪·女性"展览的组织标题。依照展览标题的百年框架，图录中讨论潘玉良、丘堤等20世纪初画家的文章，把她们视为一种"女性艺术"的先驱；这种艺术由女性独特的心理生物学禀赋所塑造。这一话语构形是后毛泽东时代女性主义人道主义思想的产物，它试图从国家对妇女的动员中收复女性主体性，并标示出一种不同于"女艺术家"（nü yishujia，即碰巧是女人的艺术家）的主体。展览"世纪·女性"的策展人贾方舟在图录导言中界定了这种艺术的主要特征：它从个人反思与经验中汲取灵感，展现"艺术直觉"，与理性思维断裂，关注日常生活的细枝末节而非政治，并从与女性相关的"手工艺"中发展出材料与方法。[^zh-ch07-15] 两年后，在中国艺术史学者吕澎所著的、这一时期的首批综合概览之一《中国当代艺术史：1990—1999》中，几乎所有女性艺术家都被归入题为"女性艺术"的一章，而不是作为政治波普、玩世现实主义或观念艺术等其他章节所讨论运动的参与者。[^zh-ch07-16]


〔原书 243, 244〕

In 2002, Lei Yan brought the three ideological categories of woman soldier, military artist, and woman artist together in *What If the Long March Had Been a Women’s Rights Movement*? and *What If They Had Been Women*?, exhibited in the “women’s art” section of *The Long March* project. While she created these images in response to Judy Chicago’s fantasy “what if” projection, her visual materials reference not a universal female subject but a formative Chinese historical event, as Communist activists regrouped in order to revolutionize a rural peasantry. Their appeal to disenfranchised men, “bare sticks” without the means to marry, held out the promise of equal opportunity to carry on one’s patriline rather than women’s liberation from the inner quarters of family life. Red Army guerrilla activities gradually prioritized class over gender in a way that suppressed thinking about class and gender as interlocking or mutually constitutive systems of power, even as representations of women raped and exploited by class enemies served a prominent symbolic function.[^en-ch07-17] This ideological suppression produced the double binds at Yan’an that Ding Ling exposed so trenchantly in “Thoughts on March 8”: female comrades were denounced for pursuing politics over family responsibilities, but then when compelled to marry and bear children, they were denounced for being “Noras returned home,” unable to survive independently and thus consigned to a destiny of “backwardness.”[^en-ch07-18] “It would be better,” she wrote before being attacked as “narrowly feminist,” “if there were less empty theorizing and more talk about real problems, so that theory and practice would not be divorced, and better if all Communist Party members were more responsible for their own moral conduct.”[^en-ch07-19] An investigation of this relationship between theory and practice, between ideology and image making became part of Lei’s emerging praxis.

2002年，雷燕把女兵、军旅艺术家和女性艺术家这三个意识形态范畴汇聚于《如果长征是一场女权运动？》和《如果他们是女人？》中，并在"长征"项目的"女性艺术"部分展出。尽管她是为了回应朱迪·芝加哥幻想式的"如果"投射而创作这些图像，她的视觉材料所指涉的并不是普遍的女性主体，而是一个塑造现代中国的历史事件：共产党活动分子重新集结，以便在农村发动农民革命。他们对被剥夺权利的男性——无力娶妻的"光棍"——的号召，许诺的是延续父系血脉的平等机会，而不是把妇女从家庭生活的内闱中解放出来。红军游击活动逐渐把阶级置于性别之上，从而压抑了把阶级与性别视为相互扣连、相互构成的权力体系来思考，尽管阶级敌人强奸和剥削妇女的表征仍发挥着突出的象征功能。[^zh-ch07-17] 这种意识形态压抑在延安造成了丁玲在《三八节有感》中尖锐揭示的双重束缚：女同志因追求政治而置家庭责任于不顾遭到谴责，可当她们被迫结婚生育后，又被斥为"回家的娜拉"，无法独立生存，从而被判定为"落后"。[^zh-ch07-18] "与其空谈理论，不如多谈实际问题，使理论与实践不致脱节；"她在被攻击为"狭隘女性主义"之前写道，"如果所有共产党员都能对自己的道德行为更负起责任，那就更好了。"[^zh-ch07-19] 对这种理论与实践、意识形态与图像生产之间关系的探究，成为雷燕逐渐形成的实践的一部分。


〔原书 244〕

Lei Yan first developed her technique of digital manipulation as a military artist. In 1994, she and colleague Tang Zhigang produced a photograph of military heroes titled *Group Photo of an Era* (figure 7.02), with the handwritten inscription of “A Souvenir of the People’s Photo Studio Serving the People.”[^en-ch07-20] The layers of translucent color applied to the soldiers’ hands and faces accentuate the montage construction of the photograph, as it brings together, in the Maoist tradition of reworked historical images, a group of heroes in the impossible reality of a studio shot. The washed out national colors of red and yellow that shade their skin mimic old hand-colored photographs, tingeing the image with nostalgia and parody. In her 2002 *What If* photos, Lei reproduces this technique but also inserts herself, as part of the represented collectivity *and* distantiated creator-observer of its power. She becomes a frontline observer from the future within the historical photograph, who brings into focus an oppositional consciousness, posing historiographical questions about her own social formation.

雷燕首次发展出数码处理技术，是在她做军旅艺术家期间。1994年，她与同事唐志冈制作了一张题为《一个时代的合影》的军人英雄照片（图7.02），上面有手写题字"为人民服务的人民照相馆留念"。[^zh-ch07-20] 敷在士兵手和脸上的半透明色层，突出了照片的蒙太奇构造：它延续毛泽东时代改写历史图像的传统，把一群英雄聚合进照相馆合影这一不可能的现实之中。晕染他们皮肤的红黄两种国家象征色因褪色而显得暗淡，模仿着手工上色的老照片，为图像染上怀旧与戏仿的色调。在2002年的《如果》照片中，雷燕复制了这种技术，同时也把自己插入其中：她既是被再现的集体的一部分，又是对其力量保持距离的创作者—观察者。她成为历史照片中来自未来的前线观察者，把一个对抗性的意识带入焦点，并对自身的社会构形提出史学问题。


〔原书 244, 245〕

She continued the series with several more pieces. *What If Our Factory Were Still Here*? (figure 7.03) emerged from video and photographic documentation of a factory within her military work unit as it underwent demolition. Like other artists who focused on the massing turning over of China’s urban landscape, Lei used her camera to explore sites of physical change. Her images bring to this presentist form of documentation questions of temporality, history, and memory. She inserts herself again within the frame, but this time the figure seems more a camouflaged observer from the past in panoramic projects of future destruction. Her image of the factory, an institutional space that once organized and defined social life, is imbued with a sense of loss: through the question she asks of it, her use of the possessive pronoun “our,” and her digitally manipulated spectral appearance within it. She stands in miniature with her binoculars, amid the rubble, witness to the dismantling of the political fervor and everyday activity that once filled the now empty space. The military as a site of female opportunity, talent development, and collectivity, as well as oppression, is demolished in the push toward market reform, demobilization, and privatization.

她继续创作这个系列，又增添了几件作品。《如果我们的工厂还在？》（图7.03）源于她对自己军队工作单位内一座工厂拆除过程的录像与摄影记录。与其他关注中国城市地貌大规模翻建的艺术家一样，雷燕用相机探索物质变迁的场所。她的图像为这种当下主义的记录方式带来了时间性、历史与记忆的问题。她再次把自己放入画面，但这一次，她更像未来毁灭全景图中的一名来自过去的迷彩观察者。她镜头下的工厂——一个曾经组织和界定社会生活的机构空间——弥漫着失落感：这来自她向它提出的问题，来自所有格"我们的"，也来自她经过数码处理的幽灵般现身。她以微缩身形举着望远镜站在瓦砾之间，见证着曾经充满这片如今空荡空间的政治热情与日常活动被拆解。军队作为女性获得机会、发展才能和集体归属之地，同时也是压迫之地，在市场化改革、裁军与私有化的推进中被拆除。


〔原书 245〕

![*图7.02　雷燕、唐志冈，《一个时代的合影》，1994年，数码照片。艺术家提供。*](web/assets/ch07-b019.jpg)

FIG 7.02 Lei Yan and Tang Zhigang, *Group Photo of an Era*, 1994. Digital photograph. Courtesy of the artist.

*图7.02　雷燕、唐志冈，《一个时代的合影》，1994年，数码照片。艺术家提供。*


〔原书 245, 246〕

*What If Woman Were Written by the Book*? shifts to a sociological investigation of reform-era femininity produced out of and against previous norms, retrospectively framed as having unnaturally suppressed an essential femininity. For this piece, Lei Yan photographed the covers of popular books for sale on the streets of Kunming with titles containing the word “woman.” An inordinate number of them addressed issues related to health, beauty, sexuality, and family, positioning women as consumers of domestic pleasures rather than producers in the public sphere. She digitally montaged them together to form a black-and-white mosaic, over which the English word *woman* in capital letters floats as a layered mask that reveals the gaudy colors of the book covers below. The question of the piece’s title suggests the disciplining of woman into a particular subject position by this proliferating abundance of material on her, while also holding open in its grammatical construction a gap between signifier and signified, in which the signifiers do not wholly make the signified in its image.

《如果女人按书本来塑造？》转向对改革时代女性气质的社会学考察：这种女性气质是在先前规范之内并针对先前规范生产出来的，而那些规范又被回溯性地框定为曾不自然地压抑了一种本质性的女性气质。为此，雷燕拍摄了昆明街头出售的畅销书封面，书名中都含有"女人"一词。其中相当多涉及健康、美貌、性与家庭，把女性定位为家庭乐趣的消费者，而非公共领域中的生产者。她用数码技术把它们蒙太奇式地拼成黑白马赛克，上面浮着大写的英文单词 woman，像一层叠置的面具，透出下方书封艳俗的色彩。作品标题的疑问暗示：铺天盖地、不断增殖的关于女人的材料，正把女人规训进特定的主体位置；而标题的语法构造同时保持着能指与所指之间的缝隙——能指并不能在其形象中完全制造所指。


〔原书 246〕

![*图7.03　雷燕，《如果我们的工厂还在？》，2002年，数码照片。艺术家提供。*](web/assets/ch07-b021.jpg)

FIG 7.03 Lei Yan, *What If Our Factory Were Still Here*, 2002. Digital photograph. Courtesy of the artist.

*图7.03　雷燕，《如果我们的工厂还在？》，2002年，数码照片。艺术家提供。*


〔原书 246〕

Bullet Shot through a Young Heart

子弹穿过年轻的心


〔原书 246, 247〕

In 2002, following her *What If* series, Lei Yan created another digital photographic piece titled *Bullet Shot through a Young Heart* after a return trip to Laoshan, where she had served as a military nurse during the Sino-Vietnamese War. This prolonged series of conflicts along China’s border with Vietnam began with a bloody month in 1979 that left tens of thousands on both sides dead and injured. The war pitted, in almost a 180-degree turn, former socialist allies against one another. Cold War geopolitical alignments and the ideological battles of the Sino-Soviet split begun in the 1960s played out in deadly ways for Chinese and Vietnamese soldiers and civilians. After the Communist victory of the Viet Cong in 1975, a postcolonial, pro-Soviet regime was established in Vietnam. In neighboring Cambodia, the Chinese backed the Khmer Rouge. When their troops attacked ethnic Vietnamese in Cambodia and threatened the border, Vietnam counterattacked in a conflict that led to the deposing of Maoist client-leader Pol Pot. The Chinese retaliated with the 1979 invasion that launched the Sino-Vietnamese War. Border skirmishes continued throughout the 1980s until relations between the two countries finally normalized in the early 1990s. A devastating battle occurred at Laoshan in 1984, during Lei Yan’s deployment, and 959 Chinese soldiers and support personnel were buried there in the Malipo Martyrs Cemetery. Tombstone inscriptions indicate that many of those buried had enlisted only months before dying young, between the ages of sixteen and twenty. Upon returning to Laoshan almost twenty years later, Lei Yan noted that the rebranding of the area as a vacation destination remained haunted by Malipo: “I climbed to the top of the cemetery. Backlit, the tombstones appeared like a group of soldiers in uniform. A gust of wind swept by, and a chill struck through me, like a bullet shot through the tombstones and the spirits underneath. It shot through my young heart, through time and space, through memory, and through peace.”[^en-ch07-21]

2002年，完成《如果》系列之后，雷燕重返老山，随后创作了另一件数码摄影作品《子弹穿过年轻的心》。她曾在中越战争期间作为军队护士驻守老山。中国与越南边境上这场旷日持久的冲突系列，始于1979年血腥的一个月，双方数万人死伤。战争几乎来了个一百八十度大转弯，让昔日的社会主义盟友兵戎相见。冷战地缘政治格局与1960年代开始的中苏分裂意识形态斗争，以致命的方式落在中国和越南的士兵与平民身上。1975年越共取得胜利后，越南建立起一个后殖民、亲苏的政权。在邻国柬埔寨，中国支持红色高棉。当红色高棉军队袭击柬埔寨境内的越南族并威胁边境时，越南反击，冲突导致受毛主义阵营扶植的领导人波尔布特被推翻。中国以1979年的入侵进行报复，中越战争由此爆发。边境冲突贯穿整个1980年代，直到1990年代初两国关系最终正常化。1984年，雷燕驻防期间，老山发生了一场毁灭性的战斗，959名中国士兵和支援人员葬于麻栗坡烈士陵园。墓碑铭文显示，许多死者入伍仅数月便阵亡，年仅十六到二十岁。近二十年后重返老山时，雷燕注意到，该地区被重新包装为度假目的地，却仍被麻栗坡的幽灵萦绕："我爬到了陵园顶上。逆光中，墓碑看上去像一队身着军装的士兵。一阵风扫过，寒意刺透了我，像一颗子弹穿过墓碑和下面的亡灵。它穿过我年轻的心，穿过时间和空间，穿过记忆，也穿过和平。"[^zh-ch07-21]


〔原书 247, 248〕

*Bullet Shot through a Young Heart* (figure 7.04) is a triptych of three photographs, each tinted a single color, which hung side by side resemble the bars of an exploded national flag. In the central, black-and-white image, superimposed layers of tombstones crowd the frame. While the Malipo tombstones are uniform in height and shape and laid out in straight, uniform rows, Lei digitally varied their size to create an overlapping pattern of haptic replication. Some recede into the background, others rise to the surface, creating an overall sensation of floating upward and outward, an otherworldly irruption of the past into the present. In the images that flank it, tourist snapshots of the cemetery are montaged together in an almost abstract pattern; the actual subject of the photos can only be discerned on close inspection. The tinting of one red and the other green suggests either the demarcation of political bodies on either side of a border or the division between a bloody past and a verdant future. In an installation of the piece in 2011 at the Suzhou Creek Art Center in Shanghai, the three photographs were hung on the white wall of a gallery with a concrete floor and florescent lighting. A line of text ran the entire length of adjacent walls, to the left and right of the image, listing diplomatic details of Chinese-Vietnamese relations from 1950 to 2000, from alliance to conflict to normalization.

《子弹穿过年轻的心》（图7.04）是一组三联照片，每幅染成单色，并排悬挂时像一面炸裂国旗的色带。中央的黑白图像中，层层叠叠的墓碑挤满画面。麻栗坡的墓碑原本高度、形状统一，排列成笔直的队列，雷燕用数码手段改变其大小，制造出相互重叠、触感般的复制图案。有些退入背景，有些浮向表面，整体产生一种向上、向外漂浮的感觉，像是过去幽灵般闯入现在。两侧的图像把陵园的游客快照蒙太奇式拼成近乎抽象的图案，只有细看才能辨认照片的实际对象。一幅染红、一幅染绿，暗示着边界两侧政治身体的划界，或血染的过去与苍翠未来之间的分野。2011年，这件作品在上海苏州河艺术中心展出时，三幅照片挂在画廊白墙上，下面是水泥地面，头顶是荧光灯。一条文字沿两侧相邻墙壁的整个长度延伸，在图像左右列出1950年至2000年间中越关系的外交细节，从结盟、冲突到正常化。


〔原书 248〕

![*图7.04　雷燕，《子弹穿过年轻的心》，2002年，数码照片。展览现场，雷燕个展，苏州河艺术中心，上海，2011年。艺术家提供。*](web/assets/ch07-b025.jpg)

FIG 7.04 Lei Yan, *Bullet Shot through a Young Heart*, 2002. Digital photographs. Installation view, Lei Yan solo exhibition, Suzhou Creek Art Center, Shanghai, 2011. Courtesy of the artist.

*图7.04　雷燕，《子弹穿过年轻的心》，2002年，数码照片。展览现场，雷燕个展，苏州河艺术中心，上海，2011年。艺术家提供。*


〔原书 248, 249〕

*Bullet Shot through a Young Heart* brings back to public consciousness the camouflaged history of loss in what is now often remembered only as a forgotten war. It serves as a meta-ideologizing return to a 1986 color print Lei Yan created after her deployment to the border. *Southern Border Dream* (plate 17) depicts her longing for peace and for her young son from whom she was separated during her service. Although the woman at the battlefront reverses the gender positions in the classical lament of separation when a conscripted son leaves his mother, she has not been liberated from the sacrifice required by militarism. Only in sleep can the exhausted solider, arm and head draped over her medical supply kit, generate the glowing vision that staves off the black grid at her back. Against that abstraction—the entombing grate of a bunker, the emplotting matrix of history—her dream radiates outward in a ring of orange and red. The motif that encircles the soldier features a mythical mother clothed in the flowing robe of an immortal and surrounded by a flock of doves. She reaches for her child, serenades him, and finally holds him in her arms. Almost twenty years later, that dream returns, not in the guise of an idealized woman soldier whose service and sacrifice is justified by visions of peace, but in her challenge to the national diplomatic narrative by remembering the untold young lives the conflict laid waste to. It also marks Lei Yan’s position as an artist in southwestern China, with its historical and shifting economic and cultural relations with bordering Southeast Asian nations.

《子弹穿过年轻的心》把被伪装起来的丧失历史重新带回公共意识——这场战争如今往往只被记得为一场被遗忘的战争。它是一次元意识形态化的回归，回到雷燕驻守边境后于1986年创作的一幅彩色版画。《南疆之梦》（图版17）描绘她在服役期间与年幼儿子分离时对和平、对儿子的思念。尽管这位身处前线的女性颠倒了古典离别哀歌中应征入伍的儿子离开母亲时的性别位置，她并未从军国主义所要求的牺牲中获得解放。只有在睡梦中，这位疲惫的士兵——手臂和头伏在医疗包上——才能生出那团挡住背后黑色网格的辉光。在那片抽象——掩体的墓穴般格栅、历史的情节化矩阵——之前，她的梦以橙红色的光环向外辐射。环绕士兵的图案中，一位神话中的母亲身穿飘逸的仙人衣袍，周围是一群白鸽。她伸手去够自己的孩子，为他哼唱摇篮曲，最后把他抱在怀里。近二十年后，那个梦回来了，但不再是借理想化女兵的形象——她的服役与牺牲由和平幻象来辩护——而是借雷燕对国家外交叙事的挑战：她记住了那场冲突所摧毁的无数无名年轻生命。这也标明了雷燕作为中国西南艺术家的位置，那里与接壤的东南亚国家之间有着历史上的、不断变化的经济与文化关系。


〔原书 249, 250〕

Wang Nanming, the curator of Lei Yan’s 2011 solo show, has asserted that her work breaks through the marginalizing category of nüxing yishu because of its overt political engagement. In an attempt to revitalize this theoretical language, he coins the term *kuanüxingzhuyi yishu*, translated as transfeminist art. He writes, “In trans-feminist art, women constitute a vital political power in the public sphere and are capable of discussing all sorts of issues of civic politics. Lei’s photograph series, *Bullet Shot through the Young Heart*, fights against the female identity superimposed upon female artists by Chinese modernity.”[^en-ch07-22] Wang’s use of the prefix “trans” emphasizes crossing and questioning boundaries, public and private, male and female, East and West, and the ways these categories are mapped onto one another. It suggests how art by Chinese women moves across and into local and global debates about art and politics. It also implies a new category of art that supersedes gendered binaries and forms of power, demonstrating a progressive logic similar to that of postfeminism. This latter claim that feminism is over and done—that its demands for justice have already been achieved or actually hold women back, or that Western-style gender equity need only be exported to other, less enlightened parts of the world—willfully ignores ongoing and intersectional forms of social hierarchy.[^en-ch07-23] Another understanding of Wang’s term of transfeminism emerges, however, if we consider that he arrives at it through his interpretation of work by He Chengyao and Lei Yan. The emphasis then shifts from overcoming feminism to thinking transhistorically across feminist movements, debates, and ruptures over the long twentieth century, in which women as a propositional category capable of shifting mass consciousness and as a collectivity of living social actors have since the beginning of Chinese modernity constituted “a vital political power in the public sphere.” The irony of the progressive-minded neologism authored by the male critic thus becomes its dependence on artists whose work is political not in spite of but because they are women who have focused a critical eye on the historical and political genealogies of gender that have caught and enabled them. It is through identification with and interrogation of subjects of Chinese modernity, the woman solider, military artist, and woman artist, that Lei Yan emerges as what Wang labels a transfeminist artist.

王南溟是雷燕2011年个展的策展人，他断言，由于雷燕作品中明显的政治介入，它突破了"女性艺术"这一边缘化范畴。为了复兴这套理论语言，他创造了"跨女性主义艺术"（kuanüxingzhuyi yishu）一词，英译为 transfeminist art。他写道："在跨女性主义艺术中，女性构成公共领域中一股重要的政治力量，能够讨论公民政治的各种问题。雷燕的摄影系列《子弹穿过年轻的心》，对抗中国现代性强加于女性艺术家的女性身份。"[^zh-ch07-22] 王南溟使用前缀"跨"，强调穿越和质疑边界——公共与私人、男性与女性、东方与西方——以及这些范畴相互映射的方式。它暗示中国女性的艺术如何穿越并进入关于艺术与政治的本地和全球争论。它也意味着一种超越性别二元与权力形式的新艺术范畴，展现出与后女性主义相似的进步逻辑。后一种主张——女性主义已经结束，其正义要求已经实现，或实际上阻碍了女性，或者西方式的性别平等只需输出到世界上其他不那么开化的地方——刻意无视持续存在且相互交织的社会等级形式。[^zh-ch07-23] 然而，如果我们注意到王南溟是通过对何成瑶和雷燕作品的解读得出这一术语的，那么对他所谓"跨女性主义"的另一种理解便浮现出来。此时重点不再是克服女性主义，而是跨历史地思考漫长二十世纪中的女性主义运动、争论与断裂；在这一视野中，女性作为能够推动群众意识的命题性范畴，也作为活生生的社会行动者的集体，自中国现代性肇始以来一直构成"公共领域中的一股重要政治力量"。于是，这位男性批评家所创的进步主义新词的讽刺之处，恰在于它依赖于这些艺术家——她们的作品之所以具有政治性，不是尽管她们是女性，而是因为她们是女性，而且她们把批判的目光投向性别的历史与政治谱系——这些谱系既束缚她们，也为她们提供行动的可能。正是通过认同并质询中国现代性的主体——女兵、军旅艺术家和女性艺术家——雷燕才成为王南溟所称的跨女性主义艺术家。


〔原书 250〕

Arrested Ephemerality

被截停的短暂性


〔原书 250〕

Lei Yan’s meditation on national, revolutionary iconography continued as she subjected objects from its corpus to material transmutation. Her works in ice, cloth, and paper capture the transience of image worlds. They arrest the process of disappearing, of being made ephemeral. They explore the contradiction between social idealism and social engineering. They evoke the volatile relationship between personhood and thingness, in which people can be treated as disposable, reproducible things, as much as things can be enchanted with humanity and life. In Arjun Appadurai’s conceit, “All things are congealed moments in a longer social trajectory.”[^en-ch07-24] Lei’s experiments explore the social lives of things as congealed moments in a longer trajectory of cumulative history, in which revolutionary collectivity serves as the substrate for a politics of market desire and efficiency. Her return to her military past challenges the soft-glow feminization of revolution in the avant-garde guise of come-hither Red Guards (see figure 1.01) and the liberal subject often assumed in Western feminist thought and art. It connects past fields of disaster to those that persist in the present.

雷燕对国家革命图像学的沉思仍在继续，她让这套图像语汇中的物件经历物质转化。她的冰、布、纸作品捕捉图像世界的短暂性。它们截停了消失、被化为短暂之物的过程。它们探索社会理想主义与社会工程之间的矛盾。它们唤出人格与物性之间不稳定的关系：人可以像物一样被当作一次性、可复制的东西，物也可以被人性与生命赋魅。用阿尔君·阿帕杜莱的比喻来说，"一切事物都是更长社会轨迹中的凝结时刻。"[^zh-ch07-24] 雷燕的实验探索物的社会生活，将它们视为更长累积历史轨迹中的凝结时刻；在这一轨迹中，革命集体性成为市场欲望与效率政治的基础。她对军旅过去的回归，挑战了先锋派表征中那种挑逗姿态的红卫兵式的、对革命的柔光女性化（见插图1.01），也挑战了西方女性主义思想与艺术中常预设的自由主义主体。它把过去的灾难场域与延续至今的灾难场域连接起来。


〔原书 250, 251〕

In 2006, Lei Yan created her *Frozen Red* series. She froze personal military insignias—pins, badges, medals, a Red Guard armband, a folded military jacket, Mao’s little red book—in blocks of ice and photographed them. The images are titled according to the year of the preserved object, such as her Red Guard armband from 1969 or her *Bayi* (eight-one) badge from 1985 after her Sino-Vietnamese War service.[^en-ch07-25] The interplay between lighting and imperfections in the ice produces different effects. A red flag pin glows ethereally just under the slick surface of ice. A round badge falls into its depths, with Mao’s face on it blurred and opaque. The folded jacket of Lei’s dress uniform, with its distinctive lapels marking it as that of a woman soldier, lies shiny and stiff in encrusted ice. After photographing the frozen jacket in her studio, she transported the slab of ice to the edge of the city and erected it at the bottom of a slope covered in green foliage. *Unnamed Tomb* (plate 18), the photographic record of this ritual of mourning, documents a ghostly sentinel surrounded by leafy groundcover. It momentarily preserves and remembers the possibilities, the woman soldier and her talent development, as well as the losses, of life and revolutionary belief, as her tombstone melts into a forgotten landscape.

2006年，雷燕创作了《冰封的红色》系列。她把个人的军旅徽记——领花、像章、奖章、红卫兵袖标、叠好的军装、毛主席语录——冻在冰块里，然后拍摄下来。这些图像按被保存物品的年份命名，例如她1969年的红卫兵袖标，或1985年中越战争服役后的八一徽章。[^zh-ch07-25] 光线与冰中瑕疵的相互作用产生不同效果。一枚红旗像章在光滑的冰面下发出空灵的光。一枚圆形像章沉入冰的深处，上面的毛泽东面孔模糊而不透明。雷燕军礼服的外套叠放着，其独特翻领表明这是一名女兵的军装，在结霜的冰中闪着光，僵直不动。在工作室拍完冰冻的军装后，她把那块冰运到城市边缘，竖立在一片绿荫覆盖的坡地底部。《无名之墓》（图版18）记录了这场哀悼仪式，拍下一名幽灵般的哨兵，周围是茂密的叶被。它短暂地保存并记住女兵及其才华发展的可能性，也记住生命与革命信念的失落，而她的墓碑正融入一片被遗忘的风景。


〔原书 251〕

![*图7.05　雷燕，《冰封的青春》第26号，2007年，摄影。艺术家提供。*](web/assets/ch07-b031.jpg)

FIG 7.05 Lei Yan, *Frozen Youth, No. 26*, 2007. Photograph. Courtesy of the artist.

*图7.05　雷燕，《冰封的青春》第26号，2007年，摄影。艺术家提供。*


〔原书 251, 252〕

In a subsequent series titled *Bullet Shot through a Young Heart II*, Lei Yan froze old photographs of life on the Sino-Vietnamese front and then rephotographed them. The ice warps and fissures the original images: soldiers carrying supplies and loading tanks guns, the corner of a sandbag bunker, a dark hole in a white concrete structure with “tomb of nine female heroes” scrawled above it. In the thirty-six photographs of a series from 2007, *Frozen Youth*, Lei hones in on her own military career. *Frozen Youth, No. 26* (figure 7.05), for example, features an ice-encased black-and-white photograph of the artist ten months after she joined the army. The face of the rifle-bearing teenage girl in uniform appears, through the refraction of light through ice, partly doubled. The unpredictability of the freezing process produces, by her own account, a remove from history that allows for observation of the past and consideration of it in relation to the contemporary moment, not unlike her binoculars in the *What If* images. The crystalline clarity of ice reflects the purity of collective spirit and sacrifice that were strong ideological elements of her military training but also sealed her off from other ways of thinking.[^en-ch07-26]

在随后题为《子弹穿过年轻的心II》的系列中，雷燕把中越前线生活的老照片冻入冰中，然后重新拍摄。冰使原图像扭曲、开裂：背着补给、给坦克装弹的士兵；沙袋掩体的一角；白色混凝土结构中的一个黑洞，上方潦草地写着"九位女英雄之墓"。在2007年系列《冰封的青春》的三十六幅照片中，雷燕聚焦于自己的军旅生涯。例如《冰封的青春》第26号（图7.05）把艺术家入伍十个月后的一张黑白照片封在冰里。照片中，那个持枪、穿制服的少女，面孔透过冰的折射，出现部分重影。按她自己的说法，冻结过程不可预测，制造出一种与历史的距离，使她得以观察过去，并把它与当下联系起来，就像她在《如果》图像中举起的望远镜。冰晶般的清澈映照着集体精神与牺牲的纯粹——这些是她军事训练中强大的意识形态元素，但也把她与其他思考方式隔绝开来。[^zh-ch07-26]


〔原书 252〕

Lei Yan’s use of old photos in these two series followed a 1990s trend examined by Wu Hung in “The ‘Old Photo Craze’ and Contemporary Chinese Art.” The low-budget, mass-produced serial *Lao Zhaopian* (Old photos), launched in 1996, gave its readers a platform to publish everyday photographs accompanied by written reflections. Wu argues that *Lao Zhaopian* served as a vehicle for “constructing a different type of history—history as collage and chance result, and as the synthetic voice of a multitude of amateur authors.”[^en-ch07-27] In turning to the use of old photos by Chinese contemporary artists, he identifies three approaches: works that represent memories of major, often suppressed historical events such as the Cultural Revolution; works that construct ordinary, personal histories; and works in which photos appear as “ruins” reflecting the instability of historical memory.[^en-ch07-28] Lei Yan’s *Frozen Youth* employs all three of these approaches at once.[^en-ch07-29] The series assembles an ordinary, personal history of participation in suppressed historical events meant to produce collective identification, including the Cultural Revolution and the Sino-Vietnamese War.[^en-ch07-30] It preserves these forgotten memories in a way that captures the magnifying and obscuring effects of the preservation process. It seizes on the multivalent visual idexicality of old photos.

雷燕在这两个系列中使用老照片，呼应了巫鸿在《"老照片热"与当代中国艺术》中考察的1990年代潮流。1996年创刊的低成本、大众化系列读物《老照片》，为读者提供了发表日常照片并附文字感想的平台。巫鸿认为，《老照片》是"建构另一种历史——作为拼贴与偶然结果的历史，作为众多业余作者合成声音的历史"的载体。[^zh-ch07-27] 在考察中国当代艺术家使用老照片的方式时，他辨认出三种路径：表现对重大、往往遭压抑的历史事件（如文化大革命）之记忆的作品；建构普通个人历史的作品；以及照片作为"废墟"出现、反映历史记忆之不稳定性的作品。[^zh-ch07-28] 雷燕的《冰封的青春》同时采用了这三种路径。[^zh-ch07-29] 该系列汇集了一部普通的个人史，其中参与的是那些旨在制造集体认同、却遭压抑的历史事件，包括文化大革命和中越战争。[^zh-ch07-30] 它保存这些被遗忘的记忆，同时捕捉保存过程本身的放大与遮蔽效应。它抓住了老照片多价的视觉指示性。


〔原书 252〕

Moving on to the medium of cloth, Lei Yan created a series of soft sculptures titled *Camouflage Production* (figure 7.06), which grew out of her obsession with the material she wore for thirty years as a soldier. While camouflage ostensibly provides cover and protection for military personnel on the battlefield, it also produces a uniform, national body to which other forms of identification are subordinated. Lei likens its patterning to the mixed, patchwork identities of those such as herself who have lived through multiple political movements in China. The fabric is also a global commodity entangled in the hierarchical, gendered relations of outsourced labor and related political battles over whether national military uniforms should be produced overseas.[^en-ch07-31] Lei’s sculptures crafted out of camouflage include daily-use items, such as kettles, teacups, cooking utensils, vases, sewing machines, telephones, and laptop computers. The gleaming utilitarian surface of industrially produced objects, which in the model kitchen turned battlefield once signified Cold War narratives of surpassing the enemy, now appear handmade, floppy, and rumpled. As readymade replicas cut from a textile developed for combat, they parody the symbolic myth-making power of things.

转向布这一媒介，雷燕创作了一系列题为《迷彩生产》的软雕塑（图7.06），其源于她对她作为士兵穿了三十年的材料的迷恋。迷彩表面上为战场上的军人提供掩蔽与保护，同时也生产出一种统一的、国家的身体，其他形式的认同都从属于它。雷燕把迷彩图案比作像她这样经历过中国多场政治运动者混杂、拼贴式的身份。这种面料也是一种全球商品，纠缠于外包劳动的等级化、性别化关系，以及关于国家军服是否应在海外生产的政治争斗。[^zh-ch07-31] 雷燕用迷彩制作的雕塑包括日用品，如水壶、茶杯、炊具、花瓶、缝纫机、电话和笔记本电脑。工业化生产物品那光亮的实用表面——在样板厨房变成战场的年代，它曾意味着超越敌人的冷战叙事——如今显得手工、松软而皱巴。作为用为战斗开发的纺织品裁出的现成品复制品，它们戏仿了物的象征神话制造力。


〔原书 253〕

![*图7.06　雷燕，《迷彩生产》，2007年，织物雕塑。艺术家提供。*](web/assets/ch07-b035.jpg)

FIG 7.06 Lei Yan, *Camouflage Production*, 2007. Fabric sculpture. Courtesy of the artist.

*图7.06　雷燕，《迷彩生产》，2007年，织物雕塑。艺术家提供。*


〔原书 253, 254〕

Lei Yan’s reference to domestic space and use of needlework resonate with works often included in a global canon of feminist art, such as the *Womanhouse* project that Judy Chicago hoped to re-create with Chinese interlocutors, but Lei injects these now familiar tropes with the Chinese history of woman soldier/art soldier. In *I Love Kitchen*, camouflage items cover gallery walls in a random, almost haphazard way.[^en-ch07-32] This installation amasses and scatters across white walls the signs of household containment and geopolitical conflict; frenzied materialism and national sacrifice; domestic and global economies. Its chaotic arrangement suggests the dual frontlines the modern Chinese woman has faced: the double duty of political and domestic labor. Tasked with both symbolic representation of the nation and sociobiological reproduction of the family, she has been mobilized and demobilized, pulled into public production and returned to the kitchen, according to the needs of the state.[^en-ch07-33] At the catachrestic conjunction of woman soldier/art soldier/woman artist, Lei Yan confronts the double bind of either serving the nation, regardless of its repressions, or being stuck in “inner quarters” of domestic introspection. The enthusiastically titled *I Love Kitchen*, which spoofs patriotic love of country and the idea of domestic bliss, stitches together public and private, as domains that are not dichotomous but differentially constructed through each other.

雷燕对家庭空间的指涉和对针线活的使用，与全球女性主义艺术经典中常收录的作品产生共鸣，例如朱迪·芝加哥希望与中国对话者一起重建的"女人屋"计划；但雷燕为这些如今已为人熟知的意象注入了女兵／艺术战士的中国历史。在《我爱厨房》中，迷彩物品以随意、近乎杂乱的方式覆盖画廊墙面。[^zh-ch07-32] 这件装置把家庭禁锢与地缘冲突的符号、狂热的物质主义与国家牺牲、家庭经济与全球经济，积聚并散布在白墙之上。其混乱布置暗示中国现代女性面临的双重前线：政治劳动与家务劳动的双重职责。她既被要求承担国家的象征表征，又承担家庭的社会生物学再生产，于是随着国家需要被动员、被复员，被拉入公共生产，又被送回厨房。[^zh-ch07-33] 在女兵／艺术战士／女性艺术家这一词语误用式的交汇处，雷燕直面双重束缚：要么服务于国家，不论其压迫；要么困于家庭内省的内闱。那个热情洋溢的标题《我爱厨房》戏仿了对国家的爱国之爱与家庭幸福生活的观念，把公共与私人缝合在一起，视为并非二分、而是通过彼此差异化建构的领域。


〔原书 254〕

![*图7.07　雷燕，《梦开始的地方》第6号，2011年，纸与线软雕塑。艺术家提供。*](web/assets/ch07-b037.jpg)

FIG 7.07 Lei Yan, *A Place Where Dream Starts, No. 6*, 2011. Paper and thread soft sculpture. Courtesy of the artist.

*图7.07　雷燕，《梦开始的地方》第6号，2011年，纸与线软雕塑。艺术家提供。*


〔原书 254〕

After ice and cloth, Lei Yan began sculpting objects out of paper, producing ghostlike facsimiles that evoke the absent human presence of those who once wore or carried these things. Her 2011 series, *A Place Where Dream Starts* (figure 7.07), consists of objects from everyday military life: cap, sneakers, artillery belt, cups, canteen, and handheld missiles. Fashioned after the things she once had an intimate material relationship with, they are reminiscent of traditional Chinese funerary offerings, paper objects burned to accompany the dead into the afterworld. The dream implied by the title and the ethereal quality of the spot-lit sculptures suggest the reveries of youth and idealism. Their light, crumpled paper surfaces take recognizable shape and simultaneously make it appear insubstantial. The dream then becomes one of redemption for those lost to past worldings and the work of art that set up those worlds and made them visible, tangible, desirable, material.

在冰与布之后，雷燕开始用纸塑造物件，制作出幽灵般的仿制品，唤起曾经穿戴或携带这些东西的人不在场的存在。她2011年的系列《梦开始的地方》（图7.07）由军旅日常生活中的物品组成：帽子、运动鞋、炮兵腰带、杯子、水壶和手持导弹。这些仿照她曾与之有亲密物质关系的物品做成，让人联想到中国传统丧葬明器——为陪伴死者进入来世而焚烧的纸物。标题所暗示的梦，与聚光灯下雕塑的空灵质感，暗示着青春与理想主义的遐想。它们轻薄、皱褶的纸面呈现可辨认的形状，同时又显得虚幻不实。于是梦变成一种救赎之梦，既为那些失落于过往世界营造的人，也为艺术曾经承担的工作——建立那些世界，使它们可见、可触、可欲，并具有物质实在。


〔原书 254, 255〕

This meta-ideological meditation on her military past emerged from a piece Lei Yan created two year prior. The question of its title *How Do I Protect You*? (figure 7.08) is posed to the children who died en masse in the 8.0-magnitude earthquake that hit the Sichuan counties of Wenchuan and Beichuan on May 12, 2008. Shoddy construction of classrooms and dormitories amplified the natural disaster’s death toll. Collapsed school buildings crushed and killed thousands of students, many of whose bodies were never recovered. Their grieving parents declared the engineering of the buildings, some recently constructed, not just tofu but tofu dregs. Those who demanded a count of the number of student deaths and investigation into corrupt officials and contractors who had taken shortcuts were silenced in the name of stability. From this landscape of disaster, official media broadcast a story of humanitarian aid and the reestablishment of “harmonious society” after an exceptional event.[^en-ch07-34] Social critics attempted to peel back the veneer of this picture and the loss it obscured.
