The Wen-chuan earthquake, like other social crises and controversies, became a touchstone for artists negotiating a new market-driven valuation of art, its traffic in images, and a legacy of aesthetic commitment to social commentary and collective political struggle. Ai Weiwei, for example, responded to the student deaths with projects that blended the creation of modernist art objects on a spectacular scale with online social activism, performative confrontations with Chinese police and legal systems, and documentary filmmaking. While the international place of prominence given to Ai’s activities has tended to eclipse other work, he was one among many artists moved by this and related scenes of chronic disaster amid an everyday landscape of environmental degradation and economic inequality.[^en-ch07-35]

这场对她军旅过去的元意识形态沉思，源自雷燕两年前创作的一件作品。其标题《我如何保护你？》（图7.08）中的问题，是向2008年5月12日四川汶川、北川8.0级地震中成群罹难的孩子提出的。教室与宿舍的劣质建筑放大了自然灾害的死亡人数。倒塌的校舍压死数千名学生，许多人遗体始终未能找到。悲痛欲绝的家长宣称，这些建筑——有些还是新近建成的——不只是豆腐，而是豆腐渣。那些要求统计学生死亡人数、调查偷工减料的腐败官员与承包商的人，被以稳定之名噤声。官方媒体从这片灾难景观中播出的，是一个人道主义救援的故事，以及在非常事件之后重建"和谐社会"的故事。[^zh-ch07-34] 社会批评者试图剥开这幅画面的表皮，揭示它所遮蔽的丧失。汶川地震像其他社会危机与争议一样，成为艺术家们处理的试金石，涉及艺术在市场驱动下的新估值、图像的流通，以及美学上致力于社会批判与集体政治斗争的遗产。例如，艾未未以多种项目回应学生之死，把壮观尺度的现代主义艺术物品创作，与网络社会行动、与中国警察和法律系统对抗的行为表演，以及纪录片制作结合起来。尽管艾未未的活动所获得的国际显要位置往往遮蔽了其他作品，他只是在环境退化与经济不平等的日常景观中，被这幕及类似慢性灾难场景所触动的众多艺术家之一。[^zh-ch07-35]


〔原书 255, 257〕

From a distance, Lei’s installation of *How Do I Protect You*? looks like a pile of trash. On closer inspection, it becomes apparent that she has meticulously re-created the site of a collapsed school building. Working with translucent white filter paper, needle, and thread, she sculpted crumpled walls, pillars, and furniture. Small details buried within pull viewers closer, implicating them as voyeuristic witnesses to a crime scene. Shoes, pencil boxes, and backpacks spill out from the rubble. Small black-and-white student photographs are tucked into the front pockets of the backpacks (figure 7.09). Tiny paper flowers on long, weedy stems sprout from the scattered personal effects. For the parents of children whose bodies were never recovered, these objects remained all they could collect. Some assembled possessions pulled from the rubble together with stuffed animals, snacks, and bottled drinks to builds altars to their disappeared children in front of school ruins. These ritual offerings, which inverted the Chinese practice of ancestor worship, with a parent feeding the memory of a child instead of the other way around, insisted on the existence of lost lives the state tried to erase with money offered for families’ silence. Lei Yan’s hand-sewn re-creation of everyday use objects reenchants them in a similar way, while her choice of materials echoes the condemnatory criticism of poorly constructed buildings as tofu dregs. These ghost objects, rather than easing spiritual passage like their ritual counterpart of joss paper burned in veneration of the dead, stand in instead for life after life in a field of death and disaster, where the unequal distribution of life and death are justified by the intertwined projects of late socialism and late liberalism. The paper sculpture series that followed include *A Place Where Dream Starts* and *On the Road*, a cluster of bags and suitcases arranged on the cement floor of an empty factory space. Together these three-dimensional explorations in the flimsy medium of paper evoke the precariousness of life—the ubiquitous traffic between personhood and thingness—for the young soldier, the migrant worker, the lost child, those unaccounted for and gone missing again and again.

从远处看，雷燕的装置《我如何保护你？》像一堆垃圾。靠近观察，才会发现她一丝不苟地重建了一栋倒塌校舍的现场。她用半透明的白色滤纸、针和线，塑造出皱褶的墙壁、柱子和家具。埋在其中的细小细节把观者拉近，使他们成为犯罪现场的窥视证人。鞋子、铅笔盒和书包从瓦砾中溢出。小小的黑白学生照塞在书包前袋里（图7.09）。细长、杂草般的茎上开着纸花，从散落的私人物品中钻出。对于遗体始终未能找到的孩子的父母来说，这些物品仍是他们所能收集的一切。有些家长把从瓦砾中找出的物品与毛绒玩具、零食、瓶装饮料摆在一起，在校舍废墟前为他们失踪的孩子搭建祭坛。这些仪式供品颠倒了中国祖先崇拜的实践，变成父母喂养对孩子的记忆，而不是反过来；它们坚持那些被国家试图用封口费抹除的逝去生命的存在。雷燕对手缝日常用物的再创造，以类似方式使它们重新赋魅；而她选择的材料，呼应了把劣质建筑斥为豆腐渣的谴责性批评。这些幽灵般的物件不像其仪式对应物——为敬奉死者而焚烧的纸钱——那样帮助灵魂过渡，而是代表死亡与灾难场域中一个生命又一个生命的存在；在那里，生与死的不平等分配，由晚期社会主义与晚期自由主义相互交织的工程所辩护。随后的纸雕系列包括《梦开始的地方》和《在路上》——一组袋子和手提箱，摆在一处空置厂房的水泥地上。这些以轻薄纸张为媒介的三维探索，共同唤出生命的不稳定性——人格与物性之间无处不在的流转——为年轻士兵、民工、失去的孩子，为那些一次又一次下落不明、消失无踪的人。


〔原书 256〕

![*图7.08、7.09　雷燕，《我如何保护你？》，2011年，纸雕，展览现场及局部。艺术家提供。*](web/assets/ch07-b041.png)

FIG 7.08 AND 7.09 Lei Yan, *How Do I Protect You*? 2011. Paper sculpture, installation view and detail. Courtesy of the artist.

*图7.08、7.09　雷燕，《我如何保护你？》，2011年，纸雕，展览现场及局部。艺术家提供。*


〔原书 257〕

Monumental Ephemeral

纪念碑式／短暂性


〔原书 257, 258〕

At the turn of the millennium, a new culture industry took up contemporary art as a way to advance China’s national image on the global stage. The state enlisted the names and talents of “dissident” figures who had spent years abroad or whose work had once been censored. Artists like Ai Weiwei and Cai Guoqiang and filmmakers like Zhang Yimou and Jia Zhangke contributed to the monumental spectacles of the 2008 Beijing Olympics and 2010 Shanghai World Expo. These twenty-first-century spectacles of awe-inspiring national achievement continued a legacy of form that runs through imperial and Maoist China: of artworks, buildings, and rituals executed on a grand scale. Large-scale structures from the Great Wall to the Monument to the People’s Heroes in Tiananmen Square to the Bird’s Nest Stadium are invested with the power of monumentality, the control and shaping of collective memory. As Wu Hung notes in an essay on the subject, “The Latin root of monumentality means recalling and admonishing. In order to exercise the function of admonition, official monuments always are awesome, majestic, and inhuman structures; their huge mass controls the public space in which they are placed.”[^en-ch07-36] As a challenge to this function, Chinese avant-garde artists in the 1980s and 1990s experimented with antimonumentality, creating pieces that Wu identifies as either countermonuments or attempts to achieve antimonuments. Hence, the large number of experimental art projects on the Great Wall. The problem with an antimonumental critique of monumental power is that it often slides toward that which it aims to deconstruct. The propensity of Chinese experimental artists to make large-scale pieces that command the world’s attention perpetuates the socialist mandate to forge a new political order through cultural production and revolution. This like-sized response to the hegemony of art as state politics and to the global cultural order of things risks mimicking and reproducing the spectacular society it purports to critique. It engages in a politics of scale that continues to *world* in powerful ways.

世纪之交，一种新的文化产业把当代艺术当作在全球舞台上推进中国国家形象的方式。国家征用了那些曾在海外多年、或作品曾被审查的"异见"人物的名字与才华。艾未未、蔡国强等艺术家，张艺谋、贾樟柯等电影人，参与了2008年北京奥运会和2010年上海世博会这些纪念碑式的盛景。这些21世纪令人惊叹的国家成就景观，延续了一种贯穿帝制中国与毛泽东时代中国的形式遗产：以宏大尺度创作艺术品、建筑与仪式。从长城到天安门广场的人民英雄纪念碑，再到鸟巢体育场，大型结构都被赋予了纪念碑性的力量，即对集体记忆的控制与塑造。正如巫鸿在一篇相关论文中所说："纪念碑性（monumentality）的拉丁词根意为回忆与告诫。为了行使告诫功能，官方纪念碑总是令人敬畏、庄严、非人的结构；其巨大的体量控制着它所置身的公共空间。"[^zh-ch07-36] 作为对这种功能的挑战，1980年代和1990年代的中国先锋艺术家实验反纪念碑性，创作出巫鸿所说的反纪念碑，或试图达成非纪念碑的作品。因此才有大量以长城为题的实验艺术计划。对纪念碑式权力进行反纪念碑批判，问题在于它常常滑向它想要解构的东西。中国实验艺术家偏爱创作吸引世界注意的大型作品，这延续了社会主义的使命：通过文化生产与革命锻造新的政治秩序。这种以同等尺度回应艺术作为国家政治的霸权，以及全球文化物序，可能模仿并再生产它声称批判的景观社会。它参与一种尺度政治，并继续以强大的方式从事世界营造。


〔原书 258〕

Ai Weiwei, who gained local and global distinction through his role as design consultant on the National Stadium for the Beijing Olympics, serves as the most prominent example of this phenomenon, as well as the contradictions that arose during this turning-point period for Chinese contemporary art. Even in his later critique of the Olympics, antagonism to the state, and commitment to art as social activism, his activities assumed an epic scale: in their formal aesthetics, resources commanded for their realization, and international recognition for their bad boy political dissent. In William Callahan’s analysis of Ai as a figure of ironic tensions, he observes the mutual dependence of dissidents and officials for “their respective legitimacies and identities,” in which “Ai’s anti-state oppositional discourse thus tends to reproduce the state even as it resists it.”[^en-ch07-37] The pieces Ai Weiwei created in response to the Wenchuan earthquake, exhibited in museums around the world, are monumental in scale. They admonish state silence, even as they represent that same nation-state in the international art arena.

艾未未因担任北京奥运会国家体育场设计顾问而获得本地与全球声誉，是这一现象最突出的例子，也是中国当代艺术这一转折时期出现的矛盾的例子。即便在他后来对奥运会的批判、对国家的对抗，以及把艺术当作社会行动的承诺中，他的活动也呈现出史诗般的尺度：形式美学、为实现作品所调动的资源，以及因其坏男孩式的政治异见而获得的国际认可，皆如此。在威廉·卡拉汉把艾未未分析为反讽张力人物的文章中，他观察到异见者与官员"各自合法性与身份"的相互依赖："艾未未反国家的对抗话语因此往往在抵抗国家的同时再生产国家。"[^zh-ch07-37] 艾未未为回应汶川地震而创作、在世界各地博物馆展出的作品，在尺度上是纪念碑式的。它们谴责国家的沉默，同时又在国际艺术舞台上表征同一个民族国家。


〔原书 258, 259〕

In Lei Yan’s *How Can I Protect You*?, paper sculptures of backpacks spill out from insubstantial, ghostly rubble. In Ai Weiwei’s *Remembering*, installed in 2009 across the façade of Munich’s Haus der Kunst, nine thousand colorful children’s backpacks write out in bubbly Chinese characters, “She lived happily in this world for seven years.” A Beichuan mother who refused compensation money for her daughter’s death wrote this sentence as what she wanted people to remember. For *Straight*, an installation piece first exhibited in his 2012–13 survey show at the Hirshhorn Museum in Washington DC, Ai purchased thirty-eight tons of mangled rebar salvaged from the earthquake reconstruction zone and hired a team of workers to hammer it straight. He then arranged it in piles of various heights to create a long, rolling landscape of rusted steel ruptured by fault lines. The accompanying wall text read, “The tragic reality of today is reflected in the true plight of our spiritual existence. We are spineless and cannot stand straight.” *Sichuan Name List* (2008–11) records the name, gender, age, school, and class of 5,212 children who perished in the earthquake, information collected by the hundreds of citizen volunteers who responded to Ai Weiwei’s online call for an investigation into the student deaths. Installed at the Hirshhorn, the list spanned a massive, curving wall. A monument to the dead and the collective labor it took to document them, it resembles a war memorial. Lei Yan’s small rumpled paper sculpture *Ten Years of Dying Young*, created in 2012, also presents a list. Three flower-strewn tablets record crises of the millennium’s first decade with the Wenchuan earthquake inserted into a transnational field of death and injury in combat zones, terrorist actions, industrial accidents, and natural disasters.

在雷燕的《我如何保护你？》中，背包的纸雕从不坚实的、幽灵般的瓦砾中溢出。在艾未未的《铭记》中，九千个彩色儿童书包于2009年铺满慕尼黑艺术之家的立面，用圆润的中文字体写出："她在这个世界上幸福地生活了七年。"一位北川母亲拒绝为女儿之死接受赔偿金，她写下这句话，作为她希望人们记住的内容。在《直》中——这件装置作品首次展出于华盛顿赫希洪博物馆2012—13年艾未未回顾展——艾未未购买了从地震重建区回收的三十八吨扭曲钢筋，雇了一队工人把它锤直，然后将其堆成高低不一的垛，构成一片被断层线撕裂的锈蚀钢地景。展墙上的说明文字写道："今日的悲剧现实，映照出我们精神存在的真实困境。我们毫无脊梁，无法站直。"《四川名单》（2008—11）记录了5212名在地震中罹难儿童的名字、性别、年龄、学校和班级；这些信息由数百名公民志愿者收集，他们响应艾未未的网上呼吁，要求调查学生死亡。安装在赫希洪博物馆时，名单铺满一整面巨大的弧形墙。它是一座献给死者的纪念碑，也是记录他们所付出的集体劳动的纪念碑，形似战争纪念碑。雷燕2012年创作的小型皱纸雕塑《早逝的十年》也呈现了一份名单。三块散布着花朵的碑板记录了新千年第一个十年的危机，把汶川地震插入一个跨国死亡与伤痛场域——战区、恐怖行动、工业事故与自然灾害。


〔原书 259〕

It would be facile in comparing these works—the monumental and the ephemeral—to reinscribe familiar dichotomies of male/female, liumang/nüxing, public and private. Such a normativizing move would erase the traces of the ephemeral in the monumental and of the monumental in the ephemeral. Considering art by Ai Weiwei and Lei Yan together, while a seeming “impossible reality” in current curatorial rules of the game, makes it possible to see them also as ethnographic fragments of avant-garde/xianfeng cultural transition. As much as Lei Yan’s work inhabits an image world of late Qing and early Republican illustrations of women with binoculars to their eyes, so too is it in relationship with pieces like Ai Weiwei’s *Remembering, Straight*, and *Sichuan Name List*. Holding these works together is a way of understanding Chinese contemporary art in the expanded field, putting those marginalized by globalized, professionalized circuits back in and asking what new questions and lines of sight this method of montage opens up. How does a feminist lens highlight the contradictions of an emerging art world and enable a differential consciousness about the shifting role of art—as ideological, institutional, and imaginative—within various configurations of power?

比较这两类作品——纪念碑式的与短暂性的——时，若只是重新刻写男／女、流氓／女性、公共／私人这些熟悉的二分法，便流于肤浅。这种规范化举动会抹去纪念碑中的短暂性痕迹，以及短暂性中的纪念碑性痕迹。把艾未未与雷燕的艺术放在一起考虑，尽管在现行策展游戏规则中看似"不可能的现实"，却使我们得以把它们也视为avant-garde／先锋文化转型的民族志碎片。正如雷燕的作品栖居于晚清民初举望远镜女子的图像世界，它也与艾未未的《铭记》《直》《四川名单》等作品发生关系。把这些作品放在一起，是在扩展场域中理解中国当代艺术的一种方式：把被全球化、专业化循环边缘化的人重新放回去，并追问这种蒙太奇方法开启了什么新问题与新视线。女性主义镜头如何凸显一个新兴艺术世界的矛盾，并使人们形成一种差异意识，去理解艺术——作为意识形态的、制度的与想象的——在各种权力配置中不断变化的角色？


〔原书 259, 260〕

The biographies of these two artists, born within months of each other in the early years of the People’s Republic, read in parallel reveal shifts and struggles among what Bourdieau identifies as the fields of cultural production, of power, and of economics or class relations.[^en-ch07-38] Ai Weiwei was born in 1957. His father—a poet who had studied in France, endured Guomindang imprisonment, joined Mao at Yan’an, and edited *People’s Literature*—was denounced that same year in the Anti-Rightist Campaign and sent to China’s northwest with his family. After seventeen years of exile in Heilongjiang and Xinjiang, they returned to Beijing. In 1978, Ai Weiwei briefly attended the Beijing Film Academy. A red princeling, heir to a patriline of art and politics, vagrancy and imprisonment, he left China for the United States in 1981. For twelve years he lived in New York, where he studied at the Parsons School of Design, befriended Allen Ginsberg, and became a peripatetic photographer of East Village life. Lei Yan was also born in 1957, into the family of a career officer in the People’s Liberation Army. She followed her father into the military, studied printmaking as part of her army training, photographed life on the Sino-Vietnamese front, and received advance training at the pla’s Arts Academy. When Ai Weiwei became the official Chinese consultant to the Swiss firm designing the Beijing Olympics National Stadium, it seemed like the ultimate *tizhi wai* (outside-the-system) artist had reversed position in service to a monumental statement of China’s arrival on the world stage. When Lei Yan posed “what if” questions to Mao retrospectively adorned with a 1930s female hairstyle, it seemed like the ultimate *tizhi nei* (inside-the-system) artist had reversed position in a deconstructive tour of the past and its archives.

这两位艺术家都生于中华人民共和国成立后的早期岁月，出生时间相隔数月；并置阅读他们的传记，可以揭示布尔迪厄所说的文化生产场域、权力场域以及经济或阶级关系场域之间的转变与斗争。[^zh-ch07-38] 艾未未1957年出生。他的父亲是一位诗人，曾留学法国，经历国民党监禁，赴延安追随毛泽东，后来主编《人民文学》；就在同一年，他在反右运动中被批判，和家人一起被送往中国西北。在黑龙江和新疆流放十七年后，他们回到北京。1978年，艾未未曾短暂就读于北京电影学院。作为一个红色太子党——继承着艺术与政治、漂泊与监禁的父系血脉——他于1981年离开中国前往美国。在纽约生活的十二年间，他在帕森斯设计学院学习，与艾伦·金斯伯格成为朋友，成为东村生活的游走摄影师。雷燕也生于1957年，出身于中国人民解放军职业军官家庭。她追随父亲进入军队，在部队训练中学习版画，在中越前线拍摄生活，并在解放军艺术学院接受高级培训。当艾未未成为瑞士公司设计北京奥运会国家体育场的官方中方顾问时，那个看似最彻底的"体制外"艺术家仿佛转变了立场，为一个宣告中国登上世界舞台的纪念碑式作品服务。当雷燕以1930年代女性发型追溯性地装扮毛泽东，并提出"如果"问题时，那个看似最彻底的"体制内"艺术家仿佛转变了立场，展开了一场穿越过去及其档案的解构之旅。


〔原书 260, 261〕

Their unfolding lives and works, shaped by a history in which art and politics were never understood as autonomous realms, briefly approach each other in their responses to Chinese state image management of the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake. Are they part of the same or competing sectors of the field of cultural production? Their reversals in relation to the “system,” as well as the depth of their conceptual practices and aesthetic excavations, force a reworking of Bourdieu’s analytic framework, which was developed in a bourgeois European context. Art in the Maoist field was theorized as aligned with revolutionary power, rather than in a dominated or inverted relationship with it. It did not tend toward the dominant pole of the field of capitalist class relations; its superstructure was intended to lead the base, to smash colonial and class hierarchy. Chinese contemporary art in the era of late socialism–late liberalism is a field of contradictory historical and ideological forces and of competing institutionalized authorities and economies. This has become the playing field for an artist like Ai Weiwei, imprisoned and embraced by the monumentalizing gestures of canonization. His art commands public museum spaces the world over, exposing (and solidifying) the Chinese state in the name of freedom and progress. The work of Lei Yan, a former pla propagandist working from the edge of the nation and the margins of the international art world, raises the following questions: What spectres of “always already absent present” haunt Ai Weiwei’s aesthetic experiments?[^en-ch07-39] For whom are these heroic politics of exposure most persuasive? What makes London’s Tate Modern broadcast from its rooftop the message “Release Ai Weiwei,” rather than “Recognize and compensate the families of lost children” or “The people have suffered from the coalition of government and business”? [^en-ch07-40]

他们展开的生命与作品，由一段艺术与政治从未被理解为自主领域的历史所塑造；在回应中国国家对2008年汶川地震的图像管理时，二者短暂地彼此接近。他们属于文化生产场域中相同的部分，还是相互竞争的部分？他们相对于"体制"的反转，以及他们观念实践的深度与美学挖掘，迫使人们重做布尔迪厄的分析框架——该框架是在欧洲资产阶级语境中发展起来的。在毛泽东时代的场域中，艺术被理论化为与革命权力结盟，而不是与它处于被支配或颠倒的关系。它并不趋向资本主义阶级关系场域的主导极；它的上层建筑意在引领基础，粉碎殖民与阶级等级。晚期社会主义—晚期自由主义时代的中国当代艺术，是一个充满矛盾的历史与意识形态力量、相互竞争的建制化权威与经济的场域。这里已成为像艾未未这样的艺术家的竞技场；他既被经典化过程中的纪念碑化姿态所禁锢，也被其接纳。他的艺术占据全世界公共博物馆空间，以自由与进步之名暴露（并巩固）中国国家。雷燕的作品出自一名前解放军宣传干部之手，她从民族国家的边缘与国际艺术界的边缘工作，提出以下问题：什么样的"总是已经缺席的在场"的幽灵萦绕着艾未未的美学实验？[^zh-ch07-39] 这些英雄式的暴露政治对谁最有说服力？又是什么让伦敦泰特现代美术馆从屋顶发出"释放艾未未"的信息，而不是"承认并赔偿失去孩子的家庭"或"人民饱受政府与商业联盟之苦"？[^zh-ch07-40]


〔原书 261〕

In June 1994, five years after the events of June 4, Ai Weiwei photographed his wife, the artist Lu Qing, in Tiananmen Square. She stands in front of the Gate of Heavenly Peace, her back against the pedestrian barricade on the opposite side of Chang’an Boulevard, far away enough that her head appears next to and the same size as Mao’s in the larger-than-life portrait that hangs behind her. Her head cocked to the side and one foot propped up on the metal barricade, she stares casually at the camera while lifting her translucent black skirt with both hands to expose her underwear. In a twist on the socialist use of the female body to expose and attack class enemies, her flippant pin-up pose disregards and diminishes the monumental power of Mao. Although the photograph has since circulated as an early example of Ai Weiwei in “Fuck Off” mode, at the moment of its initial exposure, the question of artistic agency remains open to speculation. Is Ai Weiwei as photographer or Lu Qing as performer the artist? Who is the image made for? A year later Ai Weiwei stood further from the Gate in Tiananmen Square and photographed his own hand flipping a middle finger to Mao’s portrait. In *Study in Perspective*, his raised digit in the foreground takes the place of Lu Qing’s body next to the Chairman, looming large beside the portrait, threatening to blot it out. The woman and her conflicted, embodied politics of exposure disappear from the picture. Almost two decades later, Ai Weiwei created a large-scale piece for the 2013 Venice Biennale titled *S.A.C.R.E.D*. Its six parts—Supper, Accused, Cleansing, Ritual, Entropy, Doubt—depict in realist detail his eighty-one day prison detention in 2011. Large iron boxes, installed in the place of pews in a church turned art gallery, contain half-scale plexiglass dioramas of the incarcerated artist being interrogated, showering, eating, shitting, and sleeping. Spectators can observe these scenes through small glass windows on the sides or tops of the boxes. In a sculptural installation that takes on the weight and scale of history painting, the artist’s own body on display becomes the locus of indignity, suffering, and resistance. It is a spectacular form of self-portraiture haunted by a Maoist legacy of charismatic male leadership.

1994年6月，即6月4日事件五年后，艾未未在天安门广场拍摄了他的妻子、艺术家路青。她站在天安门前，背靠长安街对面的行人护栏，距离足够远，使她的头出现在身后那幅巨型毛泽东画像旁边，且大小相同。她歪着头，一只脚搭在金属护栏上，随意地盯着镜头，同时用双手撩起半透明的黑裙，露出内裤。这是对社会主义利用女性身体来揭露和攻击阶级敌人的一次反转：她轻佻的招贴女郎姿态无视并缩小了毛泽东的纪念碑式权力。尽管这张照片后来作为艾未未"滚蛋"（Fuck Off）模式的早期例子流传，但在它最初曝光之时，艺术能动性的归属仍有待探究。作为摄影师的艾未未，还是作为表演者的路青，才是艺术家？这张图像是为谁而作？一年后，艾未未站得更远，在天安门广场拍摄自己向毛泽东画像竖中指的手。在《透视研究》中，前景里他竖起的手指取代了路青在主席旁边的身体，在画像旁赫然耸立，几乎要将其遮蔽。女人及其充满冲突的、具身的暴露政治从画面中消失了。近二十年后，艾未未为2013年威尼斯双年展创作了一件大型作品《S.A.C.R.E.D.》。它的六个部分——《晚餐》《被告》《清洗》《仪式》《熵》《怀疑》——以写实细节描绘他2011年被监禁的八十一天。大型铁箱安装在由教堂改成的美术馆里，取代了长椅，里面装着半比例的有机玻璃立体模型，再现这位被囚艺术家受审、洗澡、进食、排便和睡觉的场景。观众可以通过铁箱侧面或顶部的小玻璃窗观察这些场景。在这件具有历史画重量与尺度的雕塑装置中，艺术家自己的身体成为屈辱、受难与抵抗的展示场所。这是一种奇观式的自画像，被毛泽东时代富有魅力的男性领导遗产所萦绕。


〔原书 261, 262〕

Lei Yan’s paper sculptures are similarly haunted but respond to the legacy by a refusal to authoritatively represent. Her arrested objects resist the temporal pull of narrative and modernity’s myth of progress. Their empty presence decenters the human subject, drawing attention instead to absences and omissions in normative stories of art, feminism, and nation. Her lightweight sculptures turn away from the tradition of history painting so central to socialist aesthetics and toward the genre of the still life. An evacuated pair of military sneakers was one of the first forms she fashioned out of paper. They give shape to what Norman Bryson analyzes in still life painting as the voiding of individual or idealized human presence: “Still life takes on the exploration of what ‘importance’ tramples underfoot.” [^en-ch07-41] Jacques Derrida likewise ruminates on the relationship between subject and object through a still life painting of shoes: “As soon as these abandoned shoes no longer have any strict relationship with a subject borne or bearing/wearing, they become the anonymous, lightened, voided support (but so much the heavier from being abandoned to its opaque inertia) of an absent subject whose name returns to haunt the open form.” [^en-ch07-42]

雷燕的纸雕塑同样被萦绕，但它回应这份遗产的方式是拒绝权威性再现。她被截停的物件抵抗叙事的时间牵引与现代化的进步神话。它们空无的在场使人类主体去中心化，转而把注意力引向规范性的艺术、女性主义与民族故事中的缺席与遗漏。她轻巧的雕塑背离社会主义美学中如此核心的历史画传统，转向静物画。一双被掏空的军旅运动鞋，是她最早用纸塑造的形态之一。它们赋予诺曼·布列逊在静物画分析中所说的个体或理想化人类在场之清空以形状："静物画承担了对'重要性'所践踏之物的探索。"[^zh-ch07-41] 雅克·德里达同样通过一幅鞋子静物画来思考主体与客体的关系："一旦这些被遗弃的鞋子不再与任何被承载或承载／穿着它们的主体保持严格关系，它们就成为一个缺席主体之匿名、轻盈、被清空的支撑（但因为被遗弃于其不透明的惰性中而沉重得多），这个主体的名字回来萦绕这开放的形式。"[^zh-ch07-42]


〔原书 262〕

The Hallowed Object

神圣之物


〔原书 262, 263〕

Lei Yan has continued to work in paper, manipulating, creasing, and sewing the flat material into a surfeit of three-dimensional objects, each of which would readily fit in the hand. For *The Hallowed Object*, a 2016 solo exhibition in Beijing’s Caochangdi art district, she displayed seventy-six sculpted objects en masse, arranged along a narrow shelf the entire length of a gallery wall. The exhibit also included black-and-white photographs of the objects—some taking representational shape, others uncanny in form—as single pieces or in small groupings. A tall, slender cone topped with a five-point star stands forlornly on its own. An upright axe and sickle turn away from each other. A larger assembly of objects (figure 7.10) resembles a domestic still life with bottles, vases, and a candlestick, but it also includes the axe and sickle, a bugle, an antitank missile, and a trench mortar bomb nose down and fins in the air. What might seem to be an ornamental vessel with a handle turns out to be a hand grenade. Eccentrically shaped containers mingle with those of recognizable use. In the long three-dimensional display along the wall, the accumulated abundance of objects becomes a procession, a tableau vivant, even a cityscape. Overproduction, whether of symbolic imagery or industrial goods, is hallowed and hollow. The wrinkled, white shapes vacillate between solid and void. The Chinese title for the series, *Shengwu*, can also be translated as relic. The reliquary Lei Yan has created, however, does not produce reverence for or the aura of an individual hero. They invoke reflection on cast-off ideals of collectivity and on who or what endures.

雷燕继续用纸创作，通过摆弄、压折和缝纫，把扁平材料变成大量三维物品，每一件都能握在手中。在2016年北京草场地艺术区个展《神圣之物》中，她集中展示了七十六件雕塑物品，沿着一面画廊墙全长的窄搁板排列。展览还包括这些物品的黑白照片——有些呈现具象形状，有些形态诡谲——单件或小组合呈现。一只高而细的圆锥顶端顶着五角星，孤零零地立着。一把竖立的斧头与镰刀彼此背对。一组更大的物品（图7.10）像是一幅家庭静物，有瓶子、花瓶和烛台，但其中也包括斧头与镰刀、一把军号、一枚反坦克导弹，以及一枚弹头朝下、尾翼朝上的迫击炮弹。一个看似带把手的装饰性容器，其实是手榴弹。奇形怪状的容器与用途可辨的容器混杂在一起。在沿墙的长长三维展示中，积聚的丰富物品变成队列、活人画，甚至城市景观。过度生产——无论是象征图像还是工业产品——既神圣又空洞。皱褶的白色形体在实体与虚空之间摇摆。该系列的中文标题"圣物"，也可以译为 relic（遗物）。然而雷燕创造的这件圣物匣，并不生产对个体英雄的崇敬或灵光。它们引发对集体性这一被丢弃理想的反思，以及对谁或什么得以持存的反思。


〔原书 263〕

![*图7.10　雷燕，《圣物》第20号，2016年，纸雕摄影，50厘米×33厘米。艺术家提供。*](web/assets/ch07-b053.jpg)

FIG 7.10 Lei Yan, *Relic, No. 20*, 2016. Photograph of paper sculpture, 50 cm × 33 cm. Courtesy of the artist.

*图7.10　雷燕，《圣物》第20号，2016年，纸雕摄影，50厘米×33厘米。艺术家提供。*


〔原书 263〕

Lei Yan takes what is ready-to-hand—techniques of her training as a military artist, badges and photographs of revolutionary identification, the fabric and tools of warfare and subordination—and subjects them to material transmutation.[^en-ch07-43] They may resemble their former selves, but they no longer serve a taken-for-granted use in the world. The tool, the symbol, the sign become resistant *and* ephemeral. Her body of work is not an archive of cultural facts but an artistic repertoire that reflects and returns the remade object back into the world. In her aesthetics of arrested ephemerality, materiality matters, even or especially at its vanishing point, because the thing represents a congealed moment in a longer social trajectory. It registers the process of being caught in the double bind of institutions that purport to represent and protect even as they use up, silence, and make waste of. She invests things with agency and personhood, with a critical historiographical consciousness.

雷燕取用唾手可得之物——她作为军旅艺术家受训的技法、革命认同的徽章与照片、战争与从属关系的织物与工具——让它们经历物质转化。[^zh-ch07-43] 它们也许仍像原来的自己，但不再承担世上理所当然的用途。工具、象征、符号变得抵抗而短暂。她的全部作品不是文化事实的档案，而是一套艺术实践的形式与方法，映照并把重造之物送回世界。在她那被截停的短暂性美学中，物质性至关重要，甚至尤其在其消失点上，因为物代表着更长社会轨迹中的一个凝结时刻。它记录着被机构双重束缚所捕获的过程——这些机构声称代表并保护，实际上却消耗、噤声并废弃。她以批判性的史学意识赋予物以能动性与人格。


〔原书 263, 264〕

Lei Yan’s experiments serve not to admonish but to bring back into consciousness lost lives and camouflaged histories. They exhibit a feminist epistemology of thinking relationally about social hierarchy, aesthetic form, and ideology; about the ongoing production of social abstractions and markings that create inequality and injustice. Her binoculars trained backward, across the field of history, trace feminist sight lines of knowledge, recognition, affiliation, and alliance in which art takes on an ethical dimension, of remembering, of attending to loss and erasure, of taking care. Art becomes less a stable, lasting, authoritative object than the work of sensuous engagement with one’s material and social environment.

雷燕的实验不是为了告诫，而是为了把失去的生命与被伪装的历史重新带回意识。它们展示了一种女性主义认识论：在关系性中思考社会等级、美学形式与意识形态，思考那些制造不平等与不公的社会抽象与标记是如何被持续生产出来的。她的望远镜向后调转，穿越历史的场域，描画出知识、承认、归属与联盟的女性主义视线；在其中，艺术承担伦理维度——记忆、关注丧失与抹除、给予关怀。艺术不再是一个稳定、持久、权威的客体，而是与自身物质与社会环境进行感性互动的工作。


〔原书 264〕

In Lei Yan’s practice, art is not warfare, but a methodology of making things speak from beyond death to register the disappearance of that taken from us. Her contemplative body of work at the intersection of woman soldier, military artist, and woman artist echoes over a hundred years later the words of anarchist-feminist writer He-Yin Zhen, whose theoretical writings have only recently been pulled out from under the monumental edifice of history. In an essay written in 1907, “On Feminist Antimilitarism,” she challenges hawkish Chinese ideals espoused in the name of national self-strengthening. She describes the ideology of male superiority and female inferiority, of social hierarchies and classes, of heaven and earth, as rooted in the long history of militarism and male conscription. She lambasts the condition of women and the common people alike as willing slaves taken advantage of by the government and capitalists. She writes, “It is truly absurd that everyone boasts about becoming a militarized people. There are even a handful of women who ardently hope to become like Mulan or Liang Hongyu. This is especially senseless. Today, in contrast to these sentiments, I will explain why women should be opposed to militarism.... antimilitarism can help the common people seize their own freedom; it can extend protection to all human lives.” [^en-ch07-44] Lei Yan’s practice of art as an iterative ritual of reflection and care, posed in queries of “what if” and “how can I,” presents a contrast to the premise of Chinese contemporary art as a mark of global arrival.

在雷燕的实践中，艺术不是战争，而是一种让物在死亡之后发声的方法，以记录那些从我们身边被夺走者的消失。她沉思性的作品位于女兵、军旅艺术家与女性艺术家的交汇处，在一百多年后回响着无政府主义—女性主义作家何殷震的话——她的理论著作直到最近才从历史的纪念碑式大厦下被拉出来。在1907年写的一篇文章《论女性主义反军国主义》中，她挑战以民族自强之名宣扬的鹰派中国理想。她把男尊女卑、社会等级与阶级、天与地的意识形态，描述为植根于军国主义与男性征兵的漫长历史。她痛斥妇女与平民同样沦为政府与资本家利用的甘心奴隶。她写道："人人都夸耀成为军国主义之民，实在荒谬。甚至还有少数女性热切希望成为木兰或梁红玉那样的人。这尤其没有道理。今天，与这些情绪相反，我要解释为什么女性应当反对军国主义……反军国主义能帮助平民夺取自己的自由；它能将保护延伸至所有人类生命。"[^zh-ch07-44] 雷燕把艺术当作反复进行的反思与关怀仪式，以"如果"和"我如何"的追问提出，与中国当代艺术作为全球抵达标志的前提形成对照。

Besides Ai and Lei’s works in response to the Wenchuan earthquake, see also Du Haibin’s film *1428* and Zhang Huan’s *Hope Tunnel*. For a documentary profile of Ai Weiwei, see *Ai Weiwei: Never Sorry*, directed by Alison Klayman.

## 尾声　递归的世俗寓言


〔原书 265〕

Epilogue: Recursive Worldly Fables

尾声　递归的世俗寓言


〔原书 265〕

Over a decade after Li Tianpian’s death, one of her *shuang nü ti* (double female figure) studies in oil reappeared in the public eye, repurposed in a painting by a male contemporary. Wang Xingwei, like Li Tianpian, hails from Shenyang and originally trained in socialist realism. In 2013, the Ullens Center for Contemporary Art (ucca) in Beijing’s 798 Art District held a midcareer retrospective of Wang’s work, seventy-four paintings spanning two decades. Executed in a wide range of styles, the paintings juxtapose in weird, witty, and reiterative ways references drawn from European classical, Chinese socialist, and “global” contemporary art canons. They mix, in a seemingly indiscriminate manner, figures and poses from the likes of Sandro Botticelli, Jean Auguste Dominique Ingres, Marcel Duchamp, Joseph Beuys, Li Chunhua, Quan Shanshi, Allen Jones, Jeff Koons, Fang Lijun, and Wang Guangyi, as well commercial imagery and cartoons from reform-era Chinese newspapers, magazines, and public blackboards.[^en-epilogue-1]

李天翩去世十多年后，她的一幅"双女体"油画习作重新出现在公众视野中，被一位男性同代艺术家挪用进自己的画作。与李天翩一样，王兴伟也来自沈阳，最初受的是社会主义现实主义训练。2013年，北京798艺术区的尤伦斯当代艺术中心（UCCA）举办了王兴伟的艺术生涯中期回顾展，展出横跨二十年的七十四幅油画。这些画作以多种风格绘成，以怪异、机智而反复的方式并置取自欧洲古典、中国社会主义和"全球"当代艺术经典的参照。它们看似不加区分地混合了桑德罗·波提切利、让-奥古斯特-多米尼克·安格尔、马塞尔·杜尚、约瑟夫·博伊斯、Li Chunhua、全山石、艾伦·琼斯、杰夫·昆斯、方力钧和王广义等人的人物与姿态，以及改革时代中国报纸、杂志和公共黑板上的商业图像与漫画。[^zh-epilogue-1]


〔原书 265, 266〕

A 2002 painting was hung as the final piece in the ucca exhibit.[^en-epilogue-2] *Untitled (Three Nudes*) copies and composes together figurative works by Yang Feiyun and Li Tianpian. Yang’s *Male Nude*, painted in 1981 while he was a student at the Central Academy of Fine Arts, features a model in a powerful upright stance. His raises one fist to his chest; the other, clenched around a stone, extends down and to his side. The spotlit pose, accentuated by a dark background, shows off muscular definition and realist anatomical representation. In Wang’s restaging, Yang’s male nude stands at the rear of the pictorial space, behind the two female figures from Li Tianpian’s *Women of the Republic of China*.[^en-epilogue-3] In her original, painted in 1998 while she was a student at the China Art Academy, two nudes rest side by side on a chaise lounge draped with a white sheet: one sits facing the back wall, her head bent down as if looking at something in her hands; the other faces forward and reclines to the side, in an odalisquelike pose. *Untitled (Three Nudes*) stages the figures from these staid academic studies in a triangulated charade of sexual service and visual consumption. The woman with her back to the viewer buries her face in the genitalia of the male nude who towers above her. His gaze, in turn, falls directly upon the exposed body of the second woman. She stares blankly out, as if oblivious to the scene into which she’s been conscripted. The ucca exhibit wall text for the painting notes, “Wang cheekily combines two classics of Chinese academic realism.” The painting, hung at the end of his retrospective, might be read as a parting shot at the academic art of copying, his critique of and creative rise above it, even as his globally recognized oeuvre of formal repetition and juxtaposition depends on the skills and references of this training.

一幅2002年的画作被挂在尤伦斯展览的最后。[^zh-epilogue-2] 《无题（三个裸体）》复制并组合了杨飞云与李天翩的具象作品。杨飞云的《男人体》作于1981年他在中央美术学院读书时，画中模特以强有力的直立姿态出现。模特的一只拳头举到胸前，另一只紧握石头，向下伸向身侧。聚光灯下的姿态被深色背景衬托，展示出肌肉的轮廓与写实的解剖表现。在王兴伟的重置中，杨飞云的男性裸体站在画面空间后方，位于李天翩《民国女性》中两个女性形象之后。[^zh-epilogue-3] 在原作中——她1998年在中国美术学院读书时所作——两个裸体并排歇在一张铺着白床单的贵妃榻上：一人坐着面向后墙，低头仿佛在看手中的东西；另一人面向前方，侧身斜倚，姿态如后宫侍女。《无题（三个裸体）》把这些古板学院习作中的人物搬演成一场三角形的哑剧，涉及性服务与视觉消费。背对观者的女人把脸埋进高耸于她之上的男性裸体的生殖器。他的目光则直直落在第二个女人裸露的身体上。她茫然地向外凝视，仿佛浑然不觉自己已被征召进这场戏。尤伦斯展览为这幅画写的展墙说明指出："王兴伟俏皮地结合了两件中国学院写实主义的经典之作。"这幅画挂在他回顾展的末尾，或可读作对学院临摹艺术的一记临别之击，是他对它的批判与创造性的超越，尽管他那些以形式重复与并置而获全球承认的作品，恰恰依赖这种训练所赋予的技能与参照。


〔原书 266〕

When I first saw the painting, none of this critical apparatus mattered. It simply felt like an affront. What did it mean for Li Tianpian to be returned to the world in this way? Detached from her now (almost) disappeared body of work—her struggles with the medium of painting, its politics of representation, and gendered norms of work and duty—she is cast without recourse in the role-playing games of another. This recruitment as readymade, a well-worn conceptual move, ignores the fact that at the same moment she painted *Women of the Republic of China*, whose title harkens to the early twentieth-century introduction of nude model painting from Europe to China, she also painted *Red Souvenir*. Her own experimentation with montage, its layers of gendered representation and repression, slides out of history.

我第一次看到这幅画时，所有这些批评论述都无足轻重。它只让人感到受到冒犯。以这种方式让李天翩重返世界，意味着什么？她被从如今（几乎）消失的作品整体中剥离出来——剥离了她与绘画媒介的搏斗、绘画的表征政治，以及关于工作与责任的性别规范——毫无还手之力地被抛进另一个人的角色扮演游戏。这种把她当作现成品征用的做法——一种屡见不鲜的观念艺术手法——无视了一个事实：她画《民国女性》的同时，也画了《红色纪念品》；前者的标题呼应20世纪初欧洲裸体模特写生被引入中国的历史。她本人对蒙太奇的实验，其层层叠叠的性别化再现与压抑，就这样滑出了历史。


〔原书 266〕

I just wanted to put these artistic representations side by side, and then add historical reality to the picture. To put them all together like this... Think about it, these original women when they started out were so beautiful, wearing military uniforms, with straps and supply bags crisscrossing their chests, wearing these kinds of clothes, some in dresses. They have such a valiant and heroic bearing. Then after they were captured... this picture was taken when they were in jail... they’re wearing old clothes. It wasn’t long after their release that they married the enemy.

我只想把这些艺术再现并置，然后给画面加入历史现实。就这样把它们全部放在一起……想想看，历史上这些真实的女性刚开始时多么美丽，穿着军装，带子和补给袋交叉绑在胸前，穿着这样的衣服，有些人穿裙子。她们有那样英勇豪迈的姿态。后来她们被捕……这张照片是她们在狱中拍的……她们穿着旧衣服。获释没多久，她们就嫁给了敌人。


〔原书 266, 267〕

Wang Xingwei, in his incessant return to and collision of iconic images and poses, seems intent on exposing their ideological underpinnings, the systems of social, cultural, and political meaning that grant them value.[^en-epilogue-4] His aesthetics of montage—like many of the artworks and modes of practice I have focused on in this book—show Chinese contemporary art to be a zone of cultural encounter. His paintings emerge from and contend with shifting conditions for cultural production in China. While worldings overlap with or haunt one another in his work, they remain centrally structured, perhaps even critically so, by patriarchal gender norms. But to the extent that *Untitled (Three Nudes*) makes Li Tianpian the butt of a joke—that of the self-fellating masterpiece—it robs her of the power to world.[^en-epilogue-5] Its irreverent surface conceals the material sociality of her position in an emergent art world. Its front affronts the laboring bodies of the models, the memory of Li Tianpian, and the embodied, resistant histories of those disciplined by visual regimes of typification.[^en-epilogue-6] If *Wang Xingwei*, the eponymous retrospective exhibit at ucca, an eponymous museum founded by a Belgian businessman who over three decades amassed one of the largest collections of Chinese contemporary art, represents a kind of monumentality, its final work remains haunted by what it makes ephemeral.

王兴伟不断回返并碰撞各种标志性图像与姿态，似乎执意要揭露它们的意识形态根基，那些赋予它们价值的社会、文化与政治意义系统。[^zh-epilogue-4] 他的蒙太奇美学——像本书聚焦的许多艺术作品与实践方式一样——表明中国当代艺术是一个文化相遇地带。他的画作从中国不断变化的文化生产条件中产生，并与之角力。在他的作品中，各种世界营造相互重叠或彼此萦绕，但在核心处仍由父权制性别规范所结构，甚至可能是批判性地结构。然而，就《无题（三个裸体）》把李天翩变成笑柄——那个自我口交的杰作——而言，它剥夺了她营造世界的力量。[^zh-epilogue-5] 它不敬的表面掩盖了她在新兴艺术世界中位置的物质社会性。它的画面正面冒犯了模特劳动的身体、李天翩的记忆，以及那些被典型化的视觉体制所规训者具身的、抵抗的历史。[^zh-epilogue-6] 如果尤伦斯当代艺术中心举办的同名回顾展《王兴伟》代表某种纪念碑性——这座以创办者命名的美术馆由一位比利时商人创办，他三十多年间积聚起全球最大的中国当代艺术收藏之一——那么它最后一件作品仍被它所化为短暂之物的东西所萦绕。


〔原书 267〕

Throughout the many years of researching and writing this book, I have sought to situate Chinese contemporary art in an expanded field that takes into account gender and globalization articulated together. Doing so has required laying out and puzzling through the interlocking double binds that catch art world social actors up. It has meant cultivating a dialectical understanding of monumental and ephemeral across time, seeing one as the shadow of the other in a historical field of ruin, erasure, and excavation. When certain forms of representation and life take on weight, solidity, and authority, a particular worlding comes to seem self-evident. Yet the creative striving and critical labor of those never quite concealed by this process continually disrupt its smooth surface, even or especially when the worlding enlists them—their bodies and their imaginations—at their own expense. From my position in the U.S. academy, where self-evident worldings are challenged but also often reproduced, I understand my creative, critical labor to be that of recognizing, unforgetting, and making visible these disruptions.

在研究和写作本书的许多年里，我一直试图把中国当代艺术置于一个扩展场域中，同时考虑性别与全球化的相互勾连。这样做要求铺陈并苦思那些捕获艺术世界社会行动者的相互扣连的双重束缚。它意味着培养一种跨越时间的、关于纪念碑式与短暂性的辩证理解，在废墟、抹除与挖掘的历史场域中把一方视为另一方的影子。当某些再现形式与生活形式获得重量、坚实性与权威时，一种特定的世界营造便显得不言自明。然而，那些从未被这一过程完全遮蔽者的创造性努力与批判性劳动，不断扰乱它光滑的表面；甚至尤其当这种世界营造以他们自身为代价征用他们——他们的身体与想象——时，情况更是如此。从我在美国学界的立场来看——在那里，不言自明的世界营造受到挑战，但也常常被再生产——我把自己的创造性、批判性劳动理解为辨认、拒绝遗忘并让这些扰乱变得可见。


〔原书 267, 268〕

Approaching the art world as a feminist anthropologist shaped my knowledge, such that I cannot see a painting like Wang Xingwei’s *Untitled (Three Nudes*) without placing it within an expanded image world that also includes a Red Detachment retrospective of Li Tianpian as presented in chapter 5. If I had conducted my research primarily through attention to Chinese contemporary art exhibits, events, and discourse, this feminist sight line would have been occluded. The time I spent as a participant observer attuned to questions of gender and power in classrooms, in encounters between Chinese and Western artists and curators, and in interviews and activities with a broad range of people engaged in the pursuit of something they called art informs my interpretation of the images produced in the process. If not an ethnographer, I most likely would never have met Li Tianpian or spent the time to see the world from her perspective, as I did through fragments of conversation on the mattress on the floor, our backs to the wall, of the small room in which she lived as unmarried teacher of oil painting in the socialist realist tradition.

以女性主义人类学家的方式接近艺术世界，塑造了我的知识；以至于我看到王兴伟《无题（三个裸体）》这样的画时，无法不把它置入一个扩展的图像世界，其中也包括第五章所描述的对李天翩的"红色娘子军"式重新审视。如果我主要通过关注中国当代艺术展览、事件与话语来开展研究，这条女性主义视线就会被遮蔽。我作为参与观察者，在教室里、在中国与西方艺术家和策展人的相遇中、在与广泛人群的访谈与活动中，始终关注性别与权力问题；这些人所追求的某种东西，他们称之为艺术。这段经历塑造了我对过程中产生的图像的解读。如果我不是民族志学者，我极可能永远不会遇见李天翩，也不会花时间从她的视角看世界；我是在她作为社会主义现实主义传统中未婚油画教师的狭小房间里，坐在铺在地板上的床垫上、背靠着墙，通过一段段零碎的交谈做到这一点的。


〔原书 268〕

Since the now historical turn-of-the-millennium moment of my initial fieldwork, contemporary art from China has achieved global recognition in museums, galleries, and auction houses throughout Europe, North America, Asia, and beyond. High-profile Chinese artists have made individual names for themselves on this circuit, as solo shows for some abate, to an extent, the sense of being the face of the other in Western exhibitions of “global art.” New cultural institutions within the Chinese Mainland showcase, collect, and sell this work almost as a matter of course. Artists in border locations like Hong Kong, Taiwan, Korea, and Vietnam, as well as Chinese diasporic artists in other parts of the world, increasingly feel the hegemony of Mainland China’s place in an international art world order. Official leadership still periodically exercises a heavy hand with regard to artistic expression, as evidenced by high-profile events like the arrest of Ai Weiwei in 2011 or closure of the Beijing Independent Film Festival in 2014. In that same year, President Xi Jinping gave an internal speech on the arts as part of his overall consolidation of power and control of dissent. The full text was publicly released one year later. Modeled after Mao’s “Talks at the Yan’an Conference on Art and Literature,” Xi tasked artists and writers with upholding morality, progress, and the “Chinese spirit,” lambasting those who produce “cultural garbage” that does not distinguish between good and evil or conform to party discipline.[^en-epilogue-7] Nonetheless, the culture industry that arose in conjunction with China’s twenty-first millennial push to go global as an economic and political force to be reckoned with remains alive and well. Culture and creativity have, indeed, become new modes of governmentality, ways of cultivating and celebrating individual aspiration, talent, and authorship even as these discursive constructions control, through stratification along class, ethnic, and gender lines, those who may or may not receive recognition and material rewards.[^en-epilogue-8] My ethnography, of a turning point in Chinese contemporary art, provides an account of the history that underlies this contemporary situation.

自最初田野调查那个如今已成历史的千禧年之交时刻以来，中国当代艺术已在欧洲、北美、亚洲及其他地区的博物馆、画廊和拍卖行获得全球承认。高知名度的中国艺术家在这个圈子中打出了个人名声，对其中一些人而言，个展在一定程度上减轻了在西方"全球艺术"展览中沦为"他者面孔"的感觉。中国大陆的新文化机构几乎理所当然地展示、收藏并销售这些作品。香港、台湾、韩国和越南等边境地带的艺术家，以及世界其他地方的华人离散艺术家，日益感受到中国大陆在国际艺术世界秩序中之位置的霸权。官方领导层仍间或对艺术表达施加铁腕，2011年艾未未被捕或2014年北京独立影像展被关闭等高曝光事件即为明证。同年，习近平主席发表了一篇关于文艺的内部讲话，这是他全面巩固权力、控制异见的组成部分。讲话全文在一年后公开发表。这篇讲话仿照毛泽东《在延安文艺座谈会上的讲话》，要求艺术家和作家维护道德、进步与"中国精神"，猛烈抨击那些生产不分善恶、不服从党的纪律的"文化垃圾"的人。[^zh-epilogue-7] 尽管如此，伴随中国21世纪作为不可忽视的经济与政治力量走向全球的推动而兴起的文化产业，依然生机勃勃。文化与创造力确实已成为新的治理术模式，成为培养并颂扬个人抱负、才华与作者性的方式；与此同时，这些话语构形又通过阶级、族群与性别界限的分层，控制着谁可能或不可能获得承认与物质回报。[^zh-epilogue-8] 我这部关于中国当代艺术转折点的民族志，为理解当前处境背后的历史提供了一份叙述。


〔原书 268, 269〕

In the introduction, I reflected on a question I wrote in a 2002 field note: Am I trying to write an ethnography about a city in which art plays a part or an ethnography about art in which the city plays a part? My research explored the questions that unfolded from that one. How do aesthetics do more than simply reflect political, social, and economic change? How does cultural production actively shape collective consciousness and social identity, perceptions of time and space, and visions of the world? What is the legacy of past forms of visual praxis on contemporary production? How are envisioned timespaces always-already uneven and gendered? While the rise and recognition of Chinese contemporary art may now seem a fait accompli, the questions and struggles explored in these pages persist. A closely observed story of the past, related through the experiences, words, and images of the social actors involved in its making, provides a challenge to future master scripts of it. As the artists I worked with taught me again and again, the past is an open resource. As I write this epilogue in 2016, a new opera *The Long March* plays at Beijing’s National Centre for the Performing Arts to celebrate, with full nationalistic fervor, the historical event’s eightieth anniversary. The words of the opening chorus—“We differ in status, but we have the same aspiration: to join the Red Army. To change the world!”—reverberate through a theater designed by Paul Andreu as part of the effort to remake the capital city and launch it anew on the global stage.[^en-epilogue-9] Spectacular productions like this one are meant to smooth over the ironies and contradictions of the differing politics and systems of art it enfolds together. The motley “what if” struggles of participants who, as recounted in chapter 4, gathered on the shores of Lugu Lake in 2001 for an earlier restaging of *The Long March*, serve as a discomfiting counterpoint to this choral expression of national unity. They likewise unsettle ideas about global art and global feminism raised by exhibits and projects organized under these banners.

在引言中，我反思了2002年一条田野笔记中写下的问题：我是在写一部艺术在其中扮演角色的城市的民族志，还是在写一部城市在其中扮演角色的艺术的民族志？我的研究探索了由这个问题展开的一系列问题。美学如何不只是反映政治、社会与经济变迁？文化生产又如何积极塑造集体意识与社会认同、对时间与空间的感知，以及对世界的想象？过去的视觉实践形式对当代生产留下什么遗产？被构想出来的时空如何总是已经不均等且性别化的？尽管中国当代艺术的崛起与获得承认如今也许看似既成事实，本书探讨的问题与斗争仍然持续。一个通过参与其建构的社会行动者的经验、言语与图像讲述的、细致观察的过去故事，为未来关于它的主导叙事脚本提供了挑战。与我共事的艺术家们一再教导我，过去是一种开放的资源。我在2016年撰写这篇尾声时，一部新歌剧《长征》正在北京国家大剧院上演，以十足的民族主义热情庆祝这一历史事件八十周年。开场合唱的歌词——"我们地位不同，但志向相同：参加红军。改变世界！"——回荡在保罗·安德鲁设计的剧院中；这座剧院是重塑首都、使其以新面貌登上全球舞台的努力的一部分。[^zh-epilogue-9] 像这样的奇观式演出，意在抹平它所并置的不同艺术政治与艺术体系之间的反讽与矛盾。如第四章所述，2001年一群参与者聚集在泸沽湖畔，为"长征"做更早一次重演，他们形形色色、以"如果"为题的挣扎，构成对这种合唱式民族统一表达的令人不安的对照。它们同样扰乱了在这些旗帜下组织的展览与项目所提出的关于全球艺术与全球女性主义的观念。


〔原书 269, 270〕

In the prologue, “Worldly Fables,” I sketched the lives of two early twentieth-century artists as a way of refuting the myth of China’s millennial “linking tracks with the world” as brand new. I paired Xu Beihong and Pan Yuliang because of their historical proximity and the ways their paths crossed each other in European and Chinese art institutions. Their adaptation of academic oil painting to different representational ends fed into a heated debate about the social role of art in the Chinese cultural politics of their time. I also paired them to demonstrate that at every turn of their careers gender politics influenced what they painted, the opportunities that opened or closed to them, and their artistic afterlives. When this prefatory conceit, of twinned male and female artists, continued to reappear in my own developing narrative, my initial instinct was to tamp it down. Why, I thought, in writing about Lei Yan did I need to bring Ai Weiwei into the picture, even if I could make him the shadow story to her life and work instead of the other way around? Did the surfacing of Wang Xingwei’s *Untitled (Three Nudes*) in the wake of Li Tianpian’s death make it worth writing about it? Why couldn’t I simply write about artists like Pan Yuliang, Lei Yan, and Li Tianpian without reference to male peers whose visibility has often eclipsed theirs? Wouldn’t inverting the usual rules of the game serve some notion of justice? Then it dawned on me that these troublesome pairings, which seemed to arise from my research materials against my internal critic’s will, demonstrated with utter clarity and specificity the conceptual mechanism of *nannü youbie* (male/female differentiation) as first theorized by He-Yin Zhen prior to the historical emergence of Pan Yuliang and Xu Beihong. The work of art actively produces social distinctions as a form of power and domination. It reiterates symbolic orders, sometimes with a radical difference, always within a relationship of past to present.

在序言"世俗寓言"中，我勾勒了两位20世纪初艺术家的生平，以此反驳中国千禧年"与世界接轨"是全新事物的神话。我把徐悲鸿与潘玉良配对，是因为他们历史时间的接近，以及他们的道路在欧洲与中国的艺术建制中交错的方式。他们把学院油画改编为不同的表征目的，投入当时中国文化政治中关于艺术社会角色的激烈争论。我把他们配对，也是为了表明，在他们生涯的每一个转折处，性别政治都影响着他们画什么、哪些机会向他们敞开或关闭，以及他们的艺术身后事。当这个由一男一女两位艺术家组成的开篇构想在我逐渐展开的叙述中不断重现时，我最初的本能是把它压下去。我想，为什么在写雷燕时，我需要把艾未未带进画面，即使我可以让他成为她生活与作品的影子故事，而不是反过来？王兴伟的《无题（三个裸体）》在李天翩去世后出现，是否值得写它？为什么我不能只写潘玉良、雷燕和李天翩这样的艺术家，而不提那些可见度常常遮蔽她们的男性同侪？颠倒通常的游戏规则，难道不服务于某种正义观念吗？然后我恍然大悟：这些麻烦的配对似乎违背我内心批评者的意愿，从研究材料中浮现出来，却以极其清晰而具体的方式展示了男女有别（nannü youbie）的概念机制；这个概念最早由何殷震在潘玉良与徐悲鸿历史性地出现之前提出。艺术工作积极生产社会区分，将其作为一种权力与支配的形式。它重述象征秩序，有时带着激进的差异，却始终处于过去与现在的关系之中。


〔原书 270〕

In this book, guided by the artists who have opened my feminist sight lines, I emphasize the possibility of radical difference, of differential historiographical consciousness, of imagining a world that is not hierarchically structured by these social abstractions and markings. As much as *nannü* hierarchies persist in the pairings I present, the artistic practice of the women I focus on confront them in deep and complex ways that open up interpretation of work by male peers and the work of art enmeshed in global power relations. Feminist art as a relational epistemology thus moves beyond recognition of the “woman artist” to the act of making visible multidirectional tensions between colonial and decolonial forces in struggles over what counts as art. Finally, the artists I bring to the fore also demonstrate that feminist movement in China, even though its Sinophonic articulations are less than fully translated by this catchall in English, are as far from brand new as China is to the world.

在本书中，在那些为我打开女性主义视线的艺术家引导下，我强调激进差异的可能性，强调差异化的史学意识，强调想象一个不被这些社会抽象与标记按等级结构出来的世界。尽管男女等级在我呈现的配对中持续存在，我所聚焦的女性艺术实践以深刻而复杂的方式直面它们，从而开启了对男性同侪作品以及深陷全球权力关系的艺术工作的解读。因此，作为关系认识论的女性主义艺术超越了承认"女性艺术家"，转向让殖民与去殖民力量之间在"何为艺术"之争中的多向张力变得可见。最后，我所凸显的艺术家也表明，中国的女性主义运动——尽管其在华语中的表述无法被这个英语统称完全译出——绝非崭新之物；中国对世界而言也同样并非新来者。


〔原书 270, 271〕

The first images of this book, Wang Nengtao’s *Subversion*, Yin Xiuzhen’s *Portable Beijing*, and Chen Lingyang’s *25:00*, laid the ground for my argument about Chinese contemporary art as a zone of cultural encounter. They respond aesthetically to the *chaiqian* (demolition and relocation) turning over of China’s capital, in which art and urbanism intertwine in the global city under construction, and in which gender and sexuality figure centrally in iterative conceptions of China’s modernity and worldliness. In 2006, multimedia artist Cao Fei began creating an online interactive environment in Second Life (sl) that figuratively collides the worldings imaged by the artworks I chose as my entry point.[^en-epilogue-10] She describes this three-dimensional virtual world—named *rmb City* after the *reminbi*, or “people’s currency,” of the prc—as an expression of the forces that “made China, my country, such a syncretic experimental place.”[^en-epilogue-11] The sl-user “residents” who populate the city interact through customized avatars and instant messaging. Designed by Cao in collaboration with Guangzhou’s Vitamin Creative Space and overseas sl builders, *rmb City* theatricalizes in a speculative, open-ended way the development of the Chinese global city as an uneven and gendered timespace.

本书开篇的图像——王能涛的《颠覆》、尹秀珍的《便携北京》和陈羚羊的《25:00》——为我关于中国当代艺术是文化相遇地带的论点奠定了基础。它们以美学方式回应中国首都拆迁翻建的进程；在这一进程中，艺术与城市主义在建设中的全球城市里相互交织，性别与性则在中国现代性与世界性的反复构想中占据核心位置。2006年，多媒体艺术家曹斐开始在"第二人生"（Second Life，SL）中创造一个在线互动环境，以比喻方式碰撞我选作切入点的那些作品所想象的世界营造。[^zh-epilogue-10] 她把这个名为《人民城寨》（RMB City，取自中华人民共和国的"人民币"）的三维虚拟世界，描述为一种力量的表达，这些力量"使中国——我的国家——成为如此兼容并蓄的实验场所"。[^zh-epilogue-11]填充这座城市的"第二人生"用户"居民"，通过定制的化身和即时通讯互动。《人民城寨》由曹斐与广州维他命空间及海外"第二人生"建造者合作设计，以思辨、开放的方式戏剧化中国全球城市的发展，将其呈现为一个不均等且性别化的时空。


〔原书 271〕

The virtual world of *rmb City* consists of an island cut in the cartographic shape of modern China, which emerges from the middle of the ocean. Balanced atop the island is an elaborate structure of disparate architectural elements assembled together to create a three-dimensional fantasy park that sl users explore via their avatars. At one edge of the island city, a statue of the Great Helmsman sinks into the ocean, his hand raised toward the rusted out remains of the Olympic Bird’s Nest stadium. Karl Marx floats on an embroidered cushion over a winding highway between I. M. Pei’s Hong Kong Bank of China Tower and a giant golden Buddha. The bubbly pink and silver spaceship-like Oriental Pearl Tower from Shanghai rises in the center at a precarious tilt. Rem Koolhaas’s cctv Tower dangles upside down, suspended over the city, from a monstrous crane. Four ancient stone pillars—one balanced on an armed tank, another on a warship—rise into the sky to support the Gate of Heavenly Peace. A waterpark, instead of Tiananmen Square, extends in front of it. A portrait of a panda hangs on the gate, between two large slogans in white and red. Instead of “Long Live the People’s Republic of China” and “Long Live the Great Unity of the World’s Peoples,” they declare in English “My City Is Yours” and “Your City Is Mine.” This updated billing was provided by a gallery in New York’s Chelsea district, which provided the artist with real-life (rl) retail space for an “advanced preview and sale” of the planned city. In a dramatic mimicry of the conjunction of real estate, urban planning, and art explored through chapter 2, investors and institutions used rl cash to rent virtual buildings and commission virtual projects in *rmb City*.[^en-epilogue-12]

《人民城寨》的虚拟世界由一个按照现代中国版图形状切割的岛屿构成，岛屿从海洋中央升起。岛屿顶端平衡着一座精巧结构，由互不相干的建筑元素拼装而成，形成一座三维奇幻公园，"第二人生"用户通过化身在其中探索。在岛屿城市的一侧，伟大舵手的雕像沉入海洋，他举起的手指向锈蚀残破的奥运鸟巢体育场遗迹。卡尔·马克思坐在一只绣花坐垫上，漂浮在蜿蜒公路之上；公路位于贝聿铭的香港中银大厦与一尊巨大金佛之间。来自上海、粉银相间、泡泡般圆润、形似飞船的东方明珠塔在中央以一种危险的倾斜角度升起。雷姆·库哈斯的央视大楼倒悬在城市上方，由一台巨型起重机吊着。四根古代石柱升向天空，支撑着天安门；其中一根稳立于一辆武装坦克上，另一根立于一艘军舰上。它前方延伸开的不是天安门广场，而是一座水上乐园。门楼上挂着一幅熊猫画像，两侧是红白两色的大标语。标语并非"中华人民共和国万岁"和"世界人民大团结万岁"，而是用英文写着"我的城市属于你"和"你的城市属于我"。这一更新版的标语来自纽约切尔西区的一家画廊；该画廊为艺术家提供了现实生活（RL）中的零售空间，用于这座规划城市的"提前预览与销售"。这是对第二章所探讨的房地产、城市规划与艺术结合的戏剧性模仿：投资者与机构用现实货币在《人民城寨》中租赁虚拟建筑、委托虚拟项目。[^zh-epilogue-12]


〔原书 271, 272〕

Cao Fei inhabits *rmb City* as the avatar China Tracy, whose sexy cyberpunk warrior fashion shows off the exaggerated proportions of the typical female body in gamer culture. She wanders the city, walking through and flying over it, and interacts with other users’ avatars. The piece has been exhibited around the world, primarily in video form but also in a *yangbanxi* (model opera) adaptation that combined actors and video projection.[^en-epilogue-13] For the 2007 Venice Biennale, Cao staged an onsite and sl China Tracy Pavilion, which screened a three-part cyber epic based on six months of China Tracy’s journeys through a city for sale, including her love affair with a young male avatar, Hug Yue, whom she later discovered was a sixty-five-year-old American. Produced as machinima, the technique of filming a virtual environment using video game software, *i-Mirror: A Second Life Documentary Film* opens with a black screen and the sound of typing on a computer keyboard. The following lines appear in glowing yellow font: “I construct, and I am constructed, in a mutually recursive process that continually changes my fluid, permeable boundaries and my endlessly ramifying networks. I am a spatially extended cyborg.”[^en-epilogue-14]

曹斐以化身"中国·翠西"（China Tracy）栖居于《人民城寨》；她性感的赛博朋克女战士时尚，展现出游戏文化中典型女性身体被夸张的比例。她在城中漫游，步行穿过它，也从它上方飞过，并与其他用户的化身互动。这件作品在世界各地展出，主要以影像形式，也有一种结合演员与影像投影的样板戏改编版本。[^zh-epilogue-13] 2007年威尼斯双年展，曹斐搭建了一个现场与"第二人生"并置的"中国·翠西馆"，放映一部三部分赛博史诗，取材于中国·翠西在六个月里穿越一座待售之城的旅程，包括她与年轻男性化身 Hug Yue 的恋情——她后来发现对方是一名65岁的美国人。《i·镜：一部第二人生纪录片》以游戏引擎电影（machinima）手法制作——即用电子游戏软件拍摄虚拟环境的技术——开场是黑屏和敲击电脑键盘的声音。随后，发亮的黄色字体出现以下句子："我建构，也被建构，在一个相互递归的过程中，这个过程不断改变我流动、可渗透的边界与我无尽分岔的网络。我是一个空间上延展的赛博格。"[^zh-epilogue-14]


〔原书 272〕

In 2009 Cao created the machinima *Live in rmb City*, commissioned by Tokyo’s Shiseido gallery for a solo show of her work. As reflection on life after the birth of her son, the film features China Tracy leading a toddler avatar, China Sun, through their virtual world while answering his stream of questions about its buildings, inhabitants, and the meaning of their existence. The mother frankly, if sometimes elliptically, tutors her curious son—not so subtly named after the “East is Red” national metaphor of the ccp as the shining sun—in the political, creative, and sexual economies of their world. Conspicuously absent is a father figure, suggesting an alternative to national traditions of patriarchal hegemony in the real and representational realms. When Cao returns to the real world and China Tracy disappears, China Sun has to endure the loneliness of life without her, a mirroring of the artist’s navigation of divisions between real and virtual, artistic and affective, productive and reproductive labor. Their mother-child dialogue ends with a set of questions from China Sun about his parentage: “Father? Who is father? What does he look like? Like Godzilla? Or Ultraman? Or Doraemon.... Mother, how do I get to the real world? When you have time, can you bring me along with you? Is there a *rmb* City like this one too?”[^en-epilogue-15] Cao Fei eventually brought an end to *rmb City* by sinking it into the ocean. The project made its final appearance in *Apocalypse Tomorrow: Surf in rmb City*, a 2011 one-person-game art installation that lets players surf, using a monk avatar, through the flooded ruins. In a screen shot of *Live in rmb City* (plate 19) that circulates as one of its afterimages, China Tracy rises above her virtual world. She looms large in the foreground with the darkened backdrop of the city behind her shrouded in smoke. Faint lights illuminate the contours of its miniaturized monuments. Her voluptuous body is encased in a suit of shiny silver metal. Her right arm, a large mechanical, armed claw, wraps protectively around China Sun. They both look past the viewer toward another horizon.

2009年，曹斐受东京资生堂画廊委托，为她个展创作游戏引擎电影《生活在人民城寨》。这部影片是对她儿子出生后生活的反思，片中中国·翠西带着幼儿化身"中国·太阳"（China Sun）穿过他们的虚拟世界，同时回答他关于城中建筑、居民及其存在意义的一连串问题。这位母亲坦率——尽管有时隐晦——地给好奇的儿子讲解他们世界中的政治、创造与性经济；儿子的名字相当直白地取自中共"东方红"的国族隐喻，把党比作照亮万物的太阳。父亲形象明显缺席，暗示着在现实与表征领域中替代民族传统父权霸权的可能。当曹斐回到现实世界、中国·翠西消失后，中国·太阳不得不忍受没有她的孤独生活；这映照着艺术家在真实与虚拟、艺术与情感、生产性劳动与再生产性劳动之间的区隔中穿行。他们的母子对话以中国·太阳关于自己出身的一连串问题结束："爸爸？爸爸是谁？他长什么样？像哥斯拉？还是奥特曼？还是哆啦A梦……妈妈，我怎么才能到真实世界去？你有空的时候，能带我一起去吗？那里也有一座这样的《人民城寨》吗？"[^zh-epilogue-15] 曹斐最终让《人民城寨》沉入海洋，结束了它。这个项目最后出现在《明日启示录：在人民城寨冲浪》中——一件2011年的单人游戏艺术装置，玩家使用僧人化身在被淹没的废墟间冲浪。在作为其余像之一流传的《生活在人民城寨》截屏（图版19）中，中国·翠西升到她的虚拟世界之上。她在前景中赫然耸立，身后城市昏暗的背景笼罩在烟雾中。微弱的灯光照亮城中微缩纪念碑的轮廓。她丰腴的身体裹在一套闪亮的银色金属服装里。她的右臂——一只巨大的机械武装利爪——保护性地环抱着中国·太阳。两人都越过观者，望向另一道地平线。


〔原书 272, 273〕

Born a generation after most of the artists whose lives and works fill this book, Cao Fei, a.k.a. China Tracy, continues, as she moves through the monumental ruins of the past and present toward a speculative future, to explore the “ramifying networks” of image worlds that unfold over space and time. I imagine flashing across the illuminated billboards of *rmb City* a palimpsest of other images bearing an aesthetic relationship with China Tracy’s appearance on the horizon: a woman with binoculars to her eyes gazing out toward a flying machine, or back toward soldiers on the battlefield of history; the visage of actress Ruan Lingyu superimposed over the glittering lights of colonial-era Shanghai in her 1934 silent film role as a hard-working prostitute driven to desperation, or projected in a scale-model animation for a cinema at the center of the Grand moma apartment complex in new millennium Beijing; a maidservant who exposes her wounds as a gesture of protest, or a woman in a purple wig and sunglasses who wields a cleaver in the sprawling scale model for Beijing’s SOHO real estate development; a bare-breasted woman atop a watch tower on the Great Wall likened to *Liberty Leading the People* or transformed into a blur of light and motion; a giantess who becomes as large as she likes and does whatever she likes at the magic hour of *25:00*.

曹斐（又名中国·翠西）比本书所写的大部分艺术家晚出生一代；当她穿过过去与现在的纪念碑式废墟、走向一个思辨的未来时，她继续探索在空间与时间中展开的图像世界"分岔网络"。我想象，在《人民城寨》闪亮的广告牌上掠过一组重写本式的其他图像，它们与中国·翠西在地平线上的现身构成美学关联：一个把望远镜举到眼前的女人，望向一架飞行器，或回望历史战场上的士兵；演员阮玲玉的面容叠印在殖民时代上海璀璨的灯火上，那是她在1934年默片中饰演一个辛勤劳作却被逼至绝境的妓女，或投射在为千禧年北京当代MOMA公寓建筑群中心一座影院所作的缩尺模型动画中；一名露出自己伤口以示抗议的女佣，或一名戴着紫色假发和墨镜、在北京SOHO房地产开发项目庞大缩尺模型中挥舞菜刀的女子；一名裸胸女子站在长城的一座烽火台上，令人想到《自由引导人民》，或化为光影与运动交织的模糊身影；一个在25:00的魔幻时刻想变多大就变多大、想做什么就做什么的女巨人。

Several threatened legal action against those who had subjected them to public scrutiny without consent. Kraus, *The Party and the Arty in China*, 87–89.

[^zh-epilogue-6]: 随着裸体画在1980年代的中国正常化——杨飞云等艺术家正是在那时崭露头角——女性画室模特的再现劳动引发了道德政治与抗议。当中央美术学院画家的作品在1988年北京一场广受宣传的裸体艺术展上展出时，曾为他们摆姿势的模特遭到了骚扰。有几位威胁要对那些未经同意便把她们置于公众审视之下的人采取法律行动。Kraus, *The Party and the Arty in China*, 87–89。

## 译校说明与术语

译校说明（编者附录）

本稿依据 Sasha Su-Ling Welland 的 *Experimental Beijing: Gender and Globalization in Chinese Contemporary Art*（Duke University Press，2018）制作。译校以所附底本为准。原书印刷页码与 PDF 文件页序分别记录；阅读稿重新分页后，文中指向原书的页码仍指底本，不指新稿页码。

文中的访谈、文学引文、演出对白与新闻引文，原则上由本书所载英文译成中文。除逐项校注明确注明已与中文原件核合者外，不应把这里的中文引号内容当成历史中文原句或访谈录音的逐字转录。即使引文涉及中文作品，作者的英文选译、节录、转述及译者的中文回译仍须区分；原注保留检索线索。文字来源的这一限制不影响作者对访谈或引文的署名归属。

艺术作品、展览及出版物的中文题名，未能由原件或可靠机构记录确认者，应视为便于阅读的译名。双语稿保留对应英文题名；参考文献保留原文著录。拼音人名不能仅凭读音反推汉字；存在疑问时须保留原拼音或在专名表说明证据层级。

对原书自身的年代、地名、拼写或引文疑点，不以无声改写替代作者文本。已确定的抽取断词、串行和图像解码错误在数据中留有修复记录；需要讨论的原作疑点单列校注。书目和索引中底本实际印出的异常也与抽取错误区分。

图像沿用底本，包括原作的黑白／彩色状态和组合关系。彩色图版的原始 JPEG 数据在直接查看时会发生反色；交付稿使用按照 PDF 色彩参数解码的 PNG，原始抽取文件保留作来源证据。图中的旧行政区划及原文标签保留，不能误认作当今地图。

本稿的校对证据区分逐段语义比较、来源覆盖、外部事实核验、版面检查及线上发布核验。语义校对与结构覆盖不等于对全部引用文献和历史陈述进行了独立查证。



## 已确认的底本文字差异

第七章原注43将 Graham Harman 的书名写为 *Tool-Being*，而原书参考文献印刷页310印为 *Tool-Beijing: Heidegger and the Metaphysics of Objects*。本稿保留两处底本写法，便于对照；这不是抽取过程引入的差异。

原书索引印刷页332的 neoliberalism 条目实际印有 “andartists at Lugu Lake”，其中 and 与 artists 之间没有空格。本稿保留底本著录，检索时应将其理解为 “and artists”。

导论印刷页23引述 Danto 的句子出现 decry，中文按该论述语境译为“辨识”。关于它与 descry 的差别，正文校注保留疑点；本次没有取得足以认定原刊印刷文字及勘误的证据，不能把这一处理称为已证实的作者笔误。

## 专名和原作陈述的处理

Wu Weihe、Bai Chongmin、Shan Lianxiao、摄影者 Yan Yan 与 Han Lei 的汉字身份，本次没有完成针对具体人物的一手来源确认，因此统一保留书中罗马字写法。这不意味着此前汉字写法必然错误。作品题名与引文未另注核验者，仍适用前述译名和回译原则。

正文及原注中的年代差异、回忆性表述、旧行政区划和历史判断按作者文本保留。校对不以未经证实的推测改写这些陈述，读者应结合原注所列材料研究。本稿未声称对所有历史事实、采访身份或引用资料作独立查证。



worlding / worldings — 世界营造。指通过表象与实践构成世界的过程，与 globalization（全球化）区分。

globalization — 全球化。不与 worlding 合并。

zone of encounter — 相遇地带。强调相遇中的权力差异和意义生产。

feminist sight lines — 女性主义视线。第三部分的组织概念；不是单纯的视觉方向。

avant-garde / xianfeng — 前卫／先锋。保留作者对英文概念与中文先锋的翻译史讨论，不机械统一。

nüxing / funü — 女性／妇女。作为被历史建构的范畴保留拼音和区别。

nannü — 男女。保留文中的关系性用法。

nüxing yishu — 女性艺术。不自动改成女性主义艺术；作者讨论两者间的历史距离。

feminism / feminist — 女性主义／女性主义的。历史原名中的女权、妇女运动等保留，不全局替换。

late socialism / late liberalism — 晚期社会主义／晚期自由主义。保留理论搭配。

catachresis — 词语误用（转义性挪用）。此处为理论术语：旧词脱离既定用法而建构新范畴，不是作者判定某人用错词；见第七章对女兵、军艺、女性艺术家的界定。

future anterior — 将来完成时。作为追问历史中被预期的未来的方法；见第七章对白露的讨论。

suzhi — 素质。保留社会分类与治理语境，不一概改成个人能力。

liumang — 流氓。保留其历史和性别化含义。

site specificity — 场域特定性。指作品与具体地点及制度、社会关系的关联。

monumentality / ephemerality — 纪念碑性／短暂性。形容词式表述可用纪念碑式、短暂的；不把ephemeral误译成无意义。

chromogenic print — 彩色显影照片。不是透明片；灯箱等载体另行说明。

machinima — 游戏引擎电影。在虚拟环境中以游戏软件制作影像。

Ocean Paradise — 远洋天地。开发商中英项目表及原书图2.03门头确认。

East Modern Art Center / Yuanyang yishu zhongxin — 远洋艺术中心。保留英文名与原书拼音，中文采用当时报导使用的机构名。

Tani Barlow — 白露。采用南京大学高研院学者记录的中文名，修正前后章音译不一致。
